If (b) lived in `relim-ports` the SDK core couldn't be Relim-free. | Split: the Tachyon-swappable seam is the SDK-internal `SyncEnginePort` (§3.2); `relim-ports::WalletSyncPort` stays the thin Relim-consumption seam, designed at W5. **Manager decision owed** (it may instead rename/retire the relim-ports trait); flagged in the log. Reciprocal edit owed at fold: glossary.md's `WalletSyncPort` entry carries the same conflation ("Tachyon-swappable") and follows the manager's call. No relim-ports edit in this track. |

| A4 | **ZIP-302 byte ranges:** ADR-0005 refinement 3 says "leading byte ≥0xF5 = Relim's structured envelope". ZIP 302 / librustzcash actually define: ≤0xF4 UTF-8 text, 0xF5 reserved, 0xF6+zeros = no memo, 0xFF = arbitrary 511-byte payload. | Not a real conflict — the ADR cites the non-text range loosely. No duplicated predicate/mechanism found: seed derivation stays in

## 1. Design decisions

### 1.1 The problem

Ship ZEC send/receive/tips (vision v1.0) **as a community-usable Flutter
Wallet SDK first** (ADR-0013: no good Flutter ZEC SDK exists), consumed by
Relim second. The SDK's headline security property: **seed and spending keys
never leave Rust** — Dart sees addresses, balances, history, sync status, and
swap state only. One package, two consumers:

1. **A third-party Flutter app** — feeds its own mnemonic (or asks the SDK to
   generate one), uses the Dart package.
2. **Relim** — feeds the 32-byte `WalletSubSeed` (frozen label
   `relim/wallet/zip32-seed/v1` — identity.md §2.1; the port: identity-core
   §3) **in Rust**, via `WalletSeedPort` at composition time. The sub-seed
   never touches Dart.

### 1.2 Package topology (brief §6 item 1 — adopting the manager proposal, refined)

```
sdk/                           WALLET-SDK WORKSPACE ROOT (own Cargo.toml +
                               lockfile — carved out of the main workspace;
                               §1.2a gate-0 resolution, founder 2026-06-13)
  ├── zec-wallet-core/            RUST CORE (the extraction unit's engine)
  │                            librustzcash-direct, sync, SwapPort + providers.
  │                            NO relim-* deps. NO FRB. forbid(unsafe). Public
  │                            Rust API usable by any Rust host.
  ├── zec-wallet-swap-near/  [SDK deliverable — ADR-0525; LANDED W-swap-1] the
  │                            NEAR Intents 1Click SwapPort adapter — a SEPARATE
  │                            crate, never a module of the core (§3.5 kill
  │                            layer 1; isolates its HTTP/TLS/JSON deps from the
  │                            always-on core). Thin HAND-AUDITED typed REST
  │                            client; rides NetDialer/TorPolicy.
  └── zec_wallet/              FLUTTER PACKAGE (FFI plugin; working name §1.3)
      ├── lib/                 Dart API (this spec §3.3)
      ├── rust/                FRB bridge crate `zec_wallet` (package name =
      │                        artifact name — Cargokit ignores `[lib] name`) —
      │                        depends ONLY on zec-wallet-core(+swap-near optional);
      │                        cdylib+staticlib; member of the sdk/ workspace

                               core; receives WalletSubSeed via WalletSeedPort.
                               NOT part of the extraction unit; lives in the MAIN
                               workspace (it has relim-* deps). W5 consumption
                               note: it must NOT path-dep zec-wallet-core directly
                               (that would re-pull the SDK's pre-release `digest`
```

#### 1.2a Own workspace (gate-0 resolution — founder-authorized 2026-06-13)

The wallet SDK is its **own cargo workspace** (`sdk/Cargo.toml`, own lockfile),
carved out of the main workspace. **Why:** the ZEC key-derivation/sync stack
(`zcash_client_backend`/`zcash_client_sqlite` → `zcash_transparent` → `bip32
=0.6.0-pre.1` → `digest =0.11.0-pre.9`) cannot share ONE lock with the main
workspace's Mostpost pq-crypto path (ml-dsa → sha3 → STABLE `digest ^0.11`) —
same 0.11 semver bucket, unresolvable (root Cargo.toml gate-0). The SDK is
extraction-ready (ADR-0013) with **no Mostpost/relim-\* deps**, so its own lock
takes the pre-release `digest` with no collision — **proven** (`cargo add
zcash_client_backend` in `sdk/` locks cleanly). This is the gate-0 option (b),
and it ALSO realises ADR-0013's "extraction = move one dir" (extraction is now
`git mv sdk/` to a new repo; the written procedure is `docs/plan/stage-7-extraction.md`,
which writes the `.extracted` marker at the new root — without it the supply-chain policy
tests panic by design, the S262 adjudication's owed step). Pins are mirrored from the root
`[workspace.dependencies]` into `sdk/Cargo.toml` (kept in sync on bumps). CI:
`just ci` runs the main workspace; a `cd sdk && cargo …` pass covers the wallet
workspace (Justfile delta, handed to the manager — the Justfile is manager-owned).
- **Why a separate bridge crate:** keeps the core FRB-free (pure Rust,
  consumable by non-Flutter Rust hosts — including Relim, which never goes
  through Dart), and gives FRB codegen a single dedicated input crate.
- **Extraction-readiness invariant (named test, §8):** the core's public API
  and the bridge crate reference no `relim-*` crate. CI-checkable with the
  existing dep-boundary tooling pattern.
- **Extraction dep policy (stronger than "no relim-*"):** every dependency of
  the extraction unit (core + bridge + Dart package) must be **publicly
  resolvable** — crates.io / pub.dev only, no git pins. This rules out the
  Mostpost consumed crates (`crypto-primitives`, `identity` — private git
  pins, ADR-0002): the SDK's sealing uses **RustCrypto directly**
  (misuse-resistant AEAD, e.g. `chacha20poly1305` XChaCha — same audited
  family the consumed crates wrap; "audited libs whole" holds either way).
  A second deliberate pattern-instance, NOT a second source of truth: the
  Relim-side predicate (how Relim seals ITS stores) stays owned by
  local-storage/identity-core.

### 1.3 Name

Dart package **`zec_wallet`** (dir `sdk/zec_wallet/`), with `zec_wallet_ui`
and `zec_wallet_ui_platform` beside it; the bridge crate and native library
are `zec_wallet` / `libzec_wallet`; the engine crates are `zec-wallet-core`
and `zec-wallet-swap-near`; the C header is `include/zec_wallet_net_dialer.h`.
**The working name became the public name on 2026-09-16 (founder, S282):**
descriptive ticker use, no Zcash-trademark implication, no Relim branding
(founder-confirmed 2026-06-10); the Zcash Foundation answered that no
permission is needed to use "ZEC" and that attribution names the Foundation
only (`docs/handoff/zf-trademark-request-2026-09-15.md`); the identifiers are
free on pub.dev, crates.io, npm and GitHub (`docs/plan/rename-zec-flutter.md`
§5a). One name family for every layer, on purpose: "flutter" is what pub.dev
already says and would be wrong on the engine (a `zec_flutter` rename landed
and was reversed the same day — the same plan, §7). The independence notice
names the discontinued ZecWallet project as unrelated. Nothing in the package
hard-codes the name in user-visible strings (there are none — §6/§8 i18n) or
storage paths (`WalletConfig.db_dir` is host-supplied). **Frozen, never
renamed:** the reference consumer's data-dir leaf `zec_wallet`, the Android
keystore alias base `zec_wallet.wrap` (§4.3a), and every exported C symbol
(`zec_wallet_*` seed-port and net-dialer verbs, the `ZW_*` constants) a host
resolves by name.

### 1.4 How Relim consumes it (decided here, built at W5)

**Relim consumes the Rust core directly — never the Dart package.** Reason:
the sub-seed handoff must stay in Rust; two FRB-generated native libraries in
one app cannot share a `Wallet` instance, so a Dart-side handoff would force
key material across the bridge — forbidden. Concretely (W5):

- `relim-wallet-host` implements `relim-ports::WalletSyncPort` over the core
  and constructs the wallet with the `WalletSubSeed` obtained via
  `WalletSeedPort` (identity-core §3: relim-core implements it; composition
  roots never see the value).
- Wallet UI state reaches Relim's Flutter via **relim-ffi** with mirrored
  DTOs (`#[frb(mirror)]` over the core's DTO types — single source of truth
  stays the core; the mirror is codegen, not a copy).
- *Alternative considered:* linking both FRB bridges into one binary so the
  Relim app dogfoods the Dart package via an "attach by handle" registry.
  Deferred to a W5 manager decision — clever but adds symbol/init collision
  risk for no v1 user value.

### 1.5 FRB codegen for a standalone package (brief §6 item 1)

FRB **v2** (current 2.12.0 — verified), the shareable-package template:
`flutter_rust_bridge_codegen create <name> --template plugin` ("a shareable
Flutter package usable across multiple applications" — the supported path
for third-party distributable packages), `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml` at the
package root with `rust_input: crate::api` pointing into
`sdk/zec_wallet/rust/src/api/`, **Cargokit** build glue (copied into the
package) so `flutter build` compiles the Rust for every target. Honest
pub.dev caveat (verified): library packages get **no prebuilt binaries** —
consumers compile the Rust from source (need a toolchain); a prebuilt-binary
flow is a post-extraction work item, stated in the package README from day
one. Regeneration discipline = the known gotcha: regenerate after ANY
`api/*.rs` change; a `just` recipe wraps it once the package exists (W3;
Justfile edits are manager-coordinated). iOS/macOS static-link loader quirk
per the project's Flutter rules applies to the example app. (Two
independent FRB cdylibs in one app — the rejected §1.4 alternative — was
indeed broken on web until FRB 2.12.0 and remains the least-battle-tested
path; the rejection stands on evidence, not caution.)

### 1.6 Scope cuts (principle 9 — one thing done well)

- **One account (ZIP-32 account 0) per wallet instance** in v1, shielded-only
  (Orchard + Sapling, no transparent — the G7 default UA); the DTOs
  carry no account field but the DB schema (zcash_client_sqlite) already
  supports more — additive later.
  - **(Amended 2026-06-22, founder-directed — §3.3a Recv-2):** v1.x adds a
    host-toggleable transparent **RECEIVE** address surfaced ALONGSIDE the
    shielded UA (for CEX withdrawals + swap-in deliveries that land transparent,
    §1.7). The shielded UA stays the DEFAULT + recommended; this widens the
    receive surface only — still ONE account, still no multi-account, and the
    shielded-only G7 default UA is unchanged.
- **No fiat price feeds, no telemetry, no update checks** — the SDK makes
  exactly two kinds of connections, ever: the configured lightwalletd-protocol
  endpoint, and (only if the host constructs it) the swap provider (§5).
- ~~**No UFVK/viewing-key export** in v1 (watch-only is a post-1.0 candidate;
  it is privacy-sensitive surface, not a key-leak, but stays out until the
  public API stabilizes).~~ **SUPERSEDED (#397, ADR-0538):** watch-only +
  the ONE sanctioned, deliberately-gated UFVK export ship per §3.7 — the cut
  held until the API stabilized, exactly as written; §3.7 is the promised
  "new spec + review cycle".
- **No WASM** (§9). No multi-asset balances (ADR-0014: ZEC-centric).

### 1.7 Prior art — Zodl/Zashi mining (2026-06-10; ADR-0005 "mine as reference implementation")

Web-verified against the zcash swift/android wallet SDKs (MIT, under the
`zcash` GitHub org) **and the Zodl app repos** (`zodl-inc/zodl-ios`,
`zodl-inc/zodl-android` after the Feb-2026 rebrand). Headline: **the
standalone `zcash-light-client-ffi` is gone — the Swift SDK absorbed the Rust
layer in-tree** (the ecosystem itself converged on librustzcash-direct,
independently validating ADR-0005). What we adopt vs reject, filtered against
the Relim vision:

| Zashi/Zodl solution (evidence: their `Synchronizer`/`ZcashSDK`/`CompactBlockProcessor` + CHANGELOGs) | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Spend-before-Sync** — non-linear scanning via `suggest_scan_ranges`; funds spendable mid-sync | ADOPT (free with the built-in engine); surfaced as `spendable_ready` in `SyncStatus` (§2.5) |
| propose → create → submit with **per-tx `TxSubmitResult`** — one proposal can yield SEVERAL txs (pool-crossing); `NotAttempted` is a first-class outcome | ADOPT — §3.1 send shape corrected; partial failure never collapsed (§2.5) |
| **Transparent-funds shielding** (`proposeShielding` + threshold) — exchange withdrawals land transparent | ADOPT — §3.1 `propose_shield`; `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT` named constant; privacy-positive, very on-vision |
| **Bundled checkpoints** (modern spacing 2,500 blocks, refreshed every release; nearest ≤ birthday) + `estimateBirthdayHeight(date)` + new-wallet **live tree state at tip−100** with bundle fallback | ADOPT the bundle + `estimate_birthday` UX (§3.1); **INVERT the live/bundle priority** — the crypto audit (2026-06-14, §3.2f) proved a live frontier is cryptographically unverifiable (the backend trusts lightwalletd for tree state), so we provision the birthday frontier from the BUNDLE only, never a live `get_tree_state` (the M2 live-frontier threat eliminated, not "fallback") |
| **Retry-forever sync loop** — their retry-capped loop generated "manually restart the synchronizer" bug reports, so `defaultRetries = Int.max`; backoff cap 600 s; 10-min stuck-sync watchdog | ADOPT (§6.2/§7) |
| **Tor `ServiceMode` circuit isolation** — per-txid circuit groups; broadcast/fetch-tx/tree-state over Tor; bulk compact-block download Direct-only (hard `require` in their client) | ADOPT the isolation mechanism; **TIGHTEN the policy** — verified: their Direct-only split is an app-level perf choice, NOT an upstream limit (full gRPC-over-Tor works, §2.3) — so our `Required` = genuinely zero clearnet; the residual Q7 is restore-speed UX posture |
| Seed **per-call transient**; spending key **derived on demand, never stored**; try-without-seed → `SeedRequired` → retry-with-seed (Rust migrations occasionally need the seed) | ADOPT — validates §4.2; adds the `SeedRequired` contract to `open` (§6.1) |
| Stable, subsystem-prefixed, greppable **error codes** (their 217-case generated enum; release notes cite codes) | ADOPT the pattern (codes by subsystem), not the generator |
| **No DB encryption** (plain rusqlite; OS file protection + backup-exclusion: Android `no_backup/`, iOS `isExcludedFromBackup`) | **DIVERGE** — we add sealed-key at-rest (§4.3); their backup-exclusion flags adopted ON TOP (cheap, orthogonal) |
| USD exchange-rate fetch (median-of-exchanges, isolated Tor circuit) | **REJECT** for the SDK core — no fiat feeds (§1.6); the isolated-circuit pattern noted for any host-side opt-in |
| View-only accounts (UFVK import) · PCZT hardware-wallet signing · multi-endpoint `Broadcaster` | View-only accounts: **ADOPTED at #397 (§3.7, ADR-0538)** — `import_account_ufvk` + `AccountPurpose::ViewOnly`, the same upstream seam. PCZT signing + multi-endpoint `Broadcaster`: still DEFER post-1.0 |
| Multi-account keyed by **UUID, not ZIP-32 index** (their painful late retrofit) | NOTE — our single-account v1 keeps identifiers opaque so the retrofit stays cheap |

App-level mining (Zodl app, both platforms):

| Zodl app solution (evidence: `WalletBirthday`/`SmartBannerStore`/`SwapAndPay*`/`WalletStorage` + issue tracker) | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Restore birthday UX**: optional height field + *"estimate my block height"* month/year picker (`estimateBirthdayHeight`); skip ⇒ clamped to Sapling activation (full scan); *"Keep the app open"* restore guidance | ADOPT as the host UX contract over `estimate_birthday` (§3.1); skip-cost surfaced honestly (§9 iOS row) |
| **One-tap shield banner** when transparent balance > threshold **= 100,000 zatoshi (0.001 ZEC) on BOTH platforms** + typical-fee display + opt-in auto-shielding | ADOPT the threshold value (§7) + `propose_shield`; banner/auto-shield policy is host-side |
| **Swap opt-in gate, disclosures-as-blocking-UX**: two explicit toggles ("Allow Third-Party Requests" / "Turn on IP Address Protection" = Tor) + forced acknowledgments ("my IP will be leaked by the NEAR API" without Tor); *"transactions executed via the NEAR API are transparent — all information public"* | ADOPT as DATA: `provider_legs_transparent` + `IpUnlessTor` in `SwapPrivacyDisclosure` (§2.6) — our disclosure DTO must be able to express every sentence of their copy |
| Swap deposit-screen rules: exact amount or refund; no exchange-source sends; deadline-bounded deposits (their "24 h" = Zodl's own chosen deadline, NOT a platform constant — verified); **under-deposit ⇒ top-up-by-deadline or refund**; "realized slippage" in history; slippage default 2% (0.5/1/custom) | ADOPT: `SwapStatus::UnderDeposited` (§2.6), `SLIPPAGE_DEFAULT_BPS = 200`, `SWAP_DEADLINE_DEFAULT`, `realized_slippage` on the terminal record |
| Swap-out destination validation: *"Zcash address is not allowed"* | ADOPT (§2.6 `destination`) — a ZEC→ZEC "swap" is a fee-burning provider round-trip |
| **Swap TRANSPORT (code-verified 2026-06-13, `zodl-inc/zodl-android`):** `KtorNearApiProvider` (`ui/common/provider/NearApiProvider.kt:48–76`) is a HAND-ROLLED Ktor REST client over the four 1Click endpoints (`/v0/{tokens,quote,deposit/submit,status}`), with hand-written DTOs, a CLOSED `SwapStatus` enum, and transparent/shielded deposit-address modeling (`NearSwapDataSourceImpl.kt:11,13,203–225`) — **NOT** the TS `@defuse-protocol/intents-sdk`, **NOT** the generated `one-click-sdk-rs` | **VALIDATES `zec-wallet-swap-near` (W-swap-1)**: the reference wallet independently made the SAME choice — same four endpoints, hand-rolled client, closed status enum, bounded hand-written DTOs, quote-validation test. The intents-sdk (TS-only, 6 bridge impls + multi-chain signing, ~8.2k LOC) is the wrong tool for a Rust ZEC core (and is what 1Click abstracts away). DIFFERENCE: Zodl's swap client is plain clearnet Ktor (no Tor in the swap path); our `NetDialer`/`TorPolicy`-forced transport is a deliberate hardening over the baseline (§3.2 m5) |
| **Seed custody = app-side** (iOS Keychain `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`; Android EncryptedSharedPreferences) → their `keysMissing` wallet-loss scare cluster (#1024/#1068/#1076) | **DIVERGE + inherit the lesson**: SDK-side sealed persistence option instead (`SeedPersistence`, §4.2) — app-side custody in Flutter would mean seed-in-Dart; their keychain-vs-DB inconsistency becomes our typed `KeystoreInconsistent` (§6.1), never a silent fresh wallet |
| Per-screen **reference-counted FLAG_SECURE** (Android), none possible on iOS | NOTE — host-app guidance (SDK has no UI); flagged for the W4 app-frame spec |
| **Note fan-out pain**: sequential sends blocked while single change note confirms (their #2124; "increase note fan-out after spends") | ADOPT as a requirement probe — **tips in channels are exactly sequential small sends**; §7 + named test (§8) |
| Biometric/app-lock (`BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL`; allow-when-no-device-auth fallback) | NOTE host-side; the silent allow-on-no-passcode fallback is the anti-pattern — Relim's gate posture is identity-core's, not ours to spec |

Pitfalls inherited as design constraints: SQLite block-cache blowup → a
**BOUNDED, disposable, delete-after-scan block cache from day one** (their
failure was an *unbounded* cache *coupled to* the wallet DB — a multi-GB cache
DB they deleted, not migrated; we keep SQLite's crash-atomicity + encryption but
make the cache a SEPARATE, `CACHE_MAX_BYTES`-bounded, blow-away-able DB —
§3.2e); the **pending-tx DB removal** lesson — tx state lives
chain-derived only (matches §6.2: our queue stores INTENTS, never tx state);
**adaptive batch size** in output-dense ranges (their hardcoded "sandblasting"
window is the fossil of a one-size batch); **unary vs streaming gRPC timeouts
split** (their `[ZUTXO0001]` regression); reorg constants (max 100 / rewind
10); tx expiry inherited from the Rust backend (verified:
`DEFAULT_TX_EXPIRY_DELTA = 40`, ZIP-203 post-Blossom — their CHANGELOG "20"
is stale; we inherit the constant, never duplicate it); the `shardtree`
note-commitment corruption fix floor folds into A8's pin verification;
**"birthday not respected as sync start"** (their #823) — the restore-start
named test (§8) asserts it.

### 1.8 Build vs reuse (verified 2026-06-10 — what we write, what we consume)

**REUSE WHOLE** (crates.io, pinned exact per refinement 5; "audited libs

### 1.9 Universality across custody tiers (the custody invariant — SDK design law, FR-23)

The SDK is signing-capability-**agnostic**: an embedder that keeps no seed at
rest and grants the wallet no standing signing capability (a per-spend
credential, biometric-per-send, or an external/hardware signer) must reach
every money capability a held-seed embedder reaches. The one principle that
makes this true, adopted as design law:

> **The custody invariant.** No money flow may require a *standing* signing
> capability. Every spend either (1) signs inside the host's authorize-spend
> bracket at a user-present moment, or (2) parks visibly ("needs your
> authorization") until a user-present moment and then signs in the bracket.
> A background/queue-drain step may (re-)**broadcast** an already-signed tx,
> but never **signs**. (The seed chokepoint is `Inner::acquire_seed` — held
> bytes for `SealedKeychain`, else `WalletSeedPort::provide_seed`, which is
> `Unavailable` at a background drain with no live user.)

This generalizes beyond swap — it is the rule every money path (send, shield,
move, swap deposit, TEX two-step) obeys. It is the reason a host-custody tier
is a first-class SDK target, not a degraded one.

**The universality tier table** — the public-SDK release yardstick. Rows =
custody tiers (from `SeedPersistence` §4.2 + the #327 authorizer seam);
columns = money capabilities; each cell is the *honest* support state.

- **T0 core-only** — no UI package; the embedder drives the Rust core directly.
- **T1 UI-package · held custody** — `zec_wallet_ui` + `SeedPersistence::SealedKeychain`
  (seed at rest, offline-derivable; pass-through authorizer).
- **T2 UI-package · host custody** — `zec_wallet_ui` + `SeedPersistence::None` +
  `WalletSeedPort` (no seed at rest; per-spend credential; the seed is transient,
  present only inside the authorize-spend bracket). Relim's tier.

| capability | T0 | T1 held | T2 host-custody |
|---|---|---|---|
| receive (fresh, offline) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ FR-24 (`freshlyGenerated: true` on create, or a configured ≤-bundle-tail birthday — §3.2f) |
| sync / balance | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| interactive send | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (in-bracket sign) |
| offline **queued** send | ✓ | ✓ | **✓ FR-23-b (parked authorization)** |
| shield / move | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (in-bracket sign) |
| **OutOfZec swap deposit** | ✓ | ✓ | **✓ FR-23-a (in-bracket sign-at-execute)** |
| IntoZec swap (receive) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

The T2 OutOfZec-deposit cell is the one FR-23-a turns from **bug** → supported:
pre-FR-23 `SwapHostPolicy{enabled:true}` was accepted but the deposit sat
`Queued` forever (signed only at a background drain the port can't serve) — a
bug, not a policy. The T2 offline-queued-send cell is FR-23-b's: supported, but
by clause (2) rather than clause (1) — the send parks visibly and signs in a
LATER bracket the user opens, not in the one that committed it. The distinction
is real and stays visible in the UI ("Send now" on the parked row), so the cell
reads ✓ with its mechanism named rather than an unqualified ✓.

### 1.9.1 FR-23-b — parked authorization (the invariant's clause-2 mechanism)

Clause (2) of the custody invariant says a spend that cannot sign now **parks
visibly and signs later, in a bracket**. FR-23-a implements clause (1) for the
swap deposit. FR-23-b implements clause (2) generically, for every durable
`Queued` intent in the §4.4 outbox.

**The verb.** `Wallet::authorize_parked_send(id, created_at)` — drive ONE
already-committed queued intent through the SAME propose→claim→create(sign)
core the background drain uses (`send::prepare_queued`), **synchronously, at a
user-present moment**, then hand the signed group to the detached broadcast
kick. It is `send_deposit_now`'s sign-half generalized from the deposit row to
any row: the row is already durable (the commit happened at `queue_send`), so
this call moves only the *timing of the SIGN* — never the commitment.

**Why a new verb and not `retry_parked_send`.** `retry_parked_send` re-arms the
ZIP-320 retry budget and nothing else ("nothing is signed or sent by this
call"); at T2 the later background pass it re-arms *for* still cannot sign, so
the re-arm can only loop. The two verbs compose and stay distinct: a paused row
re-arms first (budget, no money), then authorizes (sign, in-bracket).

**Granularity is forced, not chosen (founder decision D1, 2026-07-25).** The
host's per-spend credential is take-once and every queued row presents ITS OWN
FR-17 `SpendBinding` on the seed pull (`intent.binding` → `acquire_seed`), so
one staging can serve exactly one row: **one row = one bracket = one signed
group**. A batch affordance is a host/UI loop over N brackets, never one
bracket signing N rows — an N-row bracket would require the host to pre-stage N
credentials, which is precisely the multi-slot staging FR-18 exists to prevent.
A TEX two-step row is still ONE bracket: the engine signs the `[tx0, tx1]`
chain in a single `create_proposed_transactions` call, so leg-2 needs no second
authorization. (If leg-1 mines and leg-2 dies, the row goes `Stranded` and the
recovery is the manual ephemeral sweep — itself an authorizer-bracketed,
user-present flow at every tier.)

**Capability advertisement stays HOST-SET (founder decision D2, 2026-07-25).**
`walletOfflineQueueSupportedProvider` remains an explicit host flag, not one
derived from "a parked authorizer is wired": wiring the seam is not proof the
host can *stage a credential on demand*, and this flag's whole job is the
honesty rule "never advertise a queue that cannot drain". Its doc now states
that a prompt-per-spend host MAY set it true once it serves
`authorizeParkedSend`.

**Money-safety envelope (unchanged guarantees, new call site).**
- The durable claim still precedes signing — `mark_submitting` is the atomic
  conditional claim, so a racing background drain and a user-paced
  authorization can never both sign one intent (the loser reads `Retry`).
- The seed still resolves at the ONE chokepoint (`Inner::acquire_seed`), still
  presenting THAT row's binding, still B1-verified against the stored account
  (`ensure_seed_controls_account`) before a tx exists.
- A watch-only wallet refuses at the chokepoint (`WalletError::WatchOnly`,
  §3.7 D3) — the verb needs no watch-only branch of its own.
- The `created_at` identity pin matches `cancel`/`retry`: a reused rowid
  authorizes NOTHING.
- Nothing new is broadcast in-bracket. The signed group rides the detached
  kick, with the §6.1 Phase-1 `ReBroadcast` arm as the durable fallback —
  identical to FR-23-a, and for the same reason (an unbounded in-bracket
  broadcast would extend a host-timed future).

**The kick's bounded retry, and the residual under sync-off (#400 R1).** "The
drain covers a missed broadcast" holds only for a wallet that SYNCS:
`resubmit_queued_sends` — and with it the `ReBroadcast` arm above — is driven
exclusively by `after_synced`. A host running with its sync policy off issues no
passes, so for it that fallback never runs, and a single dropped packet left a
signed, note-spending transaction that nothing would ever re-send, after the user
had been told the payment was on its way. The kick therefore retries the group up
to `KICK_BROADCAST_MAX_ATTEMPTS` times with a doubling backoff, re-running BOTH
gates (deadline, open) on a fresh clock each round, and stops as soon as the
group's **FINAL tx — the one that pays the recipient — has been ACCEPTED** in any
round — a duplicate parent beside an accepted final tx is delivery, not a fault; a
rejected final tx is not (#401 R4b, below). (Corrected 2026-10-06, follow-up review
N01: the rule was "every tx has an endpoint verdict and at least one was accepted",
which stopped on tx0 accepted beside a rejected payout tx1.) This closes the
transient-miss case, not the process-death case: a kill mid-kick still hands the row back to §6.1. That is why the SIGNED outcome carries
different copy when no sync pass will run — it names the residual. It names NO
remedy (#401 R5, and #403 R9f correcting this paragraph): the same condition is
reached by a FAILED sync start, where "re-enable syncing" is simply the wrong
instruction, so the copy is cause-agnostic and the screen's own sync notice carries
whichever remedy applies.

Two limits of the retry, stated because the first draft of this section overclaimed
both:

- **The duration bound is on EXECUTED time.** A compile-time assert pins the
  worst case (geometric backoff sum + a full group of jittered unary timeouts per
  attempt) well inside the tx-expiry headroom. `tokio::time::sleep` measures
  executed time, so a phone that suspends mid-backoff resumes the sleep whenever
  the app is next scheduled — hours later, in principle. The retry therefore
  cannot push a transaction past expiry *while the app runs*; it can re-broadcast
  an already-expired transaction after a long suspension. That is money-safe (the
  endpoint rejects it; nothing double-spends and no note is re-committed) but it
  is not the stronger claim, and for a parked row the per-round deadline gate is a
  structural no-op — `authorize_parked_send` only reaches rows whose
  `deposit_deadline` is `None`, which `deposit_gate` answers `Proceed`
  unconditionally. The deadline arm of the loop exists for the FR-23-a deposit
  origin, which shares the code.

  **DELIBERATELY NOT bounded on ELAPSED time (#403 R7 added such a bound; #407 R1
  removed it).** A suspension that outlasts the backoff resumes into a fresh round,
  by design. The removed budget compared `now_unix` against the kick's start and
  stopped at 600 s — but the transaction it was protecting carries a ~50-minute
  expiry window (`DEFAULT_TX_EXPIRY_DELTA`, 40 blocks) with a guaranteed ≥ 20-block
  floor after `send`'s re-anchor, so at 600 s the round it suppressed was almost
  always a round on a STILL-VALID transaction. And because the gate above answers
  `Proceed` unconditionally for a parked row, it could only ever suppress on the
  ONE origin with no §6.1 drain behind it — so at a sync-off or failed-start host
  it abandoned the payment outright. The trade, priced both ways: a late round
  costs one endpoint rejection (the loop writes no durable state — its tally is
  logged, never latched, so a rejection cannot mark the row terminal); a skipped
  round costs the user's money. The kick stays bounded by the attempt cap and the
  compile-time `KICK_BROADCAST_EXECUTED_CEILING_SECS` assert.
- **`Rejected` is code-only, so an all-rejected round is not terminal (#401 R4b —
  this bullet used to state the limit and leave it).** `SubmitOutcome::Rejected`
  carries a number and nothing else, folding the endpoint's OWN transient failures
  (a lightwalletd that cannot reach its backend answers a successful gRPC call with
  a non-zero code) in with already-known, expired and invalid. That transient class
  is exactly what the retry was written for, and treating the whole class as
  delivery stopped the kick on round 1 with `faults = 0`, leaving a signed,
  note-spending transaction that — with no sync passes — nothing would ever re-send.
  So the stop condition now also requires **at least one `Accepted`**: a partly
  already-known, partly accepted group is done; an all-rejected round costs a fault
  and another attempt. The waste in the benign direction is bounded and moves no
  money (a dead tx is re-offered at most `KICK_BROADCAST_MAX_ATTEMPTS` times and
  rejected again), and the two shapes stay distinguishable in the event stream:
  `accepted = 0` with `rejected > 0` is the rejected one, `rejected = 0` the
  transport-starved one. (`rejected` accumulates across rounds, so it is not
  comparable to `tx_count`, which is the group size.) Deliberately NOT split by numeric code: the taxonomy is the
  upstream node's, this crate has no vetted table for it, and guessing which codes
  are terminal is how a money path acquires a wrong constant.

**The MID-SIGNATURE row is now visible (#400 R2).** `mark_submitting` commits
before the unbounded ZK prove, so a process kill in that window leaves a durable
`Submitting` row. It used to appear on ZERO host surfaces — `list_queued` filters
it out, `list_in_flight_sends` wants `Sent` + multi-tx, and (until the engine's
create commits) no transaction exists for the activity list — which is the #331
silent-hide shape (a committed spend the user cannot see, so they re-enter it and
both send), and since FR-23-b it is reachable by a user TAP at the moment they
are watching. `list_parked_sends` now reads `Queued` **or** `Submitting`
(`intent_store::list_parkable`) and flags the latter as `ParkedSend::sending`.
Recovery is unchanged and already existed: `list_in_flight` includes
`Submitting`, so the §6.3 reconcile re-queues an unfinished claim on the next
pass. This is a visibility fix — but for a host with no sync passes there is no
next pass, so the hole was permanent, not a window.

**A `Submitting` row spans TWO different truths, and #400 stated only the first
(#401 R2c).** The claim commits before `create_signed_core`; the engine's create
commits the transaction to the wallet DB before `mark_sent_multi` flips the row
to `Sent`. So:

- Before the create commits, the row has no transaction anywhere, and its amount
  is still an earmark over a spendable balance.
- After it commits and before `mark_sent_multi`, the SAME payment can render on
  BOTH surfaces — parked-as-preparing AND a Pending activity row — and its notes
  have already left the spendable balance, so the earmark contract does NOT hold.

A host surface must therefore not assert the earmark of a `sending` row, and must
not tell the user the payment is absent from activity. Presentation contract:
PREPARING, never "failed" and never "sent"; no CANCEL (the verb is `Queued`-guarded
and a confirm dialog promising "nothing leaves your wallet" would be false past the
create); and no authorize affordance — with ONE exception, that the caller's own
open bracket is what put the row in `Submitting`, where hiding the button would
delete the in-flight cue mid-proof.

**Honest outcomes.** The verb returns a typed outcome so the surface never
lies about what happened: `signed` (signed + kick dispatched), `stillQueued`
(nothing signed — a momentary insufficiency, a cap-parked TEX row, or the
crash-recovery read saying wait; funds untouched, the row stays), `expired` (a
deadline-tagged row whose quote lapsed — deleted, terminal), `notFound`
(already gone / sent / rowid reused, **or a racing background drain that won the
claim** — re-read the list).

A RACING DRAIN YIELDS `notFound` HERE, not `stillQueued`, and this section said
otherwise until #401 R7a. The two origins differ because their loads do:
`intent_store::load_parked` (FR-23-b) filters `state = Queued`, so once the drain
has claimed the row the guarded read misses and the verb answers `notFound` before
`mark_submitting` is ever reached; `intent_store::load` (the FR-23-a deposit
origin) has no state guard, so there the loser really does fall through to
`Prepared::Retry` ⇒ `stillQueued`. Host copy for `notFound` must therefore not
say the payment is gone — the commonest cause leaves it visible as PREPARING on
the very same surface. `stillQueued` is
deliberately NOT an error: nothing failed, the send simply did not become
sendable yet.

**Deposit rows are REFUSED**, exactly as `cancel_parked_send` /
`retry_parked_send` refuse them: `list_parked_sends` excludes deposit rows, so
there is no sanctioned source for a deposit's `(id, created_at)` pin, and one
verb of the family reaching rows the other two cannot would be a surface
inconsistency, not a feature. The FR-23-a sign-failure zombie (a deposit durably
`Queued` after a failed in-bracket sign, holding the one-deposit-in-flight guard
until its quote deadline) therefore keeps its availability wait; its user-paced
exit is a SWAP-SURFACE affordance over the swap↔deposit id linkage, still open.

**The guard is the QUERY, and it is re-run under the claim's lock.** All four
conditions — `id`, `created_at`, `state = Queued`, `deposit_deadline IS NULL` —
live in `intent_store::load_parked`'s WHERE clause, so the read cannot return a
row the verb would then reject. It runs twice: once before the seed pull (fast
fail, no credential burned) and once while holding the `aux_db` lock
`prepare_queued` keeps held across its `mark_submitting` claim. The second run
is load-bearing: `mark_submitting` pins only `id + state`, and the window
between the first read and the claim spans a HUMAN-latency credential prompt —
long enough for a delete plus a rowid-reusing re-enqueue, which would otherwise
sign the first read's request under a different row's id. A miss at either point
is `notFound`, never `stillQueued` (the row is gone; "saved and unchanged" would
be a false money statement).

## 2. Domain types (Rust core; all public DTOs are SDK-owned — librustzcash
types never leak into the public API, so nu-churn is absorbed inside the
core, ADR-0005 refinement 5)

**Enum extensibility policy (review G2 — the one unfixable-post-1.0 class):**
every public state/status enum (`SyncStatus`, `TxStatus`, `SwapStatus`,
`TorState`, `StallReason`, `Memo`, `Network`, error enums) is
`#[non_exhaustive]`; the Dart mirrors are sealed classes with a **required
default arm**, so an SDK upgrade can add variants without breaking compiled
hosts. CI lint lands at W2 (`public_enums_non_exhaustive`, §8).

### 2.1 Money, network, identifiers

```rust
/// Zatoshis. i64 (max ZEC supply ≈ 2.1e15 < 2^53), so the value survives the
/// FRB i64→Dart-int mapping exactly on all shipped platforms (§9 — no web).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Debug)]
pub struct Zatoshis(i64);          // constructor rejects negatives/overflow

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Network { Main, Test }    // runtime param (consensus params), not a cargo feature

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub struct TxId([u8; 32]);
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Debug)] pub struct BlockHeight(u32);
```

### 2.2 Seed input (the boundary type — brief §6 item 3)

```rust
/// Seed input. Zeroize + ZeroizeOnDrop; NO Clone/Debug/Display/Serialize
/// (crypto-rules). Constructors zeroize their inputs.
pub enum SeedSource {
    /// SDK generates 24 words via OsRng (third-party create flow).
    Generate,
    /// Third-party restore: BIP39 mnemonic (+ optional BIP39 passphrase).
    /// Validated (checksum) before use.
    Mnemonic { phrase: Zeroizing<String>, passphrase: Zeroizing<String> },
    /// Raw seed bytes, 32..=252 bytes — BOTH bounds enforced HERE with a
    /// typed error (verified: upstream from_seed PANICS under 32 and ignores
    /// the ZIP-32 upper bound; never let a panic cross FFI). Never truncated.
    /// THE RELIM PATH: WalletSubSeed (32B) enters here, in Rust.
    /// A raw-bytes wallet stores NO mnemonic → reveal_mnemonic is
    /// structurally unsupported for it (§3.1). RESTORE-shaped: possible
    /// prior history is assumed (activation floor, restore-pessimistic
    /// refund seeding).
    RawBytes(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>),
    /// Raw seed bytes the host ATTESTS were minted for the first time
    /// immediately before this call (FR-24 fresh-flag, §3.2f): same 32..=252
    /// door + no-mnemonic contract as RawBytes, but the create takes every
    /// freshly-generated behavior Generate takes — the #356-F4 creation
    /// stamp, the eager offline account import, the fresh birthday default.
    /// The attestation is LOAD-BEARING for money visibility: marking a seed
    /// with prior chain history fresh HIDES its pre-stamp funds + refunds
    /// (§3.2f lying-host contract). Constructor `raw_bytes_fresh`.
    FreshRawBytes(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>),
}

/// Seed-at-rest mode (§4.2 — the deliberate divergence from upstream's
/// app-holds-the-seed contract, which in Flutter would put the seed in Dart).
pub enum SeedPersistence {
    /// SDK seals the seed (keychain-random wrap key, OS ACL — the §4.3
    /// sealing pattern). Default for Dart-path consumers: enables
    /// reveal_mnemonic after restart + internal SeedRequired handling.
    SealedKeychain,
    /// Nothing persisted (the Relim path): SeedRequired bubbles to the host,
    /// which re-derives via WalletSeedPort (cheap, Rust-side).
    None,
}
```

The frozen label `relim/wallet/zip32-seed/v1` and its derivation live in the
identity crate (identity.md §2.1) and are **deliberately absent from this
SDK** — the SDK sees opaque bytes. ZIP-32 derivation inside the core:
`UnifiedSpendingKey::from_seed(network, seed, AccountId(0))` (audited crate
whole; coin type 133/1 comes from `Network`).

### 2.3 Config

```rust
pub struct WalletConfig {
    pub db_dir: PathBuf,             // host-owned location (platform app dir)
    pub network: Network,
    pub endpoint: LightServerEndpoint, // https://host:port — lightwalletd-protocol
                                       // (Zaino-compatible) gRPC. REQUIRED, NO
                                       // DEFAULT (founder 2026-06-10): the SDK
                                       // never picks an endpoint silently — DX
                                       // mitigated by README + example app;
                                       // Relim feeds manifest-listed endpoints (W5)
    pub sync_servers: Vec<SyncServer>, // sync-server-picker.md §2 (S276): the
                                       // OFFERED list — may be empty. `endpoint`
                                       // above is then the DEFAULT; a persisted
                                       // user choice WINS at open (§3.1 there)
    pub tor: TorPolicy,              // REQUIRED field — no default; forces a
                                     // conscious privacy decision (§5.2)
    pub seed_persistence: SeedPersistence, // §4.2; Relim passes None
    pub birthday: Option<BlockHeight>, // restore-from height; None on create
                                       // (= current tip), saves full-chain scan.
                                       // VALIDATED at first sync against the
                                       // endpoint tip: above-tip ⇒ typed
                                       // BirthdayInFuture + event (a too-HIGH
                                       // birthday silently never finds the
                                       // user's notes = "stolen funds" UX);
                                       // below activation ⇒ clamped to
                                       // activation (the Zodl clamp, §1.7)
    pub broadcast_jitter: JitterPolicy, // §5.3; default BROADCAST_JITTER_DEFAULT
}

/// POLICY (what must happen) × RUNTIME (whose Tor does it) are orthogonal —
/// founder 2026-06-10: the SDK must be able to REUSE the host app's
/// Tor/network infrastructure instead of always spawning its own.
pub enum TorPolicy {
    Off,                                  // direct gRPC
    Preferred { runtime: TorRuntime },    // falls back to clearnet WITH a
                                          // surfaced TorFellBack event (§6)
    Required  { runtime: TorRuntime },    // fail-closed: runtime unreachable
                                          // ⇒ no traffic, sync Stalled
}

pub enum TorRuntime {
    // THREE runtimes, none SDK-owned. The June `BuiltIn` arm (SDK-owned arti
    // behind the cargo feature `tor-builtin`) was REMOVED at FR-5 C1
    // (2026-09-17; ADR-0548 D3): no consumer existed — a Dart host adds the
    // `zec_wallet_tor` plugin, which registers through `HostDialer` below,
    // and a Rust host wraps `dialer-tor` in a `Dialer`.
    /// Host-side Tor speaking SOCKS5 (Orbot on Android, system Tor on
    /// desktop, a host sidecar). isolation keys map to per-key SOCKS
    /// credentials (Tor's IsolateSOCKSAuth). REFUSED at the config door
    /// (T0-6; ADR-0543: the loopback-proxy shape is OUT) — the Dart-
    /// expressible path is `HostDialer` below.
    ExternalSocks5 { addr: String },
    /// RUST-level injection: any byte-stream dialer (`NetDialer`, §3.2) —
    /// for a host in the SAME Rust workspace. Cannot cross a dylib seam.
    Dialer(Arc<dyn NetDialer>),
    /// FR-29 (`host-transport-crossing.md`; ADR-0542/0543/0544/0545/0546/
    /// 0047): the dialer a host's NATIVE LIBRARY registered across the
    /// library boundary through the C contract
    /// `sdk/zec_wallet/rust/include/zec_wallet_net_dialer.h` (three verbs,
    /// a completion-callback vtable, a descriptor the host names). The
    /// Relim path: wallet traffic rides Relim's ONE transport (Tor,
    /// Shadowsocks, VLESS, whatever the host runs) behind a trampoline the
    /// host registers at trusted init. Expressible from DART as the unit
    /// `TorRuntimeConfig.hostDialer()`; a `HostDialer` policy validated
    /// while nothing is registered is refused at the door (RW-CFG-001).
    HostDialer(Arc<dyn HostDialer>),
}
// When Tor is on, circuit ISOLATION follows the upstream ServiceMode pattern
// (§1.7): outbound BROADCAST rides a fresh per-tx isolation key so a send is
// unlinkable from everything else. (ASPIRATIONAL for the inbound SYNC fetches —
// tree-state, subtree-roots, GetAddressUtxos, and the §3.3 tx-enhancement
// GetTransaction all ride the SHARED sync circuit today, NOT per-txid keys;
// §3.3 discloses the resulting shielded-receive-set exposure + the deferred
// per-txid-isolation hardening. Reconcile here if that hardening lands.) The
// per-tx broadcast keys flow
// through every runtime (ExternalSocks5 → per-key SOCKS auth; Dialer → the
// host's mapping; HostDialer → passed on every dial, and the `zec_wallet_tor`
// plugin maps them to arti circuit groups). VERIFIED (2026-06-10):
// `tor::Client::connect_to_lightwalletd` builds a full tonic HTTP/2 channel
// over an arti DataStream — unary AND streaming RPCs (incl. bulk block
// download) CAN ride Tor; Zashi's download-Direct-only split is their
// app-level perf choice, not an upstream limit. So Required mode genuinely
// means zero clearnet packets; the cost is restore speed over Tor (a UX
// posture question, §11 Q7 — not a capability question).
// HONEST TRUST BOUNDARY for external runtimes: the SDK can verify it sent
// bytes to the proxy/dialer — it CANNOT attest that the host's
// infrastructure actually routes through Tor. "Required + external runtime"
// = fail-closed on proxy unreachability + the host owns the torness claim;
// stated in the SDK docs, never implied otherwise.
```

### 2.4 Memos & payments (ZIP 302 / ZIP 321)

```rust
/// Follows librustzcash `Memo` semantics (audit A4): we do not invent memo
/// framing. MEMO_BYTES = 512 on the wire; Arbitrary carries 511 (0xFF tag).
pub enum Memo {
    Empty,
    Text(String),            // UTF-8, validated ≤ MEMO_TEXT_MAX_BYTES
    Arbitrary(Vec<u8>),      // ≤ MEMO_ARBITRARY_MAX_BYTES (511); the host's
                             // typed envelope (e.g. Relim tips) rides here — A6
    /// ZIP-302 reserved space (upstream `Future` — verified: 0xF5,
    /// non-canonical 0xF6, 0xF7..=0xFE; canonical 0xF6‖zeros is Empty):
    /// RECEIVABLE as opaque bytes (it exists on-chain — dropping it would
    /// lie); construction-for-send is rejected (we never emit reserved framing).
    Reserved(Vec<u8>),
}

/// ZIP-321 payment request: built programmatically or parsed from a
/// `zcash:` URI (HOSTILE input — §4.5; fuzzed).
pub struct PaymentRequest { pub payments: Vec<Payment> }
pub struct Payment {
    pub recipient: Address,       // parsed + network-checked unified/sapling/transparent
    pub amount: Option<Zatoshis>, // SPEC-DELTA (implemented 2026-06-13): ZIP-321
                                  // allows the request to leave the amount to
                                  // the SENDER (None — the bare donation-QR
                                  // `zcash:ADDR` form); the draft's required
                                  // amount would have rejected valid donation
                                  // QRs. `propose()` rejects amount-less legs
                                  // typed (`SendAmountRequired`/`RW-SEND-002` —
                                  // SHIPPED W3-inc-2d-1; the dedicated §8 test
                                  // `propose_rejects_amount_less_legs_typed` is
                                  // owed at the inc-2d-2 Wallet-integration tier)
    pub memo: Memo,               // memo + transparent recipient = construction
                                  // error; zero-valued output to a transparent-
                                  // only recipient = construction error
                                  // (consensus rule; `transparent_only` comes
                                  // from the AUDITED ZcashAddress predicate,
                                  // NOT kind()==Transparent — a transparent-
                                  // only UA still classifies as Unified)
    pub label: Option<String>,    // ZIP-321 display fields — never sent on-chain
    pub message: Option<String>,
}
```

**IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-13, the ZIP-321 chunk; full review — security ∥ arch ∥
crypto, then code review APPROVE; all findings folded):** `payment_uri.rs`
carries the §3.1 free functions over `zip321 =0.8.0` taken WHOLE (gate-0
re-probed clean: no `zcash_transparent`/`bip32` in its graph; adds only
base64/nom/minimal-lexical to the lock). `Memo::from_wire/to_wire` delegate
every ZIP-302 verdict to `zcash_protocol::memo` — arms only relabel
(Text("")→Empty canonicalization; Arbitrary = full 511 zero-padded, no length
framing, hosts frame inside per A6; Reserved carried whole, receivable, never
sendable). Address capability predicates (`memo_capable`, `transparent_only`)
now come from the audited `ZcashAddress::can_receive_memo` /
`is_transparent_only`; the W2 hand-rolled receiver scan is DELETED (one source
of truth). New errors RW-PAY-006..008 (`MemoInvalid` /
`ZeroValuedTransparentOutput` / `PaymentUriInvalid`), all payload-free —
upstream zip321 error values ECHO URI content and are dropped at the funnel
(§5.4). Bridge `api/payments.rs` ships under the **lossless-token contract**:
the URI string is the canonical form; `ParsedMemo` is a display projection
(machine memos cross as length only — raw bytes never cross THIS path).
`ParsedMemo.Reserved{len}` exists for the future incoming-memo lane
(parse-unreachable today, documented), and core `Memo`/`AddressKind` are wired
into the `bridge_enums_cover_core_variants` drift guard.

**AMENDED 2026-09-05 — the two sentences above used to be wider than the code,
and both halves have since moved.** This paragraph read "composition is
text-memo-only drafts (machine memos are host/Rust constructs, A6)" and "raw
bytes never cross the bridge" flatly. Neither survives:

- **Compose (FR-28, shipped):** `PaymentDraft.memo_bytes` lowers OPAQUE host
  bytes through the audited `Memo::arbitrary`. The A6 justification the old
  sentence carried was never in A6 (nonce hygiene + parser obligations + a fuzz
  target); the real asymmetry is direction — outbound bytes are the CALLER'S OWN.
- **Read (FR-27, this change):** raw machine-memo bytes cross INBOUND at exactly
  ONE verb, `WalletHandle::machine_memos(txidHex)`, **prefix-scoped and opt-in**.
  `ParsedMemo` is untouched and stays length-only — the display projection is
  still a projection, and `inbound_parsed_memo_never_carries_raw_bytes` pins
  that it cannot grow bytes under FR-28's file-wide policy waiver.

The standing rule is therefore not "bytes never cross" but: **bytes cross only
where a host has NAMED the scope it wants, and never as a side effect of a
display read.** Both crossings are `Arbitrary` (`0xFF`) only. `Reserved`
framing is never sendable and never returned as bytes.

### 2.5 Wallet state DTOs (what Dart sees)

```rust
pub struct BalanceSnapshot {
    pub spendable: Zatoshis,        // confirmed ≥ MIN_CONFIRMATIONS, spendable now
    pub pending_incoming: Zatoshis, // received, not yet spendable: below depth OR witness-held (P2-4)
    pub pending_change: Zatoshis,   // our own change in flight
    pub transparent: Zatoshis,      // UNSHIELDED funds — a real, privacy-
                                    // relevant user state (drives the host
                                    // shield banner §1.7; nonzero after a
                                    // failed auto-shield must be visible)
    pub total: Zatoshis,
}

pub enum SyncStatus {
    Idle,                                        // wallet open, sync not started
    Connecting { tor_bootstrap_percent: Option<f32> }, // first-launch arti
                                                 // bootstrap can take MINUTES —
                                                 // an opaque "Connecting" would
                                                 // be a silent hang; arti
                                                 // exposes progress, surface it
    Scanning { from: BlockHeight, to: BlockHeight, percent: f32,
               spendable_ready: bool,
               rewound: bool },                  // rewound (#317): THIS pass has
                                                 // hit ≥1 reorg rewind — first-
                                                 // class, so a host latch reacts
                                                 // explicitly instead of inferring
                                                 // a reorg from a shrinking `to`;
                                                 // resets with the pass (depth
                                                 // stays observability-only,
                                                 // wallet.reorg_rewind §5.4).
                                                 // Spend-before-Sync (§1.7):
                                                 // funds usable before 100%.
                                                 // percent = MONOTONIC scanned/
                                                 // total — never range position
                                                 // (non-linear scan order would
                                                 // make naive percent regress).
                                                 // from/to: to = tip; from is the
                                                 // percent-DERIVED monotonic
                                                 // scanned-equivalent height
                                                 // (scanned_equiv), so to - from =
                                                 // round(span·(1-percent)) — an
                                                 // honest blocks-left that AGREES
                                                 // with percent. NOT the jumping
                                                 // download frontier (which would
                                                 // render "1%, 289 blocks left")
    UpToDate { tip: BlockHeight },
    UpToDateLimited { tip: BlockHeight },        // scanned to the tip, but this
                                                 // BUILD could not read every
                                                 // block (ironwood-nu63-support
                                                 // §6.4): balance is a FLOOR,
                                                 // next step "update the app"
    UpToDateDegraded { tip: BlockHeight,         // scanned to the tip, but this
                       pools: PoolServiceReport },
                                                 // SERVER refused / lied about /
                                                 // withheld a pool's subtree
                                                 // roots (T0-1b): per pool,
                                                 // Served{roots} | Withheld
                                                 // {proven} | Unsupported |
                                                 // HeightViolation; Withheld =
                                                 // served FEWER than the bundle
                                                 // proves — none or a prefix
                                                 // (T0-1d) — and carries the
                                                 // proof, not the gap; next step
                                                 // "switch servers"; a pool name
                                                 // + a bounded count only
    EndpointBehind { tip: BlockHeight,           // scanned to THIS SERVER's tip,
                     newest_known: BlockHeight,  // which is BELOW the newest row
                     pools: Option<PoolServiceReport> },
                                                 // the signed bundle carries for
                                                 // the network, or below the
                                                 // wallet's OWN scanned height
                                                 // less REORG_MAX_BLOCKS
                                                 // (T0-1c; T0-1c-R2): the
                                                 // server is behind the chain,
                                                 // the balance is current only
                                                 // as of `tip`; newest_known is
                                                 // the reference that fired —
                                                 // a public constant of the
                                                 // build or our own height
                                                 // less the margin (a LOWER
                                                 // bound on the lag); a behind
                                                 // pass writes NO last_synced
                                                 // stamp and never sets
                                                 // ever_synced (T0-1c-R2);
                                                 // pools is the report
                                                 // above, carried so a withheld
                                                 // pool is not hidden by the
                                                 // ranking; next step "switch
                                                 // servers". Or scanned to
                                                 // NOTHING (T0-1c-R3, INC-024):
                                                 // when the account's birthday
                                                 // is above tip + 1 and nothing
                                                 // is scanned past the tip, the
                                                 // pass reports the tip without
                                                 // recording it or asking for a
                                                 // block (upstream's
                                                 // update_chain_tip asserts on
                                                 // the inverted range) — same
                                                 // variant, same remedy.
                                                 // Precedence:
                                                 // UpToDateLimited >
                                                 // UpToDateUnverified > this >
                                                 // UpToDateDegraded > UpToDate
    UpToDateUnverified { tip: BlockHeight,       // scanned to the tip, but THIS
                         grace: UnknownBranchGrace, // SERVER will not say which
                         pools: Option<PoolServiceReport>,
                         streak_reported: bool },  // network it is on (GRACE-1,
                                                 // ironwood-nu63-support §6.3 —
                                                 // the Unknown verdict): grace
                                                 // Running { blocks_left,
                                                 // secs_left } (the time on
                                                 // whichever rule expires first;
                                                 // a capable time the clock
                                                 // cannot vouch for is Ended
                                                 // { by: Clock } since GRACE-2,
                                                 // never a None here) or
                                                 // Ended { by: Blocks | Clock |
                                                 // NeverConfirmed, .. }; read
                                                 // from the durable stamp against
                                                 // the device clock after every
                                                 // clean pass, so it survives a
                                                 // relaunch; carries pools so the
                                                 // ranking drops no pool fact;
                                                 // next step "switch servers"
                                                 // (+ "check the device time" for
                                                 // Clock), NEVER "update the app".
                                                 // streak_reported (P3-12, founder
                                                 // S278, Q2 option 2): the rewinding
                                                 // streak has reached its report —
                                                 // the Stalled { EndpointMisbehaving }
                                                 // this claim outranks (P2-6) — so
                                                 // the host DROPS "your balance is
                                                 // current" and names the rewinds;
                                                 // same next step, "switch servers"
    Stalled { reason: StallReason },             // honest degradation — typed,
                                                 // renderable: EndpointUnreachable
                                                 // (transport), TorUnavailable,
                                                 // StorageFull, ChainReorg,
                                                 // Internal (this device: a
                                                 // corrupt store — restore),
                                                 // EndpointMisbehaving (this
                                                 // server answered wrongly —
                                                 // switch servers; when the
                                                 // answer conflicts with a
                                                 // record an EARLIER server
                                                 // wrote, the wallet cannot say
                                                 // which lied, so if every
                                                 // server is refused the exit
                                                 // is a rescan, never a
                                                 // restore — T0-1d),
                                                 // BirthdayInFuture (the
                                                 // configured birthday is
                                                 // above the chain as this
                                                 // server reports it AND above
                                                 // the bundle's newest row —
                                                 // check the height or switch
                                                 // servers; T0-1c-R2 — or, on
                                                 // any pass, the account's
                                                 // birthday above tip + 1 with
                                                 // the tip at or above the
                                                 // grade's reference; T0-1c-R3,
                                                 // unreachable from any shipped
                                                 // resolver today),
                                                 // StorageUnavailable (this
                                                 // device's store busy or an
                                                 // I/O fault — transient,
                                                 // retried, never restore;
                                                 // R10. Internal and it are
                                                 // LOCAL: the loop publishes
                                                 // one only at the second
                                                 // local fault before a pass
                                                 // completes), …
    Offline { last_synced: Option<SyncStamp> },  // no connectivity; queued ≠
                                                 // error; the AGE of what the
                                                 // user is looking at is data
}
/// {height, at}: when the balances/history shown were last chain-confirmed.
pub struct SyncStamp { pub height: BlockHeight, pub at: u64 }

pub struct TxSummary {
    pub txid: TxId,
    pub batch_id: Option<BatchId>,   // groups the txs minted by ONE proposal —
                                     // after a kill, history can reconstruct
                                     // "payment X half-landed" (§6.3); also
                                     // tags shield + swap-deposit txs
    pub mined_height: Option<BlockHeight>,
    pub status: TxStatus,            // Queued | Pending | Confirmed(u32) | Expired | Failed
    pub net_amount: Zatoshis,        // signed effect on this wallet
    pub fee: Option<Zatoshis>,
    pub has_memo: bool,
    pub timestamp: Option<u64>,
}

/// Incoming-funds stream item — the host's tip-detection hook (A6), reshaped
/// by ADR-0536 (#392, FR-11): the ORIGINAL reservation here was a rich per-tx
/// `IncomingTransaction { summary, memos }`; it lost to a MINIMAL counts+heights
/// event whose payload is §5.4-safe BY CONSTRUCTION (a host can log or forward
/// it to a notification path with no sanitizing layer). Attribution — which tx,
/// amount, memo — stays a PULL via `transactions()`/`transaction_memos()` in the
/// main app (FR-11: never the NSE). Delivery: at-least-once over a latest-wins
/// `watch` channel — `new_tx_count`/spans are advisory under coalescing;
/// `total_tx_detected` is the coalesce-proof monotonic. The stream is a
/// FRESHNESS SIGNAL, not an accounting/unlock ledger (FR-10 stays host-side).
/// **`MemoRefresh` has TWO causes (ADR-0539, amending ADR-0536 Decision 4).** It means "an
/// enhancement pass changed how existing rows read": EITHER decrypted tx data was stored
/// (attribution may have improved) OR a `GetStatus` request was answered with a chain status,
/// which flips a send out of "expired" with nothing new to decrypt. A host must NOT read the
/// kind as proof new memo data exists; "re-pull" is correct under both. Core gate:
/// `enhanced > 0 || status_set > 0`.
pub struct IncomingFundsEvent {
    pub kind: IncomingFundsEventKind,   // Replay | Live | MemoRefresh
    pub new_tx_count: u32,              // txs in this edge (advisory)
    pub total_tx_detected: u64,         // monotonic since wallet-open (i64 at the FFI)
    pub span_from_height: Option<u32>,  // height span of the detections
    pub span_to_height: Option<u32>,
    // Opaque versioned watermark — "w1:<height>", a DISTINCT version prefix
    // from the HistoryPage keyset token ("v1:…") so a cross-API mix-up
    // rejects TYPED instead of silently mis-parsing into a wrong window.
    pub cursor: String,
}

/// Queryable Tor/network-privacy state (review G1 — Relim's
/// network-transparency panel needs "is Tor active for the wallet" COLD,
/// without replaying event history). Also a stream (§3.1). In `Dialer` mode
/// the SDK reports policy + flow only — torness ATTESTATION belongs to the
/// host's transport (Relim's dialer over the shared `dialer-tor` crate,
/// `sdk/dialer-tor` — S284), and the variant says which
/// runtime is speaking so the panel can attribute the claim honestly.
pub enum TorState {
    Off,                                   // by configuration
    // The failing arms carry the REGISTERED transport's own name (FR-30 (a),
    // C1): `Some(descriptor.name)` where one is registered, `None` otherwise —
    // the UI then renders its transport-neutral noun. The SDK names no
    // transport the host did not name (ADR-0547).
    Bootstrapping { percent: Option<f32>, transport: Option<HostTransportName> },
    Active { runtime: TorRuntimeKind },
    FellBack,                              // Preferred degraded to clearnet
    // Zero traffic: Required + unreachable, nothing registered, OR the
    // registrant declared `health = FAILED` (ABI v3, ADR-0549). Since S1
    // `truth` this is the GENUINELY-DOWN case only — a dial that FAILED.
    Unavailable { transport: Option<HostTransportName> },
    // S1 `truth` (S291, ADR-0554): the path is READY and nothing has come back
    // over it for `TOR_PATIENCE_SECS` after the first observed failure, while
    // the wallet was trying — the path OR the server, and the SDK does NOT say
    // which, because one connection cannot tell them apart. Payload is
    // `Active`'s, so a host renders the same transport name with a different
    // sentence. Reached from an ACCEPTED dial that carried nothing; a dial that
    // failed is `Unavailable` instead, promptly.
    Unanswered { runtime: TorRuntimeKind },
}
/// Discriminant of §2.3's `TorRuntime` (DTO-safe for Dart). The `HostDialer`
/// arm (FR-29, `host-transport-crossing.md` §2/§3.4; ADR-0547) carries what
/// the host DECLARED for its registered transport: its OWN bounded display
/// name (rendered verbatim — the SDK has no list of transport kinds),
/// whether its path keeps the wallet's per-purpose connections apart, and
/// whether it hides the device's address from the server. No key material,
/// no unbounded text.
pub enum TorRuntimeKind {
    // No `BuiltIn`: removed with the runtime at FR-5 C1 (ADR-0548 D3).
    ExternalSocks5,
    Dialer,
    HostDialer { name: HostTransportName, isolation: IsolationSupport, exposure: TransportExposure },
}

/// The on-resume snapshot bundle (§3.1 `snapshot()`).
pub struct WalletState {
    pub balance: BalanceSnapshot,
    pub sync: SyncStatus,
    pub tor: TorState,                   // G1 — cold-queryable, pre-W3 freeze
    pub tip: Option<BlockHeight>,
    pub last_synced: Option<SyncStamp>,  // balance age — LIVE since #317: the
                                         // PERSISTED stamp (aux `last_synced_stamp`
                                         // row, written by the controller before
                                         // each UpToDate via SyncEnginePort::
                                         // record_synced; read in snapshot());
                                         // survives relaunch; None before the
                                         // first completed pass AND after a
                                         // rescan (the rebuild clears the row —
                                         // a stale stamp would pair the old
                                         // height/time with a rebuilding
                                         // balance). Offline.last_synced MUST
                                         // read the same store when it gains an
                                         // emitter (single-source contract).
    pub seq: u64,                        // monotonic; stamps snapshot AND every
                                         // stream item — a stale stream event
                                         // can never beat a fresher snapshot
                                         // in the UI race (§3.3 contracts)
}

/// Per-transaction submit outcome. A proposal may create SEVERAL txs (e.g.
/// crossing pools — §1.7); every created tx is persisted BEFORE submit, and
/// partial failure is first-class, never collapsed into one error.
pub enum TxSubmitResult {
    Success       { txid: TxId },
    GrpcFailure   { txid: TxId },               // no endpoint verdict (transport/timeout
                                                // or a non-OK gRPC status — #307 framing)
    SubmitFailure { txid: TxId, code: i32 },    // endpoint rejected from mempool
    NotAttempted  { txid: TxId },               // an earlier tx never REACHED the endpoint
                                                // (transport latch — #307; a mempool reject
                                                // does NOT latch: later txs are still tried)
}
```

### 2.6 Swap types (ADR-0014; port-level, provider-agnostic)

```rust
pub struct AssetId { pub chain: String, pub symbol: String } // provider-namespaced
pub enum SwapDirection {
    /// other asset → ZEC. Privacy-positive END STATE. Delivery target is a
    /// FRESH per-swap address derived at a single-use external index via the
    /// audited `get_address_for_index` (§3.3b) — UNIVERSAL: the provider pays
    /// whichever receiver it supports. In practice (verified vs the Zodl
    /// reference 2026-06-23) 1Click pays the UA's TRANSPARENT receiver, so
    /// `SwapService` surfaces the Recv-3 shield step on delivery; if a provider
    /// ever pays the shielded receiver the normal scan finds it and no shield is
    /// needed — SAME code, no 2→1 refactor. `ends_shielded` is honest because
    /// that shield path exists and is one tap; the transparent leg (if any) is
    /// on-chain-visible only until shielded. (SUPERSEDES the 2026-06-10 "no
    /// shielded support → bare transparent" note — see §3.3b / ADR-0530.)
    IntoZec { from: AssetId },
    /// ZEC → other asset. DE-SHIELDS by construction: the deposit send is a
    /// shielded→transparent tx to the provider's t-addr; amount + destination
    /// exposed to the solver network.
    OutOfZec { to: AssetId },
}

pub struct QuoteRequest {
    pub direction: SwapDirection,
    pub exact: ExactSide,                  // ExactIn(Zatoshis|foreign) / ExactOut(…)
    pub slippage_tolerance_bps: u16,       // default SLIPPAGE_DEFAULT_BPS (200 =
                                           // 2%, upstream default); ≤ SLIPPAGE_MAX_BPS
    pub destination: Option<String>,       // OutOfZec: foreign receive address —
                                           // validated; a Zcash address is REJECTED
                                           // (§1.7: ZEC→ZEC = fee-burning provider
                                           // round-trip). IntoZec: None (we receive
                                           // to our own UA).
    pub refund_address: Option<String>,    // IntoZec: user-supplied source-chain
                                           // refund target. OutOfZec: IGNORED —
                                           // SwapService ALWAYS populates the
                                           // provider's refundTo with a FRESH
                                           // wallet transparent address (the
                                           // deposit comes from the shielded
                                           // pool; the provider has no
                                           // observable source to refund to —
                                           // without this the refund path
                                           // doesn't exist). Refund deliveries
                                           // are auto-shielded like swap-in
                                           // deliveries (§6.3).
}

pub struct SwapQuote {
    pub id: SwapId,
    pub deposit_address: String,    // quote-generated, single-use (provider)
    pub deposit_memo: Option<String>, // a required destination tag / memo on the
                                    // deposit (XRP tag, Cosmos/Stellar/EOS memo).
                                    // IntoZec ONLY — the user attaches it to their
                                    // external deposit (§4.4), shown on D7 with a
                                    // funds-loss warning; OutOfZec rejects a memo
                                    // (the wallet can't attach one to its own
                                    // send). §5.4 NEVER-log; bounded + display-
                                    // safety-checked at the §4.6 funnel
    pub expires_at: u64,            // deposit deadline — INTEGRATOR-requested
                                    // (direction-dependent, W-swap-4-a-3:
                                    // OutOfZec asks the 15-min
                                    // SWAP_DEPOSIT_DEADLINE_OUT_OF_ZEC window,
                                    // IntoZec the 24 h SWAP_DEADLINE_DEFAULT)
                                    // and provider-echoed; NOT a platform
                                    // constant (Zodl's "24 h" is their chosen
                                    // value — verified).
                                    // CLOCK-SKEW posture: enforcement is
                                    // anchored as a provider-relative DURATION
                                    // captured at response receipt + MONOTONIC
                                    // elapsed (− DEADLINE_SAFETY_MARGIN) —
                                    // never raw device wall-clock (a slow
                                    // clock would sign deposits to dead
                                    // quotes); wall time is display-only
    pub amount_in: String,          // foreign amounts as DECIMAL STRINGS (no
    pub min_amount_out: String,     // float, no u64-precision assumption)
    pub zec_side: Zatoshis,         // whichever side is ZEC, exact
    pub refund_to: Option<String>,  // the provider's ECHO of the refundTo we
                                    // sent — verified equal before anything
                                    // downstream (W2 as-built: the echo check
                                    // needs the echo IN the port DTO)
    pub disclosure: SwapPrivacyDisclosure,
}
// USER-ANCHORED SANITY CEILING (review M1 — the one real drain vector):
// zec_side AND the foreign side MUST lie within
// [user request ± slippage_tolerance_bps], under the hard SLIPPAGE_MAX_BPS
// ceiling; violation ⇒ typed QuoteOutOfBounds, rejected BEFORE SIGNING.
// A deposit is never signed anchored to provider numbers alone — the
// user's own request is the bound. The provider's echoed refundTo is also
// VERIFIED equal to the one we sent (mismatch ⇒ ProviderProtocol, abort
// before any deposit). So is the rest of the echo (2026-10-07 external
// review, finding 3): the NEAR adapter refuses a quote whose echo of the
// request names a different recipient, origin or destination asset, amount,
// swap type, slippage, deposit/refund/recipient type or dry flag
// (ProviderProtocol { RequestEchoMismatch }, or MissingField when the echo
// omits one) — `map::check_request_echo`. Refund/delivery t-addrs are
// SINGLE-USE — a fresh HD index per swap, never recycled (review HARD-H).

/// Honest per-direction privacy surfacing AS DATA (ADR-0014) — the UI renders
/// from this, never from its own guess.
pub struct SwapPrivacyDisclosure {
    pub ends_shielded: bool,        // IntoZec: true
    pub deshields: bool,            // OutOfZec: true
    pub provider_legs_transparent: bool, // provider-side txs are PUBLIC chain
                                         // data (§1.7 — their NEAR legs are)
```
