```rust
    pub provider_sees: Vec<DisclosureItem>, // per-direction; rendered as data (§5.1)
}
/// The data the provider learns (rendered to the user before quote acceptance).
/// IntoZec set = {CrossAssetLink, Amounts, SourceAddress (the refund address),
/// IpUnlessTor}; OutOfZec set = {CrossAssetLink, Amounts, DestinationAddress,
/// IpUnlessTor}. `Unknown` is the forward-compat arm the UI still renders (never drops).
pub enum DisclosureItem {
    CrossAssetLink, Amounts, DestinationAddress, SourceAddress, IpUnlessTor, Unknown,
}

pub enum SwapStatus {
    PendingDeposit { expires_at: u64 },
    /// Partial deposit landed (§1.7): top up by the deadline or the provider
    /// refunds. Amounts as decimal strings (foreign side).
    UnderDeposited { received: String, missing: String, deadline: u64 },
    DepositDetected,
    Processing,
    Success  { out_txid: Option<String>, realized_slippage_bps: Option<i32> },
    Refunded { refund_txid: Option<String> },   // NAMED failure path, not an error
    Failed   { code: SwapErrorCode },
}

pub struct SwapRecord {            // local history row (encrypted at rest §4.3)
    pub id: SwapId, pub direction: SwapDirection, pub status: SwapStatus,
    pub created_at: u64, pub deposit_txid: Option<TxId>,
}

/// Swap kill severity as it reaches the running SwapService (§3.5 layers 3/4;
/// W-swap-2). MONOTONIC-toward-off (review M4): the service only escalates and
/// never resurrects — re-enable is host reconstruction (layer 2). The host
/// maps its flag through `resolve_manifest_kill` so the severity is always
/// TYPED + DEFINED (default WindDown; never unresolved).
pub enum SwapKill { Live, WindDown, Hard }
pub fn resolve_manifest_kill(swap_enabled: bool, declared: Option<SwapKill>) -> SwapKill;
```

Serde: DTOs derive `Serialize` only where persistence/bridge needs it; **no
`#[serde(default)]` anywhere in this crate** (crypto-adjacent); secret types
(`SeedSource`, internal USK wrappers, DB key) derive nothing.

---

## 3. Interface design (SOLID)

### 3.1 Inbound — the core's public Rust API (what both consumers call)

```rust
pub struct Wallet { /* opaque handle */ }

impl Wallet {
    /// create/restore/open in one honest constructor set:
    pub async fn create(cfg: WalletConfig, seed: SeedSource) -> Result<Wallet, WalletError>;
    pub async fn open(cfg: WalletConfig) -> Result<Wallet, WalletError>; // existing DB only
    // ^ the endpoint it dials is the PERSISTED sync-server choice when one
    //   exists and can be honoured, else `cfg.endpoint` — with the fallback
    //   surfaced, never silent (sync-server-picker.md §1.2 D2, §3.1; S276).
    pub async fn close(self) -> Result<(), WalletError>;
    /// Crypto-shred, keychain-FIRST (§4.3a FR-14): sever the keychain wrap key
    /// (the authoritative shred — the §4.2a SealKey dies, so every on-disk seal +
    /// the DB ciphertext are instantly dead), THEN sweep the dir contents as
    /// best-effort cleanup — advisory LOCK FILE LAST (#317, the S148 unlink-race
    /// fold): the old whole-dir sweep unlinked the lock mid-hold, letting a
    /// concurrent `open` flock a FRESH inode and provision into a directory the
    /// wipe was still deleting. Leaves no orphaned keychain item on any crash point
    /// (supersedes the older files-first ordering, which left an existence oracle).
    /// Idempotent (an INTERRUPTED wipe auto-converges via the `.wipe-committed`
    /// breadcrumb). Refused while an instance holds the DB open (`WalletOpen` error).
    /// A non-empty store whose custody item can't be confirmed under the namespace
    /// fails CLOSED (`KeystoreInconsistent`) — pass the SAME db_dir you opened with.
    /// Takes ONLY `db_dir` (NOT the full `WalletConfig`, like `exists`) — a
    /// crypto-shred / panic-wipe must never be blockable by unrelated transport
    /// validation (S116 review HARDENING); the verify-real-sever guard, not config
    /// validation, is the money-safety gate.
    pub async fn wipe(db_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), WalletError>;
    /// Escape hatch for a wallet whose custody item is ALREADY gone (manual keychain
    /// deletion / pre-FR-13 bare item / iOS ThisDeviceOnly that didn't migrate): skips
    /// the verify-real-sever guard, so the host MUST be certain `db_dir` is this wallet's.
    /// Use only after a plain `wipe` returned `KeystoreInconsistent` on a wallet you own.
    pub async fn wipe_force(db_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), WalletError>;
    /// FR-53 — the DURESS force-sever (stage S16, ADR-0565): make the wallet
    /// unrecoverable within `deadline` EVEN WHILE something still holds it. Lock
    /// free → the plain destroy (`files: Removed`, `holder: None`). Held → the
    /// key-store custody is severed anyway, NO file is deleted (`LeftForHost`),
    /// every in-process instance is poisoned `Wiped`, and the path is tombstoned
    /// until a plain `wipe`. Every custody outcome is a `SeverReport` VALUE
    /// (`Severed{count}` proven / `SeveredUnproven{CountUnreadable}` / `AlreadyGone`
    /// / `NotSevered{cause}`); `Err` only for an I/O fault. Key-store budget =
    /// min(`deadline`, `KEYCHAIN_WIPE_BUDGET`); zero → no key-store call. At rest
    /// only: a live holder keeps the seed + DB key in RAM until it drops. Takes ONLY
    /// `db_dir`. Bridge: `WalletHandle.severCustody(config, deadlineMs)` →
    /// `SeverReport` (ABI 7; whole ms, clamped to the budget; the device log is
    /// quiesced FIRST, before the `dbDir` shape gate). ✅ BUILT (S308).
    pub async fn sever_custody(db_dir: &Path, deadline: Duration) -> Result<SeverReport, WalletError>;
    /// FR-14 H1 — the PRODUCTION custody disclosure (the runtime consumer of
    /// `VaultTier::erase_assurance()`): an ACTIVE, read-only tier probe (NO
    /// seed/unseal) returning `CustodyDisclosure { tier, erase_assurance,
    /// degraded }` so a host renders the wipe confirmation + a custody badge
    /// honestly. Takes ONLY `db_dir` (like `wipe`). `VaultAbsent` ⇒ tier `None`.
    /// `erase_assurance` is `HardwareKeyDeleted | BestEffort`; no value claims
    /// permanent erasure (ADR-0571, replacing `crypto_erases_on_delete: bool`).
    pub async fn custody_disclosure(db_dir: &Path) -> Result<CustodyDisclosure, WalletError>;

    /// OUTBOUND CARVE-OUT (third-party backup UX only): zeroizing word list,
    /// SYNC (a lock-free in-memory read of the held phrase — no DB), no-log,
    /// words only (NEVER the BIP39 passphrase, §4.2a). `NoMnemonic` for any
    /// RawBytes wallet (incl. the Relim None-persistence path) — the Relim path
    /// can never reveal anything (its recovery is the ONE Relim phrase via
    /// identity-core). `require_open`-gated (a Closing/Wiped wallet refuses). The
    /// bridge maps the zeroizing words → a Dart `List<String>` at the convert
    /// boundary (the documented §10 exposure). ✅ BUILT (iv-d-3-b-iii-B-2-d-2-b-iii-A).
    pub fn reveal_mnemonic(&self) -> Result<Vec<Zeroizing<String>>, WalletError>;

    /// Default UA receiver set: Orchard AND Sapling, NO transparent receiver
    /// (review G7 — RESOLVED W3-inc-2 crypto audit). Both shielded receivers are
    /// REQUIRED (not merely allowed) so any shielded payer — Orchard-capable or
    /// Sapling-only — can pay; transparent is omitted (no §5.1 transparent-leg on
    /// the default receive address). Enforced as a checked post-condition in
    /// `derivation::default_address_for` + pinned by the §8 KATs. (The wallet DOES
    /// derive transparent addresses internally for single-use SWAP refunds — a
    /// SEPARATE BIP44 external-scope path, §2.6 HARD-H / W-swap-3-a — but never on
    /// this default receive UA.)
    pub async fn current_address(&self) -> Result<UnifiedAddress, WalletError>;
    pub fn balance(&self) -> impl Stream<Item = BalanceSnapshot>;
    pub fn sync_status(&self) -> impl Stream<Item = SyncStatus>;
    pub fn tor_state(&self) -> impl Stream<Item = TorState>;   // G1; cold value via snapshot()
    /// Runtime policy change (review G3): tears down existing connections,
    /// re-dials under the new policy — no wallet restart, no old-policy
    /// socket leak-through. (Relim migration note, HISTORICAL: it said v1.0
    /// ships `BuiltIn` and v1.x flips to `Dialer` over transport-tor; Relim
    /// registers a host dialer instead — ADR-0543 — and `set_tor_policy` is
    /// not built, cut from FR-29.)
    pub async fn set_tor_policy(&self, policy: TorPolicy) -> Result<(), WalletError>;
    /// REPLAYABLE from a host-held cursor — events arriving while FRB streams
    /// are paused (or between kill and relaunch) are NOT lost: the host
    /// resumes from its last cursor; state streams are latest-wins coalescing
    /// (no unbounded buffering during long backgrounds). §3.3 contracts.
    ///
    /// **MEMO PREREQUISITE — TX-ENHANCEMENT (the foundation, building from S109).**
    /// Compact blocks omit memo bytes (the server sends only the ~52-byte note-detection
    /// prefix), so a scanned receive carries amount + status but an EMPTY memo. Recovering
    /// it needs a second step librustzcash models as `transaction_data_requests()`: after a
    /// scan pass that advanced the chain, drain the wallet's pending requests and, for each
    /// `Enhancement(txid)`/`GetStatus(txid)`, fetch the FULL tx via the lightwalletd
    /// `GetTransaction` RPC, RE-PARSE it and verify `Transaction::txid()` matches the request
    /// (a lying endpoint that returns the wrong/garbled tx is REJECTED, never stored — §4.6),
    /// then `decrypt_and_store_transaction` (audited WHOLE — recovers the memo with the
    /// wallet's own keys, Rust-side, and updates the tx's mined status). An empty reply ⇒
    /// `set_transaction_status(TxidNotRecognized)`. Hexagonal like Recv-2b: an own
    /// `TransactionFetcher` port (ISP — fake-testable, no gRPC) + the `LightwalletdClient`
    /// adapter + a `Wallet::enhance_transactions` engine method hooked into `run_pass` on the
    /// SAME sync circuit, inside the cancel race, **BOUNDED** at `MAX_ENHANCEMENTS_PER_PASS`
    /// — **PRIVACY POSTURE (reconciles §1.7; security review fold):** `GetTransaction(txid)` rides
    /// the shared sync circuit (`WALLET_SYNC_ISOLATION_KEY`), exactly like the existing
    /// tree-state / subtree-root / `GetAddressUtxos` sync fetches — NOT the per-txid isolation
    /// §1.7 aspires to for "fetch-tx" (which the tree-state fetch ALSO does not honor today; only
    /// outbound BROADCAST uses fresh per-tx keys). This is an HONEST-DISCLOSURE tradeoff: unlike
    /// compact-block scan (local trial-decryption — the endpoint learns only the birthday range),
    /// asking for a tx BY txid reveals that txid, so over a pass the endpoint sees the wallet's
    /// shielded-RECEIVE set aggregated under one identity — and, with Tor `Off`, linked to the
    /// IP. Tor (`Preferred`/`Required`) is the mitigation that keeps it off the clearnet identity;
    /// per-txid isolation keys (a fresh circuit per fetched txid — denying the endpoint the
    /// aggregation even under one provider) is the documented stronger-but-costlier alternative
    /// (up to `MAX_ENHANCEMENTS_PER_PASS` fresh circuits per restore pass). **DECIDED (founder,
    /// 2026-06-25): ship the shared-sync-circuit posture + this disclosure** (it matches the
    /// existing tree-state/UTXO fetch posture and the Zashi reference; Tor keeps the receive-set
    /// off the clearnet identity); per-txid isolation is a future hardening if it proves to
    /// matter. The host's honest-degradation UX should reflect that memo enhancement discloses the
    /// receive-set to the server when Tor is off.
    /// (a restored wallet has thousands of historic txs — converge over passes, never one
    /// giant burst), per-tx fault ISOLATION (a poison txid can't head-of-line-block the
    /// queue), best-effort/SWALLOWED (never fails sync; the chain is the source of truth),
    /// §5.4 counts-only (never a txid/memo/address). The transparent
    /// `TransactionsInvolvingAddress` variant is DEFERRED (receive is covered by Recv-2b
    /// `refresh_transparent_utxos`; calling `notify_address_checked` without truly checking
    /// would falsely hide txs — money-visibility). Memo CONTENT then surfaces via `history`
    /// (memo_count → has_memo flips true) and the `incoming` stream's `memos`; a per-txid
    /// memo-bytes accessor is the next slice. End-to-end "a real memo populates" is
    /// device-gated (the funded harness can't synthesize a full memo'd tx — `TestState::
    /// get_transaction` is None, compact blocks omit memo bytes). What IS unit-tested: the §4.6
    /// boundary against a REAL (minimal v5) tx + the filter/bound/sentinel/no-op-wiring + the
    /// money-safety of the not-found path. Named tests (`enhance` + `history::real_view`):
    /// `parse_and_validate_accepts_a_matching_tx`,
    /// `parse_and_validate_rejects_a_txid_mismatch` (the M2 lying-endpoint reject),
    /// `parse_and_validate_rejects_garbage_and_truncation`,
    /// `parse_and_validate_never_panics_on_arbitrary_bytes` (proptest) + the `fuzz_enhance_parse`
    /// cargo-fuzz target (the deepest hostile-input decoder in the SDK; `catch_unwind`-backstopped),
    /// `select_enhancement_targets_filters_orders_bounds_and_defers_transparent` (the per-pass
    /// bound + the transparent deferral + **the request KIND preserved**, and upstream's
    /// "Enhancement subsumes GetStatus" in either listing order),
    /// `map_wire_height_maps_sentinels_and_real_heights`,
    /// `enhance_transactions_is_a_silent_no_op_on_an_empty_backlog` (real-method wiring + no
    /// network hit on an idle/transparent-only backlog), `a_not_found_reply_never_unscans_a_received_note`
    /// (a lying not-found cannot hide a scanned receive). **The drain LOOP runtime is now unit-tested
    /// (GAP-3, S109):** the loop body was lifted out of `enhance_transactions` into
    /// `enhance::run_enhancement_pass` over an `EnhancementStore` PORT (the engine method is a thin
    /// adapter, `WalletDbEnhancementStore`), so the policy is driven in tests by a recording store +
    /// a scripted fetcher — no gRPC, no device. Named:
    /// `run_enhancement_pass_isolates_faults_and_tallies_every_branch` (a mixed
    /// valid/not-found/error/mismatch/garbage backlog: every txid is still attempted after a
    /// mid-batch fault, each lands in the right tally),
    /// `run_enhancement_pass_stores_with_mined_height_none_ignoring_the_endpoint_claim` (THE money
    /// decision — a lying endpoint height is ignored; the tx is stored with `None` so the audited
    /// decryptor resolves the height from our OWN scanned block),
    /// `run_enhancement_pass_is_a_silent_no_op_on_an_empty_backlog_skipping_the_tip_read`,
    /// `run_enhancement_pass_attempts_at_most_max_per_pass`,
    /// `run_enhancement_pass_aborts_the_pass_when_a_store_write_faults` (the isolate-vs-propagate
    /// asymmetry — a DB-write fault `?`-propagates + aborts the pass, unlike an isolated network
    /// fault), `run_enhancement_pass_enhances_a_mempool_reply_using_the_fallback_branch` (a
    /// height-0 reply to an ENHANCEMENT request stores via the tip fallback, still with `None`).
    /// **THE TWO REQUEST KINDS ARE ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY (INC-009, S254).** `Enhancement` and
    /// `GetStatus` are distinct upstream questions (`zcash_client_backend-0.23.0`
    /// `data_api.rs:1163-1168`): the first is answered with `decrypt_and_store_transaction`, the
    /// second with `WalletWrite::set_transaction_status`, and ONLY the second writes a mined
    /// height. The loop folded them into one txid list and answered both with the decryptor, so a
    /// status request wrote no height — and `zcash_client_sqlite` re-synthesizes a status request
    /// for every row with `mined_height IS NULL`, so the wallet asked "was this mined?", answered
    /// itself "height unknown", and re-asked forever while two confirmed on-chain sends rendered
    /// as *"expired … still yours to spend."* The port's `mark_not_recognized` is now the general
    /// `set_status(txid, TransactionStatus)`, and `EnhancementOutcome` counts `status_set` apart
    /// from `enhanced` (the sync pass nudges `MemoRefresh` on either, since a status write is
    /// exactly what flips a send out of "expired" — **ADR-0539** amends ADR-0536 Decision 4 to
    /// widen that event's meaning accordingly, and is the current contract).
    ///
    /// **A status answer is the ONE place this module writes an endpoint claim to the db as
    /// fact, and the S254 review returned CRITICAL + BLOCK on the first version of it.**
    /// Upstream's `Mined(h)` arm overwrites `mined_height` with no `mined_height IS NULL` guard
    /// (unlike its `NotInMainChain` arm three lines above, which HAS one), ratchets
    /// `min_observed_height` and `exposed_at_height` down via `MIN(…)`, and deletes the
    /// retrieval row. The first fix rested on a premise that is FALSE — that a status request
    /// only ever concerns a transaction whose height we lack. `queue_tx_retrieval` stamps
    /// `Status` whenever `raw IS NOT NULL`, and the request UNION's first arm has no height
    /// filter, so the question IS asked about already-scanned transactions. Unbounded, one
    /// endpoint answer turned a deeply-confirmed note into a one-confirmation note below the
    /// spend minimum, or locked the inputs of a never-relayed send out of
    /// `select_spendable_notes` permanently.
    ///
    /// So `chain_status` weighs four pieces of evidence, and `CheckedStatus` — unconstructible
    /// outside `enhance` — makes going around them a compile error rather than a convention:
    /// the wallet's OWN height for the txid (decisive; refuses outright), the transaction's
    /// ZIP-203 expiry (the only CONSENSUS bound, not endpoint-derived), the wallet birthday (a
    /// floor against backdating, which is the worse direction because the `MIN(…)` ratchets
    /// never recover), and the known chain tip (weakest — it is endpoint-supplied, so it is
    /// consistency between two of the endpoint's own answers, NOT ground truth). Bounding
    /// against the SCANNED tip instead was considered and rejected: it would refuse every
    /// honest answer for a restore's whole catch-up, which is INC-011's exact shape.
    /// **Residual risk accepted knowingly (founder, S254 — Option A):** between the wallet's
    /// last observation and expiry, a hostile endpoint can still land a false confirmation.
    ///
    /// Named: `run_enhancement_pass_answers_get_status_with_a_status_not_a_decrypt`
    /// (the INC-009 guard, written failing first),
    /// `a_claimed_height_never_overwrites_a_height_the_wallet_already_knows` (INC-013, the
    /// CRITICAL; anti-vacuity case: the SAME claim IS written when the wallet holds no height,
    /// so it guards the evidence and not the height),
    /// `a_backdated_claim_below_the_birthday_is_refused` (INC-014, with the birthday floor shown
    /// inclusive) and `a_claim_above_the_transactions_own_expiry_height_is_refused` (the ZIP-203
    /// ceiling, added when a review found the expiry check had NO live coverage: every fixture
    /// in the file built an expiry-0 transaction, so flipping its `>` to `>=` left the whole
    /// suite green — the test whose NAME covered it did not),
    /// `a_mined_height_above_the_known_tip_is_refused_not_written` (INC-012; its
    /// `None`-tip case exists because upstream reads `chain_tip_height(…).ok_or(…)?` BEFORE
    /// matching, so writing with no tip aborts the whole pass rather than skipping one txid),
    /// and `a_mempool_reply_to_a_status_request_is_answered_not_in_main_chain`
    /// (both wire sentinels are an ANSWER, not silence). **WATCHDOG
    /// LIVENESS (S109, Fix A):** the enhancement drain runs AFTER the scan's last progress report,
    /// so a slow backlog (≤ `MAX_ENHANCEMENTS_PER_PASS` unary `GetTransaction`s, each bounded by
    /// `GRPC_UNARY_TIMEOUT_SECS`) would otherwise go silent for the whole phase and trip a FALSE
    /// `Stalled{EndpointUnreachable}` (deferring `UpToDate` + queued-send resubmission). The loop
    /// fires a per-tx `tick` (the engine maps it to `ProgressSink::keepalive` — re-arms the
    /// stuck-sync watchdog WITHOUT republishing status, so the scan's last `Scanning` stays current
    /// until the pass returns), so the silent gap between ticks is ≤ one fetch. A genuinely wedged
    /// fetch is still caught (it times out ⇒ the gap can't exceed one timeout). Named:
    /// `keepalive_kicks_the_watchdog_tick_without_touching_status` + the per-tx tick count asserted
    /// inside the `run_enhancement_pass_*` tests (fires per attempted tx, bounded by the cap, never
    /// on an empty backlog). DEVICE-GATED (ride the real-scan path):
    /// now ONLY the memo actually populating end-to-end + the live `wallet.enhance` §5.4 span
    /// (counts-only by construction) — the per-tx fault isolation AND the `mined_height = None`
    /// decision are no longer device-gated.
    ///
    /// **MEMO-CONTENT READ (shipped, the crate accessor):** once enhancement populates the memos,
    /// `Wallet::transaction_memos(txid) -> Vec<Memo>` reads them (FR-6 — the crate API IS the Relim
    /// integration surface; the Dart `transactionMemos -> Vec<ParsedMemo>` FFI is DEFERRED until
    /// the reference app grows a memo-display UI, same posture as `transaction`). It reads
    /// `v_tx_outputs.memo` scoped to the primary account (RECEIVED memos paid to us AND our own
    /// OVK-decryptable outgoing memos — the set `memo_count` counts), classifies each blob through
    /// the audited ZIP-302 `Memo::from_wire` (never panics — A4), and FILTERS the empty memo.
    /// librustzcash stores memos TRIMMED of trailing zeros (the empty memo is a single `0xF6`
    /// byte); `MemoBytes::from_bytes` losslessly re-pads ≤512 — only >512 is corruption. The FFI
    /// projects MACHINE memos (`Arbitrary`/`Reserved`) to LENGTH-only via the SSOT
    /// `convert::memo_to_parsed` — raw memo bytes NEVER cross the bridge; only `Text` content does
    /// (§5.4). Reviewed security ∥ crypto/privacy (no blocker; folded the trimmed-storage shape +
    /// the deterministic `(output_index, output_pool)` order). Named tests:
    /// `transaction_memos_parses_filters_empty_and_scopes_to_the_primary_account` (over trimmed
    /// blobs — the real storage shape),
    /// `transaction_memos_retains_a_reserved_memo` (the accessor surfaces a ZIP-302 RESERVED memo
    /// — first byte 0xF5 / 0xF7–0xFE, or a non-canonical 0xF6 — instead of mis-dropping it as
    /// empty; the empty-filter keys on the `Memo::Empty` classification, not a naive first-byte
    /// check — the classification itself is pinned in `memo.rs`),
    /// `transaction_memos_rejects_an_oversized_memo_blob_typed` (a >512 blob ⇒ typed `MemoInvalid`),
    /// + the real-`v_tx_outputs`-schema smoke in
    /// `queries_run_against_the_real_schema_and_are_empty_on_a_fresh_db`.
    // AS BUILT (ADR-0536, S209 #392): the per-tx `incoming()` reservation is
    // SUPERSEDED by the minimal event stream — `watch_incoming_funds(since_cursor,
    // sink)` emitting `IncomingFundsEvent` (§2.5); attribution stays a pull.
    pub async fn watch_incoming_funds(&self, since_cursor: Option<&str>, sink: impl IncomingFundsSink) -> Result<(), WalletError>;
    /// KEYSET paging (stable cursor, not offset) — offset pages tear while
    /// the scanner inserts rows mid-pagination.
    ///
    /// **AS-BUILT (FR-1, SHIPPED S107 `7ee9183`):** the method is named
    /// `transactions(limit, after: Option<String>) -> HistoryPage` and the cursor
    /// is an OPAQUE `String` (not a typed `HistoryCursor`) — the host stores +
    /// returns it verbatim. The keyset key is `(mined_height, txid)`, NOT
    /// `(mined_height, tx_index)`: librustzcash fills `mined_height` but leaves
    /// `tx_index` NULL on many mined rows (the `GetStatus`/transparent-input path —
    /// exchange withdrawals + swap-in deposits), so a `tx_index`-keyed cursor would
    /// make those rows unreachable on later pages and HIDE received funds; `txid`
    /// is globally unique, an exact total-order tiebreaker. The opaque token is
    /// version-tagged + ASCII/length/size-guarded so its decode is panic-free on any
    /// host `&str` (it runs under the aux-db lock; a panic would poison it).
    /// Named tests: `keyset_pages_union_to_every_row_once_even_with_same_height`,
    /// `keyset_surfaces_mined_rows_with_null_tx_index_no_drop`,
    /// `keyset_pending_only_page_still_reaches_the_confirmed_history`,
    /// `cursor_decode_never_panics_on_adversarial_strings`,
    /// `cursor_round_trips_and_rejects_malformed_tokens`,
    /// `list_clamps_limit_to_the_max_page_size`.
    ///
    /// **MONEY-VISIBILITY FIX (deep-e2e round, found by the real-scan harness):** the row
    /// read interpreted `v_transactions.expired_unmined` as a bare `i64`, but the REAL view
    /// defines it as `(mined_height IS NULL AND expiry_height BETWEEN 1 AND max)` — an
    /// UN-MINED RECEIVED tx has no `expiry_height`, so SQLite three-valued logic makes the
    /// whole column **NULL**, not 0/1 (a payment seen before it confirms, or one orphaned by
    /// a reorg). A bare-`i64` read errored the ENTIRE page to `StoreCorrupt`, so a single
    /// unconfirmed receive made the whole activity history vanish behind an error. NOW read as
    /// `Option` → NULL maps to NOT-expired (the row is Pending). Verified the fix cannot mask
    /// a genuine §6.1 Expired (a real expiry is always 0/1, never NULL) and that the sibling
    /// SUM columns (`account_balance_delta`, `memo_count`) are non-NULL by the view's
    /// `notes`-CTE inner-join construction. Named tests:
    /// `read_row_treats_a_null_expired_unmined_as_not_expired` (the read layer) +
    /// the funded-harness deep-e2e suite over the REAL `v_transactions` (a second aux
    /// connection on a file-backed scanned DB; `mod test_support`):
    /// `keyset_pages_over_real_scanned_rows_union_to_every_row_once`,
    /// `reorg_takes_a_confirmed_receive_to_pending_then_a_rescan_reconfirms_it` (the genuine
    /// `truncate_to_height` primitive — un-mine keeps the receive as Pending, money intact,
    /// then re-confirms), `confirmation_depth_tracks_the_scanned_frontier`,
    /// `a_history_read_sees_a_consistent_snapshot_during_an_in_flight_write`,
    /// `probe_funded_scan_surfaces_received_rows_over_the_aux_connection` (+ an independent
    /// internal-vs-display txid byte-order cross-check),
    /// `a_multi_note_receive_surfaces_one_row_with_the_summed_delta` (a one-tx/many-notes receive
    /// aggregates into ONE row at the SUMMED `account_balance_delta` — under-reporting would hide
    /// funds — and a sibling single-note receive is not conflated),
    /// `a_multi_note_receive_keeps_its_summed_delta_across_a_reorg_and_reconfirm` (the WHOLE sum
    /// survives un-mine → Pending → reconfirm — never a per-note partial). NOTE: the same-height
    /// MULTI-ROW keyset case (two distinct txs in one block) is covered by the controlled-fixture
    /// `keyset_pages_union_to_every_row_once_even_with_same_height`, NOT over the real view: the
    /// `data_api::testing` harness puts every `FakeCompactOutput` into a single `CompactTx`
    /// (N notes ⇒ 1 tx ⇒ 1 row) and has no multi-tx-per-block primitive, so a same-height batch
    /// can't be synthesized from a real scan (GAP-1 — harness limitation, not a coverage hole).
    pub async fn history(&self, cursor: Option<HistoryCursor>, limit: u32) -> Result<HistoryPage, WalletError>;

    /// **RESCAN-RECOVERY (ADR-0534; SDK S105 `f6694fe`, hardened S106 `ecbcfe0`, host
    /// UI S107 `863a74c`).** Rebuild the data DB from an EARLIER birthday to recover
    /// funds an over-high restore birthday skipped ("balance reads zero, sync says
    /// done"). `from_height = None` floors to Sapling activation (full, money-safe).
    /// Rebuilds ONLY the data DB from the already-sealed seed — NO recovery-phrase
    /// re-entry, NO key material across the FFI (only a bare height); durable money
    /// state (queued sends, refund index, in-flight swap detection) is preserved.
    /// CONSUMES the handle: on success the rebuilt wallet replaces it (host swaps the
    /// fresh session into the active gate → the live-sync graph re-subscribes from the
    /// lower birthday); on ANY error the handle is left closed with the seed seal +
    /// prior data DB intact, so the host recovers by re-`open`-ing at the prior
    /// birthday (no funds lost). Crash-atomic (ADR-0534: rebuild at a temp path → copy
    /// aux tables → fsync → atomic rename). Named tests: `rescan_is_crash_safe`,
    /// `rescan_clears_a_stale_temp_db_before_rebuilding`,
    /// `rescan_disk_full_propagates_verbatim_not_folded_to_corruption`.
    ///
    /// **ADR-0534 gate-8 register RECONCILIATION (3 tests shipped RENAMED — registered
    /// here, the ADR is append-only so it is NOT edited):**
    /// `rescan_rejects_birthday_in_future` → as-built
    /// `rescan_birthday_in_future_is_rejected_at_provision` (`wallet.rs`);
    /// `rescan_phase_gates_concurrent_calls` → as-built `rescan_phase_edges_are_guarded`
    /// (`lifecycle.rs`); `rescan_on_a_closed_handle_is_typed_not_a_panic` → as-built
    /// `rescan_from_on_a_closed_handle_is_typed_not_a_panic` (`zec_wallet/api/wallet.rs`).
    pub async fn rescan_from(&mut self, from_height: Option<BlockHeight>) -> Result<(), WalletError>;

    /// The account birthday height (#317) — the scan floor a rescan rebuilds from
    /// and the lowest useful `rescan_from` target. Hosts clamp a rescan
    /// date-picker's DEFAULT with this (paired with `estimate_birthday`, §3.6)
    /// instead of a blind "one year ago", which on any wallet younger than a
    /// year silently costs hours (S148 measured 60–240 ms/block). `None` before
    /// the account is provisioned. Engine-read (`get_account_birthday` — the
    /// same floor the scan window uses); a height, never money (§5.4-loggable).
    /// FFI: `birthdayHeight()` on the handle.
    pub async fn birthday_height(&self) -> Result<Option<BlockHeight>, WalletError>;

    /// Two-step send: propose (fee + effects shown to the user) → confirm.
    /// Proposals are ONE-SHOT (second send ⇒ `ProposalAlreadyUsed` — the
    /// double-tap guard) and TTL-bounded (PROPOSAL_TTL; resumed-from-
    /// background staleness ⇒ typed `ProposalStale`, re-propose) — never a
    /// stale anchor. QUEUED sends store the PaymentRequest intent and
    /// re-propose at broadcast time (§6.2).
    pub async fn propose(&self, req: PaymentRequest) -> Result<SendProposal, WalletError>;
    /// One proposal may create several txs (§1.7) → per-tx outcomes, ordered.
    pub async fn send(&self, proposal: SendProposal) -> Result<Vec<TxSubmitResult>, WalletError>;
    pub async fn queue_send(&self, req: PaymentRequest) -> Result<QueuedSendId, WalletError>;
    /// Shield transparent funds (exchange withdrawals land transparent —
    /// §1.7). Privacy-positive. None when balance < SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT.
    pub async fn propose_shield(&self) -> Result<Option<SendProposal>, WalletError>;

    /// On-resume snapshot (flutter-patterns: re-fetch latest state after
    /// AppLifecycleState.resumed) — streams cover live changes.
    pub async fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<WalletState, WalletError>;

    pub fn sync(&self) -> &SyncController;     // start()/stop()/once() control
                                               // surface (engine behind it: §3.2)
    pub fn swap(&self) -> Option<&SwapService>; // None unless host constructed
                                                // a provider (§3.4 — the gate)
}
```

Would it work with a different adapter? Yes by construction: nothing above
names gRPC, tonic, Tor, NEAR, or Relim. Free functions: `parse_payment_uri`
/ `encode_payment_uri` (ZIP-321 both directions) and
`estimate_birthday(network, approx_date) -> BlockHeight` — powers the "around
when did you create this wallet?" restore UX without any network call; floors
to the bracketing bundled checkpoint (CONSERVATIVE, never overshoots — design +
algorithm in §3.6), output CLAMPED to [activation, last bundled checkpoint] so a
future date can't extrapolate past what we know offline (§2.3 catches the rest
at sync).

### 3.2 Outbound — SDK-internal ports

```rust
/// The Tachyon seam (ADR-0005 refinement 6; audit A2). Altitude = the WHOLE
/// sync engine, not per-RPC. Verified reality check (2026-06-10): the
/// built-in `zcash_client_backend::sync::run` is a BASELINE — its docs list
/// no progress notifications, no interruption, no tx enhancement, no
/// parallel download. Those four are exactly what a mobile wallet needs
/// (SyncStatus stream, stop(), memo retrieval, §7 batching) — which is why
/// both upstream mobile SDKs built orchestration loops instead. So
/// refinement 1's boundary, stated precisely: the SCAN/decrypt/tree logic
/// (`suggest_scan_ranges`, `scan_cached_blocks`, the data_api) is consumed
/// WHOLE and never re-implemented; `LightdSyncEngine` is OUR orchestration
/// loop over those primitives — download batching + FS cache, progress
/// events, cancellation, TransactionDataRequests enhancement (memos!) —
/// modeled on the upstream action machine (§1.7). Tor via
/// `tor::Client::connect_to_lightwalletd` (features `tor` +
/// `lightwalletd-tonic-tls-webpki-roots`). Tachyon later = a second engine
/// impl, drop-in.
// AS BUILT (W3-inc-2c-iv-d-3-a) — the decomposition refined the W2 sketch: the
// SyncController owns the LOOP (retry/backoff/watchdog/status, §3.2g iv-d-3-a),
// so the engine owns exactly ONE resumable pass + its progress. broadcast/send is
// a SEPARATE seam (inc-2d), not the sync engine.
#[async_trait]
pub(crate) trait SyncEnginePort: Send + Sync {
    // One pass to the recorded tip (or until cancelled, between checkpoints —
    // durable progress); reports live progress via the sink. Faults are typed
    // WalletError::Sync { stall }. (Cancel/watchdog CONTRACT: the engine MUST
    // timeout-bound per-batch I/O + report progress intra-batch — see the code doc.)
    async fn run_pass(&self, cancel: &CancelToken, sink: &ProgressSink)
        -> Result<SyncPass, WalletError>;
    // Best-known chain tip for the terminal UpToDate { tip } (cheap, no network).
    fn tip(&self) -> Option<BlockHeight>;
}

/// Swap provider seam (ADR-0014 rail; ADR-0525 shipping). NEAR Intents
/// 1Click is the first impl — at W2 a MockSwapProvider only; the real
/// adapter (`zec-wallet-swap-near`, thin hand-audited REST client) is an
/// SDK DELIVERABLE (founder 2026-06-13) — exposure is HOST policy (Relim
/// keeps its MiCA gate; third-party hosts own theirs).
#[async_trait]
pub trait SwapPort: Send + Sync {
    async fn quote(&self, req: QuoteRequest) -> Result<SwapQuote, SwapError>;
    /// Executes the swap: registers intent with the provider and returns the
    /// live handle ("execute" = the ADR-0014 vocabulary; it does NOT sign).
    /// For OutOfZec the DEPOSIT-SEND is then built+signed by the WALLET in
    /// Rust (§4.4) — providers never touch keys.
    async fn execute(&self, quote: &SwapQuote) -> Result<SwapId, SwapError>;
    async fn status(&self, id: &SwapId) -> Result<SwapStatus, SwapError>;
}
```

```rust
/// Network runtime seam (founder 2026-06-10 — "the SDK may reuse the host
/// app's infrastructure"). Built-in arti is ONE impl of this, not a special
/// case: the engine builds its tonic channels over whatever this dials.
#[async_trait]
pub trait NetDialer: Send + Sync {
    /// isolation_key contract: equal keys MAY share a circuit/path;
    /// distinct keys MUST be unlinkable at the network layer.
    async fn dial(&self, host: &str, port: u16, isolation_key: Option<&str>)
        -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncByteStream>, DialError>;
}
```

`SwapService` (core-owned, provider-injected) orchestrates: quote →
execute → (OutOfZec: wallet-signed **de-shielding** deposit send · IntoZec: a
fresh per-swap address at a single-use external index (§3.3b D1 / ADR-0530);
delivery's transparent leg surfaces the **one-tap Recv-3 shield nudge** (§3.3b
D3 — user-triggered, NEVER silent/forced, per ADR-0529); a sub-threshold delivery
honestly stays transparent until it accumulates) → bounded status polling (§7) →
`SwapRecord` history. Provider config
(`SwapProviderConfig { endpoint, jwt: Option<Zeroizing<String>> }`) is
host-supplied — the JWT is **optional** (without it the provider levies a
0.2% fee — verified), config, never hardcoded, never logged (ADR-0014; Relim
feeds it from the signed manifest at W5).

Provider-status mapping is fixed (verified against the 1Click API
2026-06-10): `PENDING_DEPOSIT`→`PendingDeposit`,
`KNOWN_DEPOSIT_TX`→`DepositDetected`, `INCOMPLETE_DEPOSIT`→`UnderDeposited`,
`PROCESSING`/`SUCCESS`/`REFUNDED`/`FAILED` 1:1 — the closed-enum rule (§4.6)
maps anything else to `Failed(ProviderProtocol)`. **The swap API rides the
SAME `NetDialer`/`TorPolicy` stack as sync — there is NO independent
clearnet path for swap calls, and `TorPolicy::Required` fail-closes them
too** (review m5; test `tor_required_covers_swap_api_calls`). **Resume
contract:**
`open()` re-arms polling for every non-terminal `SwapRecord` automatically —
a host that never calls `watch()` still converges; a record stuck in
`Processing` forever is a silent hang and therefore forbidden. **Poll-trigger
binding (S6 money fold; binds the swap/wallet-store chunk):** the Rust-side
poll's foreground/resume trigger keys off the wallet's OWN dormancy signal
(`set_dormant`/`open()`), NEVER off the Dart layer's lifecycle re-fetch gate
(app-frame §3 suppresses UI re-fetches on `inactive→resumed` focus noise —
wiring the poll to that gate would suppress poll resume with it, recreating
exactly the missed-transition window the gate avoids for UI redraws only). **Persisted
records survive app updates:** an unknown persisted status variant (schema
moved forward or rolled back mid-flight) quarantines THAT record
(tracking-unavailable, surfaced) — never `StoreCorrupt` for the store. **Client choice (review H1, ratified at ADR level by ADR-0525):** the
**thin typed REST client** in preference to `one-click-sdk-rs` (0.1.x,
OpenAPI-generated, verified official — defuse-protocol — but reqwest-based
and unbounded; a funds path deserves a hand-audited client; the generated
client stays as the wire-shape REFERENCE). The 1Click HTTP surface is four
endpoints (`get_tokens` / `get_quote` / `submit_deposit_tx` /
`get_execution_status`). The adapter (`zec-wallet-swap-near`, **SDK
deliverable — ADR-0525**) rides the same `NetDialer`/`TorPolicy` stack as
sync (HTTP/1.1 + TLS + JSON over the dialed stream; concrete HTTP stack
chosen WITH the adapter chunk's supply-chain pass — no client dep enters the
graph before it; the mock is dep-free). Wire contract pinned by RECORDED
fixtures from the real API (UPSTREAM.md discipline, testing-patterns §5).

**As built (W-swap-1, LANDED):** the HTTP stack is the workspace's already-
pinned hyper 1 + rustls/`ring` + webpki-roots, plus `tokio-rustls` for TLS
over the dialed duplex (already in the lock — zero new crates) and
`serde_json` for the wire DTOs; ONE CONNECTION PER REQUEST (a pooled client
would silently link distinct isolation keys). Port semantics against 1Click,
pinned: `quote()` IS the registering call (`dry: false` — the response's
`depositAddress` is the live swap handle ~~and the `SwapId`~~ — struck S293,
ADR-0555: the `SwapId` is minted by the SDK when the quote is issued (OsRng,
32 hex) and the deposit address is `provider_ref`, data the adapter is handed
for its URL and body; there is no separate create endpoint; an unexecuted
quote just expires provider-side); `execute()` is the LOCAL commit point
(mirrors the mock; the dual deadline gate lives in `SwapService`);
`status(&SwapId, provider_ref)` puts the provider address in the request and
derives the PER-SWAP isolation key from the SDK id (polls for different swaps
are unlinkable — two swaps under one provider address ride two circuits);
`submit_deposit_tx` ships as the adapter-inherent `notify_deposit_tx`
(port wiring lands with the send pipeline — the txid exists only after
broadcast). Honesty rows: **IntoZec quoting fails typed until the wallet
handle can mint receive addresses** (W3-inc-2 — the request DTO carries no
wallet receive address by design, §2.6); a provider `depositMemo` is handled
PER DIRECTION (IMPLEMENTED, IZ-polish): OutOfZec is a TYPED REFUSAL
(`DepositMemoUnsupported` — the WALLET sends its own deposit, a plain
shielded→transparent ZEC tx, and cannot attach a source-chain memo; ZEC-chain
deposits carry none, so this never fires in practice), while **IntoZec CARRIES
it** — the bounded `SwapQuote.deposit_memo` port-DTO field (mirrored across the
bridge) is rendered on the D7 deposit screen with a funds-loss warning so the
USER attaches it to their EXTERNAL deposit (§4.4), unblocking the memo-chain
IntoZec lanes — XRP destination tags, Cosmos/Stellar/EOS memos; an empty memo
normalizes to absent. Wire amounts are BASE-UNIT
integer strings; the adapter converts to the port's human decimal strings
with exact integer math via the token table's `decimals` (ZEC verified
== 8 at resolution — base units are zatoshis, checked not assumed).

### 3.2a The lightwalletd gRPC seam over `NetDialer` (W3-inc-2c-ii)

The transport-critical seam every sync RPC (inc-2c-iv scan loop) and the tx
broadcast (inc-2d) ride. **This is the increment that makes the wallet speak
gRPC over the HOST APP'S OWN NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE** — the founder requirement
(2026-06-10, re-affirmed 2026-06-14; **ADR-0526**): Relim brings its own Tor
today and **xray/VLESS (or any future transport) tomorrow**, and the wallet must
ride whatever Relim already runs rather than spawn a second, parallel network
stack.

**REUSE WHOLE (Rule Zero — we write NO protobuf, NO gRPC framing).** The
lightwalletd `CompactTxStreamer` client is `zcash_client_backend`'s
upstream-generated `proto::service::compact_tx_streamer_client::CompactTxStreamerClient`
+ its `prost` message types. We promote `zcash_client_backend 0.23.0` from a
transitive dep (via `zcash_client_sqlite`) to a DIRECT, exact-pinned
(`=0.23.0`, `default-features = false`) dep and enable ONE feature:
`lightwalletd-tonic-transport` (= the generated tonic client + `tonic/transport`
for `connect_with_connector`). Our code is the channel-construction glue only.

**Supply-chain outcome (auditor pass, 2026-06-14 — the new-deps event isolated
to this increment, same discipline as inc-2b-ii-A isolated the DB stack):**
- New transitive crates: `tonic 0.14`, `tonic-prost 0.14`, `tower`, `h2`,
  `tower-layer`/`tower-service`, `tokio-stream`, `tokio-util`, `socket2`,
  `hyper-timeout`, `pin-project[-internal]`, `sync_wrapper` (13). `prost`,
  `hyper`, `hyper-util`, `rustls`, `tokio-rustls`, `webpki-roots` were ALREADY
  in the lock (ECC's non-optional `prost` + the W-swap-1 HTTP/TLS stack).
- All MIT/Apache-2.0; **zero unfixed RustSec advisories** across the 13;
  `deny.toml` needs NO change.
- **Tor invariant CONFIRMED CLEAN:** enabling `lightwalletd-tonic-transport`
  pulls NO `arti-client`/`tor-rtcompat` — those stay behind upstream's own
  `tor` feature, which this SDK never enables. Since FR-5 C1 there is no
  feature that could: arti cannot enter `sdk/`'s lock at all (`dialer-tor` and
  the plugin are their own workspaces, ADR-0551), and P15 proves it at the
  built library's symbols. (A Tor crate appearing on this path is a BLOCKER.)
- **Omit `lightwalletd-tonic-tls-webpki-roots`** — we own TLS over the dialed
  stream (below); tonic's built-in TLS is never invoked on this path, so
  enabling it would add a second, latent (provider-less) TLS path. The SDK
  therefore has ONE TLS path — ours — for EVERY runtime, the `zec_wallet_tor`
  plugin included: the plugin registers a dialer and its stream rides this
  same connector (FR-5 C1 retired the June second path, arti's own
  `connect_to_lightwalletd`).
- `tonic`/`tower`/`h2` need NO individual `=` pins (transitive; the lock IS
  their pin record); only the direct `zcash_client_backend` carries the
  ADR-0005 r5 exact pin. MINOR follow-ups: `cargo update -p tonic -p tonic-prost`
  to the 0.14 tip; the `tonic/transport` feature compiles dead server-side gRPC
  (no finer split in 0.23.0 — `lto=thin` strips most; documented, not blocking).

**Host-infrastructure-first, PROTOCOL-AGNOSTIC by construction.** The SDK asks
the `NetDialer` for "a byte stream to `host:port` with an `isolation_key`" and
**never knows or names the host's transport** — Tor, xray, VLESS, a SOCKS
proxy, a test loopback are all indistinguishable to the wallet. The Relim path
is `TorRuntime::Dialer(Arc<dyn NetDialer>)`, where Relim hands the wallet its
existing transport. For EVERY runtime, with no exception since FR-5 C1,
there is exactly ONE place all wallet gRPC traffic enters the network —
the connector below — so "no independent clearnet path" (§3.2 m5) is structural,
not policed. ~~The built-in arti `BuiltIn` runtime is a SECOND, deferred impl of
the same `TorPolicy` contract that uses arti's verified `connect_to_lightwalletd`
(its own channel + TLS, §3.2/§2.3) instead of this connector — identical
fail-close/fallback semantics, just via the upstream helper.~~ **STRUCK at FR-5
C1 (2026-09-17): there is no second impl and no second channel. Tor for a host
without a transport is the `zec_wallet_tor` plugin, a REGISTRANT of the dialer
contract, so its traffic rides this connector like every other transport's.**

**Channel construction — the connector (`net/grpc.rs`, crate-internal):**
build the tonic `Channel` with `Endpoint::from(uri).connect_with_connector(svc)`
where `svc` is a `tower::service_fn` closure that, per connection:
1. `dialer.dial(host, port, isolation_key).await` → `Box<dyn AsyncByteStream>`
   (the host's infrastructure — TCP/Tor/xray/VLESS/loopback, opaque to us);
2. for an `https://` endpoint, wrap the duplex in a `tokio_rustls::TlsConnector`
   (`webpki-roots` trust anchors, SNI = the endpoint host) → a TLS stream; for a
   loopback `http://` endpoint (the §2.3 validator guarantees plaintext ONLY to
   loopback) skip TLS;
3. hand the (TLS-or-plain) duplex to tonic wrapped in `hyper_util::rt::TokioIo`
   so tonic runs HTTP/2 over it.
On this connector path (every runtime, no exception — FR-5 C1), tonic's
own connector and its own TLS are NEVER used. The connector is the seam
chokepoint: no RPC can construct a socket that bypasses the dialer + policy.

**`TorPolicy` → dialer resolution (the honest-off / fail-closed contract,
resolved HERE for the first time — no resolver existed pre-inc-2c-ii):**

| Policy | Dialer used | On dialer `Unreachable`/`Timeout` |
|---|---|---|
| `Off` | the SDK's **one** built-in `DirectTcpDialer` — the explicit-clearnet choice, named and honest, NEVER a hidden fallback. Dials happy-eyeballs-style (FR-21, RFC 8305-lite): `lookup_host` → per-family interleave with an **IPv4 head-start** → attempts raced `DIAL_ATTEMPT_STAGGER_MS` apart, first established stream wins (laggards aborted), all inside the one `DIAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` bound — a blackholed/unroutable IPv6 leg can no longer starve the IPv4 fallback (the S137 IPv4-only-Wi-Fi field failure: a bare sequential `TcpStream::connect` never reached the A record). Observable clearnet delta (accepted): a slow first leg now emits SYNs to further addresses across both families (≤ 8 total) — only on paths where the peer already sees the wallet's IP (`Off` / the visible `Preferred` fallback) | `Stalled { EndpointUnreachable }` (normal offline) |
| `Preferred { Dialer(d) }` | the host runtime `d` | **INSIST for `TOR_PATIENCE_SECS` = 60 (ADR-0552, the founder's minute, 2026-09-18), THEN** fall back to `DirectTcpDialer` **and surface `TorFellBack`** + `TorState::FellBack` — degradation VISIBLE, never silent (§6.1); the ANNOUNCEMENT ADR-0552 decision 3 requires is **BUILT at stage S1 `truth` (S291)**: `watch_tor_state` delivers every transition once, so a host learns at the moment instead of at its next poll, and under `Preferred` the sequence is two events — `Unanswered`, then `FellBack` at the clearnet dial, which is the one FR-34 keys on. *(This clause read "is OWED — stage 2 of `docs/plan/tor-patience-phase-1.md`, because `TorState` crosses only on the polled `snapshot()` today, so no host can see the moment" until S291. Kept visible rather than silently swapped: the sentence was true when written and is the reason the verb exists.)* Inside the window a qualifying failure returns typed and sends ZERO clearnet packets. **It reports the ORDINARY `Stalled { EndpointUnreachable }`, not `TorUnavailable`:** the honest "still trying your private path" reading was built on the existing fail-closed state and WITHDRAWN the same day (ADR-0552's correction 2) — the plan is built once for the long-lived sync client, so a latch-derived reason freezes and would keep claiming "nothing was sent in the clear" after the wallet had gone to clearnet. The honest state needs its reason resolved at FAILURE time and its own copy; **both LANDED at stage S1 (S291)** — the reason is resolved at failure time by `transport_stall`, which keys on whether the DIAL was accepted rather than on which timer fired, and the copy is the `unanswered` sentence family (ADR-0554). The window is measured from the last CONFIRMED private RPC — a response that came back over a connection the private primary served — or from the wallet's creation when none has (ADR-0552 corrections 4–5: since phase 2 the minute is one in which the path was both silent AND seen failing — a failed dial, or a failed RPC over a private connection — and since S290 an ACCEPTED private dial is left for clearnet on that evidence too, the connection whose RPC failed having been retired, so the accepting-and-silent path switches; the clearnet leg then has `FALLBACK_ESTABLISH_BUDGET_SECS` = 5 s, TCP and TLS together). **A bare DIAL does not restart it (ADR-0552 correction 3, stage 1b):** a transport that accepts and then blackholes, which is active censorship's cheapest move, would otherwise reset the window on every attempt and the wallet would never switch. An RPC that rode the clearnet fallback does not restart it either. **And the window has a SUBJECT: one per circuit family** (sync / broadcast / other, keyed by the isolation key the dial already carries — S290: and `swap`, the on-ramp's HTTP dials, the one class whose bare connect is evidence; `other` is strict again) — a single wallet-wide window let a healthy sync circuit reset the clock a starved broadcast was measuring, i.e. a payment that never leaves while the UI reads UpToDate and `Active`. The window is per SESSION (create/open/rescan take a fresh posture; only the server switch carries one across) and counts device-AWAKE time; both err towards insisting. **Before ADR-0552 the switch happened after ONE `DIAL_TIMEOUT_SECS`, 30 s — which was nobody's decision: it fell out of a liveness bound.** (That bound is 25 s since stage 1b: it must stay strictly below `GRPC_UNARY_TIMEOUT_SECS`, or a unary call cancels the dial future at the instant the dial bound fires and the switch is never evaluated on the money path.) `net/tor_posture.rs` owns the clocks and the latch; plan `docs/plan/tor-patience-phase-1.md` |
| `Required { Dialer(d) }` | the host runtime `d` | **FAIL-CLOSED: zero further packets,** NEVER falls back to clearnet — the honest-off invariant THROUGH a network failure. **Which failure it reports is a claim about the DIAL since S1 `truth` (S291, [ADR-0554](../adr/0554-wallet-transport-a-ready-path-that-carries-nothing-gets-its-own-state-and-the-sdk-does-not-guess-why.md)):** a dial that FAILED (refused, unreachable, a dial timeout, a cleared or `FAILED` descriptor) is `Stalled { TorUnavailable }` + `TorState::Unavailable`, promptly, as before — the evidence separates the path. A dial that was ACCEPTED (its `Ok`, and so a `wallet.dial … outcome=connected` line) and then carried nothing — a TLS handshake that never completes, an accept-then-close, an RPC that hangs — is `Stalled { EndpointUnreachable }` with `TorState::Active` from the first observed failure, and `TorState::Unanswered` at the founder's minute: *ready, and nothing has come back — the path OR the server*. The SDK does not guess which, because from one connection it cannot: bytes went out and nothing came back. Over `https` — the only scheme the door admits under a host runtime — the first observed failure is the connector's TLS bound (~25 s), so the user-visible minute reads ~85 s. **This replaced an over-claim, not a gap:** every transport failure and every timeout used to be stamped `TorUnavailable`, so a wedged SERVER over a healthy private path rendered "the private path is unavailable — nothing was sent in the clear" |
| `{ ExternalSocks5 }` under either policy | **none — REFUSED AT THE CONFIG DOOR (T0-6, 2026-09-11)** | `InvalidEndpoint` (RW-CFG-001) from `validate_wallet_config`, before anything opens, with a reason that says the runtime is not built and names the alternatives. **This row used to promise the `Preferred` fallback and the `Required` fail-closed for `ExternalSocks5`, and the code delivered neither**: no dialer exists for it, `runtime_dialer` returns `UnsupportedRuntime`, and `resolve_dialer` propagates that with a `?` — so `Preferred { ExternalSocks5 }` never reached the clearnet fallback its own name promised, and a host learned at the first dial, as a network-shaped error, that a privacy setting was not wired. The consequence, stated plainly: **a Dart host has no Tor option in this build**, because `ExternalSocks5` is the only runtime `TorRuntimeConfig` can express. A Rust host still has `TorRuntime::Dialer` (ADR-0526) |
| `{ HostDialer }` under either policy | the registered dialer (the host's, or the `zec_wallet_tor` plugin's) | the FR-29 crossing's own matrix — `host-transport-crossing.md` §3.3/§6.2. Nothing registered is refused at the config door; a declared `health = FAILED` is fail-closed like not-ready (ADR-0549) (S290: under `Required`; under `Preferred` a FAILED declaration is refused at the gate as `TransportFailed`, counts as the private path failing, and a minute of it — from the declaration — switches, visibly; ADR-0553 as built, ADR-0552 correction 5) |

Resolution of the **`no independent clearnet path` vs `Off`** apparent tension
(decided here): the SDK ships exactly ONE clearnet dialer, used SOLELY for the
explicit `TorPolicy::Off` config and as the VISIBLE `Preferred` fallback. It is
never reachable under `Required`, and no code path under a privacy runtime can
side-channel around the host dialer. §9's "the SDK ships no clearnet dialer"
means it ships none that MASQUERADES as Tor — `Off`'s direct dialer is the
user's stated clearnet choice, not a silent Tor-bypass.

**THE ONE WAY OUT — the span behind the privacy claim, asked for by the host
session S291 to close a duress-wipe ticket and answered at the code rather than
from memory.** *Can the SDK reach the network by any path other than the
transport the host registered?* **Under `Required`, no**, on four spans that are
worth keeping together because each is cheap to check and easy to assume:

1. **There is exactly ONE socket site in the whole SDK** — `DirectTcpDialer` in
   `net/dialer.rs` — pinned by a gate, not by prose:
   `zec-wallet-core/tests/no_network_io_outside_the_dialer.rs` scans the
   production lines of all three crates for `TcpStream`, `TcpSocket`,
   `UdpSocket`, `lookup_host`, `socket2::`, `mio::net::`, the Unix-domain
   sockets and socket-typed `std::net::` items, comments stripped, tests
   excluded, that one file exempt. It has four callers in the justfile and a
   watched mutant row.

   **This sentence was FALSE when it was written here, and what makes it true
   now is worth recording (S291 review, docs consistency MAJOR).** The scan
   stopped at each file's FIRST `#[cfg(test)]` module and never resumed, on the
   premise that a crate's test modules sit at its tail. 64 files broke that
   premise and **3,182 production lines were never read** — including, in one of
   the three crates this paragraph cites the gate for,
   `zec-wallet-swap-near/src/lib.rs` below its `mod provider_tests;` at line 73:
   the endpoint parser, the provider, and the whole `impl SwapPort`. The scan
   now skips a test module's SPAN and resumes after it, which added those lines
   and found **zero** new violations — the claim held; the evidence for it did
   not. What "tests excluded" means exactly: the `tests/` directories are never
   scanned; an inline `#[cfg(test)]` module's braces are skipped and the scan
   continues below them; a test module in its own file is skipped whole only
   when EVERY declaration of that file, anywhere in the scanned trees, is
   `cfg(test)`-gated. Guarded in the two shapes that fail independently — a
   production-LINE floor against a scan that collapses, and a named canary in
   the real tree (swap-near's `impl SwapPort` must be scanned) against one that
   truncates.
2. **`Required` never constructs it.** `resolve_dialer`'s `Required` arm builds
   `PolicyDialer::fail_closed(...)`, and `fail_closed` sets `fallback: None` —
   the clearnet branch is ABSENT, not disabled.
3. **A host's own refusal can never reach clearnet under ANY policy.** The
   switch arm admits exactly `Unreachable | Timeout | TransportFailed`;
   `NotReady`, `Retired`, `Unsupported` and `Io` fall to the catch-all. So a
   host that retires its dialer mid-wipe is fail-closed by construction.
4. **The swap adapter cannot open a socket at all:** `zec-wallet-swap-near`
   takes tokio with `features = ["time"]` only — no `net` — and its HTTPS rides
   the injected `NetDialer`.

**And under `Required` the SDK resolves no hostnames.** `lookup_host` lives only
in `DirectTcpDialer`, which that policy never builds, so the host's dialer is
handed the NAME and there is no DNS leak from the wallet — a fact worth more
than the ticket it was raised for. Two conditions carry it: the policy must be
`Required` (`Off` and `Preferred` reach `DirectTcpDialer` by design, and
`set_tor_policy` is not built, so the policy is fixed at construction), and the
optional `zec_wallet_tor` plugin — a separate crate outside the scanned
workspace, which does open sockets — must not be in the host's build.

**inc-2c-ii build scope (KISS — the seam, not the scan loop):** the connector +
`DirectTcpDialer` (`Off`) + the **first-class `Dialer(d)` host-infrastructure
path** + the `Required` fail-close / `Preferred` fallback policy resolution +
a thin `LightwalletdClient` exposing the UNARY seam RPCs the next increments
need (`get_lightd_info` for the server/network handshake, `get_latest_block`,
`get_tree_state` for iv-d's per-range `from_state` — §3.2f, NOT the birthday,
which iv-c anchors on the bundled frontier). The streaming scan RPCs
(`get_block_range`) and `send_transaction` wire in with inc-2c-iv/2d.
**The `ExternalSocks5` dialer is a named follow-up** (its own small dep
decision); arti is no longer one of them — Tor arrives as the `zec_wallet_tor`
plugin through `HostDialer` (FR-5 C1 removed the `BuiltIn` arm).
Until `ExternalSocks5` lands, resolving to it is a TYPED config error at construction
(`InvalidConfig`-class), never a silent clearnet leak. The resolution structure
is built ready for them (the table above is the contract).

**Isolation keys (§2.3) flow through the connector unchanged:** sync uses a
single stable sync-circuit key (cadence/range fetches MAY share a circuit);
swap already uses per-txid keys; the connector passes the caller's
`isolation_key` straight to `dialer.dial` — a dialer that cannot honor
isolation returns `DialError::Unsupported`, surfaced, never silently linked.

**Unstable-network posture (mobile + desktop, §6.2/§7):** gRPC timeouts are
split unary vs streaming (`GRPC_UNARY_TIMEOUT_SECS = 30` /
`GRPC_STREAMING_TIMEOUT_SECS = 100`) and are MONOTONIC (a wall-clock jump never
fires them, §7). A dialed-connection death mid-call surfaces `Stalled`, never a
dead stream (§3.3); the inc-2c-iv loop owns retry/backoff. Every dial outcome is
observable: `wallet.tor_bootstrap {percent}` (Dialer/arti bootstrap),
`wallet.private_path_fell_back` (Preferred fallback; `wallet.tor_fell_back`
until S288), `wallet.sync {…, outcome}` — field
sets inside the §5.4 allowlist (endpoint host/port/isolation key are NEVER
logged; only outcome + counts + durations).

**Desktop (§9):** identical `NetDialer` contract — the SDK owns no Tor ⇒ the
host brings its own `Dialer`, registers one, or adds the `zec_wallet_tor`
plugin (`ExternalSocks5` is still unbuilt); the SDK ships
only the `Off` direct dialer; no special desktop network path. macOS/Linux/Win
ride the same connector — pure async I/O over the dialed duplex, no
platform-specific socket code (cross-compile-safe: no new `default-features`
exposure, validated by the auditor's Tor-clean graph).

### 3.2b Account import: birthday treestate → derived account 0 (W3-inc-2c-iii)

The wallet DB is provisioned ACCOUNT-LESS (§4.3, inc-2b-ii-A: `init_wallet_db`
runs with `seed = None` because a fresh wallet has no derived account for the
migrator to validate a seed against). This increment adds the **one account the
v1 scope cuts to** (§1.6: ZIP-32 account 0 per wallet) — the step that turns a
schema into a wallet that can detect funds. It is OFFLINE and idempotent; the
network FETCH of the birthday treestate and the decision of WHEN to import are
the sync engine's orchestration (inc-2c-iv), not this chunk.

**REUSE WHOLE (Rule Zero).** Account creation is
`zcash_client_backend::data_api::WalletWrite::import_account_hd(account_name,
&SecretVec<seed>, zip32::AccountId::ZERO, &AccountBirthday, key_source)` on our
`WalletConn` (`zcash_client_sqlite::WalletDb`) — it derives the account UFVK,
records the birthday + initial scan ranges, and returns `(Account,
UnifiedSpendingKey)`. We write no account/derivation logic; we supply the seed +
birthday and DROP the returned USK immediately (function-local, never stored,
never logged — the §4.1 keys-in-Rust posture; the seed is wrapped in
`secrecy::SecretVec` only because the audited API demands it, a transient
zeroizing copy). `import_account_hd` (explicit account 0) is chosen over
`create_account` (auto-index) so the index is PINNED to 0 — the same account the
offline `derive_default_address` (§3.1, inc-2c-i) uses, which makes the two UAs
equal BY CONSTRUCTION (below). `secrecy 0.8.0` was already in the lock (a
transitive dep of the zcash stack); this promotes it to a direct, exact-pinned
(`=0.8.0`, `default-features = false`) dep — **zero new transitive crates**, not
a supply-chain event.

**Idempotent (unstable-network + crash safety, §6.3).** `ensure_account` checks
`get_account_ids()` first and is a NO-OP if account 0 already exists — so a kill
mid-import, a retry after a dropped connection, or a double-call all converge to
exactly one account. The import itself is one rusqlite write (no block scanning
happens in the call — `import_account_hd` only records the account + scan
ranges; the actual scan is the engine's `scan_cached_blocks`, inc-2c-iv), run
inside `spawn_blocking` like every other DB op (off the Dart/UI thread AND the
async runtime; mobile/desktop identical — no proving circuit, no jetsam risk).

**The birthday treestate — `AccountBirthday::from_treestate` (the M2 boundary).**
`AccountBirthday` anchors the Sapling + Orchard commitment-tree frontiers as of
the block PRIOR to the birthday height (`height() == prior_chain_state.height() +
1`), so the scanner computes correct note positions without replaying from
activation. We build it from the lightwalletd `GetTreeState` DTO (§3.2a
`get_tree_state`, now available) via `TreeState::to_chain_state()` →
`AccountBirthday::from_treestate(treestate, recover_until = None)`. **Every byte
of that treestate is hostile input (§4.6):** the endpoint is UNTRUSTED.
`to_chain_state` already validates the SHAPE (hex-decodes the block hash to 32
bytes, parses the frontier encodings) — a malformed/oversized treestate is a
typed decode error here, never a panic. What it does NOT — and structurally
CANNOT — check is whether a well-formed treestate is the REAL chain state at that
height (a lying endpoint that hands a plausible-but-wrong frontier is the M2
"silently hide funds" threat). This chunk owns only the decode + the typed-error
boundary; it makes no trust claim about the treestate's honesty.

> **SUPERSEDED FOR PROVISIONING by §3.2f (W3-inc-2c-iv-c).** The crypto audit
> settled the open question above: the backend does NOT self-verify a frontier,
> and a live frontier is cryptographically unverifiable at a recent height — so
> iv-c **dropped the live `get_tree_state` provisioning path**. The
> `birthday_from_treestate` decode boundary built here is REUSED, but it is now
> fed the **TRUSTED bundled frontier** (signed binary), not a hostile live fetch;
> the "continuity verification escalated to inc-2c-iv" is therefore not owed — it
> was eliminated, not escalated. (The unary `get_tree_state` seam survives for
> iv-d's per-range `from_state`, a different position — §3.2f.)

**The `init_wallet_db(Some(seed))` retry loop (now reachable).** Once a derived
account exists, an app upgrade that adds a seed-validating migration makes
`init_wallet_db(None)` return `WalletMigrationError::SeedRequired` (downcast via
`MigratorError::source()`, the upstream-documented pattern). `db::migrate` now
tries `None` first and, on `SeedRequired`, retries with `Some(SecretVec(seed))`
when a seed is available; with NO seed available (the `SeedPersistence::None`
Relim path holds none at rest) it surfaces the typed `SeedRequired` so the host
re-supplies it (the §4.2 / §2.2 re-derive contract). `store::open` threads the
loaded custody seed (`Some` for `SealedKeychain`, `None` for `None`-mode) into
`open_db_migrated`. Steady-state opens (no pending seed-migration) still pass
`None` cleanly even with an account present — the retry is correctness insurance
for the future-migration case, not a per-open cost.

**`current_address` reads the stored account UFVK (equality by construction;
covers None-mode).** Refined from the inc-2c-i offline shortcut: `current_address`
now reads account 0's UFVK FROM THE DB (`get_account` → `Account::ufvk()`) and
derives the default UA from it with the SAME `Require`/`Require`/`Omit` receiver
request (G7, §3.1) — so the DB-sourced UA EQUALS the seed-derived one because
both call `UnifiedFullViewingKey::default_address(request)` on the same UFVK (one
read from the DB, one derived from the seed — identical key, identical address;
the shared `encode_default_address` helper is the single source of truth, DRY).
This is what makes the address correct in **`None`-persistence** (no seed at rest,
but the account UFVK IS in the DB — the Relim path reads its own receive address
with zero key material). Before account import exists, `current_address` keeps
the inc-2c-i behavior: derive from the held seed (`SealedKeychain`) or typed
`SeedRequired` (`None`). The handle-UA == account-UA equality test
(`current_address_after_import_equals_offline_derivation`, the crypto audit S16
forward-owed) locks the `{account 0, Require/Require/Omit, default diversifier}`
triple.

#### FR-12 / inc-2c-iv — `WalletSeedPort` host-custodied seed (✅ AS BUILT S112 — wiring + crypto-change 3-angle review + code review complete)

The host-supplied per-operation seed seam that makes `SeedPersistence::None` a
real **view-only-at-rest / spend-on-supply** wallet (the deniability end-state:
nothing spendable at rest; each spend is gated by the host credential, which
re-derives the sub-seed, stages it, and the SDK pulls it for ONE op then
zeroizes). Public trait `WalletSeedPort::provide_seed() -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,
SeedSupplyError>` *(since FR-17/#396: `provide_seed(binding: Option<&SpendBinding>)`
— see the "FR-17 + FR-18" section)* + `SeedSupplyError::{Unavailable, Denied}` (both
→ typed `SeedRequired`, no oracle) shipped in `seed.rs`; the trait is Rust-only (a
host-custodied-key seam any embedder gets — NOT a Relim concept) and MUST NEVER
cross the FFI/bridge surface (Dart can't zeroize a `Uint8List`; a CI dep-boundary
grep asserts no `WalletSeedPort`/`SeedSupplyError`/`seed_port` symbol reaches
`zec_wallet/rust/src/api/*`). Sync by design (the §4.2 seed→USK→sign→drop
confinement must stay inside one `spawn_blocking`).

**Seed-free by construction (no port call):** `snapshot`/balance, `transactions`/
`transaction`/`transaction_memos`, and `current_address`/`current_transparent_address`
POST-import — all read the persisted account UFVK. The port is pulled ONLY by the
key-deriving ops: account import, signing, `fresh_refund_address`.

**The chokepoint (AS BUILT):** one private `Inner::acquire_seed() -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,
WalletError>` *(since FR-17/#396: `acquire_seed(binding: Option<&SpendBinding>)`)*
= held `seed` (SealedKeychain) → else `seed_port.provide_seed()` →
else `SeedRequired`; it **validates 32..=252 at the boundary** (the
`SeedSource::raw_bytes` SSOT — every host byte is hostile, never a deep-stack
upstream panic). Called from `run_blocking` closures ONLY, and **BEFORE any
`db.lock()`/`aux_db.lock()`** (the existing pull-before-lock ordering — preserve
it; a re-entrant/blocking port under a held non-reentrant `Mutex` self-deadlocks).
Replaces every `inner.seed.as_ref().ok_or(SeedRequired)?` in import / sign / queued-
sign / refund; `current_address` does NOT use it. (NAMED `acquire_seed`, not
`resolve_seed`, to disambiguate from the construction-time `derivation::resolve_seed`
that expands a `SeedSource` → `SeedPayload` once at provisioning — arch review fold.)

**BLOCKER requirements the wiring MUST satisfy (from the crypto ∥ security ∥ arch
design review):**
- **B1 wrong-seed → typed `SeedMismatch` (money).** Before deriving the signing
  USK, verify the supplied seed's UFVK == the stored account UFVK (reuse the
  audited `WalletRead::get_account_for_ufvk(derived_ufvk)` / `account.ufvk()`, no
  hand-rolled compare); mismatch → typed `SeedMismatch`, never opaque `SignFailed`
  and never a tx. (Today a wrong seed only fails via the engine's internal
  `KeyNotRecognized` AFTER the token is consumed.)
- **B2 pull-before-consume / pull-before-reserve.** Move the one-shot
  `proposals.consume(id)` INTO the blocking closure, AFTER `acquire_seed()` + the
  B1 UFVK check pass — so `Unavailable`/`Denied`/`SeedMismatch` leaves the send
  fully retryable (token intact). The refund path: pull + `supports_transparent_refund`
  pre-check BEFORE `reserve_next_index`/`allocate_refund_address` (a port failure
  must not burn a never-recycle HD index — HARD-H).
- **B3 no offline staging window (deniability).** Never hold the seed across the
  offline create→first-sync gap. Account import happens at a **user-present
  moment**: eager-import-at-create when the birthday is concrete (restore), else
  the host re-stages via a fresh credential gate at first sync. The host stages
  narrowly + clears immediately; the **send scope is take-once (one confirm = one
  signature)** — a second pull against a send-stage returns `Unavailable`.
- **B4 `queue_send` on a `None`-wallet.** The background Phase-2 re-sign drain
  (`resubmit_queued_sends`) has no live user → no staged seed. It must NOT silently
  skip (today's `if seed.is_some()` drops queued `None`-wallet sends forever):
  gate on `seed.is_some() || seed_port.is_some()`, attempt `acquire_seed()`, and on
  `Unavailable` leave the intent **Queued + surfaced** (retried when the host
  re-stages), never silently lost. (Phase-1 re-broadcast of an already-SIGNED tx
  needs no seed — confirmed; pin it.) The deeper "background sign needs a live
  user" tension is a host/product question — Relim v1 uses direct live-confirm
  `send`; flagged to the founder.
- **B5 constructors + footgun.** Add `pub(crate) open_with_vault_and_seed_port(cfg,
  vault, port)` (the CI test seam — `open_with_seed_port` alone needs a real
  keychain) backing the public `open_with_seed_port(cfg, port)`; thread `seed_port`
  via `OpenConfig`→`Inner` (immutable-after-open). A LOUD `create` docstring: a
  `None`-wallet's post-`create` handle has no port → first sync `SeedRequired`;
  required pattern `create → close → open_with_seed_port` (or add the symmetric
  `create_with_seed_port`).

**MUST-HANDLE:** seed dropped right after USK derivation (before the prove); USK
confined to the one blocking section (no Zeroize upstream — §4.2 residual); the
`provide_seed` non-blocking/non-re-entrant/no-wallet-lock contract (in the trait
doc); `SeedMismatch` must not become a decoy-vs-real oracle — `Denied` is the only
duress signal and a decoy identity uses a SEPARATE `db_dir` (depends on **FR-13**
keychain namespacing before the decoy claim is made); a `#[cfg(test)] mod testing`
with `StagedSeedPort`/`UnavailablePort` doubles (mirror `ports.rs`).

**Named tests (gate 8, owed with the wiring):** `import_account_via_port`,
`sign_via_port_succeeds`, `wrong_seed_is_seed_mismatch_before_consume_and_before_spend`,
`port_unavailable_leaves_the_proposal_retryable`, `port_unavailable_leaves_the_refund_index_unburned`,
`seed_zeroized_after_import_sign_refund`, `view_ops_are_seed_free_post_import`,
