### 3.2c The `LightdSyncEngine` — increment plan (W3-inc-2c-iv decomposition)

The sync engine is OUR orchestration loop over the consumed-WHOLE
`zcash_client_backend` scan primitives (`suggest_scan_ranges`,
`scan_cached_blocks`, the `data_api` — NEVER re-implemented, §3.2). It is the
last unbuilt piece of the first usable wallet (a wallet that detects funds), and
it is multi-increment — decomposed dependency-ordered, each a reviewed unit with
its own full spec section when built (the inc-2c-ii/iii discipline):

- **inc-2c-iv-a — block-download transport seam.** Extend `LightwalletdClient`
  (net/grpc.rs) with the STREAMING `get_block_range(BlockRange) -> stream of
  CompactBlock` RPC under `GRPC_STREAMING_TIMEOUT_SECS = 100` (monotonic), each
  block hostile input (the `max_decoding_message_size` cap already applies). The
  return SHAPE (raw `tonic::Streaming` vs an SDK-owned bounded batch) is co-designed
  with iv-b — they land together or iv-a exposes the minimal stream iv-b wraps. NO
  money/crypto logic; the stream pump is unit-tested through a scripted
  `CompactBlockSource` + the §3.2a dead-duplex dialer (this crate ships only the
  lightwalletd CLIENT codegen, and `tonic::Streaming` has no test constructor, so
  no in-memory server is stood up — a real-stream truncation guard is integration
  tier, §8). Mechanical sibling of the inc-2c-ii unary RPCs. **BUILT — see §3.2d.**
- **inc-2c-iv-b — the compact-block cache + the bound primitive.** A disposable
  on-disk cache the streamed blocks land in and `scan_cached_blocks` reads back,
  bounded by `CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (the read-ahead-vs-scanning bound; a full disk
  must not spin — M4), with startup sanitation (validated-or-deleted; disposable
  by design, §6.3 "sync mid-batch kill"). iv-b owns the cache + the bound
  PRIMITIVE (`total_bytes()`/`headroom()`); the download-batching LOOP that fills
  it lives in iv-d (co-located with the scan). Data plane only — no decryption.
  **DESIGN — see §3.2e** (bounded SQLCipher DB; `BlockSource` + inherent methods,
  no `sync`/`unstable` feature).
- **inc-2c-iv-c — live account provisioning over the bundled-frontier anchor
  (crypto-change review — the M2 trust root). DESIGN + AS-BUILT in §3.2f.** The
  crypto audit (2026-06-14) settled §3.6/§4.6's open question — the backend does
  NOT self-verify a birthday frontier (it trusts lightwalletd for tree state) —
  so iv-c takes the **"drop the live path"** branch: **the birthday frontier
  ALWAYS comes from the bundled checkpoint slice in the signed binary, NEVER a
  live `get_tree_state`** (a live frontier is cryptographically unverifiable at a
  recent height — "fetch-then-verify" collapses into "provision from the bundled
  anchor"; this ELIMINATES the M2 live-frontier threat, matching Zashi/Zodl).
  Resolve the birthday height (`config.birthday` ? the height : `get_latest_block`
  tip−N, §1.7), pick the newest bundled tree-state row `< requested` (never skip
  funds at `requested`), decode it via the inc-2c-iii `birthday_from_treestate`,
  drive `import_account`. **MERGE-GATE: provisioning NEVER reads a live frontier**
  — there is no fetch-then-import window for a lying lightwalletd to poison. The
  cheap correctness guards ride alongside (honestly scoped as bug/misconfig
  defense, not adversary defense): the `get_lightd_info` network-match + the
  birthday clamp. Delivers the §3.6 tree-state bundle slice (frontier table + its
  own pinned provenance hash) and the PUBLIC `WalletError::Sync` variant (+ its
  FRB `WalletErrorKind` mirror — the bridge-gate pairing). The `None`-mode seed
  re-supply seam rides here too (the re-supplied seed has no on-device anchor —
  bound it to a host-trusted identity at the composition root). Goes through the
  crypto-change review workflow (it touches the fund-detection trust root).
- **inc-2c-iv-d — the scan loop + controller. DESIGN + decomposition in §3.2g**
  (d-1 `get_subtree_roots` seam + `update_subtree_roots` → d-2 the scan loop → d-3
  the controller + live streams + first tracing). `LightdSyncEngine` driving
  `suggest_scan_ranges` → the download-batching loop (pull the iv-a `BlockStream`
  → `insert` into the iv-b cache while `headroom()` remains) → `scan_cached_blocks`
  in the non-linear Spend-before-Sync order (§1.7), with cooperative cancellation,
  checkpoint/resume (≤ one batch lost on kill, §7), and `TransactionDataRequests`
  tx-enhancement (memos). Wires the `SyncEnginePort` (the Tachyon seam, §3.2) +
  `SyncController` (`start`/`stop`/`once`). The `SyncController` core + the first
  sync-engine tracing site + the §5.4 capture-layer guard **LANDED in iv-d-3-a (✅
  BUILT)**; the real `LightdSyncEngine` + `Wallet::sync()` wiring **LANDED in
  iv-d-3-b-ii (✅ BUILT)**; the live FRB `SyncStatus`/balance streams ride iv-d-3-b-iii.
  **The reference-`run` step map iv-d MUST mirror (alignment audit 2026-06-14 vs
  `zcash_client_backend::sync::run`):**
  - **(1) `update_subtree_roots` FIRST — ⚠️ REQUIRED FOR SPENDING. ✅ BUILT
    (W3-inc-2c-iv-d-1, §3.2g).** `run`'s step 1 is `get_subtree_roots(protocol)` →
    `put_{sapling,orchard}_subtree_roots`. Detection (trial-decryption) works
    WITHOUT it, but the shardtree needs the completed subtree roots to build
    witnesses/anchors for SPEND (inc-2d) and to underpin `suggest_scan_ranges`
    prioritization. Built: the `get_subtree_roots` streaming seam (the
    `MessageStream<T>` generalization of iv-a's `BlockStream`), `sync.rs`'s
    hostile-input decode + `Wallet::update_subtree_roots` wiring. d-2's scan loop
    calls it FIRST each sync. **Departs from `run` on purpose since S15-F1
    (ADR-0569):** `run` re-fetches every root from index 0 on every pass; this SDK
    fetches each pool from 0 only when the pool is not provably settled in this
    session (the first pass of every `Inner`, any rewind, nothing stored, a server
    that cannot serve incrementally, every `SUBTREE_ROOTS_FULL_VERIFY_PASSES` = 180
    passes or `SUBTREE_ROOTS_FULL_VERIFY_SECS` = 3,600 s) and otherwise from the last
    stored root (`docs/plan/s15-f1-subtree-roots-fetch-only-what-is-new.md` §3).
  - **(2) `update_chain_tip(tip)` each iteration** (via the built `get_latest_block`)
    BEFORE `suggest_scan_ranges`, so the suggested ranges track the moving tip.
  - **(3) per-range chain state — `from_state = get_tree_state(start − 1)` for EACH
    range** (not just the birthday): because ranges scan non-linearly, every range
    `[s, e)` needs its own `ChainState` at `s − 1` to satisfy `scan_cached_blocks`'s
    `from_height == from_state.block_height + 1` assertion (it PANICS otherwise).
  - **(4) the two range conventions — get the glue exactly right** (each is faithful
    to its own upstream contract; iv-d must map both for one `ScanRange [s, e)`):
    download is INCLUSIVE → `get_block_range(s, e − 1)`; scan `from_height = s`,
    `limit = e − s`; cache `delete(s, e)` is HALF-OPEN; reorg `cache.truncate(rewind)`
    + `db.truncate_to_height(rewind)` removes ABOVE `rewind`, then re-`suggest_scan_ranges`.

Build order front-loads the non-crypto plumbing (iv-a/b) and gates the
fund-detection trust root (iv-c) behind crypto-change review; the scan loop (iv-d)
consumes all three.

### 3.2d The block-download streaming seam (W3-inc-2c-iv-a)

The mechanical sibling of the §3.2a unary RPCs: one STREAMING method on the same
`LightwalletdClient`, riding the same connector over the host `NetDialer` (so
`TorPolicy::Required` fail-closes by construction, identically). It is the
download arm the iv-d scan loop calls; iv-b wraps it to spool blocks into the
disposable FS cache. **No money/crypto logic** — pure transport.

**Reuse (Rule Zero):** ECC's upstream `CompactTxStreamerClient::get_block_range`
+ the `CompactBlock` / `BlockRange` `prost` types, whole. We write no framing.
`pool_types` is left EMPTY = the upstream legacy default (Sapling + Orchard
shielded data only) — exactly the v1 account-0 scope (§1.6, no transparent);
setting it non-empty would require first verifying server capability (the proto
contract), which we have not.

**The return shape (co-designed with iv-b, as the decomposition required):**
`get_block_range(start, end) -> Result<BlockStream, GrpcError>`. `BlockStream`
is an SDK-owned `pub(crate)` handle that CONTAINS the upstream
`tonic::Streaming<CompactBlock>` (never leaked past the seam — ADR-0005 r5) and
yields blocks via `next_block() -> Result<Option<CompactBlock>, GrpcError>`
(`Ok(None)` = clean end of range). This is the minimal stream iv-b wraps: iv-b
loops `next_block`, writes each block to the cache, bounded by `CACHE_MAX_BYTES`.
`CompactBlock` flows through `pub(crate)` because it IS the data-plane payload
`scan_cached_blocks` consumes (consumed whole, §3.2) — re-modelling it would be
pointless, and it is the same posture as the unary seam's `TreeState`/`BlockId`.

**Timeout posture (the unstable-network core):** establishment AND every
inter-block wait are bounded by `GRPC_STREAMING_TIMEOUT_SECS = 100` (monotonic,
§7), NOT the whole download — a long range legitimately runs long (the constant's
WHY). This is a PER-MESSAGE idle/stall timeout that RE-ARMS each pull, so the two
sides of the unstable-network contract both hold: a slow-but-alive link (a Tor
circuit delivering one block every ~90 s for an hour) SURVIVES — there is no
cumulative/total cap here — while a stream that goes SILENT (a blackholed socket /
dead circuit that never RSTs, the commonest flaky-mobile failure, whether at
stream-open OR after N good blocks) is killed with a typed `Timeout` rather than a
silent hang (§3.3 "a dead stream is a silent hang"). The same bound on
establishment catches a censor/DPI middlebox that completes the dial+handshake but
never sends response headers (the `DIAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` dial bound can't — the dial
SUCCEEDED). Total-progress (a stream trickling forever under the per-message
bound) is the engine's `SYNC_STUCK_WATCHDOG_SECS` watchdog (iv-d), not this seam.
`next_block` is CANCEL-SAFE: dropping a pending pull (the app backgrounded) eats
no block — tonic buffers received frames, so resuming is just another pull.

**The load-bearing reliability property:** a mid-stream fault is a typed `Err`
(idle `Timeout`, or `classify_status` → `Transport`/`Status`), **NEVER**
`Ok(None)`. A dropped connection misreported as a clean end would make
`scan_cached_blocks` believe it saw the whole range and silently skip the rest —
a fund-detection gap. `Ok(None)` is returned ONLY for a genuine end-of-stream.
Defense-in-depth (principle 10): the `BlockStream` is SPENT-ON-ERROR — any `Err`
drops the underlying stream and latches the handle terminal, so a consumer that
violates contract #2 and re-polls gets a LOUD typed `Transport` error, never the
spent `tonic::Streaming`'s silent `Ok(None)`; a clean `Ok(None)` end does not
latch (it stays idempotent for tip-following).

**Testability (no live server):** this crate ships only the lightwalletd CLIENT
codegen (no server), and `tonic::Streaming` has no public test constructor, so
the stream pump is driven through a thin `CompactBlockSource` seam (production =
`tonic::Streaming`, tests = scripted / delayed / stall-after sources). All
deterministic on a virtual clock, no real network (testing-patterns): the
per-message reset (slow link survives), the kill-after-progress and idle-at-open
bounds, the empty/single-block ranges, the spent-on-error latch + idempotent
clean end, cancel-safe drop-resume, and — over the real tonic channel via the
§3.2a dialers — the host-dialer routing and the silent-accepting-middlebox
establishment timeout. A real-`Streaming` TRUNCATION guard (tonic's
trailer-vs-abrupt-close mapping) is the one piece that needs the integration tier
(§8 E2E) — the dep floor `>=0.14.6` is the unit-level guard for it meanwhile.

### 3.2e The compact-block cache (W3-inc-2c-iv-b)

The data plane between the iv-a download stream and the iv-d scanner: a
disposable on-disk cache that the streamed `CompactBlock`s land in, and that
`scan_cached_blocks` reads back. **Data plane ONLY — no decryption, no key
material** (the crypto is `scan_cached_blocks`, consumed whole, §3.2). It is the
read-ahead buffer that lets the download run ahead of the (slower) scan without
unbounded memory or disk. (The download-batching LOOP that fills it lives in iv-d;
this increment is the cache + its bound primitive — see "the surface" below.)

**REUSE the ungated `BlockSource` trait (Rule Zero); we do NOT use the
`BlockCache` trait or `FsBlockDb`.** `scan_cached_blocks(params, block_source,
…)` reads any `BlockSource` (`zcash_client_backend::data_api::chain::BlockSource`
— ungated public trait, with one method `with_blocks`); that is the ONLY upstream
contract the scanner needs. We implement `BlockSource` over OUR storage and add
the management operations (`insert`/`read`/`delete`/`truncate`/`total_bytes`/
`headroom`) as INHERENT methods. We deliberately do NOT implement the sibling
`BlockCache` trait: it is gated behind the `zcash_client_backend` **`sync`**
feature (which would pull `lightwalletd-tonic` + `async-trait` + `futures-util` —
a new feature + supply-chain delta for management methods we own the loop for
anyway). And we do NOT use upstream's `FsBlockDb` (it lives in
**`zcash_client_sqlite`** behind the **`unstable`** feature — a no-go under the
exact-pin discipline; it enforces no size bound and is one-file-per-block / inode
pressure). Net: **zero new deps, zero new features** — just an inherent-method
type that impls the one ungated `BlockSource` trait, and we own the
`CACHE_MAX_BYTES` bound + sanitation `FsBlockDb` lacks. The cache impl is
`pub(crate)`; the upstream types it carries (`CompactBlock`, `BlockHeight`,
`ScanRange`) flow through `pub(crate)`, never the public API (ADR-0005 r5).

**Storage (founder decision 2026-06-14): a SEPARATE bounded SQLCipher
`block-cache.db` under `db_dir`, keyed by the SAME sealed `db_key`** (reuse
`db::open_keyed_connection` — the infra exists; no new key, the `db_key` is
already unsealed in `OpenWallet`). File name is a named, package-name-neutral
constant (`BLOCK_CACHE_DB_FILE_NAME`, §1.3 — like the other `db_dir` artifacts).
Schema: `cached_block(height INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL)` (the raw
`CompactBlock` protobuf bytes). Why a bounded DB and not a file-per-block "FS
cache" (the older §1.7/§7 shorthand): upstream's pain was an *unbounded* cache
*coupled to the wallet DB*; a *separate + bounded + disposable* DB removes both
root causes while keeping SQLite's free crash-atomicity + free encryption (the
money + principle-5 wins, see the two decisions below). Two decisions:
- **A separate FILE, not a table in the wallet DB:** the cache is disposable and
  can reach `CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (256 MiB); it must be blow-away-able (delete the
  file) on sanitation without VACUUM pressure on, or bloating backups of, the
  small precious wallet DB.
- **Encrypted at rest (principle 5 "metadata is as sensitive as content"):**
  compact blocks are public, but the encryption cost is negligible beside the
  trial-decryption the scan does anyway, it needs no new key, and it keeps a
  seized device from leaking even the approximate sync frontier. ONE consistent
  posture — everything in `db_dir` is encrypted. (The same-passphrase-two-DBs
  SQLCipher use is sound: each DB derives an independent key from its own salt.)

**The `CACHE_MAX_BYTES` bound (the read-ahead-vs-scanning bound, M4):** iv-b owns
the bound PRIMITIVE — `total_bytes()` / `headroom()` over the live cache — so the
download loop stops inserting once the cache is full; the download cannot run
unboundedly ahead of the scan and a full disk / a dense ("sandblasted") range
never spins `DiskFull` into a busy-loop (§6.1). Each block is independently capped
at the seam by `GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`. The pace is: fill to the bound → scan
drains → `delete` the scanned range → fill resumes. The download-BATCHING LOOP
itself (pull `BlockStream` → `insert` while `headroom()` remains) lives in iv-d,
co-located with the scan it feeds — iv-b stays a self-contained, independently
testable storage unit (it does not import the iv-a stream).

**Disposability + startup sanitation (§6.3 "sync mid-batch kill"):** SQLite
atomicity guarantees NO torn rows after a kill (an `INSERT` either committed or
rolled back via the WAL — the cache is always a clean height-prefix, never a
half-written block). On open: open the cache under `db_key` (SQLCipher validates
the header/key) + a schema check; on ANY failure (corrupt header, wrong key, bad
schema) DELETE the file and recreate empty — **validated-or-deleted**. A clean
restart keeps a valid cache (saves re-downloading the read-ahead on a flaky link);
corruption is dropped, never fed to the scanner (the money-safety default). The
cache is also fully expendable: losing it costs only bandwidth (re-download from
the scan frontier), never scan progress — that lives in the wallet DB's scan
state (≤ one batch lost on kill, §7), not here.

**The surface (`pub(crate)`):** `BlockCache::open(db_dir, &db_key)` (sanitizing) +
the one upstream `impl BlockSource for BlockCache` (`with_blocks`, for the
scanner) + INHERENT methods `tip_height` / `read` / `insert` / `delete` /
`truncate` (the loop + reorg rewind) and `total_bytes()` / `headroom()` (the
`CACHE_MAX_BYTES` bound primitive iv-d's download loop consults). The management
methods are inherent (NOT the `sync`-gated `BlockCache` trait — we own the loop,
so we don't need to be polymorphic over it). All SQLite work on `spawn_blocking`
(the `!Send` connection behind a `Mutex`, the wallet-handle pattern) — never
blocks the runtime; identical on desktop (no platform code).

### 3.2f Live account provisioning over the bundled-frontier anchor (W3-inc-2c-iv-c)

The bridge that makes inc-2c-iii's offline `import_account` seam LIVE: resolve a
birthday height, obtain a **trusted** commitment-tree frontier to anchor it, and
drive `import_account`. This is the fund-detection trust root — it goes through
the crypto-change review workflow.

**The load-bearing audit finding (2026-06-14, crypto audit vs librustzcash
0.23.0 — it RESHAPED this increment).** §3.6/§4.6 M2 left a decision open:
*"confirm the backend self-verifies tree continuity; if it doesn't, we add the
check or drop the live path."* The audit settled it: **the backend does NOT
self-verify a birthday frontier.** `AccountBirthday::from_treestate` →
`TreeState::to_chain_state` (`proto.rs:408`) reconstructs the frontier from the
DTO with no anchor/root check; `put_blocks` checks frontier *size* only (a leaf
count — `ll/wallet.rs:252`), never the ommer hashes; the one loud cross-check, a
shardtree root `Conflict` (`shardtree prunable.rs:763`), **cannot fire for a
recent birthday** (the birthday note sits in the incomplete tip shard, which has
no completed downloaded root to disagree with). The subtree roots that *would*
anchor it come from the **same** untrusted server and are stored as-is
(`commitment_tree.rs:1092`). Net: the effective model is **"trust lightwalletd
for tree state,"** and the only real external anchor is **a frontier we hardcode
in the signed binary.** A poisoned-but-size-correct live frontier yields
silently wrong witnesses → an *unspendable* balance (consensus rejects spends on
a bad anchor) — a recoverable fund-LOCK/DoS, not theft, not a privacy leak; fund
*detection* (trial-decryption) is unaffected (`chain.rs:606`).

**Why "fetch-then-verify" (the older §3.2c wording) is not implementable, so we
DROP the live frontier path.** You cannot verify a live frontier at height `H`
against a bundled anchor at a *different* height `H′ < H` without scanning
`H′→H` to re-derive it — at which point you already hold the trusted frontier
and never needed the fetched one. "Verify against the bundled anchor" therefore
collapses into **"provision from the bundled anchor."** So iv-c takes §3.6/§4.6's
"drop the live path" branch: **the birthday frontier ALWAYS comes from the
bundled checkpoint slice in the signed binary — NEVER from a live
`get_tree_state`.** This is exactly how the reference wallets (Zashi/Zodl)
bootstrap, and it ELIMINATES the M2 live-frontier threat rather than mitigating
it. (The unary `get_tree_state` seam built in inc-2c-ii stays — iv-d's per-range
`from_state` at `start−1` uses it for blocks the wallet has ALREADY scanned past,
a different trust position; see iv-d's step map. It is no longer on the
provisioning path.)

**The bundled-frontier anchor (the §3.6 tree-state slice, now built).** §3.6
always reserved the full `(height, hash, sapling_tree, orchard_tree)` slice of
the same `checkmate` bundle for "the gated sync engine." iv-c delivers it:
codegen'd `pub(super) const MAINNET_TREESTATES / TESTNET_TREESTATES:
&[(u32, &str, &str, &str)]` = `(height, block_hash_hex, sapling_frontier_hex,
orchard_frontier_hex)` in `checkpoints/data.rs`, the SAME mainnet / testnet rows
as the `(height, time)` slice (row counts live in `CHECKPOINTS.md`, their one
home — they move on each bundle refresh), from the SAME pinned source commit
(`CHECKPOINTS.md`). It is **additive**: the existing `(height, time)` tables +
`estimate_birthday` + their pinned hash stay BYTE-IDENTICAL (a shipped, reviewed
path — untouched). The tree-state slice carries its OWN pinned provenance hash
(`treestate_bundle_matches_pinned_provenance_hash`) over its canonical form, and
a row-alignment test ties the two slices to one source (same heights, same
order). Pre-NU5 rows carry an empty orchard frontier (correct — no Orchard
commitments before NU5: mainnet ≤ 1680000, testnet ≤ 1840000). Size: ≈ 1.8 MiB
of frontier hex in the signed binary (the cost of an offline, server-independent
trust anchor; the reference SDKs ship the same data as JSON assets). A
decoded-bytes/compressed embedding (~½ the size) is a deferred storage
optimization behind the provenance hash — it does not change the data or the
trust model.

**Birthday resolution (the money-critical glue — never skip the user's funds).**
`provision(requested_height)`:
1. `requested = config.birthday.map(height)` if the host gave one. Otherwise the
   default depends on **create-vs-restore** (the `freshly_generated` flag the
   handle captures from the `SeedSource` at create — the operational-3-lens money
   fix) **and on the durable creation stamp** (the #356-F4 offline-create floor,
   below): a **freshly generated** wallet (`SeedSource::Generate`, no prior
   history) ⇒ `min(get_latest_block tip − NEW_WALLET_BIRTHDAY_LAG_BLOCKS,
   estimate_birthday(created_at))` — the lag term (= 100, the reorg depth —
   lagging the tip keeps the birthday off a block a reorg could drop; the Zashi
   tip−100) alone was the F4 silent-fund-loss shape: provisioning is LAZY
   (first sync), so an OFFLINE-created wallet whose first sync ran days later
   resolved at tip−100 *of the sync day*, and a deposit received in the gap sat
   below the birthday (0 balance, "Up to date"). The `estimate_birthday(
   created_at)` term bounds the birthday at ~creation time no matter when the
   first sync runs. A **restore / imported seed** (`Mnemonic`/plain
   `RawBytes` — a fresh-marked `FreshRawBytes` takes the freshly-generated
   arms above, FR-24 — possible history) with no `config.birthday` ⇒
   **Sapling ACTIVATION** (a full
   scan, the §1.7 "skip ⇒ activation" contract) — NEVER ~tip, which would
   silently skip the user's entire history (the §2.3 too-high-birthday
   silent-fund-loss class). The host narrows a restore with `config.birthday`
   or `estimate_birthday`. (`open` can't know the original source, so without a
   stamp it defaults conservative = restore: a present account no-ops
   provisioning anyway, an account-less remnant gets the safe full-scan floor —
   but a PRESENT stamp proves this seed was minted on this device, so an
   account-less reopen provisions at the same `min(tip − lag,
   estimate_birthday(created_at))` instead: bounded-from-creation, strictly
   containing every possible deposit, instead of a multi-year full scan.)
   Clamp: above the tip reference ⇒ `BirthdayInFuture` (§2.3) — the reference
   is the live tip, or the bundle's newest row when the tip is below it
   (T0-1c-R2 M3: a below-row tip is clamped up to the row before any birthday
   arithmetic, so a lying-low or stuck server can neither floor a fresh
   wallet's birthday toward activation nor call a birthday the chain provably
   reached "in the future"); below Sapling activation ⇒ raised to activation
   (no shielded notes exist below). **The clamp is HALF of a mechanism
   (T0-1c-R3, INC-024):** a clamped birthday is above a behind server's tip by
   construction, and upstream `update_chain_tip` asserts on the inverted range
   `birthday..tip + 1` — a panic, not an error — so the same pass's
   `sync_once` asks `sync::birthday_beyond_tip` BEFORE `record_chain_tip` and,
   when the account's birthday is above `tip + 1` with nothing scanned past the
   tip, returns the pass without the write: below the grade's reference
   `EndpointBehind` with zero batches (the shipped cell — every resolver writes
   at most the anchor row + 1, below the row on both networks), at or above it
   `Stalled { BirthdayInFuture }` (unreachable from any shipped resolver
   today; the arm exists because the cell is named). Either way the loop runs
   its next pass; before R3 every fresh wallet against a validator stuck below
   its birthday died on its first pass with the last status frozen on glass.

   **The creation stamp (`wallet_created_at`, #356-F4; fresh-flag amendment
   S213).** One aux row (single
   `at_unix_secs`, the `sync_stamp` storage discipline over the same sealed/
   wiped/backup-excluded `wallet.db`) written ONLY by a FRESHLY-GENERATED
   create's FRESH provision — `SeedSource::Generate`, or the host-attested
   `FreshRawBytes` (FR-24 S213, whose lying-host contract carries the trust
   shift) — inside `db::provision_db` (`ON CONFLICT DO
   NOTHING` is residual belt — a repair/re-run never writes one at all; see
   the repair paragraph below). Never written on restore. Listed in
   `AUX_TABLES_PRESERVED` (ADR-0534) and — unlike `sync_stamp` — NEVER cleared
   by rescan (a rebuild must not lose the proof of when the seed came into
   existence); the ONE clear is the S213 DOWNGRADE UN-STAMP: `store::repair`
   completing a remnant under a RESTORE-shaped intent deletes a stamp an
   aborted fresh attempt left durable, so the documented doubt-recovery
   (retry the create restore-shaped) really delivers restore semantics —
   clearing is the conservative wider-scan direction.
   **Money-safety argument:** (a) vs the old fresh arm the new value
   is `≤ tip − lag`, so the scan window only ever WIDENS — never worse than the
   status quo; (b) a freshly-minted seed cannot have chain history before the
   stamp (for `FreshRawBytes` that premise is the HOST's attestation — §3.2f):
   clock-behind skew lowers the estimate (wider scan, safe); clock-ahead
   skew is capped at WRITE — the stamp is clamped to the CREATING binary's own
   bundle-tail time (`newest_checkpoint_time`), so even a future binary's
   fresher bundle can never estimate it above a height the creating binary
   already knew about (≤ height at binary release ≤ tip at create ≤ any
   deposit's height); a read-time-only cap would NOT survive an app upgrade
   between create and first sync; (c) the estimate itself floors to the bracketing
   checkpoint (`estimate_birthday_floors_..._never_overshoots`). The stamp is a
   MONEY input (it bounds the birthday) but only ever DOWNWARD — a garbage/
   missing stamp degrades to the pre-F4 arms (tip−lag / activation), never to a
   higher birthday; accordingly the READ is INFALLIBLE (any fault degrades to
   "absent" — a stamp fault must never brick an `open` over an optional bound),
   while WRITE faults fail the user-attended create loudly.

   **Repair NEVER stamps (S176 review HIGH, unanimous).** Only a FRESH
   provision writes the stamp. `store::repair` resumes a remnant whose sealed
   seed's ORIGIN it cannot know (the manifest records network + persistence,
   not seed source; `ResumeSealed` verifies nothing) — a `Generate` create
   resumed over an aborted-RESTORE remnant would otherwise durably stamp a
   seed with prior history, and because the stamp survives reopen AND rescan,
   it would defeat both recovery paths that healed this mis-flow pre-F4 (the
   account-less-reopen activation floor and the `rescan_from(None)`
   full-history hatch). With repair stamp-less, the crossed-flow residual is
   genuinely the pre-existing, in-session-only class: `freshly_generated=true`
   → tip−lag on that handle, healing on a not-yet-synced reopen (activation)
   and always via `rescan_from(None)`; a session whose first sync already
   imported at tip−lag keeps that account and only the rescan hatch lowers it
   — byte-identical to pre-F4 in every arm. (A fresh create killed after the
   DB step already has its stamp durable — a FRESH-shaped retry leaves it,
   while a RESTORE-shaped retry CLEARS it, the S213 downgrade un-stamp above;
   one killed earlier degrades to the stamp-less
   conservative arms. **RESOLVED #357 (manifest v2 seed-source provenance):**
   the manifest gains a fourth `seed_source` byte (`Generated` / `Restored` /
   `Unknown`; `PROVISION_MANIFEST_VERSION` 0x01→0x02, `MANIFEST_LEN` 3→4; a
   pre-#357 v1 manifest reads `Unknown` — the conservative no-stamp arm,
   unchanged). `store::repair` MAY now stamp a remnant whose manifest records
   `Generated` (a Generate-over-Generate resume); it still NEVER stamps
   `Restored` / `Unknown` — the S176 posture, now evidence-based rather than
   blanket. **Money-safety basis (corrected — a stamp is NOT "only downward"):**
   `resolve_birthday` keys its arm on `created_at.is_some()` (not on
   `freshly_generated`), and the SAME flag gates the #387 refund sweep + the
   ADR-0537 diversified sweep — so a stamp on a seed with PRIOR HISTORY floors the
   birthday at ~creation AND skips both sweeps, HIDING pre-stamp funds (and it
   re-floors `rescan_from(None)`; only a #390 deep scan recovers). Safety rests on
   WHO can land the stamp: this arm fires ONLY on the user's OWN fresh attestation
   (`freshly_generated_at.is_some()` on the retry). A fresh-attested RESTORE is
   exactly the §3.2f FreshRawBytes mis-attestation whose fund-hiding is already the
   documented lying-host consequence on a NORMAL fresh create — #357 adds no new
   exposure class, it only trades the S176 belt (which uniquely caught the
   crash-then-fresh-retry sub-case) for the killed-early-GENUINE-fresh recovery.
   The manifest is PLAINTEXT/unauthenticated (a no-DB-key attacker can flip
   `Restored`→`Generated`), but that grants NO new capability: it bites only if the
   user ALSO mis-attests fresh on the retry; retrying as a plain RESTORE hits the
   `(None,_)` downgrade-unstamp and stays safe.) Known caveat (`SeedPersistence::None`) — **RESOLVED
   #357 (seed-fingerprint binding):** a domain-separated SHA-256 fingerprint of
   the seed (`SHA-256(DOMAIN_TAG ‖ seed)`, the crate's established audited hash —
   `sha2`, as in the keychain envelope — with a frozen domain tag so it can
   never alias any other SHA-256 use of the seed) is recorded in the
   SQLCipher-encrypted aux DB at fresh provision
   (NEVER the plaintext manifest, NEVER the FFI surface, NEVER logged — §5.4;
   preimage-resistant, so at rest it discloses nothing the DB key doesn't
   already grant). When a None-persistence host later supplies a seed, `open`
   recomputes its fingerprint and constant-time-compares: a mismatch is a
   typed `SeedMismatch`, so a wrong-seed port no longer silently opens an
   empty-LOOKING wallet (the "my funds vanished" money-scare). The §4.2 port
   contract still carries the money posture generally; the fingerprint adds the
   at-rest verification the store-bound stamp alone could not. **HOST-INTEGRATION
   CONTRACT (post-ship UX):** the fingerprint verify runs at the `acquire_seed`
   chokepoint, so `SeedMismatch` can now surface on ANY key-deriving op (import,
   sign/send, sweep, refund derivation) — not just at open — for a
   `SeedPersistence::None` host. It is RETRYABLE (fires BEFORE any proposal is
   consumed, no token burned), so a None-persistence host MUST classify it as "the
   supplied recovery phrase does not match this wallet — re-supply the correct
   one", NOT a generic "signing failed, try again" (which loops on a persistently
   wrong seed). The reference UI hardcodes `SealedKeychain`, so this arm is
   unreachable there; it is a contract for None-persistence integrators.
2. `bundled_treestate(network, requested)` selects the **newest** tree-state row
   with `height < requested` (so `from_treestate` yields birthday =
   `row.height + 1 ≤ requested` — we start at or BELOW the requested height,
   never above ⇒ **never skip funds at `requested`**; we scan at most
   `requested − row.height` extra blocks, bounded by the bundle's inter-anchor
   gap, ~2,500 in the modern tail). If `requested` is at/below the first
   (activation) row, the activation row is used (birthday = activation + 1; the
   documented activation-floor edge — a pre-activation birthday whose funds land
   in the single activation block is out of scope, matches the reference).
3. The selected row is synthesized into a `TreeState` DTO and decoded by the
   EXISTING `account::birthday_from_treestate` (DRY — the same M2 decode boundary
   inc-2c-iii built; here the input is TRUSTED signed-binary data, so a decode
   failure is a corrupt-binary bug, fail-closed, not hostile input). A
   `treestate_bundle_every_row_decodes` test proves EVERY bundled row decodes
   (no runtime surprise; the row counts live in `CHECKPOINTS.md`, their one
   home — they move on each bundle refresh). The result drives `Wallet::import_account` (idempotent;
   inc-2c-iii's birthday-immutable-after-first-import contract holds — the
   resolver MUST present the earliest correct birthday on the first import).

**The cheap correctness guards (kept — but HONESTLY scoped: bug/misconfig
defense, NOT adversary defense).** Because the frontier no longer comes from the
server, these are robustness checks, not the security boundary:
- **Network-match** — `get_lightd_info` chain name **and Sapling activation
  height** must match the configured `Network`; a mainnet wallet pointed at a
  testnet endpoint (host/manifest misconfiguration) is rejected
  `NetworkMismatch` BEFORE any provisioning write, never a silently dead
  wallet. (**Corrected 2026-09-06:** this bullet used to say "chain name /
  consensus-branch". The branch half was never built — `endpoint_network_matches`
  (`provision.rs:73`) compares `chain_name` + `sapling_activation_height`, two
  immutable historical constants, so it cannot see a network upgrade. That gap
  is what let the Ironwood/NU6.3 outage — send AND receive, INC-016 — run
  silently from 2026-07-28; the
  consensus-branch comparison is specified, with its own predicate and refusal
  semantics, in `ironwood-nu63-support.md` §1.2/§3.2, which supersedes this
  bullet for the upgrade axis.) (A *malicious* server lies
  about its network too — but wrong-network only yields a dead wallet, low value
  to an attacker; this catches the honest-misconfig case.)
- **Height clamp** (above the tip reference — the live tip or the bundle's
  newest row, whichever is higher (T0-1c-R2) — ⇒ `BirthdayInFuture`,
  below-activation ⇒ activation) — config/typo robustness. The too-high-birthday
  silent-fund-loss direction is bounded by the *user-supplied* `config.birthday`
  (a trusted input), not the server tip; the too-LOW direction (a lying-low tip
  flooring a fresh wallet's birthday toward activation — a permanent write and
  a ~3 M-block scan) is bounded by the row. The clamp never lets a birthday
  above a behind server's tip reach upstream's `update_chain_tip` — that is the
  sync pass's `birthday_beyond_tip` guard (T0-1c-R3, §3.2f above), and the two
  are one mechanism.
The spec states plainly: against a malicious lightwalletd these guards protect
nothing cryptographic (every input is server-controlled) — the bundled frontier
is what defeats a self-consistent liar. (Multi-endpoint frontier *quorum* would
make a live fetch bite, but Relim feeds one manifest endpoint by design; out of
scope.)

**The `scan_cached_blocks` pairing contract (forward-owed to iv-d, flagged
here).** `scan_cached_blocks` `assert_eq!`-PANICS (`chain.rs:600`, compiled in
release) if `from_height != from_state.block_height + 1`. iv-c's birthday is the
*first* `from_state`; iv-d's per-range `from_state = get_tree_state(start − 1)`
must satisfy the same pairing for every range — our glue verifies it BEFORE the
call (a typed error), since the upstream response is an unconditional abort.

**The public error surface (the bridge-gate pairing).** A new public
`WalletError::Sync { … }` variant (code `RW-SYNC-001`) covers a provisioning
failure that must reach the host: an endpoint
unreachable during birthday-tip resolution (mapped from `GrpcError`, carrying the
`StallReason` so the host renders `TorUnavailable` under `Required` vs
`EndpointUnreachable`), and the fail-closed corrupt-bundle case. (**Corrected
2026-09-06:** this list used to include `NetworkMismatch`. A wrong-chain
endpoint is its own typed `WalletError::NetworkMismatch` / `RW-STORE-002`,
raised at `provision.rs:168` — never folded into `Sync`.) It is mirrored
by an FRB `WalletErrorKind` arm (the inc-2c-ii `TransportUnsupported` discipline)
so the Dart surface is exhaustive — paired in THIS increment, never split.

**Build scope (KISS — the trust anchor + the provisioning glue; the scan loop is
iv-d).** Built: the `data.rs` tree-state slice + its provenance hash +
`CHECKPOINTS.md` update; `checkpoints::bundled_treestate`; the engine-seam
`provision` glue (birthday resolve + clamp + network-match + `bundled_treestate`
→ `birthday_from_treestate` → `import_account`) over the §3.2a `LightwalletdClient`;
the `WalletError::Sync` variant + FRB mirror. **NOT here** (deferred past iv-c):
`update_subtree_roots` (the HIGH SPEND-path item — since BUILT in iv-d-1, §3.2g),
the scan loop, the per-range `from_state` fetch, and the import TIMING
(lazy-at-first-sync is iv-d's controller — **since amended by FR-24, below**).

**FR-24 AS BUILT (S211 #359 — EAGER import at create; crypto-change review):** the
import timing is now TWO-ARM, and the CONFIGURED birthday takes precedence
over every seed-source default. **Eager, fully offline, at `create`:** (a) a
CONFIGURED birthday at or below the bundle's tree-state tail imports account 0
INSIDE the create critical section — while the resolved seed payload is
transiently in memory, before it zeroizes — for ANY seed source, create or
restore (the height is host-asserted and the anchor is signed-binary data — no
network claim involved); (b) with NO configured birthday, a
`SeedSource::Generate` create imports the same way over
`bundled_treestate(estimate_birthday(created_at))`, where `created_at` is the
CLAMPED #356-F4 stamp READ BACK from the store (the write-clamp already bounds
clock-ahead skew at ≤ the creating binary's bundle tail, so the birthday can
never postdate a deposit — the §3.2f money argument unchanged, no live tip
consulted). The eager fresh arm omits the lazy path's `tip − lag` min term
because there is no tip offline — and `estimate_birthday(clamped stamp)` alone
is already ≤ any deposit height for a freshly-minted seed. **Lazy (unchanged)
otherwise:** a configured birthday ABOVE the bundle tail stays lazy EVEN for
a fresh create, so the `BirthdayInFuture` tip clamp — the config-typo guard,
which NEEDS a live tip (compared against `max(tip, newest bundled row)` since
T0-1c-R2) — still fires at first sync; a restore with NO
configured birthday keeps the first-sync activation full scan; a stampless
fresh remnant (pre-F4) stays lazy too.

**FR-24 FRESH-FLAG slice (S213 #359 — the T2 fresh flow; crypto-change review):**
`SeedSource::FreshRawBytes` (constructor `raw_bytes_fresh`, §2.2 — the same
32..=252 door and no-mnemonic contract as `RawBytes`) marks host-supplied raw
bytes as FRESHLY GENERATED, and `is_freshly_generated` (`Generate` ∨
`FreshRawBytes`) is now THE predicate keying every freshly-generated create
behavior: (1) the #356-F4 creation-stamp write, (2) the no-configured-birthday
eager arm (b) above, (3) the create-failing loud posture on an eager-import
error, and (4) the handle's in-session `freshly_generated` (the stamp-less
belt arm at the lazy resolver). REPAIR MODE stays keyed on `Generate` ALONE:
a `FreshRawBytes` remnant repairs as `VerifySupplied` (SealedKeychain — the
re-supplied bytes are verified against the sealed remnant, mistype ⇒
`SeedMismatch`) or `NoSeed` (None-persistence), NEVER `ResumeSealed` — only a
Generate create mints entropy the caller cannot re-supply. FFI:
`createWalletWithHostSeed(config, freshlyGenerated)` (default **false** =
today's restore shape — existing hosts change nothing). **THE LYING-HOST
CONTRACT (LOUD, on every surface of the flag):** the flag is an ATTESTATION
that the seed was minted immediately before the call and has NEVER existed
anywhere else. Marking a seed with prior chain history fresh makes
pre-stamp funds INVISIBLE (birthday floored at the stamp, and the stamp
survives rescan — `rescan(None)` re-floors AT the stamp) AND suppresses the
§3.2h #387 restore-pessimistic refund-index sweep — the silent-fund-loss
shape this SDK exists to prevent. Recovery for a mis-attested T2 wallet is
`rescanFrom` with an EXPLICIT lower height through the registered seed port
(FR-43, S2: the re-import pulls the seed at the NEXT sync, behind the #357
fingerprint — the host must have it staged for that sync; a `None` height
re-floors at the stamp and does not help), or wipe + re-create with
`freshlyGenerated: false` (a portless None-persistence wallet's `rescan` is
still typed `SeedRequired`; the host holds the seed, so re-create is
cheap). When in doubt, pass false: the only cost is the lazy activation
full scan. SECURITY WIN closing the flag's loop: with the eager import done
INSIDE create, the host may clear its staged seed the moment
`createWalletWithHostSeed` returns — the create→first-sync staging window
the `WalletSeedPort` contract warns against never opens on the fresh path.

Consequences: `current_address` serves the DB-account UA offline from second
zero for T0/T1 and — with the fresh flag or a configured-≤-tail birthday —
for T2 (the held-seed offline-derivation fallback was already covering
T0/T1). `run_engine_pass`'s lazy gate no-ops via `account_exists` (**superseded
2026-09-06:** the CS-M1 network-match used to run directly only *until the first
block scanned* — a once-per-life check, which is why a wallet provisioned before
a network upgrade never noticed it. It is now `evaluate_consensus`, on EVERY
pass; see `ironwood-nu63-support.md` §3.1); the F4
deposit-before-first-sync scenario is structural (birthday pinned at create);
IntoZec quoting un-gates on a never-synced wallet (FR-22's resolved arm). The
eager import is IDEMPOTENT (`ensure_account`) and its failure is
CREATE-FAILING for a freshly-generated create (`Generate` or
`FreshRawBytes` — a wallet that cannot import its own account at create is
mis-provisioned — fail loud, not lazily-degraded; degrading would only defer
the same corrupt-bundle fault to first sync where attribution is worse) but
LAZY-DEGRADING for the restore arm (the configured birthday survives to the
first-sync resolver unchanged). CS-M2: a FAILED fresh eager create can
still leave a COMPLETED store behind (the marker lands before the import) —
`open()` / `openWalletWithHostSeed` is the recovery verb (the account then
imports lazily from the held sealed seed / the attached port); never
re-`create`, which is typed `WalletAlreadyExists`.

**Named tests (§8).** `bundled_treestate_picks_newest_row_below_birthday`
(selection + the never-above-requested money property) ·
`bundled_treestate_floors_to_activation` (the floor edge) ·
`treestate_bundle_every_row_decodes` (every bundled row → a valid
`AccountBirthday`, no runtime decode surprise) · `treestate_bundle_matches_pinned_provenance_hash`
(the M2 integrity gate over the tree-state slice — any `data.rs` frontier change
fails CI) · `treestate_and_time_slices_are_row_aligned` (one source of truth) ·
`provision_rejects_network_mismatched_endpoint` (the `get_lightd_info` guard) ·
`provision_resolves_birthday_and_imports_account` (end-to-end over a fake gRPC
client + in-memory DB — birthday from the bundle, account imported, UA byte-equals
the offline derivation) · `provision_never_provisions_from_a_live_frontier` (the
trust-model guard: a fake client whose `get_tree_state` returns a poisoned
frontier is NEVER consulted for the birthday — provisioning is byte-identical
with or without it). All offline — NO real network.

### 3.2g The scan loop + controller — increment plan (W3-inc-2c-iv-d, DESIGN)

The last unbuilt piece of the first fund-detecting wallet: OUR orchestration loop
over the consumed-WHOLE `zcash_client_backend` scan primitives, consuming the
iv-a download stream + the iv-b cache + the iv-c birthday. It mirrors
`zcash_client_backend::sync::run` (the ECC SDK foundation Zashi/Zodl build on; the
alignment audit 2026-06-14). It is the largest increment in inc-2c, so it is
decomposed dependency-ordered, each a reviewed unit (the inc-2c-ii…iv discipline):

- **inc-2c-iv-d-1 — the `get_subtree_roots` seam + `update_subtree_roots`
  (⚠️ REQUIRED FOR SPENDING; the streaming-transport HIGH item). ✅ AS BUILT
  (W3-inc-2c-iv-d-1).** The mechanical sibling of iv-a's `get_block_range`: one
  STREAMING RPC on the same `LightwalletdClient`, same connector over the host
  `NetDialer`, same per-message idle timeout + SPENT-ON-ERROR latch +
  cancel-safety. Reuse (Rule Zero) ECC's `CompactTxStreamerClient::get_subtree_roots`
  + the `GetSubtreeRootsArg` / `SubtreeRoot` / `ShieldedProtocol` (proto i32) types,
  whole. **Shape (built):** `get_subtree_roots(protocol, start_index, max_entries)
  -> Result<SubtreeRootStream, GrpcError>` on `LightwalletdClient`;
  `SubtreeRootStream` is a `pub(crate)` handle holding the upstream
  `tonic::Streaming<SubtreeRoot>` (never leaked, ADR-0005 r5), `next_root()`.
  **DRY (done):** the pump (idle timeout + spent-on-error latch + the three
  consumer contracts) was generalized — `net/grpc.rs`'s `CompactBlockSource`/
  `BlockStream` became a generic `MessageStream<T>` over a `MessageSource<T>`
  (blanket-impl over `tonic::Streaming<T>`; the 12 iv-a tests passed UNCHANGED,
  locking the behavior), then `BlockStream = MessageStream<CompactBlock>`,
  `SubtreeRootStream = MessageStream<SubtreeRoot>`. NO money/crypto logic — pure
  transport. **Conversion + wiring (`sync.rs`, NEW):** `parse_{sapling,orchard}_root`
  decode each hostile `SubtreeRoot.root_hash` via the leaf type's canonical
  `from_bytes([u8;32]) -> CtOption` (a non-32-byte / non-canonical / >u32-height
  root is a typed reject, never a panic — byte-identical decode to the reference's
  `HashSer::read`); `fetch_subtree_roots` collects BOTH pools before ANY write (a
  fault writes NOTHING — the money-safe property); `put_subtree_roots` writes via
  `WalletCommitmentTrees::put_{sapling,orchard}_subtree_roots(0, &[CommitmentTreeRoot])`
  (the `sync::run` conversion, `sync.rs:243-282`). **Since S15-F1 (ADR-0569) the
  fetch and the put take a per-pool START:** `SubtreeRootSource::subtree_roots
  (protocol, start_index)` sends it as `GetSubtreeRootsArg.start_index`
  (`max_entries` stays 0); `sync::plan_pool_fetch` chooses it — 0 (a full fetch)
  until the pool is verified in this session, else `count − 1` (the stored run,
  `root_bind::read_stored_run`: height AND root hash) lowered for the reorg window,
  a bracket or a newly scanned completing block, rounded DOWN to a multiple of
  `SUBTREE_ROOTS_START_GRANULARITY` = 64; and `put_*_subtree_roots(start, served)`
  writes the suffix in place. A refused or mis-served non-zero start is retried
  from 0 in the same pass; an IGNORED one (the server serves from 0 anyway) is
  re-classified as the full fetch — one stream, judged exactly as one — not
  retried; a timeout, at the open or mid-drain, is not retried either: it fails
  the pass and turns the pool's incremental fetch off (ADR-0570), as do two
  dropped non-zero starts in a row whose retry from 0 was served (seven
  `wallet.sync` `outcome` codes); the bind
  runs over the virtual sequence `recorded[..start] ++ served`
  (`root_bind::check_pool_from`) after a re-check of the plan's snapshot, under
  the same lock as the write; `PoolFetch::Served` carries the ABSOLUTE count.
  Driven by `Wallet::
  update_subtree_roots` (network fetch lock-free, the DB write one short locked
  blocking section — S20). Reached via the `SubtreeRootSource` testability seam
  (mirrors provision's `ChainOracle` — fully testable with NO gRPC server).
  **Hardening folds (security+crypto+arch review):** a hostile-COUNT cap
  `MAX_SUBTREE_ROOTS_PER_POOL = 2^(32−16) = 65 536` (a flooding endpoint → typed
  `Sync`, never an unbounded-Vec OOM); honest `ShardTreeError` attribution
  (`Insert`/server-root conflict → `Sync`, `Storage`/`Query` → `StoreCorrupt`); a
  `cargo-fuzz` target (`fuzz_subtree_root`) + a proptest over the parsers. This is
  the trust-anchor for SPEND witnesses — a server lying with well-formed-but-WRONG
  roots is caught at SCAN time as a shardtree `Conflict` on a COMPLETED shard (the
  iv-c audit), so it underpins spend-correctness, not detection.
  **BIND-1 (S269, `production-readiness-phase-1.md` §4x) corrected what that
  detection then SAID.** The scan-time `Conflict` arrived as
  `SqliteClientError::PutBlocksCommitmentTree` and was folded to `StoreCorrupt` —
  the endpoint's lie, rendered on an intact wallet as "restore from your recovery
  phrase", from a condition one hostile server can produce at will — while the
  INGEST door already called the identical class the endpoint's. The two doors now
  run ONE body (`sync::map_shardtree_err`; the private `classify_shard_fault` is
  gone), so a served root the tree refuses is `Sync { EndpointMisbehaving }`
  whichever door catches it, and the residual note below about the rewind
  `truncate_to_height` folding to `StoreCorrupt` is unchanged.
  **The completion HEIGHT is the other half of a served root, and until BIND-1
  nothing bound it above the newest bundled treestate row.** `subtree_end_height`
  is written only by `put_shard_roots` — the shardtree's own scan write-back omits
  the column — so the endpoint is its sole writer, in all three pools, and a
  lowered height shrinks the shard's block window until `mark_stabilized_notes`
  latches `witness_stabilized = 1` on notes whose witness can never be built
  (INC-020's measured false-spendable half). The A11 ingest bind (`root_bind`)
  holds a SERVED sequence to the bundled frontiers, the wallet's own scanned
  counts, the recorded row and the completing block hash; above the newest bundled
  row those reach only an index that already carries a record. **BIND-1 adds the
  oracle that arrives LATER:** `root_bind::reconcile_scanned_boundaries`, from
  `sync::scan_batch`'s `Ok` arm, holds the RECORDED row to the per-block
  commitment-tree sizes this wallet counted in the batch just committed — the same
  two-sided count rule the ingest bind applies, against the wallet's own numbers.
  A refuted row is CORRECTED (to the height the scan counted the boundary at, or
  WITHDRAWN where withdrawing it is safe — see BIND-1-R below) and the
  stabilization latch it licensed is UNDONE for both shards whose window that one
  number defined — the SDK's only writer of a `0` into `witness_stabilized`, which
  upstream has no way to clear. Disposition, as at ingest: Sapling/Orchard
  pass-fatal (`EndpointMisbehaving`), Ironwood degraded and REPORTED through the
  pass's `root_outcomes` (never only a log line — an event emitted inside the
  blocking scan resolves a worker thread's dispatcher). Gated on the rewind
  ledger for the BLAME only: with a rewind outstanding the row is still corrected
  and the endpoint is not badged, which also gives the raised-boundary residual an
  exit other than a rescan. **Where it does not reach:** an ABSENCE of commitments
  refutes nothing unless the wallet has counted at least one for that pool in the
  batch — an empty tree is indistinguishable from a stream carrying nothing for the
  pool, and reading a zero as evidence refuted every truthful record too (measured:
  1545/29 against a 2-failure baseline, on the scripted chains that declare three
  zeros per block). That is the region the signed bundle already binds offline, so
  the two oracles divide the chain at the newest bundled row rather than overlap.
  **The residual, stated:** a lie is bound at ingest only up to the newest bundled
  row, and above it BIND-1 makes an accepted lie a WINDOW rather than a permanent
  state — one that closes when the wallet's scan reaches the blocks that decide it,
  and stays open meanwhile.

  **BIND-1-R (S269, §4x-R) — the REFUTATION is what is durable, and a withdrawal
  never opens a gap.** The first build of the reconcile made the CORRECTION durable
  and the refutation ephemeral, which is backwards on both counts.

  - **The gap, and it was the CRITICAL.** `truncate_tree_to_subtree_roots`
    (`zcash_client_sqlite-0.22.0 wallet/commitment_tree.rs:730-793`) collects
    survivors ordered by shard index, BREAKS at the first index gap, then
    unconditionally deletes `{prefix}_tree_shards` AND `{prefix}_tree_cap` and
    re-puts only what it collected — with `put_shard_roots` returning early on an
    empty slice. **A withdrawal is now always a whole SUFFIX rather than one row**, at
    any starting index, so the recorded heights stay the dense prefix truncation reads
    correctly and no withdrawal of ours can drop a shard whose own height is fine
    (`root_bind::plan_withdrawal`). Density is the property; the count is not.
    **The CAP invariant is GUARDED, not argued.** Emptying a pool's whole prefix
    leaves `truncate_tree_to_subtree_roots` nothing to re-put, so the
    `DELETE FROM {prefix}_tree_cap` before it stands. Two arguments were made in turn
    that this could not matter and both were wrong: *"index 0 is never withdrawn"* —
    true, and it left the refuted number ACTIVE in `mark_stabilized_notes` and
    `v_{prefix}_shard_scan_ranges`, where refusing later re-serves does not undo a lie
    already written; then *"`ResetToSubtreeRoots` cannot fire, because `update_tree`
    checkpoints the batch anchor unconditionally"* — which covers checkpoint CREATION
    and says nothing about SURVIVAL, since `prune_excess_checkpoints` keeps at most
    `max_checkpoints = PRUNING_DEPTH = 100` (`shardtree-0.7.1 lib.rs:644`) and
    upstream's own doc for the qualifying predicate names the post-migration-rescan
    geometry as reachable. So `root_bind::withdraw_suffix` refuses to leave the prefix
    empty while any `root_hash` row exists: a withdrawal from index 0 on a populated
    tree is CLAMPED to index 1 — still a suffix, still ungapped — and the guard holds
    whatever upstream does with checkpoints. **What that costs, at index 0 only:** the
    refuted number stays in the shard-0 row, so that shard's block window keeps it
    until an honest serve overwrites it. The bracket refuses every re-serve outside it
    and the un-latch is re-applied from the ledger on every batch, so the
    false-spendable half is answered; the window is not.
  - **The bracket ledger** (`subtree_boundary_bound`, `AUX_TABLES_PRESERVED`, rows
    cleared by the rescan rebuild — the `sync_stamp` posture). For each pool and
    shard index it holds the two blocks between which this wallet's own counts prove
    that subtree completed: a FLOOR (the highest block at which it was still
    incomplete) and a CEILING (the lowest at which it was already complete), so the
    true boundary lies in `(floor, ceiling]`. At the next pass's ingest
    `root_bind::check_refuted_heights` refuses any completion height OUTSIDE that
    interval (`refuted_height`) — so a re-served wrong height is refused where it
    used to be re-accepted, and so is every height in the window on that side of it,
    which a refuted-VALUE list would not have closed. **Both ends are load-bearing:**
    a floor-only ledger — the first build of this repair — is INERT wherever the
    record is too HIGH, because then no observation in the run shows the subtree
    incomplete and there is nothing to mint a floor from; measured at the S269 join
    on a run declaring `2^16+1` leaves at every block. Because each end refuses only
    OUTWARD, the HONEST height inside the bracket is still accepted and written,
    which is the property that keeps the repair from being a deadlock. A row the
    bracket refutes stops equality-binding its index (the row is known wrong); the
    bracket is withdrawn by the next accepted write that covered that index, is
    DROPPED outright by any later batch whose own counts close it to nothing (the
    anti-deadlock sweep), and abstains for the one pass a rewind buys — the same gate
    the three other memory oracles carry.
  - **Nothing is written that the signed bundle refutes.** The reconcile now takes
    the `Network`: a computed truth or a floor the bundled treestates contradict is
    dropped whole, because both derive from a chain of counts rooted at an
    endpoint-supplied anchor. **And that anchor is checked**: where this wallet has
    its own `blocks.{prefix}_commitment_tree_size` at the anchor height and the two
    disagree, the reconcile abstains for that pool on that batch rather than refute
    anything from counts built on a contradicted number. The bundle veto covers the
    CEILING as well as the floor and the computed truth, and that is the clause that
    matters most — the ceiling is the end that refuses an honest server for serving
    too HIGH, so a wrong one is the deadlock R3 forbids.
  - **One transaction per pool's correction set**, and a fault on one pool no longer
    silences the others: the loop runs Sapling → Orchard → Ironwood and carries the
    first fault to the end instead of `?`-propagating it, so a transient fault on
    Sapling can no longer skip the pool this item exists for.
  - **NO busy retry on this seam, and its ABSENCE is the repair** (`sync.rs`, the
    `NO BUSY RETRY HERE` block carries the argument). `with_aux_busy_retry`'s
    soundness contract wants ONE immediate transaction; this closure is reads →
    COMMIT → a further read, so a busy on that last read re-runs the body, finds
    the correction already applied, and returns "nothing to report" — a DETECTED
    endpoint lie silently becoming undetected, with no badge and no pass-fatal
    disposition for the required pools. A busy now fails the batch honestly
    instead. **An earlier draft of this bullet said the opposite**: the retry was
    removed later in the same fold and this sentence was not updated with it,
    which is the drift code reviewer caught at the last gate.
  - **OWED and NOT closed:** the reconcile still has no watermark, so a batch missed
    by a kill between `put_blocks`' commit and the reconcile is never re-examined
    (§4x-R R8).

- **inc-2c-iv-d-2 — the scan loop (download → cache → scan, non-linear). ✅ AS BUILT.**
  Decomposed into **2b-i (the per-batch primitive — ✅ AS BUILT)** and **2b-ii (the
  driver loop — ✅ AS BUILT)**; the db-lock split it depends on is **iv-d-2a (✅ AS BUILT)**.
  The `LightdSyncEngine` drives, per the reference-`run` order: `update_subtree_roots`
  (d-1) → `update_chain_tip(tip)` (via the built `get_latest_block`) →
  `suggest_scan_ranges` → for each `ScanRange [s, e)` in Spend-before-Sync order
  (§1.7): fetch `from_state = get_tree_state(s − 1)` (the per-range chain state —
  NOT the birthday; the live `get_tree_state` seam's real consumer, where a
  per-range poisoned frontier surfaces as a shardtree `Conflict` on completion,
  unlike the un-anchorable birthday — §3.2f), GUARD `from_height == from_state
  .block_height + 1` BEFORE calling `scan_cached_blocks` (it `assert_eq!`-PANICS
  otherwise — chain.rs:600), download via the iv-a `BlockStream` → `insert` into
  the iv-b cache WHILE `headroom()` remains (the `CACHE_MAX_BYTES` batching loop)
  → `scan_cached_blocks(params, &cache, &mut db, s, &from_state, e − s)` →
  `cache.delete(s, e)`. **Range conventions (§3.2c iv-d, get the glue exactly
  right):** download is INCLUSIVE `get_block_range(s, e − 1)`; scan `from_height =
  s`, `limit = e − s`; cache `delete(s, e)` HALF-OPEN. **Reorg (as built since
  §4q REQ-1 and §4q-R REQ-1-R, INC-025):** a `scan_cached_blocks` continuity
  error (`is_continuity_error()` — prev-hash / height / tree-size mismatch) → the
  DB's `block_max_scanned` is read (the pre-rewind frontier) →
  `db.truncate_to_height(target)` with `target = err.at_height −
  REWIND_DISTANCE_BLOCKS`, which LANDS on the highest checkpointed height ≤ the
  target (`landed`, its return value — a batch end, so the two differ whenever no
  batch ended at the target) → **when `recorded_tip > landed`**
  `sync::record_chain_tip(db, tip)` under the SAME lock (the pass-head tip,
  threaded into `scan_batch` as `recorded_tip`): upstream's truncate only TRIMS
  the scan queue to `landed` and re-queues nothing, so this is what re-queues
  `landed+1..=tip` and lets THIS pass re-scan across the fork; when
  `recorded_tip <= landed` (the endpoint is behind our own scan, or a range a
  cancelled pass left queued above the tip forked) upstream's `update_chain_tip`
  would early-return, so the call is skipped and the outcome says so →
  `ScanOutcome::Reorg { rewind_height: landed, requeued, rewound_blocks }` →
  `cache.truncate(landed)` (never the target — the cache must hold no block the
  DB does not; the one named exception is a re-queue that faults after the
  truncate committed, which fails the pass before the cache truncate and is inert
  because the scanner is only ever fed the range a batch has just downloaded) →
  re-`suggest_scan_ranges`. The pass ends "up to date" only after the exit READS
  `block_max_scanned` under the lock: at or above the recorded tip the pass is
  `Ok` (the ordinary end, and the under-claim — an endpoint behind our scan,
  where `pass.tip` names what it claimed and the DB holds more); below it the
  pass is the fail-closed belt — `Sync { ChainReorg }` + a `wallet.sync` event
  whose `outcome` is `rewind_left_queue_empty` (the last action was a rewind that
  skipped its re-queue) or `queue_empty_below_tip` (any other way there: a
  re-queue that queued nothing, rewind → advance → empty queue, no rewind at
  all) — never a stamp. The belt is REACHABLE, not a formality: the REQ-1 fold
  review reached it with a leftover range above the recorded tip (now the
  under-claim). One pass's rewinds are bounded twice — `reorg_storm` (rewinds
  since the last new high-water, a termination bound the endpoint's tip sizes)
  and the absolute `MAX_TOTAL_REORGS_PER_PASS` on `pass.reorgs` (the work bound a
  fork-advance-fork server cannot move) — and `wallet.reorg_rewind`'s `depth` is
  `SyncPass::rewound_blocks`, the pre-rewind frontier minus `landed` summed over
  the pass's rewinds, never `reorgs × REWIND_DISTANCE_BLOCKS`. The cap's BYTE
  ceiling is stated at the constant (§4u RW-6): a rewind makes the pass download
  twice — the batch that forked and the span the truncate un-scanned, under
  `REWIND_DISTANCE_BLOCKS + SYNC_BATCH_BLOCKS` blocks for a fork met in the batch
  above the frontier (the rewind target, then the nearest checkpointed row). What
  bounds the re-downloaded span is the SPAN, not a batch count: the re-queue puts
  a `Verify` range first and a `ChainTip` range after, so the span arrives as three
  ranges or more, and `DOWNLOAD_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` is a per-BATCH allowance that a
  finer split raises rather than lowers. For a span of `S` blocks in any number of
  batches the cost is `Σ min(b_i × GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES,
  DOWNLOAD_BATCH_MAX_BYTES)`, and a CEILING is the supremum over splits: the
  per-batch allowance binds only for `b_i > 16`, so any split into ≤16-block
  batches reaches `S × GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` and none exceeds it — 110 × 8 MiB
  = 880 MiB. The forked batch is one batch, but the cap is checked AFTER a block
  joins the tally, so the block that trips it has already crossed the wire: 128 +
  8 = 136 MiB. That is **1,016 MiB per rewind and `MAX_TOTAL_REORGS_PER_PASS` ×
  that = 29.77 GiB** above the forward span (still not a wire bound —
  `encoded_len()` excludes gRPC framing) (`CACHE_MAX_BYTES` is residency, not
  download; a fork met in a range scanned UNDER the frontier is bounded in count,
  not depth — `depth` measures it). The 11.25 GiB this paragraph used to state
  came from a wrong "at most two batches" step and was 2.6× too small (§4u-run
  review row 5). Across passes the cap bounds nothing: the
  controller's ladder and rewinding streak do (iv-d-3-a below). Before §4q the
  pass ended at the rewound batch, published `UpToDate { tip }` and stamped the
  full tip while the wallet sat below it (INC-025). The reference's `sync.rs:404`
  rewind-on-continuity pattern is the shape; the in-pass re-queue, the DB-read
  exit and the cap are ours.
  Cooperative cancellation (the app backgrounds mid-scan) + checkpoint/resume
  (≤ one batch lost on kill, §7 — the cache is disposable, scan progress lives in
  the wallet DB). `TransactionDataRequests` tx-enhancement (memos) rides here or
  d-3. **Lock budget (S20 mobile):** scan over SHORT per-batch critical sections —
  NEVER hold the `db` lock (iv-d-2a) across a `scan_cached_blocks` iteration
  (seconds–minutes) or every UI read parks; batch by `SYNC_BATCH_BLOCKS` and release
  between batches.

  - **2b-i — the per-batch scan primitive (✅ AS BUILT, W3-inc-2c-iv-d-2b-i).** OUR
    orchestration over the consumed-WHOLE scan primitives, factored as the iv-d-1
    "fetch (async, no lock) + apply (sync, under the db lock)" pair — the unit where
    the money-critical correctness lives. In `sync.rs`: a `ScanClient` seam

    `ChainOracle`; testable via `FakeScanClient`, NO gRPC server); `fetch_chain_state`
    (async — `get_tree_state(s−1).to_chain_state()`, a decode failure → typed
    `endpoint_unusable`, never a panic); `download_range` (async — streams the iv-a

    short/gapped/duplicate/out-of-order/overlong span is a typed `Sync`, never
    silently accepted (§3.2g) — PLUS a **byte cap** `DOWNLOAD_BATCH_MAX_BYTES`

    after the truncate + the `update_chain_tip(recorded_tip)` re-queue under the
    same lock (§4q P-R1/P-R2), leaving the caller to truncate the cache; honest

    genesis saturation, `map_scan_err` passthrough. **e2e obligation (GA-BLOCKING,

  - **2b-ii — the driver loop (✅ AS BUILT, W3-inc-2c-iv-d-2b-ii).** `Wallet::sync_once`

    (via `fetch_tip` over the new `ScanClient::latest_block_height`) → loop {

    _error`) is NOT producible with hand-built blocks — EMPIRICALLY confirmed across

    while the loop's REACTION (`classify_batch`) is fully unit-tested.

- **inc-2c-iv-d-3 — the controller + the live read surface.** Split into d-3-a
  (the orchestration core — ✅ BUILT) and d-3-b (the engine adapter + FRB streams),
  d-3-b itself split into d-3-b-i (the scan-path cancel + progress contract — ✅
  BUILT) and d-3-b-ii (the real engine adapter + FRB streams + the Tor refinement).

  - **iv-d-3-a — the `SyncController` orchestration core (✅ BUILT).**
    `SyncController` (`start`/`stop`/`once`/`subscribe`) over the
    **`SyncEnginePort`** (the Tachyon seam, §3.2 — crate-internal `pub(crate)`, a clean trait the
    controller depends on, never a concrete engine). Policy: infinite retry with
    capped exponential backoff (`SYNC_BACKOFF_INITIAL_SECS` → `SYNC_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS`,
    `defaultRetries = ∞` — the Zashi "manually restart" bug, §6.2) — **the ladder
    resets on a CLEAN pass only** (§4u REW-1, the REQ-1-R fold review's row 1): an
    `Ok` pass that rewound climbs it like a fault and sleeps `max(POLL_INTERVAL_SECS,
    backoff)`, never faster than a clean poll, so a patient forking endpoint cannot
    buy a fresh per-pass rewind budget at the 1 s rung every 20 s; **the rewinding
    streak** — `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_REWINDING_PASSES` consecutive loop passes that each
    rewound (`Ok` with rewinds, or a `ChainReorg` stall), DECAYED by one per clean
    loop pass (the REW-1 fold review's row 1, founder S269: never cleared in one)
    and moved by nothing else (a cancelled pass or a non-rewind fault leaves it
    standing) — publishes `Stalled { EndpointMisbehaving }` in place of the pass's
    terminal status from the threshold pass until enough clean passes have decayed
    it below the threshold (the stamp still written when the pass earned it — a
    fact about the DB under a judgement about the server). **Where it RANKS
    (phase-2 P2-6, founder S272 decision 5):** below `UpToDateLimited` and below
    `UpToDateUnverified` (running or ended — the grace's countdown and
    `Ended { by: Clock }`'s device-clock remedy are never hidden by "switch
    servers"), above `EndpointBehind`, `UpToDateDegraded` and `UpToDate`; the
    report line still logs under a higher claim. **What the grace CARRIES
    when it wins (phase-3 P3-12, founder S278, Q2 option 2):**
    `UpToDateUnverified { streak_reported: true }` — the same claim, telling
    the host that the streak it outranked has reached the report, so the
    host drops "your balance is current" and names the rewinds (the
    `walletSyncExplainUnverifiedStreak` body); the countdown and the next
    step are unchanged. **Where it lives (phase-2
    P2-5):** in the controller's shared state (`Shared::rewinding_streak`, one
    writer — the loop), born zero with the controller so a relaunch forgives it
    with the ladder — **and NOT zeroed by a loop start (phase-2 P2-6, decision
    6):** a `stop()`/`start()` restarts the ladder only, so the host's reconnect
    kick (which answers every `Stalled` with that pair) and "Try now" no longer
    hand the endpoint a fresh budget; only clean loop passes decay it. `once()`
    — a pull-to-refresh — READS it and neither raises nor decays it, so its
    verdict carries the loop's standing judgement and cannot take a reported
    "switch servers" down (a `once()` between `stop()` and `start()` publishes
    the last loop's count, by design);
    the `wallet.sync` pass event carries `backoff_secs` = the sleep the loop takes
    next on every loop-driven pass, and the report is the `outcome =
    "rewinding_streak"` warn; the no-progress
    stuck-sync watchdog (`SYNC_STUCK_WATCHDOG_SECS`, re-armed by each intra-pass
    progress report so a slow-but-advancing first sync is never restarted); the
    single-writer pass guard (`once()` never overlaps the loop); cooperative `stop`
    + `Drop` teardown; the live `SyncStatus` watch stream (latest-wins, §3.3). **The
    first sync-engine tracing site** (`wallet.sync {batches, reorgs, outcome,
    backoff_secs}` + `wallet.reorg_rewind {depth}`, `target: "zec_wallet_core"`) + the
    **span-aware** §5.4 capture-layer guard `tracing_spans_carry_no_address_amount
    _or_memo`. `CancelToken` gained an async `cancelled().await` (additive; the
    polling `is_cancelled()` between-batches contract is unchanged). Tested (13
    deterministic tests over a fake engine on the virtual clock — NO network, NO
    wall-clock): once→UpToDate; live Scanning; transient-fault recovery + backoff;
    retry-forever-until-success; watchdog restart of a wedged pass; persistently-
    wedged → honest `Stalled`; prompt + idempotent stop; clean restart after stop;
    double-start idempotency; `next_backoff`/`stall_for`/`stall_code` boundary; the
    capture-layer guard. **THE LOAD-BEARING CONTRACT (review, all three reviewers):
    the watchdog cancels COOPERATIVELY** (it flips the `CancelToken`; the pass honors
    it only where it checks). So d-3-b's engine adapter MUST, as a named contract on
    `SyncEnginePort::run_pass`: (1) timeout-bound every per-batch network I/O (≤ the
    watchdog window) + check cancel frequently so `stop()`/watchdog are prompt (else
    a pass wedged inside an un-timed read is un-recoverable AND `stop()` hangs); (2)
    report progress INTRA-batch so a slow batch can't trip a false stuck-restart;
    (3) lose at most in-flight re-downloadable work on cancel. A named d-3-b test
    must cover a batch blocking past the watchdog window.

0.23.0, so the build hits no surprise):**
- `WalletWrite::suggest_scan_ranges() -> Result<Vec<ScanRange>, _>` (data_api.rs:1806);
  `ScanRange::block_range() -> &Range<BlockHeight>` is **HALF-OPEN `[s, e)`** (scanning.rs:62),
  `.priority()` for Spend-before-Sync ordering. `WalletWrite::update_chain_tip(tip)`
  (data_api.rs:3167). `WalletWrite::truncate_to_height(h) -> Result<BlockHeight, _>`
  (data_api.rs:3233).
- `scan_cached_blocks(params, &cache, &mut db, from_height, &from_state, limit)
  -> Result<ScanSummary, _>` (chain.rs:586). **`assert_eq!(from_height,
  from_state.block_height + 1)` at chain.rs:600 is ALWAYS compiled** — GUARD
  `from_height == from_state.block_height + 1` BEFORE the call (fetch `from_state =
  get_tree_state(s − 1).to_chain_state()`; a one-off here is an FFI-crashing panic).
  Range glue for one `ScanRange [s, e)`: download INCLUSIVE `get_block_range(s, e−1)`;
  scan `from_height = s`, `limit = e − s`; cache `delete(s, e)` half-open.
- **Reorg = the verified reference path (sync.rs:404-427):** `Err(ChainError::Scan(err))
  if err.is_continuity_error()` (scanning.rs:517) ⇒ `rewind = err.at_height()
  .saturating_sub(REWIND_DISTANCE_BLOCKS)` [=10, matches the reference's literal 10] ⇒
  `db.truncate_to_height(rewind)` + `cache.truncate(rewind)` ⇒ re-`suggest_scan_ranges`.

**iv-d-2 OBLIGATIONS folded from the iv-d-1 operational 3-lens (S30) — do NOT lose:**
- **The db-lock SPLIT (✅ AS BUILT, iv-d-2a).** Both `scan_cached_blocks`
  (seconds–minutes) AND the d-1 `put_subtree_roots` (linear in root count, ~tens-to-
  hundreds of ms at mainnet scale) held the single `Inner.state` lock far past the S20
  ~20 ms budget ⇒ every concurrent UI read parked. **Done:** `Inner`'s single
  `Mutex<OpenWallet>` was split — the immutable-after-open UI-read fields
  (`network`/`persistence`/`status`/`seed`) became bare **lock-free** `Inner` fields
  (the optimal form of "split `db` from the UI-read fields" — genuinely immutable state
  needs no lock), and the mutable `db`+`db_key` moved behind their own `Mutex<WalletDb>`.
  A scan holding the db lock can no longer park a `network`/`status`/seed-derivation
  read; `current_address`'s brief DB SELECT still contends but interleaves with the
  scan's per-batch holds. Drop order preserved (`db` before `lock`). The deliverable is
  the **structural decoupling test** `db_lock_split_ui_reads_are_decoupled_from_the_held_db_lock`
  (deterministic, channel-synchronized — wall-clock timing tests violate testing-patterns
  §1; it compiles ONLY if those fields stay lock-free). The **per-batch lock-release
  assertion** (✅ DONE in iv-d-2b-ii: `sync_once_releases_the_db_lock_between_batches` —
  a one-shot download gate + `join!` `try_lock` proves the loop drops the db lock across
  the async fetch/download between batches). Put-CHUNKING (the linear `put_subtree_roots`
  hold) remains owed where mainnet-scale root counts matter (harmless today).
- **Witness-path error attribution (inc-2d, flag in d-2):** a witness-build
  `QueryError::TreeIncomplete` or an honest-re-put `Insert` conflict must render a
  DISTINCT "local commitment tree inconsistent — re-scan/repair required" state — do
  NOT reuse `sync::map_shardtree_err`'s `Query→StoreCorrupt` / `Insert→Sync` on the
  witness path (those are the PUT-path mappings).
- **Pre-birthday root cross-check (d-2 hardening, money-MINOR S30):** a wrong
  pre-birthday subtree root is outside the scan-conflict defense; cheaply cross-check
  ingested pre-birthday roots against the birthday treestate frontier ommers where
  indices coincide, rejecting an ingestion that disagrees with the frontier the
  account was imported against.
- **Stream COMPLETENESS (✅ DONE in 2b-i):** a clean-but-SHORT `Ok(None)` from
  `BlockStream` is rejected by `download_range`'s span check (typed `Sync`, never a
  silent gap). NEW in 2b-ii: a malformed-SHAPE block (non-32-byte hash/txid/cmu) is
  also rejected at download — it would PANIC the consumed-whole scanner (an FFI crash).
- **Tests owed (carry to d-3 / inc-2d):** `reput_from_zero_preserves_scanned_shard_data`
  (needs a scanned shard — confirms re-put doesn't churn scan-built witness data) — the
  per-batch lock-release test landed in 2b-ii.

### 3.2h The send pipeline — increment plan (W3-inc-2d; inc-2d-1 PROPOSE BUILT)

The keystone increment: the wallet learns to SPEND. The full design already
lives across §1.7 (Spend-before-Sync), §2.4 (the `PaymentRequest` intent funnel —
BUILT), §2.5 (`TxStatus`/`BatchId`/`TxSubmitResult` DTOs — BUILT), §4.2
(spending-key lifecycle), §4.4 (swap deposit sends), §5.3 (broadcast jitter),
§6.1 (error taxonomy), §6.2 (offline intent persistence), §6.3 (crash-atomic
intent↔tx). This section is the BUILD decomposition + the decisions that were
still open, so a fresh session implements without re-deriving them. The
upstream wiring below is **verified against the pinned `zcash_client_backend`/
`zcash_client_sqlite =0.23.0/=0.21.0`** (2026-06-18).

**Decomposition (decoupled along the deterministic↔key↔network seams — the iv-d rhythm):**

These are INTERNAL build slices behind the already-frozen public surface (§3.1):
`propose(PaymentRequest) -> SendProposal` (2d-1) and `send(SendProposal) ->
Vec<TxSubmitResult>` (= 2d-2 create+sign THEN 2d-3 broadcast, the public `send` does
both); `queue_send`/the outbox land with 2d-3. The public names do NOT change.

- **inc-2d-1 — PROPOSE (the FIRST slice). BUILT (S63, `zec-wallet-core::send`).**
  Implements the public `propose` (§3.1): runs upstream note-selection + fee +
  change over the wallet DB and returns a confirmable `SendProposal` (the numbers
  the user signs off on). DETERMINISTIC: no spending keys, no proofs, no network,
  no DB writes (read-only `WalletRead` + `InputSource`). The lowest-risk,
  fully-testable money core; everything else builds on it. See **AS BUILT** below.
- **inc-2d-2 — CREATE + SIGN (the first internal half of the public `send`).** Derives
  the transient `UnifiedSpendingKey` (§4.2: lives ONLY inside the `spawn_blocking`
  proving closure — never across `.await`, never stored/`Clone`/`Debug`), runs
  `create_proposed_transactions` (proofs + signatures), and PERSISTS the txs to the
  wallet DB BEFORE any submit (§6.3). CPU-heavy → `spawn_blocking`. Money-critical.
  **The create+sign CORE is BUILT (S65) and the production WIRING is BUILT (S66) — see
  AS BUILT below.** Prover packaging **DECIDED — BUNDLE** (founder 2026-06-20): the
  ~50 MB Sapling Groth16 params are embedded via `zcash_proofs/bundled-prover` so send
  works offline / first-try with NO network dependency on the money path (the per-platform
  size cost is accepted; the deferred-host-asset optimization stays open behind the
  injected-prover seam if install size demands it later). The internal
  `Wallet::sign_proposal` (consume → derive USK in `spawn_blocking` → `create_signed_core`)
  is the create+sign half; the PUBLIC `send` composes it with broadcast at 2d-3.
