      **THE §6.3 CRASH-ATOMICITY — DESIGN-LOCKED (S68) + UPSTREAM-VERIFIED (S69):** the literal
      "intent consumption atomic with tx creation in ONE DB transaction" is **NOT achievable**
      with the pinned `zcash_client_sqlite =0.21.0` without forking it — `WalletDb` exposes no
      connection accessor and `SqlTransaction`'s inner `&rusqlite::Transaction` is a private tuple
      field, so non-engine SQL CANNOT enlist in the engine's tx-persist transaction
      (`transactionally` composes engine ops atomically but admits no outside SQL). Rule Zero
      (audited-libs-whole, no fork) forbids patching upstream. **The sound alternative that
      achieves the SAME invariant** (an intent never mints two txs; a tx never orphans its
      intent): use the engine's OWN atomic note-spend state as the idempotency witness.
      - **The CLAIM** (persisted on the intent row before create) = the proposal's selected
        note set as the **chain-stable triple `(txid, ShieldedProtocol, output_index)`** read
        from the shielded inputs of EVERY step (`proposal.steps()[i].shielded_inputs().notes()`
        — this build is single-step, but the extractor iterates all steps so a future
        multi-step proposal claims every input; `ReceivedNote::txid()` / `.note().protocol()` /
        `.output_index()`, backend 0.23.0 — `output_index()` is `u16`, widened lossless to the
        `u32` the witness query takes). **NOT** the `ReceivedNoteId` `(ShieldedProtocol, i64)`
        rowid — that `i64` is a session-local SQLite primary key, not stable across a
        rescan/rebuild; the chain triple is. (This resolves the S68 serialization-stability
        question: persist the triple, never the rowid.) A proposal carrying transparent inputs
        (off in this build) or selecting no shielded input is a structural fault (`ProposeFailed`),
        never a silently-incomplete claim; the claim count is capped at the codec's
        `MAX_CLAIM_NOTES` at the producer so it can never exceed what the decoder accepts.
      - **The WITNESS** = `InputSource::get_spendable_note(&txid, protocol, index, target)`
        returning `None`. Verified against the sqlite SQL (`wallet/common.rs::get_spendable_note`
        + `spent_notes_clause`/`tx_unexpired_condition`): a note is returned `Some` iff it is
        mined + scanned + **NOT spent by an _unexpired_ tx**. So `None` ⟺ the tx was created and
        is still live (do NOT re-propose); `Some` ⟺ never created **or the created tx has
        EXPIRED** (the engine frees the note when the spending tx's `expiry_height < target` — the
        ~40-block expiry IS the safety net, enforced by upstream, that un-sticks a
        created-but-never-broadcast tx). **SAFETY INVARIANT (the double-spend hinge):** the
        witness `target` MUST be the honest current tip+1 (`get_target_and_anchor_heights(1)`),
        **never inflated** — a too-high target would read a still-live tx as expired, free the
        note in the witness, and re-propose while the original could still mine = a double-spend.
        All false-positive directions of the witness (a note unspendable for any non-spent reason
        — deep reorg un-mine, missing) only cause a conservative WAIT, never a double-create.
      - **The TXID for re-broadcast** is recovered from OUR OWN recorded `txid` column (written
        right after create), NOT from the witness — the production API exposes no "which tx spent
        this note" (`get_tx_history` is test-only). The one narrow crash window (engine committed
        the spend, our aux `txid` write didn't) resolves via expiry: the un-broadcast tx expires
        (~40 blocks) → the note frees → witness reads `Some` → re-propose. Bounded delay, never a
        loss, never a double-send.
      - **The RECONCILE decision** (pure fn): all-claims-spendable → `ReProposeFresh`; any-claim-
        not-spendable + recorded txid → `ReBroadcast(txid)`; any-not-spendable + no txid →
        `AwaitWitness` (wait for mine-or-expire). The engine records spent-notes atomically with
        the tx, so "did the tx get created" is answerable from durable wallet state with NO
        cross-table transaction.
- **inc-2d-swap** wires §4.4 (the `OutOfZec` deposit send reuses 2d-1→2d-3 with the
  quote address validated + `expires_at` re-checked before every submit). **DECOMPOSED
  (S71) along the mechanism↔provider-coupling seam** (the same build-the-tested-money-core
  -then-wire rhythm as 3-b-ii-A/B):
  - **inc-2d-swap-a — the deadline-tagged deposit-send MECHANISM through the wallet**
    (harness-proven, NO `SwapService` coupling — zero behavior change to a wallet with no
    swap, like 3-b-i/3-b-ii-A). The deposit send is just a **queued send carrying an
    absolute wall-clock deadline** (the quote's `expires_at`): the §6.2 outbox + §6.3
    double-send guard already give crash-safety, idempotent re-propose, and no-double-spend
    for free; the deposit reuses ALL of it. The ONLY new behavior is the §4.4 deadline
    exclusion — the resubmission machinery (§6.1) must never (re-)PROPOSE a fresh deposit
    tx to a quote whose deadline has lapsed ("feed a dead quote"). As built:
    - **Schema (`intent_store`, additive, the `db::migrate` chokepoint, NO
      `WALLET_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump — like the 3-b-ii-A `claim`/`txid` columns):** a nullable
      `deposit_deadline INTEGER` column. `NULL` = an ordinary `queue_send` (no deadline);
      `Some(unix_secs)` = a deposit tagged with the quote's wall-clock `expires_at`. (Stored
      `i64`, saturating like `created_at`; `enqueue` gains the `Option<i64>` arg, `queue_send`
      passes `None`.)
    - **The deadline clock is WALL-CLOCK, by necessity + honestly, with an unsynced-clock
      floor.** The `SwapService` pre-sign gate (§2.6) is monotonic-primary (a slow device
      clock can't sign a deposit to a dead quote); but monotonic does NOT survive a process
      restart, so the only restart-durable deadline a resubmission pass can read is the
      persisted wall-clock `expires_at`. The two are complementary: the monotonic dual-gate is
      the strict pre-flight at execute (inc-2d-swap-b); the persisted wall deadline is the
      crash/restart safety net here. **The mobile boot-before-NTP / reset-clock case fails
      NON-destructively** (review fold): a wall clock below `CLOCK_PLAUSIBILITY_FLOOR_SECS`
      (`1_700_000_000`) is treated as UNSYNCED — a deposit on such a clock **WAITS** (never fed,
      never deleted, since a deadline can't be time-checked by a clock that says "1970"),
      self-healing once the clock syncs. The remaining far-future-clock skew fails closed →
      deletes early → re-quote (bounded, never a fund loss). No silent feeding of dead quotes.
    - **The gate lives in the harness-tested `send` cores as ONE decision** (`deposit_gate(deadline,
      now_unix) -> DepositGate { Proceed | Expired | Wait }`, folding in `DEADLINE_SAFETY_MARGIN_SECS`
      so a deposit is never born within the margin of death; the `>=` lapse boundary is the
      canonical edge inc-2d-swap-b's monotonic gate MUST match), applied ONLY at the "would
      (re-)propose fresh" decision: `prepare_queued` — before `propose_core`, an `Expired` deposit
      is **`delete`d** (terminal — the user re-quotes) returning `Prepared::DepositExpired`, a
      `Wait` deposit returns `Prepared::Retry` (left Queued); `reconcile_inflight` — in ONLY the
      `ReProposeFresh` arm, `Expired` → `delete` + `Reconciled::DepositExpired`, `Wait` →
      `Reconciled::Awaiting` (untouched). **The `ReBroadcast` / delete-on-mined / `AwaitWitness`
      arms are UNCHANGED** — an already-CREATED deposit tx is not "feeding a dead quote" (the funds
      already left at create time), so it reconciles normally (re-broadcast until it mines, or
      expiry frees its notes → then a `ReProposeFresh` catches the now-lapsed deadline). So the
      gate only ever turns a *fresh* propose into a terminal delete or a wait — the minimal,
      money-safe reading of §4.4 "excludes a deposit tx whose deadline has lapsed."
    - **-b obligations recorded at -a review** (so they are not lost): (1) `SwapService::execute`
      must thread the EXACT `Address` that `validate_quote` blessed into `queue_deposit_send` —
      `validate_quote` should RETURN the parsed transparent `Address` (or a `DepositAddress`
      newtype) rather than discard it, so "validated" and "sent" are provably the same value and a
      second independent parse can't admit a wrong-network/non-transparent recipient (`Payment::new`

      §8 row `deposit_tx_never_resubmitted_past_deadline` (the monotonic-anchored clock-skew test)
      lands at -b.
    - **The handle:** `Wallet::queue_deposit_send(deposit: Address, amount: Zatoshis,
      deadline_unix: u64) -> QueuedSendId` (`pub(crate)`, `#[allow(dead_code)]` until -b

    - **Named tests:** `deposit_send_rejects_expired_quote` (gate 1 security) — a past-deadline

    (`ProvisionStep::PriorLifeSwept`) so kill-after-sweep-before-step-2 stays
    test-reachable. **(b) a fresh life must not
    inherit a dead life's WIPE STATE.** An interrupted wipe's warn-and-Ok cleanup can
    leave the `.wipe-committed` breadcrumb in a dir that reads `Empty`; the successor
    wallet provisioned there INHERITS it for its whole life, and its own future destroy
    reads the breadcrumb and SKIPS the verify-real-sever fail-closed guard (severed == 0
    converges as "expected" — the B1 hole reopened: a mis-derived-namespace destroy would
    delete the LIVE successor's files while its real wrap key survives). The provision
    hygiene block now sweeps `WIPE_COMMITTED_FILE_NAME`, stale `*.tmp` `write_atomic`
    remnants (a kill inside the create→rename window leaves `<seal>.tmp` —
    same-ciphertext blobs of the dead life; matched on raw bytes, not UTF-8), and the
    dead life's `wallet.db.rescan-tmp` + sidecars (otherwise untouched until a rescan
    that may never come) alongside the DB sweep; a dead `block-cache.db` is deferred to
    its own validated-or-deleted opener. S188 FOLD (#378, security MED): the hygiene
    also sweeps the dead life's FINAL-NAME seal artifacts (`seed.seal`, `dbkey.seal`,
    `wrap.artifact`). A SealedKeychain provision killed INSIDE step 2 — `seed.seal`
    durable, manifest not — reads back `Empty`, and its wrap alias stays ALIVE as the
    bounded step-1 orphan (provision never purges aliases; only destroy does). A
    SealedKeychain successor overwrites all three at step 2, but a None-persistence
    successor never writes `seed.seal` — pre-fold, the dead life's SEALED SEED sat at
    rest for the successor's whole life in a dir whose manifest promises "no seed at
    rest". PLATFORM-SHAPE PRECISION (S189 review fold): on the alias-generation
    keystore shape (Android) the dead wrap alias survives as the bounded step-1
    orphan, but the successor's unconditional step-2 `wrap.artifact` overwrite breaks
    the READY-MADE unwrap chain — recovering the dead SealKey then needs artifact
    bytes captured pre-successor or forensic recovery of unlinked blocks; on the
    fixed-item shape (Apple) the successor's custody overwrites the dead item and the
    residue is dead ciphertext outright. The manifest-promise violation is identical
    on both shapes and is what the sweep closes. Safe to sweep by construction: the
    arm is `Empty`-gated, and seals-without-manifest means the seals were never
    SDK-loadable — a mid-step-2 kill (step 2 writes seals BEFORE the manifest) or a
    mid-destroy kill (custody severed FIRST — dead ciphertext) — `read_manifest`
    fails before any seal reader runs; `dbkey.seal`/`wrap.artifact` sweep harmlessly
    (step 2 rewrites both unconditionally). Destroy already converged the state; the
    fold removes the AT-REST FILE for the successor's lifetime — an unlink, not a
    shred (unlinked-block forensics remain the platform FBE layer's problem), and the
    orphan ALIAS lives until destroy's purge (the item-(a) SEAM NOTE's
    alias-without-artifact sweep is that half's tracked closure; purging at provision
    time is impossible — this life's custody already lives in the same namespace).
    NO UPGRADE ARM (contrast the
    breadcrumb's below): a None-persistence wallet already provisioned over the
    residue by a PRE-FOLD SDK keeps the stale `seed.seal` until destroy. An open-time
    sweep on the manifest-says-None arm would be safe (a None wallet never writes
    `seed.seal`, so one beside that manifest is provably inherited) — but the state is
    producible only by a pre-fold kill+re-create, and no pre-fold build has shipped
    beyond dev devices; documented residual, destroy converges, revisit only if a
    pre-GA build ever escapes. UPGRADE ARM (review fold): the provision-time
    sweep cannot reach a successor provisioned into a dirty dir BEFORE this fix, so
    `open` sweeps the breadcrumb too — `load_custody` succeeding IS the proof the wrap
    key is alive, making any breadcrumb at open provably a dead life's. (Reach is
    OPEN-gated — honest residual: a pre-fix wallet wiped without ever opening
    post-upgrade keeps the disarm, since at destroy an inherited breadcrumb is
    indistinguishable from its own interrupted wipe, the legitimate converge exit;
    pre-existing, triple-coincidence narrow, accepted.) **(c) rescan-closure
    error-arm drop order.** The step-(5) closes moved into `run_blocking` (4-a-5) capture
    the connections + the `WalletLock` as closure fields; an early `?` (the hoisted
    sweep, the WAL fold) dropped the remaining captures in UNSPECIFIED order, so the
    flock could free while wallet.db connections were still open — violating the
    conns-close-before-lock-frees invariant (`Inner::lock`) exactly on the paths that
    already indicate a sick disk. Both early arms now close engine → aux → cache
    explicitly before propagating. **(d) the NIT basket.** The block-cache module doc's
    journal-transient bound was honest only for the fill path: a mass DELETE (reorg
    truncate / prune / cache clear) journals BEFORE-images up to ~the cache size, not one
    insert batch — doc corrected (the high-water tracks the cache FILE size,
    page-count-based). The cache opener pins `synchronous = FULL` BEFORE the
    journal flip (the flip's implicit checkpoint of a WAL-era cache rides the pinned
    durability, not a compile default) and unlinks stale `-wal`/`-shm` beside an
    ALREADY-rollback cache (dead bytes SQLite never reads in rollback mode — the flip arm
    unlinks its own). DIRECTORY PARITY (review fold, all three reviewers): every new
    tolerant unlink — provision hygiene, the cache sidecar sweep,
    `remove_db_and_sidecars` — now shares ONE helper (`db::remove_path_if_present`)
    that removes a planted DIRECTORY like destroy's sweep would; the file-only arm was
    a fresh brick shape (EPERM/EISDIR forever) in the very batch that un-bricks
    provisioning, and `remove_file` unlinks a symlink itself, never its referent. Two
    committed pins for properties S186 validated only empirically:
    a torn-mid-txn HOT rollback journal (cache_size-spill + copy-mid-txn fabrication,
    multi-page journal asserted so the canary can't shrink vacuous)
    rolls back through the keyed cache opener, and rollback-journal before-images at rest
    carry no plaintext (the `-journal` sibling of the WAL-frames canary — user data,
    not journal-header metadata, which is plaintext by design). Two
    one-sentence notes: a silent engine-conn drop-close failure would pin the step-5 fold
    `StoreBusy` until process restart, and iOS Data Protection can surface mid-fold
    faults as `SQLITE_IOERR` → `StoreCorrupt` while device-locked (both the #371 IOERR/
    BUSY taxonomy family). **(RESOLVED #371: `SQLITE_IOERR` now classifies to `Io`, not
    `StoreCorrupt` — no false seed-restore scare — at both the engine seam
    [`ClassifyStoreFault`] and the aux seam [`map_aux_err`]; see §6.1. The drop-close
    permanent-`StoreBusy` note stands.)** **(e) the FFI_INTERNAL allowlist is ENFORCED, not
    honor-system.** bf227ae's allowlist was comment-cited only — a working escape hatch
    for ANY lockstep enum (including the §5.1 de-shield disclosure ones). The gate now
    asserts each entry (i) is scoped to `WalletError` (the only enum with a documented
    internal-remap seam today; a new enum takes its own reviewed opt-in), (ii) names a
    variant that still parses from the core enum (stale entries die with their variant),
    and (iii) sits on a variant whose core doc carries the "never crosses the wallet FFI"
    marker phrase — the doc IS the contract the allowlist cites. HONEST SCOPE (security
    review): this is a DOC gate, not a remap gate — nothing asserts the internal remap
    itself exists, so a marker-phrased entry without one would cross folded to the
    bridge's `Unknown` (stable `code` string intact). Accepted while the allowlist holds
    one entry; a per-entry remap assertion is the hardening if it grows. **Named
    tests.** Rust core: `provision_custody_failure_leaves_a_prior_life_untouched`
    (bite-valid: the old order fails it),
    `successor_destroy_fails_closed_after_a_dirty_prior_wipe` (bite-valid: the
    inherited breadcrumb converges instead of trapping),
    `none_persistence_successor_inherits_no_prior_seed_seal` (S188 fold, bite-valid:
    with the seal sweep disabled the dead life's `seed.seal` survives the successor's
    provision),
    `open_sweeps_a_provably_stale_wipe_breadcrumb` (the upgrade arm),
    `provision_hygiene_removes_a_planted_directory` +
    `remove_path_if_present_covers_files_dirs_symlinks_and_absence` (dir parity),
    `cache_opener_replays_a_torn_txn_hot_journal`,
    `journal_pages_at_rest_carry_no_plaintext`, and `PriorLifeSwept` joins the
    fault-injection kill matrix. Item (c) is enforced by construction
    (explicit drops precede the return — no observable seam short of a real flock
    contender; the success tuple is additionally ordered `(open, cache, lock)` at all
    three run_blocking sites so even an orphaned un-destructured output drops
    conns-before-lock); item (e) enforces inside `bridge_enums_cover_core_variants`
    itself.
    **crypto-change review MANDATORY** (provision/destroy custody order + at-rest hygiene on
    the money path; no new primitives — file hygiene + pragma ordering on the audited
    SQLCipher stack).
  - **W-swap-4-b — parked-authorizer drain (the re-sign fallback).** After sign-at-execute a live
    deposit needs a FRESH propose (re-sign) only in the rare reorg/note-conflict edge (created tx
    orphaned, deadline NOT lapsed). For a `None`-persistence wallet at a background drain that
    re-sign can't happen ⇒ today it silently waits. -b PARKS the row visibly ("needs your
    authorization" — new Dart vocabulary; today `parked_sends_section` says "saved & pending"/
    "paused") and re-signs in-bracket at the next user-present moment. Generalizes the offline-queued
    ORDINARY send at host custody (the same silent-wait today) ⇒ makes
    `walletOfflineQueueSupportedProvider` obsolete; realizes the custody-invariant clause (2) and the
    §1.9 T2 offline-queued-send cell. Needs the swap-deposit row surfaced (today EXCLUDED from
    `list_parked_sends`). Own crypto-change review. Follow-on to -a; not the unblock.
- **inc-2d-ui — the host send screen (SHIPPED S74).** Pure host Dart in
  `sdk/zec_wallet/example` over the inc-2d-ffi bridge (the SDK surface is unchanged
  except a barrel fix — see below); the slice's tests live in the app tier, not
  this spec's §8 SDK register. AS BUILT:
  - **The ZIP-321 compose lives in the FFI ADAPTER, not the UI.** The host
    `WalletSession` port gained `composePaymentUri(recipient, amountZat, memoText)`
    + `propose(uri)` / `send(proposalId)` / `queueSend(uri)`; `FrbWalletSession`
    (the adapter, which holds the wallet `Network` threaded from config) owns the
    `encodePaymentUri` bridge crossing. So the controller calls NO native function
    and the whole flow is host-VM testable behind a fake (the hexagonal-testability
    rule the port exists for). `propose`/`queueSend` still take a URI because a
    future QR-scan flow already has one and skips compose.
  - **`SendController`** — a sealed state machine (`SendForm → SendPreparing →
    SendReview → SendSubmitting → SendSent` + the offline `SendQueuing → SendQueued`
    branch) mirroring `OnboardingController` (cached deps in `build`, `_disposed`
    guard, the synchronous transient-state re-entrancy interlock before the first
    await). Typed-error mappers read `WalletApiError.kind` ONLY (§5.4) — insufficient
    funds carries the audited figures; a broadcast failure is DATA →
    `SendSavedForRetry` (never lost money); a re-consumed token → `SendAlreadySubmitted`
    (no double-send); a stale anchor on send → back to the form to re-propose.
  - **`SendScreen`** requests FLAG_SECURE for its lifetime (a recipient address +
    amounts are sensitive); the confirm step renders the **§5.1 de-shield disclosure**
    (a prominent public-payment warning iff `SendProposal.hasTransparentRecipient`,
    the audited engine's own verdict) BEFORE the Send button. The integer-exact
    `parseZecAmount` money parser (the inverse of `formatZec`) is the host-side gate
    with a pre-multiply supply-ceiling overflow guard. The Send entry + screen are
    reachable only behind the active-wallet gate (`walletSessionProvider`).
  - **Barrel fix (in-domain):** the SDK `zec_wallet.dart` never re-exported
    `src/rust/api/payments.dart`, so the inc-2d-ffi `SendProposal`/`OutputPool`/
    `encodePaymentUri` types were unnameable from a host — added the export.
  - Full security review (crypto audit PASS ∥ security review ∥ arch review →
    code reviewer APPROVE-WITH-NITS), NO BLOCKER. **THEN a SECOND operational round**
    (money-reliability ∥ mobile/unstable-network ∥ real-world-edge): ONE real
    money-honesty defect FIXED — "Send another" after a completed send now refreshes
    the available-balance hint (`backToForm` never invalidated `walletSnapshotProvider`,
    so it showed the stale pre-send figure); +5 edge tests (partial pool-crossing body,
    mixed-pool de-shield, stale-anchor-on-resume→back-to-form, address-whitespace-trim,
    the balance refresh). Auto-hide-on-background for the confirm screen reviewed +
    DECLINED (it shows an address+amount, not a SEED; auto-hide would wipe a
    paste-from-another-app→resume flow; FLAG_SECURE + the manager iOS cover suffice);
    the no-host-send-timeout deference to the SDK's broadcast bound confirmed correct.
    **Carried/E2E-owed:** a funded propose→sign→broadcast against a real chain + the
    on-device send run; the host iOS recents-snapshot cover; a QR-scan path (would call
    `propose(scannedUri)` directly, bypassing the form's `composePaymentUri`).

- **inc-2d-ui-prefill — the FR-25 prefilled-send entry seam (SHIPPED #360).** Pure
  Dart/UI over the EXISTING inc-2d-ffi bridge (NO new FFI, NO crypto): the
  already-bridged, sync, audited `parsePaymentUri` (`api/payments.rs`, the ZIP-321
  parser over `zip321 =0.8.0`) is the single validator (DRY — the UI never re-parses
  ZIP-321 in Dart). AS BUILT:
  - **`WalletSendRequest{address, amountZat?, memo?, label?, lockRecipient}`** — an
    immutable public value object a host hands `WalletSendEntry.push(context, request)`
    to open the send flow prefilled (from a scanned QR / `zcash:` deep link / messenger
    pay-a-contact / NFC). It rides as GoRouter `extra` (in-session, not a shareable URL);
    `SendScreen`'s new optional `prefill` seeds the three screen-owned controllers in
    `initState`. The QR-scan path the inc-2d-ui note flagged as owed is now this seam —
    landing in the EDITABLE form (Enter), NOT a direct `propose(uri)` jump.
  - **`WalletSendRequest.fromUri(session, uri, {lockRecipient})`** — the ZIP-321 door,
    delegating to the port's new `parseSendRequest` (the adapter injects the wallet's OWN
    `Network`, the sole authority — a host can NOT coerce a wrong-network send, mirroring
    `composePaymentUri`'s network-hiding). Throws the typed, payload-free (§5.4)
    `WalletSendRequestException` **at the seam** (malformed / wrong-network / multi-leg /
    unsupported-memo), so the host shows an honest error and never a half-filled form.
  - **The seam policy (single-recipient form):** a multi-leg URI is rejected
    (`multiplePayments`) — this also keeps the single-payment `selfSend` authorization
    invariant intact (the coupling note on `WalletSpendIntent.recipientIsSelf`); a
    machine (0xFF) / reserved memo is rejected (`unsupportedMemo`) rather than silently
    dropped into an editable text field (a payment-reference the recipient may need must
    not vanish). The ZIP-321 `label` is CARRIED but deliberately NOT auto-rendered — an
    attacker-controllable URI string (a phishing surface) the host with trusted context
    decides to show; `message` is dropped.
  - **Prefilled ≠ pre-confirmed:** the prefill only seeds text; the SAME
    `prepare → propose → review → authorizeSpend` path + the SAME gating (recipient
    validity, sync state, spendable balance, host ceiling) run as an organic send.
    `lockRecipient:true` opens the recipient READ-ONLY (selectable — verify who you pay;
    not disabled/greyed) with an accessible lock announcement IN the field's own
    semantics node (S216: an ancestor `Semantics` label — the one channel that reaches
    the field on focus; suffix-icon/helperText semantics are sibling nodes); recipient-ONLY
    (amount + memo stay editable). **The lock is CONDITIONAL (public contract, S216):**
    applied only when the recipient classifies SENDABLE (a lock over an invalid/
    wrong-network typed address opens EDITABLE with the inline status — never a
    read-only dead-end) and RELEASED on a session flip; a host must not treat it as a
    security pin — the binding verification is the review echo + its own authorizer
    prompt. An identity-switch fires the existing session-flip controller-clear,
    so a prefilled draft never leaks across identities (the duress rule). S216 also
    hardened the entry lifecycle: `didUpdateWidget` re-seeds on an in-place route
    update (a host `replace`/`go` with a new `extra` can never leave the old request's
    fields under the new one), and a prefilled entry landing during an IN-FLIGHT step
    re-attaches first (the S153-F1 contract) then defers its fresh-form reset to the
    landing — the prior send's outcome is never attributed to the new entry.
  - **FR-26 — the entry REPORTS the flow it opened (granted 2026-09-05).**
    `WalletSendEntry.push` now returns `Future<WalletSendReport>` instead of the
    navigation future. The old return was the defect: it completed on POP, a signal
    true of the user who paid and of the user who backed out alike, so a host that
    composed a payment record on it could put a false claim of payment in front of the
    payee — and the alternative its own doc named (read the wallet's activity) is
    closed to a host whose spec forbids polling. The sealed report family is
    `WalletSendTransactionCreated{txids, broadcastCount, fundsInMotion}` ·
    `WalletSendNoTransaction` · `WalletSendQueuedOffline` ·
    `WalletSendAlreadySubmitted` · `WalletSendUnclassified`. **"A transaction exists" is
    the decidable fact, not "the broadcast succeeded"** — every arm of `TxSubmitResult`
    that carries a txid contributes one (`sendTxids`), because an unbroadcast tx is
    signed, persisted and re-sent by the resubmission machinery. An outcome claiming a
    send with NO id degrades to `unclassified` rather than handing a host a payment it
    can never reconcile. The motion axis is THREE-valued (`WalletSendMotion`): a
    two-step (ZIP-320) send with no leg accepted is the core #307 already-known race or a
    genuine nothing-out, and the reducer cannot tell — a two-state answer there invites a
    host to offer "pay another way" over money already travelling. Correlation travels
    WITH the request (`WalletSendRequest.correlationId`, opaque, echoed, never
    interpreted or logged) — the two joins a host would otherwise invent (recipient+amount,
    or the in-flight authorizer bracket) are a display-fact join on a money surface and a
    guess that is only free at one in-flight send. `WalletSendQueuedOffline` carries the
    core's parked-send id: the offline branch has no txid, so that id is the host's only handle onto
    the payment it just committed. It crosses as a **String** while `ParkedSend.id` and the
    `cancelParkedSend`/`retryParkedSend` verbs take an **int**, so a host parses before it can key
    the parked surfaces — stated because "the same id" alone reads as interchangeable and is not. Payload discipline unchanged: ids and
    counts, never form contents. The route builder still accepts a bare
    `WalletSendRequest` (a host navigating the path itself) and simply reports nothing.
    **Since stage S8 `deadline` (S293, ADR-0557; re-built S294, ADR-0558): a `NoTransaction`
    delivered by the entry's MOUNT GRACE is final for the request it names** — the grace REVOKES
    the request before it reports ("reported" and "revoked" are two bits; the revocation is a
    property of the request as the root-scoped send controller remembers it — ~~as the screen
    State holds it~~, struck S294: a fresh mount read no State and paid — read by the controller
    at `confirm()` and `queueOffline()` BEFORE the host's authorizer), so a route that mounts
    after the grace renders `SendRequestExpired` and cannot pay, and a bare `replace`/`go` with
    the same request is refused, in place or on a fresh mount (`sameSendRequest`: the same
    `correlationId` when BOTH carry one, else the same payment fields — ~~or untagged with the
    same fields~~, struck S294: a tag on one side only does not make a new request); a
    different `correlationId` on both sides, different fields, or a fresh `push` is a new act
    and pays. The other producers of `NoTransaction` revoke nothing (FR-26 row 687 stands).
    Before S8 the late route could pay under the host's negative — the 2026-09-20 review's R05.
  - **FR-26 delivery — reworked at the S250 four-angle review, which found three
    reachable ways for the report to LIE about money.** The first build had `SendScreen`
    infer the outcome from the GLOBAL `SendState` using per-screen booleans. That is
    wrong twice over: the state carries no flow identity, so a screen mounted UNDER a
    stacked entry booked the payment made above it (one send, two
    `WalletSendTransactionCreated`, two correlation ids); and the controller legitimately
    REFUSES some state writes, so a landing swallowed by the identity guard after a
    session flip read as "nothing was created" over a signed, broadcast transaction. A
    third: `catch` mapped every throwable to `SendSignFailed`, including one thrown by the
    host's own `authorizeSpend` AFTER the spend ran. As built now: `SendController` owns a
    monotonic `flowId` (a flow begins at a reset or a rebuild) and PUBLISHES its terminal
    on `sendFlowOutcomeProvider` — a separate channel, written even when the state write
    is refused — as `SendFlowSent` / `SendFlowQueued` / `SendFlowIndeterminate` /
    `SendFlowNothingCreated`. `confirm`/`queueOffline` latch whether the spend closure was
    ENTERED, which is what separates "no money moved" from "we lost the answer". A screen
    owns channels BY FLOW ID and reports only its own; a money-step latch (never cleared
    by a state transition — `build()` writes `const SendForm()` on a flip) decides
    `unclassified` vs `noTransaction` at teardown. The entry's liveness fallback no longer
    hangs off the navigation future (go_router applies redirects BEFORE attaching that
    completer, so a host app-lock redirect left the host awaiting forever) but off a
    bounded mount grace. `didUpdateWidget` keys the retire on the CHANNEL, not the
    request — two identical `const WalletSendRequest` literals are the same object, which
    made an in-place `replace` retire a channel with no answer and no completion. The
    result screen offers Done, not "Send another", once a host has been told: the channel
    is one-shot, so a second payment from a still-prefilled form would be one the host's
    record could never learn about. The delivery internals (`WalletSendReporter`,
    `WalletSendEntryArgs`) moved to `lib/src/send/` — a barrel `show` list is
    documentation and `implementation_imports` is enforcement.
  - **FR-28 — opaque MACHINE-MEMO bytes on the compose side (granted + shipped 2026-09-05).**
    `WalletSendRequest.machineMemo` takes a `WalletMachineMemo(bytes:, purpose:)`; `PaymentDraft`
    gains `memo_bytes` (mutually exclusive with `memo_text` — both-set is refused typed at
    `convert.rs::encode_payment_uri`, since silently preferring either would write a memo the caller
    did not choose onto a permanent ledger), lowered through the audited `Memo::arbitrary`. **The
    defect it fixes was SILENT:** the send form re-composes its ZIP-321 URI from its own text fields
    on every Review/Queue tap, so bytes carried only on the request were dropped the moment the user
    edited the amount — no error, no log. The memo is now screen state, forwarded on every compose,
    and released with the rest of the draft on a session flip.
    **DISCLOSURE, host-accepted and built as a MECHANISM — with its scope stated exactly.**
    `purpose` is a required constructor argument on a type that refuses empty bytes, a blank purpose
    and an over-long one, and it SANITIZES: directional-formatting characters are stripped and
    control/separator characters collapse to spaces, because a character bound is not a content
    bound and a purpose containing newlines otherwise renders a forged wallet-voice paragraph in the
    disclosure card (S250 security review reproduced it). The bytes are frozen (`List.unmodifiable`)
    so a host cannot change what is signed after construction. **An undisclosed attachment is
    unrepresentable ON THIS PATH — the `WalletSendRequest`/`SendScreen` one — and NOT package-wide:**
    `WalletSession.composePaymentUri(memoBytes:)`, `propose` and `send` are all public, so a host
    composing its own URI is outside the disclosure entirely. It defends the user against a careless
    host, not a hostile one, and the host doc says so. Rendered on the FORM (where the offline QUEUE
    commits, without ever passing a review) and again on the review, per send, non-dismissible, never
    remembered; the BYTES are never rendered; the copy states the wallet cannot check what the
    attachment contains (a label is accountability, not verification). `WalletSpendIntent.machineMemoPurpose` carries the same
    sentence to a credential host's prompt, read from `SendReview.machineMemoPurpose` so the two
    cannot drift. While a machine memo owns the slot the written memo field is disabled with its own
    stated reason (not the transparent-recipient sentence, which would be a false explanation for
    the same disabled field).
    **WIRE REALITY, stated because a host that ignores it reads padding as data:** the ZIP-302 `0xFF`
    field has no length framing, so anything under 511 bytes is zero-padded and returns as the full
    511. "Byte-for-byte" means the LEADING bytes; a host frames its own length inside.
    **Policy:** the api-surface `DENY_BUFFERS` test required an explicit SANCTIONED entry for
    `memo_bytes` — OUTBOUND caller-owned bytes only. Inbound machine-memo bytes stay unsanctioned:
    the parse direction remains a length-only display projection, because inbound bytes are hostile
    on-chain data (principle 7). The asymmetry is now deliberate and documented. Corrected in the
    same change: `convert.rs` cited ADR-0530 A6 for a "machine memos are composed host-side in Rust"
    rule; A6 verbatim is nonce hygiene, parser obligations and a fuzz target, and carries no such
    rule — the second citation-nobody-re-read in this corpus after `memo_to_parsed`'s §5.4.
  - **FR-27 — machine-memo BYTES on the READ side, prefix-scoped (granted + shipped 2026-09-05).**
    The third and last pay-to-contact seam, and the only one that was a policy decision rather than
    plumbing: it opens an INBOUND crossing for attacker-controllable bytes. Granted because the
    posture was asymmetric in the UNSAFE direction — after FR-28 the SDK helps a host WRITE an
    envelope onto a permanent public ledger and then makes that same envelope unreadable to it,
    while ADR-0530 A2 makes the memo load-bearing (a txid is public by construction, so the
    memo-free join is forgeable by anyone watching the chain — "just use the txid" is a broken
    option, not a cheaper one).
    **As built.** `WalletConfig.machineMemoPrefixes` (`List<Uint8List>`, ABSENT by default) is the
    host's declared read scope; `WalletHandle.machineMemos(txidHex)` returns, in output order, the
    `Arbitrary` (`0xFF`) memos of that transaction whose LEADING bytes match a registered prefix.
    `Reserved` never returns bytes, `Text` never comes back here (it has its own lane), and a
    transaction the wallet cannot decrypt has no memos to return. The entitlement gate is the one
    the core already owns: `history::transaction_memos` scopes to outputs the primary account sent
    or received, so this verb widens WHAT crosses, never WHOSE.
    **Prefix means "matching the registered prefix", NOT "written by this device"** — Bob's wallet
    never wrote Alice's memo, and the literal reading breaks the receive side outright.
    **The four binding conditions of the ruling, and where each one LIVES:**
    (1) the untrusted-bytes contract travels with the VERB, in its own API doc, because A6 binds
    Relim and this SDK ships to strangers; (2) **the SDK never parses the envelope** — no magic,
    version, length or purpose knowledge exists here, which is what keeps a host's format the
    host's problem; (3) prefix-matched · `Arbitrary` only · never `Reserved` · length-capped;
    (4) **prefix matching is NOT a security boundary** — forging a prefix is cheap, so it cuts
    VOLUME, not intent, and the host's own fail-closed parser sits on the hostile path by default
    rather than as defence in depth. The verb's doc says all four to the caller.
    **No silent empties.** An unconfigured scope is a typed refusal (`MachineMemoScopeInvalid`,
    `RW-PAY-010`), not an empty list — a host that forgot to register would otherwise read
    "this transaction carries nothing" over a memo that is there. An EMPTY prefix is refused at the
    config door for the same reason inverted: it matches everything, which is the failure mode the
    FR's acceptance names ("a build that returns everything fails as surely as one returning
    nothing"). Prefixes are bounded (`MACHINE_MEMO_PREFIX_MAX_BYTES` = 32,
    `MACHINE_MEMO_PREFIX_MAX_COUNT` = 8), both value-pinned in
    `named_constants_at_boundary` — that bounds the comparisons PER MEMO. **The number of memos is
    the CHAIN's, not ours**, and is bounded only by consensus transaction size: the worst case is a
    few MB of transient churn on a deliberately crafted max-size transaction. Stated precisely
    because the first draft claimed the prefix bounds made "the filter's cost bounded", which is
    the wrong bound (FR-27 security review).
    **One unclassifiable memo cannot deny the readable ones, and the two failure modes are
    separated.** ZIP-302 has exactly one upstream-invalid shape (a text lead over non-UTF-8 bytes)
    and `v_tx_outputs.memo` is stored unvalidated, so it is reachable on-chain — and the party
    paying you chooses every byte of every memo in their own transaction. The strict reader failed
    the WHOLE transaction on it, so one dust output would have suppressed the valid envelope beside
    it: the very "wrote it, then made it unreadable" failure this FR ends, handed to a hostile
    counterparty. Found independently by the crypto audit AND the security review.
    As built after a SECOND security pass over the fix itself (`history::TransactionMemos`):
    - **A classifier rejection is HOSTILE INPUT** — skipped and **counted** (`unreadable`), never
      fatal. Counted rather than dropped because a silently short list is a silent failure
      (principle 10); a caller renders "1 memo could not be read".
    - **An oversized stored blob is LOCAL CORRUPTION** — no counterparty can put one there — and
      stays a hard `MemoInvalid` on every lane. The first fix collapsed both into one skip, which
      would have hidden a broken store behind a short list.
    - **ONE readable set for both consumers.** The first fix gave the display lane `Fail` and the
      machine lane `Skip` over the same rows, which let a payer attach one malformed dust memo and
      have the HOST act on their envelope while the USER's display read returned nothing for that
      transaction — a payer-controlled screen-vs-host divergence, the class FR-26's review found
      dangerous on the send side, inverted onto the read side. There is now one reader.
      `machine_memos` drops the count provably without loss: only a TEXT lead can be unclassifiable,
      and a `0xFF` lead always classifies, so an unreadable row can never have been a machine memo.
    `TxId::from_display_hex` is the new single hex-parse door (`TxidInvalid`, `RW-PAY-009`), tied by
    KAT to the audited upstream `Display` — the same anti-explorer-mismatch invariant
    `from_display_order` already carries, now on the inbound side.
    **Policy:** the api-surface `DENY_BUFFERS` scan required TWO new SANCTIONED entries (the config
    field and the verb's exact return type). Because a file-wide strip would auto-sanction any
    future declaration matching the same text, the waiver's scope is pinned by a test asserting the
    return declaration occurs EXACTLY ONCE — the FR-28 audit built that escape once already.
    `convert.rs::memo_to_parsed`'s SSOT comment is amended in the SAME commit (the ruling's own
    condition): it cited §5.4 for the never-cross rule, but §5.4 is the NEVER-LOG list and says
    nothing about FFI crossing. The real justification is hostile/opaque on-chain data (principle
    7), and the rule now names its one exception where it lives.
    **Not built, named so it is not guessed at:** no `WalletSession` port method and no
    `zec_wallet_ui` surface. The host that needs this holds the `WalletHandle` from its own
    provisioner; adding a UI port method would need a memo-display consumer that does not exist —
    the very condition the original `transaction_memos` deferral named.
  - Tests: the pure mapper + `fromUri` (`wallet_send_request_test.dart`, over fixtures +
    the fake) and the screen prefill/lock/donation/"prefilled≠pre-confirmed" flow
    (`send_screen_prefill_test.dart`); FR-26's pure `sendTxids`/`walletSendReportFor`
    boundary (`wallet_send_report_test.dart`) and the seam driven through the REAL
    `walletRoutes()` builder (`wallet_send_entry_report_test.dart` — whose load-bearing
    row is the NEGATIVE one: a build where paying and backing out yield the same value
    fails). Four more rows landed with the S250 rework, one per reachable lie, each
    watched failing first: two idle stacked entries yield ONE report; a session flip
    mid-send is never `noTransaction`; a host authorizer throwing AFTER the spend is
    never `noTransaction`; an in-place `replace` with the same const request still
    completes the first future. FR-28 adds `send_machine_memo_test.dart` (the required-purpose
    polarities, the disclosure, a bytes-never-rendered sweep over the review's text, the memo-field
    gate, the authorizer hand-off, a text-memo anti-regression row, and the load-bearing re-compose
    row — verified failing against a mutant that drops the forward) plus the two Rust rows in
    `payment_uri.rs` that assert the on-chain bytes and the padding rule through the audited encoder
    and parser rather than by length.
    The example gains an Appearance→Developer "Prefilled send (ZIP-321)" demo
    (paste-URI + typed-request paths, reject-at-seam) which now renders the report it
    gets back — the reference consumer of the seam, not just of the entry.
    E2E-owed: the on-device demo walk (a paste-URI → prefilled form → a reported
    outcome).

**Decisions LOCKED at design (the previously-open ones):**

1. **Upstream wiring:** propose = `data_api::wallet::propose_transfer` with
   `GreedyInputSelector` (`data_api::wallet::input_selection`) + the standard
   ZIP-317 change strategy (`fees::zip317`), `OvkPolicy::Sender` (the sender can
   decrypt its own outputs for history). create+sign =
   `data_api::wallet::create_proposed_transactions` with the local Sapling +
   Orchard provers (the bundled proving parameters) and `SpendingKeys` from the
   transient USK. broadcast =
   `proto::service::CompactTxStreamerClient::send_transaction` — **CONFIRMED
   present in the pinned client** (an earlier map claimed it missing; it is not).
2. **Confirmations policy = the §2.5 spendable SSOT.** `ConfirmationsPolicy` is
   derived from the SAME ZIP-315 policy as `account::spendable_policy` (3 trusted /
   10 untrusted), so a balance that says "spendable" and a propose that selects it
   can NEVER disagree (one source of truth — no second confirmations constant).
3. **`SendProposal` carries DISPLAY data; the upstream `Proposal` is an opaque,
   Rust-retained token** (the §2.4 lossless-token pattern — `Proposal<FeeRule,
   NoteRef>` never crosses FFI; the public `send` consumes the token by id). The
   token is ONE-SHOT + TTL-bounded with the EXISTING §3.1 guards (a re-`send` ⇒
   `ProposalAlreadyUsed` — the double-tap guard; a stale anchor past `PROPOSAL_TTL`
   ⇒ `ProposalStale`, re-propose). The DTO holds: `total_zat`, `fee_zat`,
   `change_zat`, per-step recipient + amount + **`OutputPool`** (the engine's own
   `payment_pools` verdict — the §5.1 de-shield disclosure; see AS BUILT for why
   `OutputPool`, not `AddressKind`), `target_height`, `steps` (>1 ⇒ pool-crossing,
   §1.7). Integer zatoshis only — no float ever.
4. **Errors — REUSE the existing taxonomy, do not invent collisions.** propose
   surfaces `InsufficientFunds { available, required, pending_incoming }` (ALREADY in
   the §6.1 table — lets the host say "wait for confirmations" honestly); the
   one-shot / stale-anchor faults are the EXISTING `ProposalAlreadyUsed` /
   `ProposalStale` (§3.1/§6.1), NOT a new variant; `QueuedSendStale` (§6.1) covers
   the §6.2 re-propose-can't-cover case. Any genuinely-new propose fault (e.g. an
   input-selector/commitment-tree error with no existing mapping) lands as ONE
   payload-free RW-SEND variant named at BUILD time and added to the §6.1 table then
   (the §6.1-row-lands-with-the-build precedent). broadcast/outbox add RW-BCAST-* at
   2d-3. REUSE the BUILT RW-PAY-* construction errors (`MemoRequiresShieldedRecipient`,
   `AmountOutOfRange`, …) from the `Payment::new` funnel — propose does NOT re-validate
   what the intent constructor already guaranteed (DRY; one validation chokepoint).
5. **Test harness (the gate that was missing — nothing funds a wallet DB today):**
   enable `zcash_client_backend`/`zcash_client_sqlite` `test-dependencies` as a
   **dev-dependency ONLY** (never in the shipped graph — supply-chain gate), and add
   a `tests/support` funded-wallet builder over `data_api::testing::{TestBuilder,
   TestState}` — provision an account, mine fake compact outputs to give it
   spendable notes, then drive propose. This unblocks every 2d-* test and is the
   FIRST build step of inc-2d-1.

**Gate-8 named tests (inc-2d-1):**
- `propose_selects_notes_fee_and_change_for_a_simple_send` — funded wallet → a
  `SendProposal` whose `total = amount + fee` and whose change reconciles.
- `propose_insufficient_funds_is_typed_with_available_and_required` — §6.1
  honesty: never a panic, never a silent under-send.
- `propose_amount_at_spendable_boundary` — gate 7: exactly-spendable vs one-zat-over
  (the fee tips it over).
- `propose_uses_the_same_spendable_policy_as_balance` — the SSOT: a note still
  pending spendability is NOT selected; `balance.spendable` and propose agree.
- `propose_is_read_only_no_db_mutation_no_network` — deterministic: the proposal
  writes nothing, dials nothing; re-propose is idempotent.
- `propose_multi_recipient_and_a_transparent_leg_sets_disclosure` — the §5.1
  de-shield disclosure rides the DTO (a memo-to-transparent was already rejected at
  `Payment::new`).
- `propose_token_is_opaque_and_single_use` — the retained `Proposal` never crosses
  FFI; a second `send` of the same token is typed `ProposalAlreadyUsed` (the §6.3
  double-spend guard's propose-side seam, the existing §3.1 one-shot contract).

**AS BUILT (S63 — inc-2d-1, `zec-wallet-core::send`; full crypto-change review, no
blockers):**
- **`OutputPool { Transparent, Sapling, Orchard }`, not `AddressKind`.** The
  per-recipient pool on the DTO is the audited engine's OWN `Proposal::payment_pools`
  verdict, not a re-derivation from the recipient address — a Unified-address
  recipient the engine routes to Orchard is `OutputPool::Orchard`, where `AddressKind`
  would say `Unified` and HIDE the actual pool from the §5.1 disclosure. So the
  disclosure rides the true on-chain pool (`has_transparent_recipient` = any output
  pool is `Transparent`). Rule Zero: we never classify the pool ourselves.
- **`target_height`, not `expiry_height`.** Propose only knows the note ANCHOR's
  target height; the on-chain `expiry_height` is finalized when the tx is built
  (inc-2d-2). The wall-clock freshness guard is `PROPOSAL_TTL_SECS` on the retained
  token; the authoritative staleness check is the chain anchor re-validated at
  `send`-time (an inc-2d-2 hard requirement — a proposal resumed after a long device
  suspend MUST re-anchor, never trust the suspend-pausing monotonic TTL alone).
- **Errors (RW-SEND-001..005, §6.1):** `InsufficientFunds { available, required,
  pending_incoming }` (amounts as typed payload, static `Display` — §5.4),
  `SendAmountRequired` (a donation-form leg used as a send), `ProposalAlreadyUsed`
  (one-shot double-tap), `ProposalStale` (TTL/anchor — ALSO the fold for upstream
  `ScanRequired`), `ProposeFailed` (the one payload-free catch-all for any
  change/selection/structural fault, incl. an UNRECOGNISED >1-step proposal). `pending_incoming` is
  read from the SAME `account::fold_account_balances` + `spendable_policy` SSOT the
  balance uses. A DB fault in propose is the existing `StoreCorrupt` (one corruption
  door). Mirrored to the bridge `WalletErrorKind` + Dart (FRB regenerated).
- **Opaque one-shot token registry is BOUNDED** (crypto+security review fold):
  per-wallet `ProposalRegistry` in `Inner` retains the `Proposal` (never crosses FFI)
  + the originating `PaymentRequest`; `propose` reserves the id, summarizes the DTO
  with it, then `put`s the token. `put` sweeps TTL-expired entries AND caps the live
  set at `PROPOSAL_REGISTRY_MAX_LIVE = 32` (evict oldest, newest survives) so a
  propose-without-send loop can't grow it without bound (each entry holds
  §5.4-sensitive memo bytes). `consume` (inc-2d-2) takes the token exactly once.
- **Multi-step (pool-crossing): propose/summarize ACCEPTS the recognised ZIP-320
  two-step (S123, §3.2i-2 slice 2e-2a); SIGNING is gated.** `transparent-inputs` is ON
  (ADR-0528/Recv-2b), so the engine synthesises a 2-step TEX/ephemeral proposal; the
  `is_zip320_two_step` predicate recognises that exact shape and `summarize` returns a
  correct no-double-count DTO (the ephemeral hop is excluded from `change_zat`). Any
  OTHER multi-step is still `ProposeFailed`. The single-step total (Σ recipients + fee)
  is unchanged and EXACT. `Wallet::propose` AND `create_signed_core` both fail-close on a
  recognised multi-step until **slice B3** enrols the interactive-send outbox and lifts the gates
  (the multi-txid persist-before-broadcast + re-broadcast recovery MECHANISM itself LANDED S124 —
  B1 `7280ab4` + B2 `4574122`; §3.2i-2 slice B). So TEX is recognised and its display math is
  unit-tested (via `propose_core`/`summarize` directly) but NOT user-reachable in production yet.
- **Funded-wallet harness:** a crate-local `DataStoreFactory` + in-memory `TestCache`
  over `data_api::testing` (the `test-dependencies` feature, DEV-ONLY — verified
  absent from the shipped/no-dev graph; `proptest` capped `<1.7` to satisfy its
  bound). Currently inline in `send.rs::tests`; **extract to `tests/support/` at
  inc-2d-2** when `wallet.rs` integration tests need the funded builder (arch review
  MINOR, deferred). +2 registry-bound tests beyond the 7 gate-8.
- **Operational pass (S64 — money-reliability + mobile/unstable, a distinct adversarial
  round beyond the pre-commit review): NO BLOCKER.** Added 6 real-world money edge
  tests (`funded_multi` helper): multi-note selection (Σinputs = total + change across
  notes), near-max-send (conservation, change ≤ fee delta), re-propose after the chain
  advances (monotonic `target_height` — the background→resume case), the full honest
  `(available, required, pending_incoming)` triple mid-scan, a fresh/unfunded wallet is
  typed-never-panic, and de-shield change returns to a SHIELDED pool (never leaks
  transparent). **15 send tests + 1 reserved.** The one HARDENING — the monotonic TTL
  PAUSES on device suspend (mobile background; desktop laptop-lid hibernate is the same
  class), so a resumed proposal can read "fresh" against a stale anchor — is made
  un-forgettable: a `SAFETY-OBLIGATION (inc-2d-2)` contract at `ProposalRegistry::consume`
  (a returned `Ok` is NOT a freshness guarantee — `send` MUST re-anchor against the live
  tip, never trust the suspend-extended TTL) + a reserved `#[ignore]` height-fixture test
  `proposal_resumed_after_suspend_must_reanchor_at_send` (the bug is a chain-height delta,
  untestable with virtual time — it lands with `send`). Deferred (noted): a true
  transparent-only-funded test (heavier `data_api::testing::transparent` surface); a
  concurrent scan-vs-propose responsiveness model test; a host-side change-POOL DTO field
  (`change_zat` ships, the pool is engine-only — an inc-2d-ffi observability follow-on).

**MONEY-SAFETY — the large-amount confirm + self-send note + foolproof address review
(S109; founder S104/S109 decisions; SDK core SHIPPED, FFI+host UI DEFERRED):**
The send path is ALREADY money-safe — audited `Address::parse` (checksum/typo/truncation/
wrong-network via `zcash_address`, never re-implemented), integer-only amount bounds,
insufficient-funds with real figures, dust/ZIP-317 fees, the §5.1 de-shield disclosure, the
live recipient classifier + memo gating + 512-char cap (S100). These checks are USER-ERROR
hardening on top of that, NOT money gates. **Design principle (founder: "foolproof, no alert
fatigue"):** passive inline cues for the common case + EXACTLY ONE deliberate-friction confirm
reserved for the rare high-risk event (a large amount). Never a modal that fires routinely —
users must not be trained to dismiss everything.
- **Large-amount confirm — `SendProposal.large_send: Option<LargeSendReason>`.** `Some` ⇒ the
  host shows one deliberate confirm before signing; `None` ⇒ an ordinary send. Computed SDK-side
  at propose from `total_zat` (the audited debit) vs the AVAILABLE balance = shielded spendable +
  transparent (the pools the `GreedyInputSelector` draws from, ADR-0528 — so a transparent-funded
  send whose total exceeds the shielded balance can't trip a FALSE near-total alert), read from the
  same `spendable_policy` SSOT the balance uses, under the proposal's lock so the figure can't drift
  from the notes it selected. Trips on the RELATIVE (`≥ NEAR_TOTAL_SPENDABLE_BPS` = 90% of available,
  strictly < 100% so it fires before a full drain — "sending almost everything", the
  drain/fat-finger case) OR the ABSOLUTE (`≥ LARGE_SEND_ABSOLUTE_ZAT` = 1 ZEC,
  a tunable policy backstop), **whichever first** (founder S109); `LargeSendReason::{NearTotalBalance,
  OverAbsoluteThreshold, Both}` keys the host copy. Integer-only (`classify_magnitude`, i128 so
  the `× 10_000` can't overflow a near-max total). Always `None` for a shield (a self-output, not
  a parting-with-funds send).
- **Self-send note — `SendProposal.self_send: bool`.** A passive INFO cue ("sending to yourself;
  the fee still applies"), never a blocker (a self-send is money-safe, just usually unintended).
  Best-effort by design (`is_self_send`): an EXACT match of any recipient leg against the wallet's
  current unified address (the common pasted-my-own-address case); a diversified / sub-receiver
  own-address is NOT detected — a scoped v1 limitation, upgradeable to a full ownership test. A
  `current_address` read fault just omits the note — never fails the propose.
- **Foolproof address review — HOST-side, no SDK change.** The review echo renders the recipient
  in equal-weight, space-separated 4-char MONOSPACE chunks (verification, not read-only display) so
  a typo or clipboard-hijack is catchable glyph-by-glyph — passive, no extra tap. AS BUILT it reuses
  the shared `AddressVerificationText` brick (`lib/shared/address_text.dart`), which the swap
  refund-verification step ALSO uses (one source of truth — the prior duplicate `_chunked` was
  folded in); deliberately NON-selectable (a copy would capture the render-only spaces — a
  paste-back footgun), with the FULL ungrouped address as the screen-reader label. The companion
  `AddressText` (bold head+tail) stays for read-only DISPLAY (receive / deposit address).
- **DEFERRED — first-send-to-new-recipient.** Founder S109: on a rotating-address privacy wallet
  most sends look "new" ⇒ the cue would fire often and train dismissal. Revisit when a contacts /
  address-book exists (Relim is a messenger — the natural tie-in), so it means "payee not in your
  contacts" rather than noise.

**Named tests (this slice):** `classify_magnitude_trips_on_relative_or_absolute_whichever_first`
(the money math at BOTH thresholds incl. the exact-90% / exact-1-ZEC boundaries, the Both case,
zero-spendable degeneracy, and i128 overflow-safety at max supply),
`is_self_send_exact_matches_the_wallets_own_address` (match / different-recipient / empty), the
`NEAR_TOTAL_SPENDABLE_BPS` + `LARGE_SEND_ABSOLUTE_ZAT` value+range pins in
`named_constants_at_boundary`. **DEVICE/funded-GATED (owed):** the `propose`-wiring integration
(a real funded large send sets `large_send`; a real self-send sets `self_send`) — same posture
as the existing funded propose→sign→broadcast E2E. **FFI SURFACE CROSSED (the host adopts it):**
both fields now cross the bridge — the Dart `SendProposal` carries `largeSend: LargeSendReason?` +
`selfSend: bool` (FRB bindings regenerated; `LargeSendReason` registered in the
`bridge_enums_cover_core_variants` lockstep; pinned by
`send_proposal_money_safety_signals_cross_the_bridge`). The `zec_wallet` README documents the
signals as a consumer design rule. **HOST UI SHIPPED (S110, pure host Dart over the crossed DTO,
no SDK change):** the send confirm screen (`send_screen.dart` `_SendReviewView`) now (a) renders the
recipient via the shared `AddressVerificationText` brick; (b) shows a passive `_SelfSendNote` when
`selfSend`; (c) interposes EXACTLY ONE deliberate confirm dialog (`_showLargeSendConfirm`) before
signing when `largeSend != null`, reason-keyed copy (`_largeSendBody`, wildcard default → strongest
copy so a future `LargeSendReason` variant fails safe). **MONEY-SAFETY DECISION: the confirm fires
whenever `largeSend != null`, NEVER suppressed on sync/settle state** — over-firing (a mid-scan
in-flight-change send transiently reading near-total) is the SAFE direction (one extra tap), whereas
suppressing on an "unsettled" guess could hide a genuine near-total send; the rare over-fire is
mitigated upstream by the spend-before-sync gating (#228), so a real warning is never traded away.
Host named tests (`send_screen_test.dart` + `address_text_test.dart`): ordinary send signs in ONE
tap (no dialog); a large send interposes the dialog and signs NOTHING until confirm; BOTH cancel
paths (the Cancel button → `false` AND a barrier dismiss → `null`) send nothing; the reason→copy
mapping per variant (incl. the `unknown`→strongest fallthrough); the self-send note present/absent;
`groupAddress` loss-free + boundary cases; `AddressVerificationText` non-selectable + full-address
a11y label + em-dash-on-empty. Constants are tunable product policy (raise `LARGE_SEND_ABSOLUTE_ZAT`
if it fires on routine sends — alert-fatigue is the explicit constraint). **DEFERRED (recorded):**
(1) the **offline-queue path carries NO large-amount confirm** — `queue_send` defers proposing to
send-time, so there is no `largeSend` signal (and no fee preview) at queue time; a host-side guess
would duplicate `classify_magnitude` and put money logic in Dart (forbidden — Rust owns the money
decision), so any offline large-amount guard must live SDK-side (a `queue_send`-time classification)
— an SDK/spec question, not a host defect. (2) the device/funded `propose`-wiring integration (owed,
above) is what proves the SIGNAL on a real funded large/self send; the host UI tests prove the
RENDERING + gating over the crossed DTO. (3) `send_screen.dart` is now >500 lines (pre-existing,
worsened ~87 lines) — track a split of the confirm-review concern into a `send_review.dart` sibling.
**2nd-round operational pass (building-bricks ∥ ZODL ∥ unstable-net/mobile/money ∥ real-world-edge):
PASS on all lenses; folded a PRE-EXISTING mobile money-display bug** — the shared `LabeledZatRow`
(send review + shield sheet) was a fixed-width row that OVERFLOWED on a 320px phone, clipping a money
figure; the label now `Flexible`+ellipsizes so the AMOUNT is never clipped — plus a honest-degradation
**copy fix**: `ProposalStale` thrown from the SEND `confirm()` (the anchor aged out while the user
deliberated in the large dialog — now more likely) maps to a NEW `SendFaultReason.amountsExpired`
("the amounts expired — review again"), distinct from the propose-path `notSyncedYet` (can't-anchor →
offline-queue). +7 real-world-edge tests (stale-after-approve can't bypass the SDK gate; large+transparent
co-render; large+self-send; cancel-then-re-tap completes; the irreversible amount un-clipped at 2.5× scale;
a 78-char address chunked on a 320px screen; the new surfaces under dark theme). Deferred (NOT folded —
scope): a shared `confirmDialog -> Future<bool?>` brick (4 bespoke `showDialog<bool>` confirms now exist).

**AS BUILT (S65 — inc-2d-2, the create+sign CORE; `zec-wallet-core::send` +
`derivation::derive_spending_key`; full crypto-change review):**
- **Scope realized = the tested money-signing CORE; the prover-PACKAGING + public
  wiring DEFERRED + flagged.** `create_signed_core<DbT, P>(wdb, params, usk, proposal,
  spend_prover, output_prover) -> NonEmpty<TxId>` is generic over DB + network EXACTLY
  like `propose_core` (the funded `LocalNetwork` harness and the live `Network` wallet
  run the SAME code), and takes the Sapling spend/output provers **injected** — so the
  production prover-source is a wiring decision, not a core one. It runs the audited
  `data_api::wallet::create_proposed_transactions` with `OvkPolicy::Sender` (the sender
  can decrypt its own outputs for history, §3.2h decision 1) and the transient USK; the
  engine PERSISTS every built tx via `store_transactions_to_be_sent` BEFORE returning
  (verified by reading the pinned upstream — the §6.3 persist-before-submit is the
  engine's, confirmed not assumed). Returns the persisted `TxId`s (not yet broadcast —
  that is 2d-3). `#[allow(dead_code)]` until the public `send` wires it (the established
  build-the-tested-core-then-wire pattern, as `Retained.proposal` was for 2d-1).
- **The RE-ANCHOR guard `assert_proposal_anchor_fresh` — the discharged suspend
  obligation.** The upstream `Builder` sets tx expiry = `proposal.min_target_height +
  DEFAULT_TX_EXPIRY_DELTA` (40 blocks, verified in `zcash_primitives::transaction::
  builder`) and does NOT consult the live tip; upstream errors ONLY on a *pruned*
  anchor, never a merely-*stale* one. So a suspend-resumed proposal (the monotonic TTL
  paused — §3.2h consume SAFETY-OBLIGATION) whose chain advanced would build a
  BORN-EXPIRED tx (funds locked to the dead expiry height — §6.2) and upstream would not
  catch it. The guard runs FIRST, before any key is derived: it compares
  `proposal.min_target_height` against `wdb.chain_height()` and rejects `ProposalStale`
  (re-propose) when the chain has advanced past `min_target_height +
  PROPOSAL_ANCHOR_DRIFT_MAX_BLOCKS` — `20`, half the 40-block expiry window, so a signed
  tx always keeps ≥ 20 blocks of mining headroom. A wallet with no recorded chain tip
  (`chain_height() == None`, not synced) is also `ProposalStale` (sync first). This
  DISCHARGES the reserved `proposal_resumed_after_suspend_must_reanchor_at_send` (now
  height-driven + green): mine past the drift window → `ProposalStale`, never a
  born-expired signed tx. The realistic protection is the post-resume sync case (the DB
  learns the new tip, the guard sees the drift); the immediately-after-resume-before-sync
  residual (DB tip still stale, guard can't see the drift) degrades to the engine's
  expiry + the §6.2 resubmission/expiry machinery — no fund loss, an honest expiry.
- **Transient USK (§4.2 confinement) = `derivation::derive_spending_key(network,
  seed)`.** Reuses the audited `UnifiedSpendingKey::from_seed` whole (Rule Zero), behind
  the SAME `32..=252` bounds re-enforcement the address-derivation door uses (a < 32-byte
  seed PANICS `from_seed`; both ends return typed `InvalidSeedLength`, so a panic across
  FFI is structurally impossible). The USK is returned to the caller, which keeps it
  STRICTLY function-local inside the `spawn_blocking` proving closure — never stored,
  never held across an `.await`, never placed in any struct (no `Debug`-reachable
  container), wrapped into `SpendingKeys::from_unified_spending_key` and dropped at the
  closure's end. The un-zeroized residue is the documented §4.2(a) residual (upstream
  `UnifiedSpendingKey` has no `Zeroize`).
- **Errors — NEW `SignFailed` (RW-SEND-006), reuse the rest.** Payload-free, fail-closed
  for any proving/build/key/structural fault (the builder's error value can echo amounts
  AND a txid via `ChainDoubleSpend` — §5.4 — so it is DROPPED, never formatted).
  `Error::DataSource → StoreCorrupt` (the one corruption door). The STALE class — where
  re-`propose` is the honest recovery — is PRECISELY a reorg-pruned anchor
  (`Proposal(AnchorNotFound)`) or a pruned witness/checkpoint (`CommitmentTree`, a
  `ShardTreeError`) → `ProposalStale` (the arch review narrowed this from a blanket
  `Proposal(_)`: the OTHER `ProposalError` variants — double-spend / multi-step /
  transparent / ephemeral — are structurally unreachable for this build's single-step
  shielded proposals AND a re-`propose` would not fix them, so suggesting it would be
  dishonest). Everything else — proving/build faults, the structural proposal variants,
  AND `Error::KeyNotRecognized` (the USK's UFVK ≠ the account's — impossible on the
  production seed-derived path, a defense-in-depth LOUD catch otherwise, never a silent
  wrong-key sign) → `SignFailed`. Mirrored to the bridge `WalletErrorKind` + Dart (FRB
  regenerated). `map_create_err` is precision-pinned by `map_create_err_routes_stale_vs_signfailed`.
- **Tests** (funded harness, prover = `LocalTxProver::bundled()` — a DEV-dep; see the
  packaging note): a single-note sign round-trip (a REAL persisted tx — its `TxId` is
  read back from the DB, proving the engine's store-before-return), a multi-note sign
  (the selector aggregates, the signed tx spends both), the re-anchor reject (the
  discharged reserved obligation), the drift BOUNDARY at `PROPOSAL_ANCHOR_DRIFT_MAX_BLOCKS`
  (one block inside signs, one past is `ProposalStale`), and `derive_spending_key` bounds
  (typed reject at 31/253, the §4.2(b) panic guard). `zcash_proofs` stays OUT of the
  shipped graph this slice (supply-chain gate holds — verified).
- **⚠️ THE PROVER-PACKAGING DECISION (flagged for the founder — the production
  prover-source).** Spending Sapling notes needs the Groth16 proving params (~50 MB:
  `sapling-spend.params` ≈ 47 MB + `sapling-output.params` ≈ 3.5 MB). G7 REQUIRES a
  Sapling receiver on our default UA, so Sapling funds WILL arrive and MUST be spendable —
  the Sapling prover is unavoidable for a complete wallet (Orchard spends use Halo2, no
  external params). Three options, each a real product tradeoff: **(1) bundle in the Rust
  staticlib** (`zcash_proofs/bundled-prover`, `LocalTxProver::bundled()`) — simplest, but
  +~50 MB to EACH platform binary (significant for a messenger that already ships the
  Relim core); **(2) host Flutter asset + `LocalTxProver::new(spend_path, output_path)`** —
  ~50 MB in the app bundle but out of the Rust lib, on-demand/deferred-asset loadable,
  the SDK takes paths via config; **(3) verified download-once** (`from_bytes` after a
  hash-pinned fetch of the canonical ECC params) — smallest install, but a NEW
  hostile-network + integrity-verification surface that itself needs a crypto-change review.
  §3.2h decision 1 locked "bundled proving parameters" but did not quantify the size cost;
  this is the founder's call (it shapes app size, first-run UX, and the supply chain)
  before the production `Wallet::send` + the FFI land. The injected-prover core makes the
  choice a localized wiring change with zero core churn.

**AS BUILT (S66 — inc-2d-2 production WIRING; prover packaging = BUNDLE; `zec-wallet-core::
prover` + `Wallet::sign_proposal`):**
- **Prover packaging DECIDED — BUNDLE (founder 2026-06-20).** `zcash_proofs` is now a
  PRODUCTION dependency (`bundled-prover`, `default-features = false`, `=0.28.0`) — the
  ~50 MB Sapling Groth16 params (the immutable 2018 trusted-setup artifact) are embedded
  in the binary. Rationale (UX + maintainability): a censorship-resistant wallet must not
  put a network fetch of consensus-critical crypto on the money path — bundling is the only
  option with NO send-path failure mode (offline, first-try, no spinner), and it is one line
  (`LocalTxProver::bundled()`), zero new surface, an immutable artifact with no update
  lifecycle. The cost is install size (+~50 MB per platform binary, on top of the Relim
  core); the deferred-host-asset optimization (Flutter asset + `LocalTxProver::new(paths)`,
  mobile-only) stays open behind the injected-prover seam if size becomes a hard product
  constraint — a localized wiring change, not a rewrite. The verified-download option was
  REJECTED (a new hostile-network + integrity surface needing its own crypto-change review, for
  marginal install savings on an immutable artifact).
- **`prover::tx_prover() -> &'static LocalTxProver`** — the process-wide bundled prover,
  parsed ONCE on first use via `OnceLock` (the ~50 MB params deserialize in ~1–2 s) and
  shared for the process life; MUST be called inside `spawn_blocking` (the parse is CPU/alloc
  work, never on the async runtime / UI thread). Resident after first use (signing needs it
  every send; idle-drop is a future optimization). Audited crate WHOLE (Rule Zero).
- **`Wallet::sign_proposal(proposal_id) -> Vec<money::TxId>`** (`pub(crate)`) — the
  create+sign half of the public `send`. Returns the SDK-owned `money::TxId` (DISPLAY /
  block-explorer byte order) via the SSOT reversing `From<zcash_protocol::TxId>` added on

  reverses in `Display`; the conversion is done at THIS seam so the public `send` at 2d-3
  never raw-casts and silently byte-reverses every txid; KAT-pinned by
  `txid_from_upstream_reverses_internal_to_display_order` — the arch review fold). Order
  is load-bearing for money-safety: `require_open()` →
  **seed-present check** (`SeedRequired` if `inner.seed` is `None` — the Relim None-persistence
  path whose seed-resupply is W5 — BEFORE consuming, so a structural `SeedRequired` never
  BURNS the one-shot token) → **`consume`** (the registry one-shot; `ProposalAlreadyUsed` on a
  double-tap, `ProposalStale` past TTL) → `spawn_blocking { derive the transient USK from
  `inner.seed` INSIDE the closure (§4.2 confinement now LOAD-BEARING in code — never across an
  `.await`, never stored), lock the db, `create_signed_core` (re-anchor + sign + persist) }`.
  A `create_signed_core` failure (a re-anchor `ProposalStale`, `SignFailed`, `StoreCorrupt`)
  consumes-and-discards the token — correct: the engine persists txs only on FULL success
  (no notes spent on failure → re-`propose` cleanly; never a double-spend). The public `send`
  (2d-3) = `sign_proposal` THEN broadcast; the §6.2 outbox/resubmission makes the persisted-
  but-unbroadcast tx eventually reach the network.
- **The create+sign chain is reached by `sign_proposal`** (`create_signed_core`,
  `derivation::derive_spending_key`, `ProposalRegistry::consume`, `Retained.proposal`); the
  `#[allow(dead_code)]` annotations STAY and now name `sign_proposal` — the whole chain is
  unreachable from the PUBLIC API until the public `send` wires `sign_proposal` at 2d-3, so a
  lib-only build still sees it as dead (the established build-the-tested-core-then-wire
  pattern). `Retained.request` stays dead-code-until the 2d-3 re-propose path.
- **Tests + the E2E-owed gap (honest scope).** The orchestration paths are unit-tested on a

  token-not-burned). **The FUNDED end-to-end (`propose → sign_proposal → persisted` on a live
  handle) is OWED-TO-E2E**, NOT skipped: the `data_api::testing` harness funds only a
  `LocalNetwork` (Regtest) DB, while the live `Wallet` is structurally `Network` (Main/Test) —
  type-incompatible by construction, so a funded full-`Wallet` is unreachable in a unit test.
  The signing LOGIC is covered by `create_signed_core_*` on the harness; the seed→account
  key-match (the load-bearing money property — the wallet's own seed derives the USK that
  owns the funded notes) by `derive_spending_key_matches_the_account_address` +

- **Operational pass (money-reliability ∥ mobile/unstable ∥ edge-design — a distinct
  adversarial round beyond the pre-commit review): NO code defect, +5 real-world money edge

  SEQUENTIALLY — the actual double-broadcast boundary is concurrent. Added
  `consume_admits_exactly_one_under_concurrent_double_tap` (N threads barrier-race `consume`,
  exactly one Ok — the laggy-phone double-tap; testing-patterns mandates a concurrent test for
  a thread-safe type), `create_signed_core_anchors_a_mineable_future_expiry` (the re-anchor's

  never born-expired), `create_signed_core_signs_a_deshield_to_transparent` (the exchange-
  t-address off-ramp THROUGH signing — a distinct transparent-output prover path the
  propose-only de-shield test never exercised), `create_signed_core_max_send_signs_to_completion`
  (the "send everything" minimal-change builder edge), and `sign_proposal_rejects_during_teardown`
  (the most money-critical method now has the same Closing⇒`WalletBusy`/Wiped⇒`InvalidState`
  teardown gate every sibling key-method has — `require_open` fires BEFORE seed-check/consume,
  a non-burning reject). Doc folds: the §6.3 consume→persist kill-window is documented lossless
  (the registry is non-durable by design — a token is a transient UX handle; the audited engine
  marks-spent + persists in ONE tx, so no note is ever spent-but-unbroadcast); a suspend DURING
  proving is latency-only (no clock/TTL consulted after the start-of-call re-anchor — do NOT add
  a post-proving freshness re-check); the `close` "sole holder" claim clarified (by-value `self`
  + `stop()`-first ⇒ no `&self` blocking task or sync clone can be in flight — the in-flight-sign-
  vs-close race is structurally UNREACHABLE, not merely unlikely). **366 → 371 lib tests.**

**Transport / offline / desktop (lands at 2d-3, flagged now):** broadcast rides the
host `NetDialer` exactly as sync does (§3.2a), so `TorPolicy::Required` fail-closes
identically; the outbox is the offline-first heart (§6.2 — queued is NORMAL, not an
error); desktop carries the same outbox (a desktop that never backgrounds still
queues + resubmits on reconnect, the §6.2 retry-forever loop); the host send UI is a
confirm-then-queue flow (§6.3 UX corollary: honest "queued → sent", never
fake-instant).

### 3.3 The public Dart surface (pre-1.0; the package's whole API)
