**inc-D-1 AS BUILT — the swap FFI method surface (the bridge half of the facade).**
flutter_rust_bridge has no clean way to mirror a nullable `SwapService` sub-object,
so — exactly like the §3.3 send methods (`propose`/`send`/`queueSend`) — the four
swap operations are flat methods on the opaque `WalletHandle`, and the hand-written
Dart facade (D-2) groups them into the `swap` getter (returning `null` purely as a
Dart-side concern: the host knows whether it called `enableNearSwap`). The bridge
methods:

- `enableNearSwap(SwapProviderConfig config, bool swapEnabled, SwapKill? declaredKill)`
  — the §3.5 composition entry. The method is ALWAYS present (the Dart surface is stable
  across feature flavors — FRB's generated dispatcher can't honor a method-level `cfg`); its
  body is `swap-near`-gated, so a build WITHOUT the adapter degrades honestly to kill-layer-1
  `SwapDisabled` (not one byte of the adapter ships). Constructs the NEAR provider over the
  wallet's OWN transport (`Wallet::swap_dialer`,
  ADR-0526 — no independent egress; internal Tor optional), attaches it set-once behind the
  kill door, and lowers `(swapEnabled, declaredKill)` through `resolve_manifest_kill` into
  `set_kill` (monotonic-toward-off — a forged "on" can only ever be more-off). `config.jwt`
  is an optional provider auth token (a §5.4 NEVER-log value); it is wrapped `Zeroizing`
  in Rust at the boundary and never logged. NO provider is attached on any failure
  (stays at kill layer 2, Dart `swap == null`).
- `swapQuote(QuoteRequest) → SwapQuote`, `swapExecute(SwapQuote) → String` (the SwapId —
  since S293 the SDK-minted opaque handle, ADR-0555; the same value as `SwapQuote.id`,
  `SwapRecord.id` and `watchSwapStatus`'s argument, never the provider's deposit address),
  `watchSwapStatus(String swapId) → Stream<SwapStatus>`. `swapExecute` passes the whole
  `SwapQuote` DTO back (the spec-literal `execute(SwapQuote)`), which is LEAST-AUTHORITY-
  equivalent to the `send(proposalId)` token: the core `execute` PEEKS the durable record and
  compares the DTO's terms (deposit address and memo, amounts, refund, the deadline shown at
  approval) and binding to it field-by-field — a difference is typed `QuoteTermsDiffer`
  (`RW-SWAP-016`) with nothing consumed and no provider call — then claims the durable
  single-flight `issued_store.take(&quote.id)` (W-swap-3-c-3-ii), so a forged id has
  no durable claim ⇒ typed `RequestInvalid` before the provider is ever called, and the
  wallet's §4.4 deposit send uses the durable re-blessed row, NEVER the DTO ⇒ a forged
  `depositAddress`/amount cannot redirect funds (TRUE OF EVERY TERM since S293 — before
  ADR-0555 the deposit PLAN came from an in-memory registry that overwrote on a reused
  provider address, so within one process `execute(&first)` paid the second quote's amount:
  the 2026-09-20 review's R01). `watchSwapStatus` rides the `watchSyncStatus`
  StreamSink template (the core owns the detached §7 poll pump; the bridge holds no runtime,
  no lock for the stream's life); the `swapId` is size-capped at the boundary (`PROVIDER_STR_MAX_BYTES`)
  so a garbage id fails fast typed, never a forever-retrying stream. A closed handle ⇒
  `SwapStateUnavailable`; no provider attached ⇒ `SwapDisabled` (kill layer 2). `history()`
  is OWED (no core swap-history read yet — a separate core slice; swap history is a local
  encrypted-store read, readable even when swap is killed).

**inc-D-2b-1 AS BUILT — the host swap SCREEN (reference app).** The Dart UI over the
D-2a facade: an **OutOfZec** form (curated asset menu, exact ZEC in, destination)
[SUPERSEDED S103 — the curated `referenceSwapAssets` dropdown is replaced by the
shared dynamic token picker (`swapListTokens`, the same brick IntoZec uses) + a
destination QR scanner, making OutOfZec symmetric with IntoZec; §3.3b L8], a quote
review that renders `SwapPrivacyDisclosure` as **blocking UX** (the §2.6 disclosures-as-data
decision realized — the de-shield warning + EVERY `provider_sees` item incl. a forward-compat
`Unknown`, never dropped, + a required acknowledgment that gates execute), and live tracking
via the D-2a status notifier. The §3.5 host-renders-"tracking unavailable" obligation is
satisfied at the UI from a host kill-state SSOT (`swapEnabledProvider`, default OFF — no swap
surface until the host enables it; UI isolation) (superseded by inc-D-2b-2: `swapEnabledProvider`
now DERIVES from the activation outcome, with no settable default). The wallet snapshot is invalidated at the
EXECUTE money-movement transition so the balance is honest however the user leaves. OutOfZec
only this cut; IntoZec + a user-tunable slippage are follow-ons.

**inc-D-2b-2 AS BUILT — the swap COMPOSITION WIRING (reference app).** The host wiring that
makes the on-ramp go live, host Dart only (no Rust/FFI/crypto). A host-policy seam
`SwapHostPolicy{config(endpoint, jwt?), enabled, declaredKill}` (mirroring the wallet config
policy) is overridden at the composition root (`walletSwapOverrides()` in `main`); a one-time
activation provider calls `enableNearSwap` exactly once a real session exists (the money-safety
gate) and re-fires only on a NEW handle (`Wallet::enable_swap` is `OnceLock` first-wins, so a
superseded mid-flight enable cannot double-construct). **Every** enable failure — no policy,
host-disabled, `SwapDisabled` (no adapter compiled in), `providerUnavailable`, or an untyped
bridge error — **honest-degrades to swap-OFF**, logging only the coarse error code (§5.4 — the
JWT, a NEVER-log provider credential, never appears). `swapEnabledProvider` now **derives** from
that enable OUTCOME (not a hand-set bool), so the §3.5 kill-state SSOT is money-honest by
construction: the swap surface shows iff the provider genuinely constructed. The D-2b-1 owed
**teardown-on-kill** is satisfied: `SwapStatusNotifier.build` watches `swapEnabledProvider`, so a
kill flip re-runs build → `onDispose` cancels the poll → no re-subscribe (honest-off STOPS the
traffic, not just the indicator; required because the notifier is non-autoDispose and would
otherwise outlive the screen). A latent sync-stream defect was fixed in the same change: the live
`SyncStatus` notifier now resets its per-build state, so a session close/reopen can still
reconnect after a fault (without it a reopened wallet showed a STALE balance forever — a
money-honesty fix). NOTE for W5: a FUTURE dynamic (manifest-driven) swap policy must emit a
STABLE/debounced value, else policy flicker would churn the status-poll teardown. **Still owed
(device-gated):** the device real-`StreamSink` e2e (`selftest_watch_swap_status` over
`MockSwapProvider`) — its own sub-slice (it needs new public selftest scaffolding around
`SwapService` + FRB regen + a device). (The former "verify the curated asset ids against the
live 1Click registry" owed-item is RESOLVED S103 — there is no curated list; the picker sources
`/v0/tokens` directly, so the asset ids ARE the live registry.)

**Lifecycle & stream contracts (the unstable-environment rules):**

- The handle has a small state machine — `Provisioning / Repairing / Open /
  Closing / Wiped`. API calls in the wrong state get typed `WalletBusy` /
  `InvalidState` (send during a repair is an error the UI can render, not a
  race); `close()` resolves in-flight futures with `Closing`;
  `wipe` refuses while an instance is open.
- **`Wiped` is reachable by the duress sever from ANY phase** (FR-53, stage
  S16, ADR-0565): `sever_custody` poisons every live instance at the path
  (`sever_poison`, beside `transition`, not an edge of it), and from then on
  each call answers `InvalidState { Wiped }`. `begin_close` leaves a `Wiped`
  instance `Wiped` (the close still drains and frees the lock), never the
  retryable `Closing`. The **birth gate** refuses a new
  `Inner` at a tombstoned path, so a rescan, a server switch or an open in
  flight answers `Wiped` instead of coming back working; `create`/`open` there
  answer `Wiped` until a plain `wipe` of the path completes or the process
  exits (the path table and its tombstones are per process).
- **Single-writer, exclusive:** one `Wallet` per DB, enforced in-process AND
  cross-process (O_EXCL-style lock); the second opener gets typed
  `WalletAlreadyOpen` — "rejected or safe" is not a contract, rejected IS the
  contract. (SDK consumers: no multi-process DB sharing in v1; Relim's
  no-NSE-access posture in §9 is the same rule from the other side.)
- **Streams never error and never spontaneously complete** — they complete
  only on `close()`; internal faults surface as data (`Stalled`), because a
  dead stream is a silent hang. State streams coalesce (latest-wins).
  `watchIncomingFunds` replays ONE counts+heights catch-up event from the
  host's cursor (ADR-0536); its items carry a WATERMARK cursor, not the
  `WalletState.seq` stamp (§2.5 — the arrival stream is a freshness signal;
  `seq` orders the DB-derived snapshot surfaces). SECOND named exception to
  never-error (AS BUILT, S210): `watchIncomingFunds` rejects a malformed
  `sinceCursor` TYPED (`storeCorrupt`) at subscribe — the stream itself still
  never errors mid-flight.
  - **The ONE exception — `watch(swapId)` (the swap status stream) DOES
    complete**, because a swap is a finite job: the core poll loop (§7) ends it
    on a TERMINAL status (success/refunded/failed, emitted first), a Hard kill
    (§3.5), or wallet teardown — and (unlike a sync stream) it RETRIES transport
    faults internally, so it NEVER completes on a recoverable drop. Host contract
    (inc-D-2a, the cross-layer correctness `SwapStatusNotifier` proves): a swap
    status consumer must therefore treat a completion as INTENTIONAL — latch the
    terminal outcome, or, on a pre-terminal completion (Hard kill / teardown),
    render "tracking unavailable" from its OWN kill state (§3.5; the stream has no
    wire signal for it) — and MUST NOT reconnect-on-completion (a reconnect would
    re-spawn the poll the kill just stopped). Re-subscription is foreground-resume
    only.

**The explicit NON-surface (brief §6 item 2):** no seed/spending-key/viewing-key
getter, no raw-transaction signing, no `Uint8List` that contains key material,
no key-export of any kind. `revealMnemonic` is the single sanctioned outbound
exception (third-party backup; structurally impossible for Relim wallets).
Inbound, `restore`'s mnemonic crossing Dart→Rust is the sanctioned inbound
exposure (identical framing to identity-core §6: Dart memory can't be
zeroized; minimal residency; documented).

### 3.2i The Send expert layer — richer pool management (W3-inc-2e; founder 2026-06-24)

The everyday Send already crosses pools — the recipient ADDRESS is the pool
selector (a transparent recipient fires the §5.1 de-shield disclosure; more
foolproof than a per-send toggle). The expert layer adds DELIBERATE, WARNED
pool-management ACTIONS for power users + exchange interop. The founder's design
rule (S103): versatility via explicit Shield ⇄ Move-to-transparent actions +
multi-step + coin-control — NEVER a casual per-send shielded/transparent toggle
(a privacy footgun; the address already decides). De-shielding always reveals the
AMOUNT on-chain regardless of destination — the honesty caveat every slice surfaces.

Decomposed into 5 independently-shippable slices, smallest / lowest-new-trust first:

1. **Move to transparent (inc-2e-1, BUILT — §3.2i-1)** — deliberate de-shield of a
   chosen amount to the wallet's OWN transparent address; the mirror of the Recv-3
   Shield action. Host-only, ZERO new Rust (reuses the audited propose→send whole).
2. **TEX / ZIP-320 (inc-2e-2, §3.2i-2 — 2e-2a LANDED S123, slice B mechanism S124, B3 #4/#5 S125, B3 interactive enrolment S126; SIGNING still gated)** — multi-step
   pool-crossing to TEX addresses (the genuine versatility gap; exchanges increasingly
   use them). DISCOVERY corrected the original framing: the engine is feature-complete
   (auto-builds the 2-step ephemeral proposal; derivation engine-owned, NOT a crypto
   fan-out of new derivation) — the real work is the multi-txid outbox (DB migration) +
   N-tx persist-before-submit + the re-broadcast recovery + ephemeral detection. `summarize`
   now ACCEPTS the exact ZIP-320 shape (predicate-gated; the `>1-step` reject is lifted) and
   `create_signed_core` fail-closes signing until the slice-B persistence lands. Sub-sliced
   2e-2a (send + recovery — first half done) → 2e-2b (ephemeral detect).
3. **Transparent-UTXO viewer + selective shield (inc-2e-3, DEFERRED)** — per-UTXO
   list + shield-one-at-a-time (today's Recv-3 shields ALL transparent funds). Needs
   a new SDK read surface over the UTXO set. NEVER an external taint oracle (a
   privacy leak — the SDK never asks a third party which coins are "clean").
4. **Coin-control + send-unshielded (inc-2e-4, DEFERRED post-GA — founder S154)** — a
   constrained input surface over the audited engine. The one genuinely-NEW audited
   money surface; sequenced LAST, spec-first, full crypto review. **WIDENED S154:**
   the §3.2i-3 scouting proved the vendored engine cannot express ANY
   transparent-input transfer (t→t), so the S151 "send unshielded" capability needs
   the SAME custom `InputSelector` machinery — the two merge into ONE post-GA slice
   (task #332 holds the full design record; §3.2i-3 "engine discovery" has the
   ground truth). Founder decision S154: post-GA, demand-driven — NOT GA scope.
5. **Transparent-funds management (inc-2e-5, §3.2i-3 — S151 founder directive,
   calls confirmed S154)** — auto-shield default-ON + the expert gate + pool
   clarity: the engine-independent majority of the S151 directive, shippable
   now with ZERO new Rust money paths.

#### 3.2i-1 — Move to transparent (de-shield to own t-addr) — AS BUILT

**Design decision: ZERO new Rust.** Everything needed already crosses the bridge —
`currentTransparentAddress()` (Recv-2 / ADR-0528: the account external-scope P2PKH
t-addr), `composePaymentUri()` (lowers to the §2.4 ZIP-321 request), `propose()`
(the audited note-selection + fee + change; sets `has_transparent_recipient` ⇒ the
§5.1 de-shield disclosure), and `send()` (the one-shot token). So the slice is a
HOST flow that composes a payment to the wallet's OWN t-addr and runs the existing
audited propose→confirm→send. The destination is supplied BY THE SDK (not user
input), so there is no fat-finger address risk; it still rides the binding propose
path (re-parse / validate / network-check), so the SDK stays the SSOT (design
invariant 1). The slice touches NO seed/key surface — it is not a crypto-change review;
it is money + de-shield-touching, so the security ∥ arch ∥ crypto audit review
still gates it.

**Why a dedicated action (not the plain Send screen).** The founder's symmetric
pool-management model — Shield (public→private) ⇄ Move-to-transparent
(private→public) as two deliberate, well-warned actions. It lives in the wallet
OVERFLOW MENU (the "expert layer" home, alongside rescan-recovery), keeping the
everyday Send / Receive / Swap row clean. The Send screen stays
single-responsibility (lower risk to the audited send form); the new flow REUSES
its building blocks — the integer-only amount parser (`zec_amount`),
`SendOutcome`/`summarizeSendOutcome`, `LabeledZatRow`, and the shared
`DeshieldWarning` (lifted out of the send review so both render the identical §5.1
disclosure) — rather than duplicating any money logic.

**Flow** (a thin state machine mirroring the Recv-3 `ShieldController` — every
money step forwards straight to the SDK; no money state cached host-side):

- open → fetch `currentTransparentAddress()` under the receive-provider
  honest-degradation timeout (a wedged FFI → a RETRYABLE fault, never an infinite
  spinner) → **AmountEntry** showing the destination read-only (labeled "your
  wallet's transparent address") + the spendable-shielded cap hint.
- Review → `composePaymentUri(recipient: ownTAddr, amountZat, memoText: null)` then
  `propose(uri)` → **Ready(proposal)**. A transparent recipient carries NO memo
  (consistent with the send rule), so there is no memo field.
- Ready → the §5.1 de-shield disclosure FIRST (the shared `DeshieldWarning`,
  most load-bearing), an explicit own-address note ("moving to your OWN transparent
  address — the amount + address become PUBLIC and linkable on-chain; this can't be
  undone"), then the exact amount / fee / total rows; Confirm → `send(proposalId)`.
  The large-send confirmation still fires (the SDK's `largeSend` rides the proposal
  — money-safety unchanged, no alert fatigue added).
- terminal: the honest `SendOutcome` set (succeeded / saved-for-retry /
  already-submitted / sign-failed) via `summarizeSendOutcome` — a broadcast miss is
  "saved, re-sends on the next sync", never a lie, never a fund loss (the
  resubmission machinery owns it).

**De-shield disclosure is MANDATORY and load-bearing** (design invariant 5 —
metadata is as sensitive as content): de-shielding reveals the AMOUNT on-chain
regardless of destination, and a self-de-shield links the funds to the user's
reused transparent address. The action never auto-shields back; the inverse
(Recv-3 Shield) is the user's deliberate re-private step.

**Honest empty case:** with no spendable shielded balance the flow surfaces
"nothing to move yet" (never a dead spinner). **`Max` (de-shield ALL spendable) is
DEFERRED** — the user enters an explicit amount (KISS; an exchange deposit is a
specific number, and de-shielding everything would defeat privacy). §5.4 NEVER-LOG
holds throughout (the own t-addr is a never-log address; amounts are never-log; the
flow forwards opaque tokens and logs nothing sensitive).

**Tests.** Controller unit tests over a `FakeWalletSession`: own-addr fetch +
timeout-degradation; compose/propose/send happy path; insufficient-funds /
proposal-stale / wallet-unavailable typed faults; double-tap interlock;
dispose-after-await; zero-spendable honest path; de-shield always disclosed on
review. Sheet widget tests: amount gating, the de-shield warning present, the
outcome terminals. Cross-platform: pure Dart/Flutter, host-VM testable,
desktop-clean (no platform gates). **DEVICE-GATED:** the actual broadcast of a real
de-shield is the funded-device proof (same gate as every send/shield), recorded
owed in the e2e checklist.

**What TEX is (ZIP-320, Active).** A TEX ("transparent-source-only") address is a
Bech32m **re-encoding of an ordinary transparent P2PKH** — it carries exactly the
20-byte pubkey-hash a `t1…` address carries, nothing more (HRP `tex` mainnet /
`textest` testnet). It is the recipient (typically an exchange) signalling "pay me
ONLY from transparent inputs." ZIP-320 makes a normative **MUST**: a wallet spending
*shielded* funds to a TEX address creates **two transactions** — tx0 unshields to an
**ephemeral** transparent address the wallet controls, tx1 spends that ephemeral
output to the TEX destination. The privacy property: the exchange (which may run
chain-analysis) sees only a single-use throwaway t-addr as the source, **unlinkable**
(without the seed) to the wallet's persistent transparent activity or to other TEX
sends; the shielded origin stays hidden behind the unshield. Ephemeral addresses are
seed-derived ⇒ both unlinkable AND recoverable (the spec's other MUST: a wallet must
recognise + spend funds returned to an ephemeral address).

**THE KEY GROUNDING FACT — the engine already does the hard part (audited, whole).**
`transparent-inputs` is ON across the engine since ADR-0528/Recv-2b
(`zcash_client_backend`/`_sqlite`/`zcash_keys`/`zcash_transparent`). With it ON,
`zcash_client_backend 0.23.0`'s `propose_transfer` **automatically** synthesises the
2-step ephemeral proposal when a TEX recipient is in the ZIP-321 request (the feature
landed upstream in backend v0.13.0; no special flag) —
`GreedyInputSelector::propose_transaction` routes the TEX payment into a second
transaction set, allocates the ephemeral change, and returns `Proposal::multi_step`.
The ephemeral derivation is **engine-owned**: `zcash_transparent::TransparentKeyScope::EPHEMERAL = 2`
(BIP44 `m/44'/coin'/account'/2/i`, distinct from the EXTERNAL=0 receive/refund scope —
**no collision, no new wallet counter**), reserved by `zcash_client_sqlite 0.21.0`'s
`reserve_next_n_ephemeral_addresses` (gap limit 10, persisted in `ephemeral_addresses`,
called internally by `create_proposed_transactions`). So this slice is **NOT
hand-rolled crypto** — it ACTIVATES an audited path. The engine even enforces the
ZIP-320 MUSTs for us: `ProposalError::PaysTexFromShielded` rejects a single-step
shielded→TEX, `EphemeralOutputLeftUnspent` requires every ephemeral output be consumed
by a later step, `EphemeralAddressLinkability` rejects linkable ephemeral reuse. The
SDK's job is the **integration + money-safety + honest UX** around it, NOT the
derivation.

**The wallet-core work (the real surface — money-safety, not new crypto).**
> ⚠️ The spec-level review (crypto ∥ security ∥ arch) corrected an earlier draft that
> claimed the existing machinery "already handles" multi-step recovery. It does NOT.
> The *initial* broadcast loop is `Vec<TxId>`-ready, but the **resubmission/reconcile
> path is single-txid, re-propose-based, and queued-only** — so a half-broadcast 2-step
> send (tx0 mines, tx1 misses) has NO recovery on the interactive `send()` path and the
> funds become invisible. Points 4–6 below are the engineered fix; the "no new seam"
> claim is RETRACTED (a durable multi-step outbox IS a new internal seam).

1. **Accept multi-step — a single named shape predicate (the SSOT gate).** `send.rs:362`
   rejects `proposal.steps().len() > 1` `ProposeFailed`. Replace with a positive
   predicate `is_zip320_two_step(proposal) -> Option<Zip320Shape>` co-located at the top
   of `summarize` and REUSED by the total (pt 2), the claim (pt 4), and the persistence
   (pt 3). A step-count check is NOT sufficient (a future engine could synthesise a
   different 2-step). The predicate POSITIVELY asserts the engine's ZIP-320 output:
   exactly 2 steps; **step0** has shielded inputs + no transparent inputs + exactly one
   *ephemeral* transparent change output (`is_ephemeral()`); **step1** has
   `prior_step_inputs() == [StepOutput(0, Change(ephemeral_idx))]` — bound specifically to
   step0's **Change** output, NOT a `Payment` output (a step1 that consumed a step0
   *payment* could let "Σ all payments" double-count it — money-edge HARDENING) — plus
   `shielded_inputs().is_none()` + `transparent_inputs().is_empty()`, and **every step1
   `payment_pools` value is transparent** (the TEX/`Address::Tex` destination). Anything
   else (incl. arbitrary future multi-step) → `ProposeFailed`, fail-closed. **Mixed TEX +
   shielded in one request is the engine's NORMAL output** (it keeps the non-TEX payment in
   **step0**), so the all-transparent check applies to **step1 ONLY** — checking step0
   would wrongly reject a legal mixed send whose step0 carries the shielded recipient
   (crypto audit NIT). Property test: ONLY the exact shape passes; every near-miss rejects
   — incl. a step1 consuming a step0 `Payment`, a step1 with a shielded input, a 3-step, an
   unconsumed ephemeral output, a step1 paying a shielded recipient
   (`fuzz_transparent_validate` precedent).
2. **The total needs NO change; only `change_zat` does (corrected — money-edge BLOCKER
   on an earlier draft).** An earlier draft said `total = Σ payments of steps().last()`.
   That is WRONG: for a MIXED TEX+shielded send the engine puts the shielded recipient in
   **step0** and the TEX recipient in **step1**, so `steps().last()` drops the step0
   recipient and UNDER-displays the debit (the user confirms a smaller number than they
   send — and `large_send` inherits the undercount). The CORRECT total = `Σ recipient
   payments across ALL steps + Σ fees across all steps` — which is **exactly the current
   single-step loop already** (`send.rs:372-401`), with ZERO double-count risk: the
   ephemeral hop lives in `balance.proposed_change()` (flagged `is_ephemeral()`), NEVER in
   `transaction_request().payments()`, so the payments sum never sees it. So the payments
   loop is UNCHANGED. The ONLY real fix is **(b) `change_zat` MUST exclude the ephemeral
   hop** — `summarize` today sums ALL `proposed_change()`; left in, step0's ephemeral
   output (≈`recipient + fee1`) misreports in-transit money as "change returned to you"
   (a money-DISPLAY bug). Skip ephemeral change exactly as `summarize_shield` already does
   (`send.rs:561-563 if cv.is_ephemeral() { continue; }`). Named tests — a **MIXED** send
   is MANDATORY (a pure-TEX vector passes the buggy `last()` formula and hides the bug):
   `tex_mixed_total_includes_step0_shielded_recipient` +
   `tex_change_zat_excludes_the_ephemeral_hop`.
3. **Multi-txid persistence — ONE ordered column (the DB migration).** Today
   `queued_send_intent.txid` holds ONE id. Replace the dual-column temptation with a
   SINGLE ordered `txids BLOB` (`[txid(32)]×N`; single-step = `×1`) added via the
   additive path (`ensure_guard_columns` / `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`, idempotent,
   **NO `WALLET_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump** — the intent_store precedent; the
   `aux_tables_preserved_matches_what_migrate_creates` + `copy_aux_tables` guards
   updated) + `mark_sent_multi(conn, id, &txids)` in ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` txn
   (atomic, deadlock-free vs the engine's DEFERRED writer). **Reconcile reads ONLY
   `txids`** (never the legacy `txid`) so a multi-step row can't `AwaitWitness` forever
   on a NULL legacy field (security HARDENING). `InFlightIntent.txids: Vec<[u8;32]>`
   (unified; legacy single rows decode to `×1`).
4. **The 2-step recovery — re-broadcast SIGNED BYTES, delete-on-FINAL-mined (THE
   money-safety centre; redesigned per the review).** A 2-step send is NOT re-proposable
   (after tx0 spends the shielded notes, a fresh propose returns `InsufficientFunds` and
   mints a *different* ephemeral address — re-propose is structurally wrong). Recovery is
   re-broadcast of the ALREADY-SIGNED bytes (read back from the engine `WalletDb` by
   txid). Concretely:
   - **The interactive `send()` path MUST, for a 2-step proposal, enrol a durable outbox
     row** (the new seam): `mark_submitting` (claim = step0's shielded inputs — sound
     because `create_proposed_transactions` is all-or-nothing) → create+sign (engine
     persists BOTH txs unmined, atomically after building all) → `mark_sent_multi(both
     txids)` → THEN broadcast in step order. Single-step `send()` is UNCHANGED (its
     money-safety rests on shielded-note-expiry freeing a fresh re-send — a property the
     2-step LOSES because tx0 mining is irreversible, which is exactly why it must enrol).
   - **Type changes (named so the reconcile path is designed, not inferred):**
     `Recovery::ReBroadcast(Vec<TxId>)`, `Reconciled::Rebroadcast(Vec<Vec<u8>>)`.
   - **Re-broadcast is SKIP-MINED + NON-LATCHING (reliability BLOCKER — the headline
     recovery was broken as first written).** The initial broadcast latches on first
     failure (correct — tx1 truly cannot enter before tx0). A *re*-broadcast must NOT:
     re-submitting an already-mined-or-mempool tx0 returns a NON-zero code
     (`txn-already-known`/`already-in-mempool` → `SubmitOutcome::Rejected`), and the
     `broadcast_loop` first-failure latch would then mark tx1 `NotAttempted` and **never
     resend it** — exactly the tx0-mined / tx1-missed case the slice exists to fix. So the
     recovery broadcaster (a) SKIPS any step whose txid already mined (`get_tx_height(tx_i)
     .is_some()`), and (b) treats an "already-known/duplicate" rejection of an EARLIER step
     as *continue to the unmined tail*, never a latch — it must always reach tx1. This is a
     distinct broadcaster from `broadcast_loop`; do NOT reuse the latch verbatim.
     **[#307 (S144): the interactive `broadcast_loop` has since ADOPTED the Rejected-continues
     rule itself (only a transport miss latches) — the enrolled-`Sent`-before-broadcast row
     means the §1.7 pass can race the interactive call and make tx0 read already-known, the
     same shape this item fixed for recovery. The two broadcasters now differ in SHAPE
     (per-tx results vs tally + per-tx teardown re-checks), not latch rule.]**
   - **Delete-on-FINAL only:** the row clears when the LAST txid (tx1) mines — NEVER when
     tx0 mines (that would drop the tx1 obligation; today `reconcile` deletes on the single
     recorded txid — that delete must key on the FINAL txid).
   - **The whole queued/reconcile path goes multi-txid, gated on the predicate (reliability
     BLOCKER — silent truncation).** `prepare_queued` / `Prepared` / `reconcile` /
     `Reconciled` are single-txid today; a TEX 2-step would PASS `claim_from_proposal`
     (see the correction below), `create_signed_core` returns `[tx0, tx1]`, but
     `prepare_queued` records only `txids.first()` via `mark_sent` and broadcasts one —
     **tx1 persisted-but-never-recorded, then `reconcile` deletes the row on tx0-mine →
     tx1 stranded, suite still green.** All four must become multi-txid-aware AND gated on
     `is_zip320_two_step` so a multi-step proposal is NEVER silently truncated (it either
     takes the full multi-txid path or is `ProposeFailed`).
   - **The resubmit broadcast phase must order a multi-step intent's txs as a GROUP
     (reliability BLOCKER).** `resubmit_queued_sends` today flattens every intent's tx into
     one `Vec<Vec<u8>>` and deliberately does NOT latch (intents are independent). A TEX
     intent's tx0→tx1 DO have a spend dependency and must broadcast ordered; the design
     broadcasts per-intent as an ordered (skip-mined, non-latching) group while staying
     independent ACROSS intents.
   - **`claim_from_proposal` needs NO relaxation (false-alarm reversal — round-1
     overstated it).** Round-1 claimed step1's ephemeral spend is a `transparent_input`
     that trips the `!transparent_inputs().is_empty()` reject. It is NOT: the engine passes
     `transparent_inputs = vec![]` and the ephemeral as `prior_step_inputs = [ephemeral
     StepOutput]` (`input_selection.rs:1036-1045`), a SEPARATE accessor. So a TEX 2-step
     already PASSES `claim_from_proposal` (step0 supplies the shielded claim; step1
     contributes none, which the end-of-loop empties-check tolerates). Only the STALE
     COMMENT at `send.rs:774` is wrong (pt 7) — no code relaxation, and the witness
     correctly tracks step0's shielded notes (the real money source).
   - **tx0-expires-unmined branch:** the shielded notes free → reconcile re-proposes fresh
     from the persisted `uri` — but through the multi-txid `prepare_queued` above, NOT the
     truncating single-txid one. This is the only branch where re-propose is correct (no
     money has moved yet).
   - **The OFFLINE-QUEUE TEX path (UX/reliability HARDENING):** a queued TEX send drains
     later through the SAME multi-txid-enrolling path (never the truncating one), AND owes
     the §5.1 de-shield disclosure — queuing defers the fee preview, so the disclosure must
     be surfaced at QUEUE time (classification is already local/sync via
     `classifyRecipient`), or a queued TEX send moves money + goes public the user never
     saw disclosed.
   - Named tests: `tex_partial_broadcast_tx0_mined_tx1_missed_rebroadcasts_only_tx1` (the
     skip-mined non-latch), `tex_reconcile_deletes_only_on_final_txid_mined`,
     `tex_queued_drain_records_both_txids_not_just_the_first`,
     `tex_tx0_expired_unmined_reproposes_fresh`.
5. **Seed pulled ONCE (correction — NOT twice; load-bearing for the dynamic-module
   build).** `create_proposed_transactions` builds AND signs BOTH txs (the ephemeral-spend
   key for tx1 is derived from the SAME USK internally) in a single confined
   `spawn_blocking` call (one derivation, dropped at return — §4.2 unchanged); broadcast
   needs no key. There is NO "re-stage for tx1". This matters MORE under **the host's Relim ADR-0031 — the
   host (Relim) consumes the SDK as a SEPARATE DYLIB over a C-ABI**, not an in-workspace
   crate (zcash's pre-release RustCrypto can't share one cargo lock with the host's release
   ml-dsa). The seed-port crossing is then the **FR-15 C-ABI callback** (messenger-lib →
   wallet-lib, native→native, NEVER Dart), and a callback is a host credential gate +
   native seed crossing. Because TEX pulls once, it is exactly **ONE C-ABI callback → both
   signed txs** — never two. The seam is identical to the in-workspace `WalletSeedPort`
   (FR-12) the dylib reverts to if zcash → release RustCrypto (Relim ADR-0031 exit), so this
   holds in both builds.
6. **Stranded-ephemeral DETECTION is REQUIRED for v1 — not a follow-up (the silent-loss
   fix).** Re-broadcast (pt 4) covers the *transient* miss, but tx1 shares tx0's ~40-block
   expiry: if the wallet is offline past it, tx1 expires un-rebroadcastable and funds
   sit on the ephemeral t-addr — AND the scoped UTXO poll (§3.3b D2 = `{index-0 receive}
   ∪ {committed swap destinations}`) does NOT include scope-2 ephemeral addresses, so the
   balance is INVISIBLE (security CRITICAL: "never a silent loss" fails without this).
   v1 MUST wire the engine's ephemeral tracking (`get_known_ephemeral_addresses` — S133: the
   PROD read is `get_ephemeral_transparent_receivers`; that name is TEST-ONLY, see §3.2i-2
   ENGINE-READ CORRECTION) into a
   polled set and SURFACE the stranded **amount** (never the address) — covering both
   tx1-expired and exchange-RETURNED deposits. Auto-re-shield stays a follow-up
   (ECC/Zashi also ship detect-first). **The user-facing TEX send does NOT ship until
   detection is wired** (else the "in progress" copy hides stranded funds). Sub-sliced as
   **2e-2a** (multi-step send + re-broadcast recovery) → **2e-2b** (ephemeral detect +
   surface), both gating the user-facing feature.
   - **Privacy (§5 re-review, NOT deferred):** polling the ephemeral address on the
     wallet sync circuit would let the endpoint link it to the wallet — defeating the
     unlinkability ZIP-320 buys. The ephemeral UTXO query MUST use **per-ephemeral
     circuit isolation** (fresh isolation key, the §2.3 pattern), or carry a documented
     trade-off; the §3.3b D2 §5 vantage analysis is EXTENDED to cover scope-2 ephemerals.
7. **Comment de-stale — 3 CODE sites still assert the now-false "transparent-inputs
   OFF":** `send.rs:353-357` (the >1-step reject rationale), `send.rs:774` (the
   `claim_from_proposal` "transparent inputs are off … selecting NO shielded input is a
   structural fault" comment — stale ONLY as a comment: the code already handles the TEX
   shape unchanged, since step1's ephemeral spend is a `prior_step_inputs` StepOutput not a
   `transparent_input`, and step1's empty shielded contribution is tolerated by the
   end-of-loop empties-check — NO code relaxation), and
   `intent_store.rs:225-227` (the `NoteClaim` "only two shielded tags" comment). The spec
   §3.2h site (~line 3823) is already de-staled in this changeset.

**UI / host placement — Send-INTEGRATED, address-driven (the design fork; RECOMMENDED,
arch-confirmed).** A TEX address is *an address* — the ONLY way to pay a `tex1…` is to
put it in a payment. ZIP-320 + the canonical reference (Zashi, same librustzcash stack)
treat it that way: the user pastes the exchange's TEX address into the **normal Send
form** and the wallet does the 2-step transparently. This matches §3.2i's founding
principle — *the recipient address is the pool selector* — and is least-surprise (a user
who pastes a Coinbase `tex1…` should not have to discover a separate "expert" action).
So TEX lives in **Send**, NOT a new overflow flow. (Contrast move-to-transparent,
correctly a deliberate overflow ACTION: there the user de-shields their OWN funds, no
external payee — address can't drive it. TEX has an external payee and the address
dictates the flow.) The Send screen ALREADY routes a pasted TEX through
`classifyRecipient`→`composePaymentUri`→`propose` (parsed today via `memo.rs
try_from_tex` → `RecipientTransparent`, memo-incapable); the host detects the 2-step from
`proposal.steps.length > 1` (existing DTO field) — no new bridge surface. What changes is
the **review + outcome**:
  - **Review:** the §5.1 de-shield disclosure FIRES (transparent recipient), TEX-framed —
    "Exchanges accept only transparent deposits. Your wallet will unshield to a one-time
    address it controls, then forward to the exchange; the amount becomes public on-chain."
    Show the TEX recipient + the no-double-count total + the combined fee; the ephemeral
    hop is an honest footnote ("routed through a single-use address in your wallet"), not
    a second recipient to confirm. Large-send confirm + the shared `DeshieldWarning`
    (title/body override) reuse cleanly.
  - **Outcome — REUSE `SendSavedForRetry(broadcast,total)`, no new sealed variant** (arch
    HARDENING: a new `SendOutcome` subtype breaks the exhaustive `switch` in
    `move_to_transparent_sheet.dart`). The variant carries the partial info, but the
    `broadcast > 0 && broadcast < total` branch MUST get a DISTINCT terminal — **icon +
    title + body, not just body (UX BLOCKER).** The shipped partial rendering
    (`send_screen.dart` `cloud_off` icon + "Saved — we'll finish sending" + "part of your
    payment went out") is a MONEY-LOCATION LIE for a TEX partial: tx0 reaching the endpoint
    means the shielded notes are ALREADY irreversibly spent to a wallet-controlled ephemeral
    t-addr and the FULL amount moved — `cloud_off`/"Saved" reads as "offline, nothing
    happened" and "part went out" implies a fraction of the AMOUNT left, priming the user to
    **re-send and double-pay the exchange** (the form even offers "Send another"). For the
    TEX partial: an **in-motion icon** (e.g. `sync`/`hourglass`, NOT `cloud_off`), an **"In
    progress" title**, and body "Your funds already left your shielded balance and are
    routing through a one-time address your wallet controls; we'll finish the exchange
    transfer automatically — **don't send again.**" This is accept-PENDING (broadcast =
    endpoint *accept*, not mine), so NEVER assert "on-chain"/finality before a confirmation,
    AND reconcile with the stranded-detect surface (the "completing automatically" promise is
    only true inside the ~40-block window — once expired, 2e-2b's stranded-amount surface
    owns it). `broadcast == 0` ⇒ the existing "saved, nothing moved yet". `broadcast ==
    total` ⇒ succeeded. The branch keys on count ONLY because pt 1's predicate makes
    `total>1 ⟺ TEX 2-step` (everything else fail-closes) — pin that invariant at the copy
    site. The terminal also needs the `liveRegion` Semantics the move terminal has (a11y).
    `hasTransparentRecipient` + `selfSend` are correct BY CONSTRUCTION (both derive from
    `request.payments`, which excludes the ephemeral hop — it lives in `proposed_change`), so
    a TEX-to-exchange never shows "sending to your own wallet"; pin it with a test. New Dart
    no-PII test on the terminal (never a txid/address).
  - **Gap-limit + stranded-ephemeral need HONEST, ACTIONABLE copy (UX HARDENING).** The
    `ReachedGapLimit(EPHEMERAL)` ceiling (≤10 outstanding unmined TEX tx0s) needs a concrete
    `SendFaultReason` + user copy ("Too many exchange transfers are still confirming — wait
    for them to finish, then try again."), not the developer phrase "retry after recovery"
    nor a dead-end `couldNotPrepare`. A 2-fee insufficient-funds should note the exchange
    route costs an extra fee. The 2e-2b stranded-ephemeral surface MUST pin WHERE the amount
    appears and a v1 message (the #251 no-dead-end lesson): the money is yours + recoverable,
    even if v1's only action is "we'll keep trying" (auto-only re-shield deferred) — an
    amount-with-no-action reads as phantom money.
  - Desktop-clean (no `Platform.is*` gates in the send flow — arch-confirmed); pure-Dart
    testable. **Dynamic-module-clean (the host's Relim ADR-0031; in THIS repo ADR-0531 is the QR scanner):** the host messenger (Relim) consumes the
    SDK as a SEPARATE DYLIB over a C-ABI, so the host-facing surface that crosses the
    boundary is `send() -> Vec<TxSubmitResult>` + the `SendProposal` DTO (incl. the already-
    present `steps`/`largeSend`/`hasTransparentRecipient`) + the reused `SendSavedForRetry`
    outcome — TEX adds **ZERO new C-ABI surface** (the multi-step proposal, the outbox, the
    re-broadcast recovery, the ephemeral detection are ALL Rust-internal). The only NEW seam
    is that Rust-internal outbox (pt 4), invisible across the boundary. The example app (the
    FRB/static reference consumer) and the dylib host therefore consume the identical TEX
    behaviour through their respective bindings with no TEX-specific bridge work.
    NOTE: today there is NO `zcash:`/QR/deep-link ingest in the example app, and the swap
    flow has no address-entry — so "paste TEX elsewhere" can't bypass Send today; if a
    QR/URI surface lands later it MUST funnel TEX through the same Send review (forward note).

**§5.4 NEVER-LOG holds throughout:** ephemeral addresses are never-log AND never-RENDER
(linkable — pt 6 surfaces the stranded *amount* only); amounts/txids never-log; the
`txids` blob is opaque persisted bytes; heights / step-counts / booleans stay loggable.
The new error/terminal paths (multi-step reject, `mark_sent_multi`, reconcile, the Dart
partial terminal) carry no sensitive payload.

**Audited-libraries-whole (crypto-change step 2):** the multi-step proposal, the
ephemeral scope-2 derivation, the ephemeral reservation/gap-limit, and the engine's
ZIP-320 guards ALL come from librustzcash (`zcash_client_backend 0.23.0` /
`zcash_client_sqlite 0.21.0` / `zcash_transparent 0.8.0` / `zcash_address 0.12.0`) — the
SDK writes ZERO new derivation/selection code. The only new bytes are the shape
predicate, the DTO total/change math, the `txids` persistence column + `mark_sent_multi`,
the reconcile extension, and the ephemeral-detection poll — none touch key material.
Guard-citation precision (crypto audit NIT): the v1 *send* is constrained by
`PaysTexFromShielded` (create-time) + `EphemeralOutputLeftUnspent`;
`EphemeralAddressLinkability` guards the *spend-from-ephemeral* (the deferred auto-reshield),
not the v1 send. The ephemeral **gap-limit is 10** (`zcash_keys` default) — a run of
created-but-unmined tx0s can hit `ReachedGapLimit(EPHEMERAL)`; map it to an honest typed
"retry after recovery" error (NOT bare `ProposeFailed`) and document the TEX-send
availability ceiling. **[✅ LANDED S129 (B3-d-2 #7): `WalletError::TexSendLimitReached`,
RW-SEND-007.]** Both steps share one expiry window (target+40), so pt 6's detection
is the money-safety GUARANTEE, not polish.

`tex1s2rt77ggv6q989lr49rkgzmh5slsksa9khdgte`, testnet (parallel). KAT
`kat_tex_official_vectors_classify_transparent` is **LANDED (`309e88f`)** — TEX =

3-step / unconsumed-ephemeral / step1-pays-shielded near-misses); the total (Σ ALL-step

+nightly miri` pass on the new persistence path. **DEVICE-GATED:** a real TEX broadcast to

**Mandatory crypto-change review (step 7):** crypto audit ∥ security review ∥
arch review on THIS spec (round-1 DONE — folded the recovery redesign + ephemeral-detect
requirement + shape predicate, the round-1 BLOCKERs), then again on the diff, then

**2nd operational round DONE (UX ∥ reliability/unstable-net/mobile ∥ money/security-edge) —
folded into THIS revision:** the **total formula** was corrected (an earlier `last()` draft
under-counted a MIXED send → use Σ all-step payments = current code; pt 2); the **re-broadcast
latch** would have re-rejected a duplicate tx0 and never resent tx1 → skip-mined + non-latching
(pt 4); **`prepare_queued`/`reconcile`/`Reconciled`** would silently TRUNCATE a 2-step → all

lie that risks a double-pay → in-motion icon + "in progress" + "don't send again" (Outcome);
the **offline-queue** TEX drain routes through the multi-txid path + owes the disclosure at queue

to step1 (pt 1); **gap-limit + stranded** get honest typed copy (Outcome). **FALSE ALARMS

the code already passes the shape; only the comment is stale; pt 4/7); `selfSend`-on-TEX stays

**Operational review round 2 (S123) — slice-B / 2e-2b DESIGN OBLIGATIONS (UX ∥ reliability/
unstable-net/mobile ∥ money/security-edge, three reviewers).** The round confirmed the BUILT
slice-2e-2a code is money-honest (DTO total/change/self_send/large_send/disclosure all correct,
no overflow/leak, multi-TEX handled, predicate robust) and fixed two BUILT gaps in-place (the
`Wallet::propose` interim multi-step reject so a host is never handed a previewable-but-unsignable
dead-end; a `tex_mixed_shielded_first…` test pinning the engine ordering quirk). It also surfaced
design gaps that MUST be folded BEFORE slice B implements the recovery — record them here so the
implementation starts hardened (each gets a test):
1. **(BLOCKER) Expiry → stranded TERMINAL transition (the recovery state machine must terminate).**
   pt 4's multi-txid reconcile, as written, re-broadcasts a tx1 forever once tx0 has mined but tx1
   missed AND the wallet was offline past tx1's ~40-block expiry: the step0 claim reads
   not-spendable (tx0 spent the notes), so `reconcile → ReBroadcast` fires every pass, skip-mined
   skips tx0, and re-broadcasts an EXPIRED tx1 the node rejects every time — `delete-on-FINAL` never
   fires (tx1 can't mine), so the row busy-loops a doomed broadcast and never reconciles with the
   detect surface. Add an explicit branch: **tx_i unmined AND its `expiry_height < tip` ⇒ STOP
   re-broadcasting, transition the row to a terminal `Stranded` disposition, and hand the ephemeral
   off to the 2e-2b detect.** This is the "always make forward progress / never silently loop" fix.
2. **(BLOCKER, UX) Suppress "Send another" on the partial terminal.** The Outcome redesign fixes the
   icon/title/body but the reused `SendSavedForRetry` path still renders a "Send another" CTA right
   under the "don't send again" body — double-pay priming. The partial branch
   (`broadcast>0 && broadcast<total`) MUST suppress/relabel "Send another", not just fix the copy.
3. **(BLOCKER, UX) Regime-accurate stranded copy — no false "we'll keep trying".** With auto-re-shield
   deferred and tx1 past expiry, NO process is retrying; "we'll finish automatically" is phantom-
   money-with-no-action (the #251 dead-end). And exchange-RETURNED deposits route here too, where
   "finish the exchange transfer" is the opposite of what the user wants. Copy must be regime-
   accurate: the funds are YOURS, safe on an address your wallet controls, recoverable — without
   implying an automatic in-flight process that isn't running. If a manual "recover" action is
   truly deferred, the copy says so honestly.
4. **(HARDENING, UX) Durable in-progress → stranded surface, not a fire-and-forget terminal.** On
   mobile, offline > ~50 min after tx0-accept is the COMMON case, not an edge. The "in progress —
   don't send again" state must live as a durable activity/history row that TRANSITIONS to the
   stranded surface (and re-notifies), so a user told to "do nothing" is not left with silently-
   invisible money. The stranded detect (pt 6) must run on a cadence INDEPENDENT of any enrolled
   intent (the row may be terminal/deleted) and of foreground state.
5. **(HARDENING) Scope the non-latch to {mined ∪ already-known/duplicate}, NOT a transport failure
   of an earlier step.** pt 4's "always reach tx1" is too absolute: a genuine `GrpcFailure` on tx0
   (down link, tx0 neither mined nor in mempool) means tx1 has no input — firing it wastes an
   attempt every pass on a flaky link. A transport/unknown failure of an earlier step must
   latch-and-retry-next-pass exactly like the initial `broadcast_loop`; only a mined-or-duplicate
   earlier step continues to the tail.
6. **(HARDENING) delete-on-FINAL vs deep reorg.** Deleting the row at 1 confirmation means a reorg
   deeper than that (un-mining tx0+tx1 after the row is gone) has NO recovery row, and re-propose is
   structurally impossible post-tx0. Either delay delete-on-FINAL until tx1 is buried beyond a
   reorg-depth constant, or document mempool-re-mine as the sole recovery for that window and accept
   the residual.
7. **(HARDENING) Gap-limit (≤10 ephemeral) — exhaustion, expiry-reclamation, and queued surfacing.**
   **[✅ (a)+(c) LANDED in B3-d-2 #7 (S129) — see the "LANDED in B3-d-2 #7" block above; (b)'s MECHANISM
   is CORRECTED there. CORRECTION (engine-verified S129): a MINED tx0 FREES its ephemeral slot (the gap
   advances on on-chain observation), so a persistent ceiling is NOT "slots filled by tx0-MINED STRANDED
   ephemerals" — it is ephemeral indices LEAKED by expired-then-re-proposed tx0s (the engine does not
   un-reserve a dead reservation). The recovery is therefore a LEAKED-EPHEMERAL cleanup (still owed at
   2e-2b/gate-removal), DISTINCT from the tx0-mined `mark_stranded` money-strand. The original S123
   framing below is retained as the historical obligation; read "stranded" in (a)/(b) as "leaked
   never-mined reservations".]**
   (a) Reservation is at create/sign time and only "advances" once tx0 is observed; a run of tx0s
   that never confirm (offline-past-expiry → stranded) can FILL the gap and brick the 11th TEX send
   — define the honest typed ceiling error tied to the stranded surface, and pin whether a slot is
   reclaimed when a tx0 EXPIRES unmined (engine-owned `reserve_next_n_ephemeral_addresses` semantics)
   vs only when it mines. (b) The gap-limit ↔ stranded INTERACTION: "wait for them to finish, then
   retry" is an infinite-wait lockout if the slots are filled by STRANDED ephemerals — that case must
   point at the recovery surface, not a "wait". (c) The QUEUED path must surface `ReachedGapLimit`
   honestly, not swallow it into `prepare_queued`'s `Err(_) => Retry` catch-all.
8. **(HARDENING, privacy) Poll-timing decorrelation, not just vantage.** Per-ephemeral circuit
   isolation covers endpoint/vantage linkage but NOT timing: an ephemeral poll in lockstep with the
   main sync lets a network observer correlate it to the wallet by timing alone, partially defeating
   the ZIP-320 unlinkability. The 2e-2b poll needs a randomized/decoupled cadence (the project's
   cross-channel randomized-delay rule), or a documented residual.
9. **(HARDENING) Mixed-recipient ordering normalisation.** The engine only proposes a mixed TEX +
   shielded send when the TEX legs occupy the lowest payment indices (a `payment_pools` index re-map
   quirk; pinned by `tex_mixed_shielded_first…`). Today it fails closed `ProposeFailed`; once slice B
   lets multi-step SIGN, a legitimately-ordered exchange URI silently refusing to send is a real bug
   — slice B must normalise (move TEX legs to the front before `propose_core`, preserving the
   (address,amount,memo) tuples) or return a typed "reorder recipients" error, and add
   `tex_mixed_any_order_proposes`.
10. **(HARDENING) Queued TEX terminal.** `queue_send`/`queue_send_uri` accept a TEX with no gate, so
    a queued TEX sits `Queued` re-proposing every pass forever (money-safe via the slice-A guard, but
    a silently-never-completing intent). Slice B's multi-txid queued path owns the real fix; until
    then a queued TEX should surface an honest terminal, not retry indefinitely.

> **2e-2b-vi (#315) CONTRACT — leaked-ephemeral cleanup: PREVENT the #310 leak amplifier + RECLAIM the
> ceiling (spec-first S159, 2026-07-06; founder-approved scope = "prevention + self-mint reclaim").**
> Realizes the pt-7(b) recorded obligation ("2e-2b / gate-removal must reclaim leaked never-mined
> ephemeral reservations … else a persistent ceiling has no remediation") + the S129 op-round records
> [(i) known-ceiling backoff, (ii) ceiling cap-hygiene, (iii) the host-facing recovery surface, not just
> the operator log]. Money-path; the two slices below are EACH their own full crypto-change review.
> **ENGINE GROUND TRUTH (re-verified at the PINNED source `zcash_client_sqlite 0.21.0` /
> `zcash_client_backend 0.23.0`, S159 — not just the docs):**
> **(a) No un-reserve primitive.** `reserve_next_n_ephemeral_addresses` is documented "cannot be undone"
> (`data_api.rs:3266`); `find_gap_start` advances ONLY on a MINED first-use (`transparent.rs:439`
> `WHERE first_use_height IS NOT NULL`; `v_address_first_use = MIN(mined_height)`, `db.rs:1415`). A
> reserved-but-never-mined index holds its `[gap_start, gap_start+EPHEMERAL_GAP_LIMIT)` slot forever;
> `truncate_to_height` never touches `addresses.exposed_at_height`. CONFIRMS ADR-0535(b): NO engine
> reclamation. **(b) The reserve path never auto-reuses a leak** (`select_addrs_to_reserve` filters
> `exposed_at_height IS NULL`, `transparent.rs:518`), and reservation happens INTERNALLY inside
> `create_proposed_transactions` (`data_api/wallet.rs:1641`) — the caller cannot pick the index. ⇒ reusing
> a leaked index for a real tx0 (Mechanism B) would require hand-rolling the ZIP-320 two-step outside the
> audited change-strategy — an ADR-0005 Rule-Zero red line — **REJECTED**. **(c) #310 is a leak
> AMPLIFIER.** The all-legs-unmined-AND-expired → `reset_to_queued` terminal (`send.rs:1571-1584`) requeues
> a doomed TEX; on the next drain it re-proposes and the engine reserves a FRESH ephemeral (the dead one
> stays leaked). So ONE stubborn offline/censored TEX intent, requeued through ~10 expiry cycles, LEAKS
> ~10 slots BY ITSELF and permanently bricks TEX for the account — not 10 distinct sends. That is
> "deterministically cycled by #310". (Expired tx0s can NEVER mine — past-expiry ⇒ consensus-rejected — so
> a ceiling of expired leaks NEVER self-heals; recovery is NOT "wait".)
> **RECLAIM MECHANISM A (NEW — ADR-0535 did not identify it).** The engine has no un-reserve, but
> `gap_start` advances on ANY mined first-use of an index — including one WE create. So: pay a tiny amount
> from the wallet's OWN shielded pool to the HIGHEST outstanding leaked ephemeral address via a NORMAL
> shielded→transparent send (NOT a TEX send — reserves nothing new), mine it, then sweep the dust back with
> the existing `sweep_ephemeral_funds`. Mining index `k` sets its `first_use_height` ⇒ `find_gap_start`
> returns `k+1` ⇒ the entire `[k+1, k+1+GAP_LIMIT)` window re-opens in ONE transaction (indices `< k+1`
> drop below `gap_start` as harmless `GapMetadata::GapRecoverable` dead indices — `wallet.rs` backend enum
> doc: "discovered by wallet recovery by exploration", i.e. seed-rediscoverable, not a live slot). CLEAN:
> a plain send to a t-address (`check_ephemeral_address_reuse` PASSES — the leaked address never received
> on-chain), money-safe (dust lands on a wallet-controlled address + is swept back; net cost ≈ 1–2 ZIP-317
> marginal fees), double-deposit-free (the expired tx0 can never mine; the #310 precondition is
> past-expiry+buried). Needs connectivity (must mine; a still-censored wallet cannot reclaim, but neither
> can it send — no regression). Privacy: ONE one-time t-address appears on-chain, linked to nothing
> identifying (the intended TEX payment never happened); §5 per-circuit isolation applies to the mint +
> sweep. **VECTORS-FIRST GATE (crypto-change step 3):** slice 2's FIRST build step is a REAL-ENGINE harness
> proof that a tiny self-use on the top leaked index advances `gap_start` AND re-opens
> `reserve_next_n_ephemeral_addresses` (guarding `generate_gap_addresses` backfill + propose-to-own-
> ephemeral wrinkles). If the proof fails, slice 2 falls back to Mechanism C (accept the ceiling) and only
> the upstream FR + the honest-recovery UX ship for reclaim.
> **DECOMPOSITION — two independent slices, prevention lands FIRST (each fully reviewed):**
> **Slice 1 — PREVENT + honest UX (lands regardless of the Mechanism-A proof).** (1) **Re-propose backoff +
> cap** so a single requeued TEX intent cannot burn the window: bound fresh-ephemeral re-proposals per
> intent (proposed cap = small N, e.g. 3) with a per-intent backoff between attempts; on cap-exhaustion the
> intent parks as an HONEST terminal (a give-up state that stops leaking + stays user-cancellable via
> `cancel_parked_send`), NEVER an infinite re-propose. Caps per-intent leak to N ≪ GAP_LIMIT and preserves
> window headroom for other sends + for reclaim. (2) **Detect persistent-failure backoff** (the #294/#301
> deferral): a censored in-window ephemeral is re-probed every pass — add the per-address backoff.
> **[SHIPPED — #334, S165; see the #334 AS-BUILT note below.]** (3)
> **Honest ceiling recovery UX**: the ceiling is per-account + PERSISTENT; correct the copy/DTO guidance
> from "wait, then retry" (transient) to "one-time-address sends paused; your funds are safe" + (once slice
> 2 lands) a "Recover now" CTA. (4) Confirm the ceiling is inside the cap-hygiene/reap obligation (S129
> record ii; likely already via v-3's `state != Stranded` — verify, do not re-build).
> **Slice 2 — RECLAIM (Mechanism A, gated on the vectors-first proof).** A new
> `Wallet::reclaim_ephemeral_slots()` money-moving core op (+ FFI): enumerate outstanding leaked
> reservations (`outstanding_ephemeral_reservations`), self-mint a tiny use on the highest index over an
> isolated circuit, await mining, sweep the dust back, re-verify the pressure gauge dropped below the
> ceiling. Amount-only surfaces (§5.4 never-RENDER the ephemeral address). IDEMPOTENT + resumable (a kill
> between mint and sweep self-heals via the existing detect/sweep). Wire the slice-1 "Recover now" CTA to
> it. **UPSTREAM FR (lands regardless):** file a librustzcash request for an ephemeral-reservation
> release / explicit-reuse-of-unmined-index API — the clean long-term fix belongs in the audited crate;
> Mechanism A is our app-layer bridge until then.
> **REVIEW.** Each slice: full crypto-change review (crypto audit ∥ security review ∥ arch review →
> code reviewer → docs consistency) + the founder operational round, matching every prior 2e-2b money
> slice. Slice 2 additionally requires the real-engine reclaim proof before the money-moving op is trusted.
> **2e-2b-vi (#315) 4-ANGLE DESIGN REVIEW (S159, PRE-BUILD — security ∥ reliability/unstable-net/mobile ∥
> engine-correctness ∥ UX/money-red-team, all against the PINNED engine source). NO fund-loss/double-pay
> BLOCKER; the cap never touches notes/broadcast (a capped/requeued row leaves notes UNSPENT), so the slice-1
> severity ceiling is availability/honesty. Engine-correctness CONFIRMED all load-bearing claims incl.
> Mechanism A's highest-index gap-advance. The review corrected the pre-build design in two structural
> ways before any money code:**
> **SLICE-1 CORRECTION — the leak-count site was WRONG (count at the DRAIN, not the requeue).** A TEX leaks a
> fresh ephemeral on EVERY re-propose, via THREE paths, not one: (1) the burial-gated `rebroadcast_group`
> all-legs-dead-buried requeue (`send.rs:1581`, the ONLY site the original design counted — rare,
> conservative-unspendable, ~2.9 h cadence); (2) the witness `ReProposeFresh` requeue (`send.rs:1693`, the
> COMMON post-expiry notes-freed case); (3) the FAST create-fault `Err(_) => reset_to_queued; Retry` arm
> (`drain_multi` `send.rs:1947`) — the engine reserves the ephemeral BEFORE tx construction and does NOT roll
> it back on a build/prove/store failure ("reserves … even if transaction construction fails … not worth the
> complexity of being able to unreserve them", `zcash_client_backend/data_api/wallet.rs:1624`), so a persistent
> create fault (mobile memory pressure / full DB) leaks one slot per ~20 s `POLL_INTERVAL_SECS` pass → bricks in
> ~3–4 min, entirely uncounted. FIX: count at the DRAIN, where all three funnel through `create`.
> `drain_multi` atomically increments `repropose_attempts` for an ephemeral-reserving (`is_zip320_two_step`)
> proposal, folded into `mark_submitting` as ONE `IMMEDIATE` UPDATE (a separate reset-then-increment pair has a
> kill window → under-count → cap never trips). The SKIP sits in `prepare_queued` AFTER `deposit_gate` (so a
> capped swap-deposit still self-expires at its quote deadline instead of orphaning invisible — it is excluded
> from `list_parked_sends` by `deposit_deadline.is_some()`) and BEFORE `propose_core` (no propose/build/seed
> cost on a capped row): `if repropose_attempts >= MAX_TEX_REPROPOSE_ATTEMPTS => Prepared::CappedParked`. Only a
> multi-step ever increments, so `attempts > 0 ⟺ TEX` and the skip needs no shape re-check. Counter semantics:
> consecutive ephemeral-reserving attempts WITHOUT a completed send — a completed send deletes the row
> (delete-on-final-buried), so the cap only ever bites a repeat-fail intent, never a series of legit sends.
> **SLICE-1 HONESTY — a capped row must be DISTINGUISHABLE from a healthy pending send.** `parked::classify`
> (`parked.rs:170`) renders every `Queued` row identically ("saved & pending" `walletParkedSubtitle`), so a
> given-up capped intent looks like a normal in-flight TEX and the user waits forever for a send that will never
> fire. Add a `paused` status (`repropose_attempts >= cap`) to `ParkedSend` + the FFI DTO; the host branches copy
> (healthy "will send when ready" vs capped "paused — your funds are safe; retry or cancel"). Add a `retry`
> affordance (reset `attempts = 0`) so a recovered link resumes WITHOUT cancel+re-send — a fresh intent restarts
> at `attempts = 0` and re-leaks N (multi-intent cap-evasion, below).
> **SLICE-1 COPY — do NOT over-correct transient→persistent.** `ReservationPressure.outstanding` counts BOTH
> real in-flight tx0s (mine in ~40 blks → self-heal) AND dead leaks (never heal) in ONE number and cannot
> distinguish them, so flipping all ceiling copy to "persistent/paused/recover" is a NEW dishonesty for the
> genuinely-transient ceiling (would prompt a needless self-mint fee). Honest copy holds both: "some may clear as
> transfers confirm; sends that can't confirm won't clear on their own — recover to continue." (The leaked-vs-live
> split IS derivable at slice-2 enumeration time — see the deadness gate.)
> **SLICE-2 CORRECTIONS — Mechanism A CONFIRMED, but target-selection + success-check were underspecified.**
> (a) **Target deadness gate (was a BLOCKER):** `outstanding_ephemeral_reservations` returns EVERY reserved-unused
> index INCLUDING a LIVE, unexpired, in-flight tx0 — and "highest" = most-recently-reserved = most likely LIVE.
> Self-minting+sweeping a live tx0's index races its tx1 and can CANCEL a legitimate exchange deposit. FIX: reclaim
> ONLY an index whose reservation is PROVABLY DEAD — `tip − exposed_at_height ≥ (tx-expiry-delta + REORG_MAX_BLOCKS)`
> (any tx0 that reserved it is past-expiry AND buried) — enumerated over a WIDE window (the sweep's
> `all_reserved_ephemeral_addresses`, `exposure_depth = tip`, NOT the bounded detect lookback which misses old
> leaks); pick the highest PROVABLY-DEAD index. If none is provably dead ⇒ NO-OP (the ceiling is genuinely
> transient; the live tx0s self-heal). (b) **Self-mint amount > the sweep economic floor**, never "dust": the sweep
> drops UTXOs ≤ `MARGINAL_FEE` (5 000 zat), so a dust self-mint is unrecoverable + the sweep-back is a no-op; size
> it > `MARGINAL_FEE` + the sweep tx fee (net > 0). (c) **Success = a real reservation PROBE / `find_gap_start`, NOT
> the pressure gauge:** the gauge counts below-`gap_start` dead indices so it barely moves (10→9) after a full
> reopen — keying a "Recover now" CTA on it drives repeat fee/privacy burn down to index 0. (d) **Sweep the minted
> address DIRECTLY** (the reclaim knows it — an old leak is outside the detect lookback). (e) **Await BURIAL of the
> self-mint before declaring success** — a reorg rolls `first_use_height` back → `gap_start` regresses → re-brick
> after "fixed". (f) **De-shield: rides the #327 authorizer, EXPLICIT only never auto**, + honest disclosure
> (costs ~4 ZIP-317 marginal fees — self-mint + sweep are TWO full txs, not 1–2 — from your funds, needs
> connectivity, briefly exposes a one-time address). (g) **Recover ↔ capped-intent (the double-pay hinge):** pin +
> disclose the resumption semantics. RECOMMENDED: reclaim unblocks the WINDOW only; the paused payment STAYS paused
> (the user explicitly retries or cancels it) so "Recover now" NEVER silently re-sends → no double-pay. (h)
> **Privacy residual (calibrated — our "linked to nothing" was an over-claim):** an OFFLINE leak (tx0 never
> broadcast) → the self-mint is E's first on-chain appearance, linked to nothing. A CENSORED leak (tx0
> broadcast-then-dropped) → the censor already saw tx0/tx1; the self-mint makes E PUBLICLY wallet-controlled (a real
> residual) but does NOT put the intended exchange payment on-chain (tx1 never mines), so a PUBLIC observer learns
> only "E is wallet-controlled", not the exchange target. Document; product decides reclaim-under-active-censorship.

> (true for NOTES, FALSE for the reservation — it IS committed + not rolled back on a create fault), and the
> transient-only user copy at `error.rs:176` + `walletSendFaultOneTimeAddressLimit` (`wallet_en.arb:1358`
> "wait … then try again"). Fold into slice-1 impl.

> **l10n:** new keys (paused status, Recover-now CTA + disclosure, retry) + VALUE changes to
> `walletSendFaultOneTimeAddressLimit` + `walletParkedSubtitle` (a value change invalidates the existing 15

> returns k+1 ⇒ `[k+1, k+1+10)` reopens; lower leaks fall below `gap_start`, harmless); a normal send to a

> never-render-address; the burial cadence claim (SOUND for the successful-`Sent` path — the create-fault path was
> the blind spot, now covered by count-at-drain); no slice-1 fund-loss/double-pay. Our TWO own over-claims are

> OFFLINE (not censored) leak.
> **AS-BUILT (#315 slice 1, S160 — landed per the corrected design + a second 3-angle CODE review
> [security ∥ money-path red-team ∥ arch/docs], all SHIP-WITH-HARDENING, findings folded).** Mechanism as
> reviewed: `repropose_attempts` column (appended LAST); `mark_submitting_counting` (transition + count, ONE
> `IMMEDIATE` UPDATE) at the drain for a multi-step proposal; cap gate in `prepare_queued` after the deposit
> gate, before propose ⇒ `Prepared::CappedParked`; `ParkedSend.paused` + `Wallet::retry_parked_send` (+FFI/UI);
> `MAX_TEX_REPROPOSE_ATTEMPTS = 3`. Four decisions BEYOND the reviewed text, all deliberate:
> **(1) A typed CEILING refusal REFUNDS its count** (`reset_to_queued_refunding_attempt` — claim release +
> refund in one write): the count is taken pessimistically BEFORE `create` (a fault must stay counted — the
> engine reserved), but `TexSendLimitReached` is the engine's own proof the attempt reserved NOTHING, and
> leaving it counted would pause a healthy TEX behind a transiently-full window in ~3 poll passes (~1 min),
> long before the ~40-block self-heal — the transient→persistent over-correction this review forbade, caught
> in behavior by the S160 red-team. An all-leaked window therefore keeps the row honestly waiting at the
> ceiling (pressure gauge + per-pass `ceiling` telemetry are the window-level stuck signal; slice 2 is the
> remedy) while the cap budget stays reserved for attempts that actually LEAK. Kill window between refusal
> and refund ⇒ over-count by 1 (conservative, money-safe).
> **(2) The INTERACTIVE two-step enrol counts too** (`create_two_step_enrolled` uses the counting door): on
> the synchronous paths the tally dies with the row (success → delete-on-buried; fault → delete), but a
> process kill between enrol and create recovers the row into the queued drain, which must inherit
> attempts = 1 (the reservation may already be consumed), never a fresh 0.
> **(3) No inter-attempt backoff shipped** (the parent CONTRACT's slice-1 item 1 sketched one): the requeue
> paths are naturally paced by expiry + burial (~hours per cycle), the ceiling no longer consumes budget
> (item 1), and the one remaining fast path — a persistent create fault, ~`POLL_INTERVAL_SECS` per leak —
> is exactly where a FAST park is wanted (each attempt leaks a slot; backoff would only slow the bleeding
> the cap stops). The per-address DETECT probe backoff (contract item 2, the #294/#301 deferral) was
> subsequently SHIPPED in #334 (S165) — see the #334 AS-BUILT note below.
> **(4) Retry hygiene:** `retry_parked_send` re-arms under cancel's exact guards PLUS `repropose_attempts > 0`
> (an untouched row is a no-op `false`, never a silent mid-budget refill). The host-automation cap-evasion
> loop (retry spam ⇒ ~1 leak per pass) is CONTRACTUAL, not self-enforcing — documented on the DTO both
> sides + the host action board read-first #3 (never auto-retry; rate-limit swap-deposit creation under a
> standing ceiling) — accepted per the trust model (the host already holds the seed).
> Telemetry: `capped` rides `wallet.resubmit` as its own field but is EXCLUDED from `did_work` (like
> `awaiting_burial`) — a long-paused send is an event-silent steady state; the durable signal is the paused
> surface. Review doc-sweep also corrected the remaining transient-only ceiling copy family
> (core+FFI `TexSendLimitReached` docs, `ReservationPressure` both sides, `list_parked_sends` both sides,
> `prepare_queued`/interactive-sign NBs, the Dart routing comments).

> `self_mint_on_the_highest_leaked_ephemeral_reopens_the_whole_window`).** Over a gap-3 window with THREE

> leaked address proposes as a plain SINGLE-step and signs (`check_ephemeral_address_reuse` passes — never

> full `REORG_MAX_BLOCKS` burial of that expiry block needs `tip − exposed ≥ 41 + REORG_MAX_BLOCKS`.
> At 140 the boundary delivered only `REORG_MAX_BLOCKS − 1` of burial (a maximal reorg could re-enable

>   Settings reveal is a different threat model from onboarding (a device someone picked up already
>   unlocked), so the reveal is gated. A reveal is NOT a spend, so it is a SEPARATE seam from
>   `WalletSendAuthorizer` — a plain `Future<void> authorizeReveal()` gate (no signing credential to

>   on-screen reveal + warning + screenshot/recents protection are the reference posture); a credential host

>   GATE ORDERING is money-safe: `revealMnemonic()` (the unseal) runs ONLY after `authorizeReveal()`
>   resolves — a denied or faulted re-auth reads NO words (tested: `revealCount == 0`).

>   two ways — a null provisioner (session-only host, the common case; up front, no re-auth dead-end) and a
>   `revealMnemonic()` that throws `WalletErrorKind.noMnemonic` (classified by KIND only, §5.4) — both land
>   on an honest "no separate recovery phrase" state that never invents/blanks words. (In the Relim host,
