> **AS-BUILT (#344, S167 — reference-count the `ScreenSecurity` port; UI-only, no core/derivation change;
> realizes the "per-screen reference-counted FLAG_SECURE" the plan flagged at the §W row above):** the raw
> adapter contract is a single window-level flag (Android `FLAG_SECURE` is one Activity flag), so the last
> `disable()` wins — unsafe the moment two secure surfaces are alive at once (a secure screen pushes
> another; a sheet/dialog over one): popping the top would clear the flag while the screen underneath still
> shows a seed. A new `RefCountedScreenSecurity` decorator (`onboarding_providers.dart`) keeps the flag
> engaged while ANY holder is active: the first `enable()` (0->1) engages the adapter, the last `disable()`
> (1->0) releases it; intermediate calls only move the count. The 5 secure screens (onboarding
> reveal/restore, Settings backup, Send, Swap) keep their plain `enable()`-on-show / `disable()`-on-dispose
> pair — the counting is invisible to them. Wired at the ONE seam every screen reads: the
> `screenSecurityProvider` default AND the `walletOnboardingOverrides` production override both hand out the
> adapter refcount-wrapped (the provider caches the single instance, so all screens share one count).
> Transitions are SERIALIZED on an internal future (a rapid enable->disable->enable can never leave two
> native calls in flight out of order; a piggyback `enable()` awaits the in-flight engage before reading
> the shared engagement truth, so every stacked screen gets the same honest "screenshots off" ack). A
> transition that throws is swallowed (never poisons the chain, never breaks the screen — the port's
> best-effort contract); an unbalanced `disable()` clamps at zero (never negative — a negative count would
> skip a real 0->1 engage) and reports in debug without throwing out of a `dispose()`.
> `screenSecurityCoWiringHolds` (crypto audit H2) now UNWRAPS the decorator, so a mis-wired Noop can never
> hide behind it. The `_openingBackup` tile guard in `security_screen.dart` is demoted to a pure UX
> double-push guard (the screenshot race it partly closed is now handled durably here). 12 new tests
> (coalescing; last-disable-releases; interleaved + no-await-between call ordering; underflow clamp;
> throwing-adapter resilience; honest-Noop; delegation; + a real go_router widget test that stacks two
> secure screens and proves the flag survives popping the top). Full package suite green (`flutter analyze`
> clean).

> **AS-BUILT (#334, S165 — passive-DETECT per-address probe backoff; §3.2i-2 2e-2b-vi contract slice-1
> item (2), the #294/#301 deferral. Availability/battery only, money-SAFE, NOT a crypto-change review; DESIGNED
> then implemented behind a 3-angle review of the design [arch/SOLID ∥ security/§5.3 ∥ reliability/mobile],
> all no-BLOCKER, hardening folded.):** a new pure `EphemeralProbeBackoff` (in `ephemeral_detect.rs`,
> beside `in_detect_scope`/`run_detect_loop`/`shuffle_targets`) held on `Inner` behind a LEAF
> `std::sync::Mutex` (the `proposals`-registry shape — mutable subsystem state behind its own small lock;
> taken/dropped synchronously in the detect, never across `.await`, never nested with `db`). Each cold
> probe (empty `Ok(vec![])` or a transport fault) pushes the address's next-eligible instant out by a
> DOUBLING interval (`EPHEMERAL_DETECT_BACKOFF_INITIAL_SECS = 60` → `..._MAX_SECS = 600`), so a
> persistently-cold in-window ephemeral settles to ~1 probe/10 min (≈30× fewer) instead of every ~20 s pass.
> **(1) Target-set-driven, no loop-signature bloat.** The detect filters `targets` by `due(addr, now_i)`
> (a MONOTONIC `tokio::time::Instant`, deliberately distinct from the engine's persisted wall-clock
> `next_check_time`); `record_probe` is FOLDED into the EXISTING `probe` closure (the loop calls it exactly
> for the committed set — post cancel/gate/deadline break, post `polled += 1`), so a deadline-truncated /
> starved tail is never recorded and keeps NO backoff — the shuffle+truncation anti-starvation property is
> preserved and `run_detect_loop` gains only a `pre_deferred` counter, no `on_probe` arg (arch fold).
> **(2) In-memory, GC'd each pass.** `retain_scope(not-funded-in-window)` drops entries that left the set
> (funded → skip-funded, aged-out, or reorged-away → re-admitted with NO stale backoff), bounding the map
> by the in-scope set, not wallet lifetime. Not persisted (a monotonic instant is meaningless across a
> restart; losing it costs one extra pass — harmless).
> **(3) Honesty ladder extended.** A new `deferred` count rides `wallet.ephemeral_detect` and enters the
> finished-predicate (`polled + skipped + deferred < scope ⇒ incomplete`), so a healthy backoff pass is
> never a false `incomplete`. A NEW `throttled` headline fires when a pass opens NO circuit because all
> in-scope ephemerals were skipped-or-deferred (≥ 1 deferred) — so a censored link's quiet passes are not
> laundered into a healthy `clear` (security fold); benign-EXPECTED, an INFO signal, not a fault.
> **(4) §5.3 anti-clustering jitter.** The scheduled interval is a DOWNWARD jitter (`(interval/2, interval]`,
> OsRng-injected like `shuffle_targets`) — breaks the deterministic doubling SHAPE a malicious endpoint
> could use to cluster a wallet's cold ephemerals by their identical re-probe ramp, and being downward-only
> never exceeds the `max` latency budget.
> **MONEY-SAFETY (re-confirmed by the security angle, traced to source):** the backoff only DELAYS a passive
> re-probe — never un-surfaces funds, never feeds the reap (the §3.2i-2 censor-forgeable-empty ban). The
> ACTIVE manual sweep (`sweep_ephemeral_funds`, `all_reserved_ephemeral_addresses`, wide window) does NOT
> gate on it — a user recovering funds always probes fresh. Worst-case ADDED surfacing latency for a cold
> ephemeral that later funds = `max` (10 min) of ACTIVE time (the monotonic clock freezes in deep-sleep, so
> more wall-clock on a suspended phone — still money-safe: funds durable on-chain, the manual sweep is the
> always-fresh escape). RESIDUAL (accepted, documented): a PERSISTENT censor's fresh-vantage retry rate
> drops ~30× on the passive path (minutes → hours against a partial censor) — funds never hidden, and the
> manual sweep escapes it. Tests: 6 new (`ephemeral_detect` unit — doubling→cap, downward-jitter bound,
> due/record window under a paused clock, retain_scope GC, the throttled/deferred ladder; `wallet`
> integration — a cold ephemeral probed once is deferred, not re-probed, next pass). Full core suite green;
> clippy + fmt clean.

#### 3.2i-3 — Transparent-funds management: auto-shield + expert gate + pool clarity (inc-2e-5; founder S151 directive, calls confirmed S154)

**Founder directive (S151, verbatim intent):** users must be able to MANAGE
transparent funds — shield, unshield, send shielded, send unshielded,
auto-shield — because recipient requirements differ, with CLEAR visibility of
what is shielded vs not; privacy-shielded stays the DEFAULT and advanced actions
live behind an expert gate. **Founder calls confirmed S154 (2026-07-06):**
(1) auto-shield DEFAULT threshold = **0.001 ZEC** (100_000 zats; host-tunable —
this is the shipped default, and the core `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT` floor at
`send.rs` means a host can only RAISE it, never lower); (2) battery-saver =
**DEFER** (no auto-shield while OS power-save is active; fires on the next
normal-power sync edge; desktop is always "normal power"); (3) expert-gate copy
tone = **PLAIN-FACTUAL** (state the visibility facts in the package's honest-copy
voice; no warning theatre, no shaming the exchange use case).

**THE ENGINE DISCOVERY (S154 scouting — the ground truth that re-sliced this).**
The vendored `zcash_client_backend 0.23.0` CANNOT express a transparent→transparent
transfer: `GreedyInputSelector::propose_transaction` selects shielded notes only
(Sapling+Orchard, vendored `input_selection.rs:717`) and hard-wires an EMPTY
transparent-input slice into `compute_balance` (`input_selection.rs:641`); there
is no pool-filter knob on `propose_transfer`. The ONLY transparent-input spends
the engine offers are `propose_shielding` (forced shielded destination) and the
ZIP-320 ephemeral hop. There is also NO durable transparent change type
(`ChangeValue` = `Shielded` | `EphemeralTransparent` only — the latter is
semantically an auto-swept hop), and a TEX recipient is unconditionally routed to
the shielded-origin two-step (`input_selection.rs:463`) so direct t→TEX is equally
inexpressible. CONSEQUENCE: "send unshielded" is NOT a policy flag over the
audited engine — it is a custom `InputSelector` + change-as-explicit-own-t-addr
output, i.e. the genuinely-NEW audited money surface class this section always
sequenced last (inc-2e-4, where it now lives; task #332). The signing/broadcast
machinery for wallet t-UTXOs is PROVEN (the Shield path is a t-input spend
end-to-end, device-proven) — the gap is proposal-layer only. **Founder decision
S154: t→t is post-GA, demand-driven.** Honest product note recorded with it: t→t
only genuinely serves funds RECEIVED transparent (forwarding without two hops of
fees); for shielded-origin funds a de-shield-then-t→t gives only cosmetic
distance, and the TEX two-step already solves the exchange-deposit case.

**S103 rule reconciliation.** The S151 UX model sketched a send-form POOL
SELECTOR; with t→t deferred there is NO source pool to select — so no selector
ships and the §3.2i S103 rule ("the recipient ADDRESS is the pool selector; never
a casual per-send shielded/transparent toggle") stands UNCHANGED. If/when
inc-2e-4 lands, its selector must be expert-gated and deliberate, and must amend
S103 explicitly at that point — not silently.

**What ships (inc-2e-5) — three sub-slices, all Dart/`zec_wallet_ui` except one
read-only FFI field:**

**(a) Auto-shield policy loop (Dart — policy is host-side per ADR-0529/§6.3;
`proposeShield` is the ready primitive).** Default **ON** (the founder posture:
everything shielded; "Spendable now" ≈ total shortly after any arrival — the
S151 balance-confusion fix). Mechanism: a non-autoDispose policy controller (the
`WalletSyncController` structural sibling — lifecycle-aware, `_disposed` +
per-build `_generation` guards, riverpod-reuse-safe) that observes the
wallet-active sync edges (reachedTip / becameSpendable — the same edges that
refresh the balance), reads the refreshed `BalanceSnapshot.transparent`, and when
it is ≥ max(host threshold, core floor) runs the ONE audited money sequence:
`proposeShield()` → `authorizeSpend(intent, () => send(proposalId))` →
outcome-landing invalidations. Rules:
- **At-most-one in-flight attempt**; a new edge while an attempt runs is a no-op.
  Re-attempts ride subsequent sync edges (the natural rate limit) — never a hot
  retry loop. `proposeShield() == null` (below the core floor) is a quiet no-op.
- **Authorization is NEVER bypassed** — an automatic shield is still a spend and
  rides the #327 authorizer seam. `WalletSpendIntent` gains
  `origin: {userInitiated (default) | automatic}` (non-breaking named param) so a
  host policy can auto-approve automatic self-transfers, prompt, or deny them. A
  denial STOPS the loop for the session (no prompt-spam) and the failure cue
  shows. The identity-switch spend fence + `_disposed` arms apply to the loop
  exactly as to the S153 controllers (capture the session OBJECT, fence inside
  the action closure).
- **Power-save DEFER (founder call 2):** gated on a new host seam
  `walletPowerSaveActiveProvider` (default `false`; hosts wire the OS signal —
  Android Battery Saver / iOS Low Power Mode; desktop stays `false`). While
  active the loop skips edges; arrivals stay VISIBLY transparent (the honest
  state), and the next normal-power edge shields.
- **Manual-flow yield:** the loop skips an edge while a manual shield is
  in-flight (no proposal race against the sheet; a lost race would only produce
  a typed inputs-spent failure, but skipping is cleaner).
- **FAILURE HONESTY (the §2.5/`state.rs` invariant, already load-bearing):** a
  failed or denied auto-shield leaves `transparent` visible — never silently
  folded, never retried into oblivion — PLUS an honest balance-card cue ("didn't
  complete; these funds are still public; Shield manually or it retries on the
  next sync"). Offline: propose/send fails typed → same cue; the loop is edge
  driven so it naturally re-attempts when sync resumes.
- **Duress/decoy note (§4.5):** the loop acts on the ACTIVE session object only
  and spends decoy funds to the decoy's own pool (a self-transfer) — no
  cross-identity surface; the fence forecloses the flip window.
- **COMPAT (S151):** auto-shield default-ON would sweep existing deliberately-held
  transparent balances — so it ships IN THE SAME RELEASE as the expert gate
  (opt-out exists from day one).

**(b) The expert gate ("Advanced: transparent funds", default OFF).** A persisted
host-UX boolean (the `OnboardingStore` category — a new small `WalletSettingsStore`
port + SharedPrefs impl; NOT Rust state), exposed as a provider hosts can
override/wire to their own settings UI. Package surface: a "Transparent funds"
entry in the wallet OVERFLOW MENU (the §3.2i-1 expert-layer home) opening a sheet
(desktop `walletSheetMaxWidth`) with plain-factual explanation + the expert
toggle; with the gate ON it reveals (i) the AUTO-SHIELD toggle (default ON;
turning it OFF is the expert's deliberate hold-transparent choice) and (ii) the
promoted Move-to-transparent entry (unshield stays in the overflow too). With the
gate OFF, non-experts get pure default posture: auto-shield on, no toggle, no
promoted unshield — and NOTHING existing is hidden behind the gate
retroactively (Shield button, balance transparency lines, §3.2i-1 overflow entry
all stay).

**(c) Pool clarity.** (i) The send REVIEW step states the payment's visibility
class explicitly — a "Privacy" row: shielded (private) vs transparent (publicly
visible; renders alongside the existing §5.1 `DeshieldWarning`) — derived from
the proposal's own `has_transparent_recipient`/`is_shield` (no new propose
input). (ii) ACTIVITY transparency badge: `TxSummary` gains a read-only
transparency indicator (core classification over the wallet DB's output-pool
data: a non-change transparent OUTPUT leg = the §5.1 public-payment class; FFI
field + regen ×2 + convert lockstep; UI badge follows the `hasMemo`-glyph
pattern) — a public payment must be distinguishable in history. (iii) Balance
clarity is ALREADY BUILT (S151-2 transparent line + note); (a)'s failure cue
extends it.

**New seams (all host-overridable, `wallet_providers.dart` conventions):**
`walletExpertTransparentFundsProvider` (persisted, default OFF),
`walletAutoShieldEnabledProvider` (persisted, default ON),
`walletAutoShieldThresholdZatProvider` (`int`, default 100_000; core floor still
applies), `walletPowerSaveActiveProvider` (`bool`, default false — host wires the
OS signal), `walletAutoShieldControllerProvider` (the loop). l10n: one 16-locale
batch covering the sheet/toggles/cue/badge/review-row.

**Tests (named-contract additions).** Loop: fires-at-edge-over-threshold,
below-threshold no-op, power-save defers then fires, denial stops-without-spam +
cue, failure leaves transparent visible + cue, at-most-one in-flight, manual
shield yields, identity-flip fence (zero bridge calls against the new session),
disposal/generation guards. Gate: default-OFF posture, toggle persistence across
restart, auto-shield-off honored (no proposal at edge). Clarity: review row both
classes, badge rendering, core classification unit tests + extraction-policy
lockstep for any new bridge enum. Full review round (security ∥ UX ∥
reliability → folds) before landing; device/desktop selftest unchanged (no
bridge-shape change beyond the `TxSummary` field).

**S154 REVIEW-ROUND AMENDMENTS (3-angle review on the built slice; all folded
same-session):**
- **TWO fences, not one.** The propose await spans a real FFI round-trip, so an
  identity flip landing inside it could open the DEAD identity's authorization
  prompt over the new identity's screen — a duress DISCLOSURE (the intent's
  amount = the other identity's balance) the SPEND fence cannot stop, because
  it fires inside the action, after the prompt. The loop therefore re-checks
  `disposed ∥ generation ∥ session-identity` BEFORE `authorizeSpend` (the
  PRE-PROMPT fence) in addition to the S153 fence inside the action. "The
  fence forecloses the flip window" above reads as BOTH fences.
- **Every cross-await latch write is generation-guarded** — including the
  denial latch: a stale denial (the documented host behavior at an identity
  switch) landing after a flip must not disarm the NEW session's loop
  (probe-confirmed by two reviewers pre-fold). The in-flight slot is
  generation-AWARE (an identity flip abandons the old cycle's slot), so a
  never-completing host prompt wedges only the session it belongs to.
- **Latch/cue semantics:** turning the switch ON re-arms a denied loop (the
  latch guards against prompt spam, not deliberate restarts); turning it OFF
  clears a lingering failure/denial cue (the cue would contradict the explicit
  opt-out); busy/not-synced propose failures during startup stay QUIET (idle —
  a false "didn't complete" at cold start is an alarm, not honesty); a LOADING
  snapshot (which can still carry the PREVIOUS session's figure) is never an
  evaluation basis.
- **Conditional copy:** the sheet's automation sentence tracks the actual
  switch (`AutoOn(min)`/`AutoOff`) — a persisted OFF is stated even while the
  expert gate hides the switch; the move-to-transparent CONFIRM discloses the
  revert (auto-shield ON would shield a deliberate unshield right back for a
  second fee) whenever the loop would fire (S14 below); rendered thresholds
  clamp to the engine floor; the transparency badge copy is direction-neutral
  and the fact SURVIVES into the tx detail sheet (asserted only positively —
  the flag's absence is not a "fully private" proof, e.g. a shield tx spends
  transparent INPUTS).
- **Move below the shield floor (stage S14, founder S307/S308: warn).** Until
  S14 the revert note showed for ANY amount, and under the floor it promised a
  sweep that never came (walked S307). The review now computes the public
  balance after the move = (the snapshot's `transparentZat` less the one-time-
  address subset, clamped by the shared `clampRecoverableToTransparent`) + the
  moved amount (`move_public_after.dart`); a loading snapshot counts nothing
  public (toward the warning), and a recoverable list not yet read, or failed
  with no earlier read, counts no one-time funds, as the auto-shield loop
  assumes, so the review and the loop agree on whether the loop ATTEMPTS a
  sweep (a warm failure keeps the last good list). Under the core floor the
  review shows the founder's warning with that figure ("…under the 0.001 ZEC
  needed to shield it back. It stays public until more arrives."), swaps the
  own-address note for the variant without "You can shield these funds again
  later", and hides the revert note. Over the floor the revert note shows only
  if the loop would fire, judged as the loop judges it: the RAW public balance
  after the move against the host's threshold. Confirm stays enabled. *What
  the user loses:* funds on a swap-refund address (external index ≥ 1,
  ADR-0528) count in `transparentZat` but are no shield source, so a wallet
  already holding a failed swap's refund can miss a warning it should have
  seen (the loop makes the same approximation); a public deposit still pending
  is counted (`transparentZat` is the unshielded total), so one that never
  confirms can hide a warning the same way, and so can one-time funds while
  their list is not yet read or failed with no earlier read, in which case the
  review can also promise a sweep the core then declines (the loop attempts
  it, `proposeShield` finds the index-0 gross under the floor and answers
  nothing); a prior move still unmined is not
  yet counted, so a quick second move can warn when the pair would clear the
  floor (the safe direction). Plan:
  `docs/plan/stage-14-move-below-the-shield-floor.md`.
- **Settings are DEVICE-GLOBAL** (theme-prefs class): a duress/decoy host must
  override the store with an identity-namespaced one — hazard documented in
  the store + the swap-in guide; identity-scoped storage recorded as a host
  follow-up (#318).
- **Recorded-owed:** a `real_view` core test asserting the classifier against
  engine-WRITTEN transparent rows (the controlled fixture pins logic, the
  real-schema test pins names; the engine-written `is_change` semantics are
  verified against the vendored view SQL but not yet exercised end-to-end).

### 3.3a Receive surface — QR + shielded/transparent management (Recv epic; founder 2026-06-22)

`currentAddress()` (§3.3) hands the host the account-0 unified address; the
RECEIVE SCREEN is the user-facing read surface over it. Founder directive
(2026-06-22): make it a real wallet-receive UX (address **+ QR**), add
**shielded vs transparent address management**, keep it host-themeable.
Decomposed into three independently-shippable slices; the themeable-SDK-
**package** extraction (the screens live in `sdk/zec_wallet/example` today, §1.4 —
the third-party-host reference consumer) lands LAST, once the receive AND swap
surfaces are final — extract once, no churn (founder-chosen sequencing).

**Recv-1 — address + QR (host UI; NO core change). [build order: first]**
The screen renders `currentAddress()` as a scannable **QR** above the selectable
address + a copy control, in the standard wallet-receive layout (QR-on-top,
address below — Zashi/Zodl parity). The QR encodes a PUBLIC value (the address;
the spending key never leaves Rust — §4.1), so rendering/copying/QR-encoding it
is safe; §5.4 NEVER-LOG still holds (display/copy/render only, never logged).
**Money-correctness invariant (named test):** the exact bytes encoded into the
QR == the displayed string == the copied string == `currentAddress()`'s return,
with NO truncation / normalization / whitespace — a QR that drops one character
sends funds to nowhere. QR encoding is the audited pure-Dart `qr_flutter` brick
(MIT, `CustomPainter`, no network, no native code — Rule Zero / building-bricks,
never a hand-rolled encoder); error-correction level **M** (the ~213-char
unified address auto-selects a high QR version — verify renders + scans
on-device). Themed via the `RelimColors` ThemeExtension; the QR tile itself
pins a light background + dark modules + quiet zone — a SCANNER requirement, not
a theme choice (the one justified color pin, documented at the call site).

**Recv-2 — transparent receive address (core + bridge + UI + ENGINE; crypto-change review).**
AMENDS §1.6's "shielded-only, no transparent receiver" scope cut (founder-
directed): surface a transparent receive address alongside the shielded UA,
behind a shielded/transparent toggle (default = shielded), for the documented
real need (§1.7 — CEX withdrawals + swap-in deliveries land TRANSPARENT, which a
shielded-only wallet cannot receive). Honest framing (the UI renders it, never
hides it): the shielded UA stays default + recommended; the transparent address
is labeled PUBLIC ("transparent — visible on-chain, reused-address-linkable; use
only when a sender can't pay a shielded address; shield after receiving" — Recv-3).

GROUNDED in the locked crates (`zcash_client_backend 0.23.0` /
`zcash_client_sqlite 0.21.0` / `zcash_transparent 0.8.0`) — two non-obvious
facts drive the decomposition:
1. **A naked external-index-0 receive address COLLIDES with the swap-refund
   allocator** (`refund_index.rs` hands out EXTERNAL-scope `m/44'/coin'/0'/0/i`
   from i=0; ADR-0527). A receive address at the same scope/index would equal a
   refund address — a privacy + reuse bug. **Resolved (ADR-0528, SHIPPED):** the
   receive address takes external index 0 and the refund counter is floored at
   index 1 (`REFUND_INDEX_FLOOR`) — collision-free by construction, with the
   refund allocator left UNBOUNDED (the engine's own gap-limited allocators were
   rejected for refunds; see the decision below).
2. **Transparent funds are NOT detected by `scan_cached_blocks`** (it scans
   shielded notes only). Detection needs `transparent-inputs` ON
   `zcash_client_backend`/`_sqlite` (today OFF) + a SEPARATE lightwalletd
   `GetAddressUtxos` poll in the sync loop (`utxo_query_height` start →
   `put_received_transparent_utxo` → `get_transparent_balances`). So a
   display-only transparent address shows funds the wallet can't see or spend (a
   footgun) until detection lands.

Decomposed:
- **Recv-2a — derive + display (SHIPPED, ADR-0528).** A STABLE transparent
  receive address = the account's canonical external-scope (`m/44'/coin'/0'/0/0`)
  P2PKH receiver, derived PURELY from the stored account UFVK's transparent
  component (`ufvk.transparent()` → `derive_external_ivk()` → `default_address()`),
  exactly as the shielded UA derives from the stored UFVK — so it works in
  `None`-persistence (no seed). The collision with the refund allocator
  (`refund_index.rs`, also external scope from index 0) is removed by **reserving
  external index 0 for the receive address** and flooring the refund counter at
  index 1 (`REFUND_INDEX_FLOOR`). The custom refund counter is **kept** (ADR-0528,
  not retired): an evaluation of moving refunds onto the engine's ZIP-320
  **ephemeral** allocator was rejected because that allocator is gap-limited (10)
  and refunds are reserved per-quote (protocol-bound) — a successful swap never
  funds its refund address, so the wallet would be permanently blocked from
  quoting OutOfZec after ~10 lifetime swaps. The custom counter is unbounded.
  New core `current_transparent_address() -> String` (§3.1) → bridge
  `currentTransparentAddress()` → `WalletSession` port →
  `walletTransparentAddressProvider` → the receive screen's address-type toggle.
  HD-recoverable; never key material. KAT-pinned.
- **Recv-2b — detection + balance.** Enable `transparent-inputs` on the engine
  (additive schema `transparent_addresses` + `transparent_received_utxos`, no
  `WALLET_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump; deps `bip32`/`secp256k1` already locked), wire
  the `GetAddressUtxos` poll into the sync engine, and surface a transparent
  balance in `BalanceSnapshot`. This WIDENS the §5 privacy surface (a
  relay/explorer can correlate transparent deliveries) — user-controlled,
  honestly labeled, paired with the Recv-3 shield nudge. Gated by the FULL
  crypto-change review + a §5 privacy re-review + an ADR (the
  transparent-management posture + the ADR-0527 reconciliation).

  **SHIPPED (S89).** Detection wired as a focused port `sync::TransparentUtxoSource`
  (ISP — segregated from the shielded-scan `ScanClient`, so the sync test fakes are
  untouched), implemented only by the production `LightwalletdClient`
  (`net::grpc::get_address_utxos`, a UNARY poll; `max_entries = 0` so the per-message
  `GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` cap is the DoS bound — a giant reply fails decode LOUDLY,
  never a silent entry cap). The poll rides INSIDE the engine pass after a clean
  `sync_once` (`Wallet::refresh_transparent_utxos`, hooked in `run_pass`'s cancel
  race), on the SAME sync circuit (`WALLET_SYNC_ISOLATION_KEY`) — so it adds **no new
  §5 correlation surface beyond sync itself** (the relay already sees this circuit
  doing wallet sync). Best-effort + SWALLOWED like the §6.3 resubmission hook: a fault
  logs `wallet.utxo_scan { outcome = <code> }` (counts only) and the sync loop
  never fails — the chain is the source of truth, the next pass retries.

  **The §4.6 hostile-input boundary is `transparent::validate`** (pure + total, the
  unit of the §8 KATs): every field of every returned UTXO is validated — txid exactly
  32 bytes (INTERNAL order, the `OutPoint`/`TxId::from_bytes` door, NO display
  reversal), index ≥ 0, value in `[0, MAX_MONEY]` (audited `Zatoshis::from_nonnegative_i64`),
  height fits `u32`, script ≤ `MAX_TRANSPARENT_SCRIPT_BYTES` — and, the **M2
  lying-endpoint defense**, the recipient is RE-DERIVED from the endpoint's actual
  `script_pubkey` (audited `Script`/`Code`, no custom parsing) and required to equal
  OUR receive address; the reply's own `address` field is never trusted, so a UTXO for
  an address we do not own is rejected, never put (no phantom balance of unspendable
  funds). The audited engine's `put_received_transparent_utxo` applies the SAME check
  again (`AddressNotRecognized` for an address absent from its `addresses` table) — two
  independent layers. A malformed field rejects that ONE record (counted), never the
  poll, never a panic. **Detection targets the external-index-0 RECEIVE address only**:
  `add_account` (with `transparent-inputs`) pre-generates the external-scope gap
  `0..gap_limit`, so index 0 is engine-tracked by construction (the §8
  `refresh_transparent_utxos_detects_…` integration test verifies it end-to-end — no
  `AddressNotRecognized`). Swap-refund detection (indices 1..N via the custom counter)
  was the ADR-0527-deferred migration obligation — **DISCHARGED at #368** (refunds
  engine-register at quote + arm the scoped watch at execute + backfill-register behind a
  durable marker; see the §4.4 "Swap refund visibility (#368)" block). **(Update
  2026-06-23 — §3.3b / ADR-0530: the IntoZec
  on-ramp adds a SCOPED active-swap poll — `{index-0} ∪ {committed swap destinations}`
  from the durable store, NOT `get_transparent_receivers()` wholesale — so fresh
  swap-DESTINATION addresses are detected; it mints destinations via `get_address_for_index`
  on the SAME single-use external counter as refunds (engine-PERSISTED for detection, not the
  auto-advancing engine allocator). OutOfZec REFUND addresses joined that same scoped poll
  at #368.)** `BalanceSnapshot.transparent` already sums the engine's
  `unshielded_balance().total()` (the put is what makes it nonzero). Build: +0 new lock

**Recv-3 — shield flow (money path; crypto review).** The companion to Recv-2:
move transparent funds into the shielded pool. Our public `propose_shield`

SAME `Proposal` one-shot token shape, so `send(proposalId)` consumes it
unchanged. Privacy-POSITIVE (public → shielded); the §5.1 de-shield disclosure
does not apply (opposite direction).

  **SHIPPED (S90, ADR-0529).** `send::propose_shield_core` wraps the audited

  it works in None-persistence). The engine's gate (`balance.total() >=
  shielding_threshold`, where `balance.total()` is the GROSS being shielded) is
  passed `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT`; BOTH `Error::InsufficientFunds` (below the
  threshold) AND `Error::Change(ChangeError::InsufficientFunds)` (no spendable

  yet", an honest no-op, the host hides the CTA), while DataSource→`StoreCorrupt` /
  ScanRequired→`ProposalStale` / else→`ProposeFailed` stay typed — so corruption is

  gross − fee), the lone recipient the wallet's OWN shielded output (pool read from
  `ChangeValue::output_pool`, never re-derived), `has_transparent_recipient = false`,
  `is_shield = true`.

  **The registry token is the enum `RetainedProposal { Transfer | Shield }`**

**Recv-4 — FR-8 public diversified receive UAs (#393, ADR-0537, crypto-change review).**
Mint-next unlinkable per-contact/per-invoice UAs that all credit account 0,
deterministic per diversifier index. DESIGN (S217):

- **Region (FROZEN, ADR-0537):** public mints derive at diversifier indices in
  `[DIVERSIFIED_INDEX_BASE, BASE + 2^31)` with `DIVERSIFIED_INDEX_BASE = 2^40` —
  disjoint by construction from the swap/refund space (`[1, NON_HARDENED_MAX]`),
  the default UA's forward search, AND the engine's own timestamp-based shielded
  allocator band (`now + 2,817,325,936` — sits above 2^32 since genesis, below
  2^40 until ~year 36,000; the S217 crypto audit moved the base off the first
  draft's `2^32` pre-commit). Disjointness is the crypto property: equal
  diversifier index ⇒ byte-identical shielded receivers across ANY receiver set, so
  any overlap is public linkability. The receiver set is **G7**
  (`Require`/`Require`/`Omit` — extracted as the shared `g7_receive_request()`, one
  builder for the default UA and the mint). A sapling-invalid fixed index is a real
  ~50% per-index miss here (engine maps `InvalidSaplingDiversifierIndex` → `Ok(None)`):
  burn the single-use index, advance — bounded by
  `DIVERSIFIED_DERIVE_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 64` (P(all miss) ≈ 2^-64), typed `KeyDerivation`
  on exhaustion, never a silent orchard-only degrade.
- **Counter (`diversified_index.rs`, aux DB):** dedicated singleton table
  `diversified_address_index (singleton CHECK(singleton=0), next_index)` — never-reuse,
  `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` read-modify-write, first reserve returns the BASE, stored value
  validated in `[BASE, BASE + NON_HARDENED_MAX]` else fail-closed `StoreCorrupt`
  (never a wrapped/recycled/below-region index). **Restore story (day one,
  ADR-0527 law; RANDOMIZED S218-b):** the #387 restore-pessimistic first seed ONLY —
  at `store::open`, counter-row-absent ∧ ¬`freshly_generated_here` ⇒ counter =
  `BASE + k·DIVERSIFIED_RESTORE_BAND` for an OsRng band `k ∈ [1, 2^18]`
  (`DIVERSIFIED_RESTORE_BAND = 4096` ≈ 2048 mints — sized in MINTS honestly: the G7
  `Require`-sapling walk burns ≈2 indices per mint; the original S217 constant 1024
  was sized in indices but disclosed in mints, a 2× overstatement, and being
  CONSTANT it re-seeded identically on every chained restore ⇒ certain re-issue of
  the post-restore life's mints — both S218-b review catches). Counter is the only
  row (no bounds table), so the seed is one idempotent `INSERT OR IGNORE`; highest
  floor `BASE + 2^30` leaves half the region as headroom (const-asserted). No
  backfill/deep-scan/polling analog: shielded trial decryption detects funds at ANY
  diversifier, so the restore harm is bounded to a random band landing inside a
  prior life's used span — ≤ ⌈used/4096⌉/2^18 per prior life (~2^-18), replacing
  the old certain re-issue past the breadth (two contacts share a UA —
  attribution, never funds); bands are free (no scan cost). The counter survives rescan (aux); the engine `addresses` rows
  (courtesy registration via the audited `get_address_for_index`, ADR-0530 — no gap
  burn) drop on rescan harmlessly. Aux counter = sole never-reuse authority.
- **Core:** `pub async fn mint_diversified_address(&self) ->
  Result<MintedDiversifiedAddress, WalletError>` — `{ address: String,
  diversifier_index: u64 }`. Blocking body on the pool, `lifecycle.require_open()`
  first, **fail-fast no-account pre-check before any reserve** (no burned index on a
  doomed call — the `fresh_destination_address_blocking` precedent), then the one
  documented lock order db→aux held across the whole reserve+mint (the engine
  deferred-write vs aux `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` deadlock, §3.3b). Reuses the un-gated
  `allocate_single_use_external` loop (the `#[cfg(swap)]` moves off the loop + the
  extracted `ua_at_index`; `mint_swap_destination` delegates). Local, offline,
  NOT swap-gated, NOT gated on sync. §5.4: address + index NEVER logged;
  `wallet.diversified_mint { outcome }` — success `outcome = "minted"`, failure the
  stable error code, and deliberately NO per-mint attempt count (the miss
  run-length is a deterministic function of the viewing key — a same-seed
  correlator in exfiltrated host logs; S217 security fold). FOUNDER-ACCEPTED
  residual (S218-b): the success event's existence still leaks mint COUNT +
  TIMESTAMPS to a log-exfiltration adversary — kept as the standard money-op
  observability shape; a change here is a founder decision, not hardening.
- **FFI:** `mint_diversified_address() -> Result<MintedDiversifiedAddress,
  WalletApiError>` on `WalletHandle`; DTO `{ address: String, diversifier_index:
  u64 }` (first u64 in the DTO surface — BigInt over FRB; the region's top `< 2^41`
  keeps the Dart-side `int` narrowing exact everywhere, guarded loudly in the
  adapter). Host-facing docs disclose the two caveats verbatim: the randomized-band
  restore story (deterministic ≤ ~2048 mints/life, ~2^-18 band-overlap beyond),
  and "the index is WALLET-INTERNAL — never share it
  with a counterparty" (it is a sequential mint ordinal). Errors ride the existing
  kinds (`KeyDerivation`, `StoreCorrupt`, `InvalidState`, `StoreBusy`).
- **Dart:** port `Future<WalletMintedAddress> mintDiversifiedAddress();` with the
  pure-Dart value `WalletMintedAddress { String address; int diversifierIndex; }`
  (bridge-agnostic, the `WalletSendRequest` pattern); thin `FrbWalletSession`
  forward; `FakeWalletSession` knobs (`Result`/`Throws`/`Count`/`NeverCompletes`).
- **UI affordance (receive screen, shielded tab only):** a "fresh address" action
  below Copy — tap → in-button progress (mint under `walletFfiWedgeTimeout`) → the
  QR + `AddressText` + Copy all switch to the minted UA + a one-line caption naming
  the property (unlinkable, still this wallet). Visit-scoped screen-local state:
  leaving resets to the default UA; a session/identity flip clears it; the
  transparent tab is untouched. Failure = honest SnackBar, display unchanged.
  a11y: the switch is announced (liveRegion caption), button keeps a stable
  semantic label. Prefill/l10n keys ×16 locales.
- **Named tests (Gate-8):** Rust —
  `kat_fixed_seed_mints_pinned_diversified_address` (mainnet + testnet goldens,
  KAT_SEED_32), `kat_bip39_vector_seed_mints_pinned_diversified_address` (Trezor),
  `diversified_mint_is_deterministic_per_index`,
  `diversified_address_shares_no_receiver_with_the_default_ua` +
  `…_with_a_swap_destination` (the disjointness teeth),
  `diversified_mint_enforces_g7_receivers` (independent `zcash_address` decode),
  `diversified_reserve_starts_at_base_and_is_monotonic`,
  `diversified_reserve_persists_across_reopen`,
  `diversified_reserve_concurrent_mints_never_collide`,
  `diversified_counter_out_of_region_is_store_corrupt`,
  `diversified_restore_pessimistic_seed_skips_into_a_random_band` (+ the
  fresh-create and first-wins arms),
  `diversified_restore_floors_differ_across_restores` (the chained-restore teeth),
  `diversified_mint_with_no_account_burns_no_index`,
  `diversified_mint_advances_past_a_sapling_invalid_index`,
  `minted_dto_debug_is_redacted` (the §5.4 Debug belt),
  `diversified_index_never_recycles_across_a_full_wallet_reopen`, and the
  `rescan_is_crash_safe` extension pinning the counter's uncleared rescan ride. Dart —
  fresh-address tap swaps QR/copy to the EXACT minted string, in-flight disable +

### 3.3b Swap redesign — IntoZec on-ramp (other-asset → ZEC; founder 2026-06-23)

Completes the swap surface (OutOfZec shipped D-2b/S85). IntoZec lets the user buy
ZEC with another asset over the same 1Click rail. The port types already carry the
direction (§2.6 — `SwapDirection::IntoZec`, `slippage_tolerance_bps`,
`refund_address` ALL cross core→bridge→Dart today); the NEAR adapter fail-closes
IntoZec quotes for now (`zec-wallet-swap-near` — the ZEC receive-address wiring
was the one missing piece, Rust-blocked until the Recv epic). **Now UNBLOCKED by
Recv-2/3.** Aligned to the real `zodl-android` reference (read 2026-06-23); the
deliberate hardenings are called out. Six decisions:

**D1 — Destination = a FRESH per-swap address at a SINGLE-USE EXTERNAL INDEX
(`get_address_for_index`).** The ZEC receive target handed to 1Click (`recipient`)
is a fresh address derived at a DISTINCT external index via the audited
`get_address_for_index(account, index, request)` — NOT `get_next_available_address`
(it auto-advances the gap → burns it on abandoned quotes), NOT a stable index-0
reuse (linkage). Mechanism settled by the `zcash_client_backend 0.23.0` probe
(2026-06-23, ADR-0530):
  - **The index comes from the SAME single-use external counter as refunds**
    (generalize `refund_index` → a single-use swap-external-address counter:
    distinct, never-recycled, floored above the index-0 receiver, one
    `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` reservation — concurrency-safe). Refunds (OutOfZec) and
    destinations (IntoZec) never co-occur for one swap and draw distinct indices.
    ONE counter (DRY — no second allocator answering the same "give a distinct
    never-recycled external address" question).
  - **Engine-persisted ⇒ detectable.** `get_address_for_index` derives via the
    audited UFVK path AND persists the address to the engine `addresses` table, so
    `put_received_transparent_utxo` accepts it (no `AddressNotRecognized`) WITHOUT
    advancing the gap allocator. This is the piece refunds defer (refunds derive
    read-only; ADR-0527 deferred their detection) — destinations add persist + poll
    + shield. No gap burn (the counter is unbounded; `get_address_for_index` does
    not touch the gap).
  - **Reserve-at-quote, persist-in-the-durable-record.** The 1Click quote binds
    the deposit address to `recipient`, so the destination is reserved at QUOTE time
    and persisted INTO the durable `IssuedQuoteRecord` (the W-swap-3-c store that
    already writes fail-closed before the quote returns). A crash between quote and
    execute does NOT strand funds — recovery reconstructs the destination from the
    durable record + re-adds it to the detection set. Distinct index per ISSUED
    quote ⇒ no reuse even across abandoned quotes ⇒ unlinkable (§2.6 HARD-H).
  - **Universal** — the address carries the UA receivers; the provider pays
    whichever it supports. 1Click pays the TRANSPARENT receiver in practice (Zodl
    evidence: `requestNextShieldedAddress(): WalletAddress.Unified` → `recipient` →
    a `createShieldProposal` after delivery), so Recv-3 shields it; a
    shielded-paying provider just works via the normal scan — **no 2→1 refactor**.
  - **`ends_shielded: true` is the NUDGED expected end state**, not a guarantee:
    delivery's transparent leg surfaces the one-tap Recv-3 shield (never silent —
    ADR-0529). A sub-threshold delivery (< `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT`) honestly stays
    transparent until it accumulates; the disclosure means "the shield path is
    available + nudged," and the transparent leg is on-chain-visible until shielded
    (disclosed AS DATA). Works in `None`-persistence (UFVK-derived, no seed). Key
    material never crosses FFI.

  RECOVERY caveat (residual, documented): `get_address_for_index` persists in THIS
  wallet's DB so same-device detection always works; an external index beyond the
  gap window is NOT auto-found by a FRESH seed-restore scan (the same caveat as the
  ADR-0527 refund counter), mitigated by PROMPT shield (the transparent leg is
  brief; shielded funds are recoverable). IZ-1 VERIFY: `get_address_for_index` is
  reachable on the locked `WalletDb` (else fall back to `UnifiedFullViewingKey::address`
  + the engine address-registration path). **Port (hexagonal):** `SwapService`
  obtains the destination through a port following the `RefundAddressSource`
  precedent — a `next_destination_address()` that derives + engine-persists + returns
  the address for detection-registration; `SwapService` NEVER calls `WalletWrite`
  directly. Refund + destination may share one `SwapAddressSource` port (both draw
  the one single-use external counter) or stay sibling ports — IZ-1's call, but the
  service depends on the trait, the wallet supplies the adapter.

**D2 — Detection polls a SCOPED active-swap set, NOT all receivers.**
`refresh_transparent_utxos` polls exactly `{ index-0 receive } ∪ { committed
swap-destination addresses whose delivery is not yet shielded }` (since #368 the union
also carries `{ executed OutOfZec refund addresses }` + the one-window ADR-0527
backfill rows — same store, same lifecycle, same privacy envelope) — a set the wallet
maintains from the durable swap/issued-quote store — NOT
`get_transparent_receivers()` (the probe confirmed it returns the WHOLE
gap-pregenerated external set, which would disclose a wallet fingerprint to the
endpoint). A destination retires from the set once its delivery is shielded (or the
swap terminates with no delivery), so the polled set shrinks back toward index-0 at
idle. SAME unary `GetAddressUtxos`, SAME `transparent::validate` §4.6 boundary + M2
lying-endpoint re-derivation, SAME sync circuit (`WALLET_SYNC_ISOLATION_KEY`, Tor
fail-closed), SAME best-effort SWALLOW. **§5 (re-review gate, ADR-0530):** the
endpoint sees only `{ index-0 } ∪ { addresses we asked a provider to pay }`, each
already disclosed to + paid by that provider — no wholesale gap-set disclosure, no
new correlation channel. On a §3.5 `Hard` swap kill the destinations DROP from the
set (back to index-0 only): honest-off stops the swap-attributable traffic; an
in-flight delivery still lands on-chain and is detected on the next user-initiated
full sync (surfaced honestly, not silently polled). Discharges the
ADR-0527-deferred non-index-0 detection for the DESTINATION case (OutOfZec refund
auto-shield can later add its addresses to the same scoped set). Gated on
swap/chain activity so an idle wallet polls nothing.

**D3 — Auto-shield on delivery via the existing Recv-3 path.** When the scoped poll
detects ZEC at a swap-destination address, the wallet surfaces the Recv-3 shield
(the same `propose_shield` CTA/nudge, gated at `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT`) — the
Zodl posture (`ShieldFunds` home nudge), one tap, **never silent/forced** (ADR-0529
— the shield is user-triggered; delivery NEVER auto-broadcasts a shield). The swap
status reaching `Success` + a transparent-balance bump is the nudge trigger; the
re-shield is idempotent across a crash (engine spent-UTXO exclusion, ADR-0529).

**D4 — User-tunable slippage.** Expose the `slippage_tolerance_bps` the port
already carries (default `SLIPPAGE_DEFAULT_BPS = 200` / 2%; hard core ceiling
`SLIPPAGE_MAX_BPS = 1_000` / 10%, both in `constants.rs`, enforced in
`validate_request`) as a host control: presets 0.5% / 1% / 2% + custom (Zodl
parity), advisory tiers (below ~0.5% "may fail", above ~3% "risky"; the hard 10%
ceiling rejects beyond), and the realized value on the terminal
`Success { realized_slippage_bps }`. The USER-ANCHORED SANITY CEILING (§2.6) still
bounds every quote to `[request ± tolerance]` under `SLIPPAGE_MAX_BPS` — the
user's own request is the drain guard, never provider numbers alone. The
`slippage_beyond_max_bps_is_rejected` test asserts the boundary (exactly-at-ceiling
accepted, one-bps-over rejected), mirroring the bridge `swap_id_bound` boundary
pattern.

**D5 — Dynamic token list from 1Click `/v0/tokens`.** The source-asset list is
FETCHED from the provider (`GET /v0/tokens` over the host dialer, Tor-optional),
not hardcoded (Zodl parity): filtered (drop $0/null-price + the ZEC asset itself),
cached, surfaced through a new `SwapPort::list_tokens()` (IZ-2). The fetch is
**LAZY + cached** — fired only when the user opens the IntoZec form (NOT on app
launch), so an uninterested/idle user emits no token traffic (§5.2 honest-off). It
rides the SAME `NetDialer`/`TorPolicy` stack as the rest of the swap API
(`Required` fail-closes zero-clearnet) under its OWN isolation key (a dedicated
tokens key, NOT shared with sync — so the relay can't link "this circuit does
wallet sync AND token-listing"); `tor_required_covers_list_tokens` pins the
fail-closed guarantee. Provider strings inherit the `PROVIDER_STR_MAX_*` §4.6
bounds. Icons are BUNDLED locally (token + chain drawables + a placeholder
fallback) — never CDN-fetched (censorship/privacy; matches Zodl's `ic_token_*`
drawables). §5.4: token metadata is never logged beyond coarse counts
(`wallet.swap_tokens { count, outcome }`, allowlisted in §5.4).
  - **IMPLEMENTED (IZ-2, S94):** `SwapPort::list_tokens() -> TokenList { tokens: Vec<TokenInfo>,
    fresh }` (new trait method; `TokenInfo { chain, symbol, decimals, provider_asset_id, price_usd }`).
    The NEAR adapter reuses its existing `/v0/tokens` fetch/parse/cache machinery; `list_tokens`
    filters the full table (drop the ZEC asset + any `$0`/null-price entry) and maps to the port DTO,
    under a DEDICATED `swap/tokens` circuit isolation key (distinct from sync AND quote/status). On a
    fetch fault it serves the last good cache with `fresh = false` (L6); a first-ever fault with no
    cache is the typed error. `SwapService::list_tokens` delegates (with the §3.5 `ensure_live` gate)
    and emits the §5.4-clean `wallet.swap_tokens {provider, count, outcome}` span (`outcome` =
    `ok`/`stale`/`RW-SWAP-NNN`). The bridge crosses it as `SwapToken`/`SwapTokenList` via
    `swapListTokens()` (FRB-regenerated). The Dart picker UI that CONSUMES it is **IZ-3 — SHIPPED
    S95** (the `WalletSession.swapListTokens` forward + a lazy `autoDispose` `swapTokensProvider` →
    the picker sheet with the L6 "couldn't refresh" banner / honest no-assets empty / error+retry
    states, and a monogram PLACEHOLDER icon — bundled drawables are a content follow-up, NEVER CDN).
    The
    operational round folded +6 real-world-edge tests (empty-but-fresh, malformed-entry-strict-map,
    shared-cache-refresh, always-refetch, duplicate-rows-quote-rejects-ambiguous, bridge empty-fresh)
    and — guard-forced by `bridge_enums_cover_core_variants` (RED since IZ-1a) — LANDED the bridge
    `SwapErrorKind::DestinationAddressUnavailable` arm + Dart regen (no longer the IZ-3-deferred
    "degrades to Unknown").

**D6 — Refund address: user-supplied source-chain + QR scan.** IntoZec's
`refund_address` is the user's address ON THE SOURCE CHAIN (where their coins go
back if the swap fails) — supplied by the user (Zodl asks explicitly, with a
"refund address" info screen the host SHOULD mirror, since it's user input with no
wallet ground truth — see below). Entry is paste/type + a QR scan (`flutter_zxing`
— on-device ZXing, NOT Google ML Kit / `mobile_scanner`: the ML Kit telemetry
channel has no opt-out, rejected for a censorship-resistant wallet — ADR-0531,
IZ-4); desktop (no camera) is paste-only — identical money path.
  - **ONE Rust-side boundary chokepoint** `validate_refund_address`: the pasted
    string AND the QR-scanned string (untrusted camera input) converge on the SAME
    core validator — NEVER a Dart-side check on one path and a Rust check on the
    other. Treated as OPAQUE bytes (bounded ≤ `PROVIDER_STR_MAX_BYTES`, non-empty,
    REJECT control bytes + embedded whitespace), NEVER parsed as a Zcash address
    (it is a foreign-chain address).
  - **Wire-injection guard (inherited Mostpost lesson):** `refund_address` reaches
    the 1Click request ONLY as a `serde_json`-serialized string value (serde is the
    escaper — a `"` / CRLF cannot break out and forge a second field); NEVER via
    string interpolation/format. Any future non-JSON wire format for this value
    re-opens this question. Paired test `refund_address_json_injection_is_escaped`
    (embed `","refundTo":"attacker",...` + CRLF; assert exactly one `refundTo`,
    bytes escaped not structural).
  - **Echo + trust posture:** the provider's echoed `refundTo` is VERIFIED equal to
    ours before any state (§2.6 → `ProviderProtocol` on mismatch; since 2026-10-07
    so is every other term of the echoed request, `map::check_request_echo`) — this catches
    provider tampering/protocol drift, NOT user typos (it compares our-input to the
    echo, both carrying the same value). Per §4.4 HARD-G the refund is provider-API
    data, not cryptographically bound; the host MUST surface a confirm-the-refund-
    address review step (the Zodl info screen, made a contract not just prior art).
  - **Disclosure:** the IntoZec `provider_sees` set includes `SourceAddress` (the
    refund address) + `CrossAssetLink` + `Amounts` + `IpUnlessTor` — the §5.1
    disclosure honestly tells the user the provider learns their source-chain refund
    address.
  §5.4 NEVER-log (it is an address). The wallet drives NO deposit for IntoZec
  (§4.4) — the USER sends the source coin to the provider's `deposit_address`; we
  only receive + shield.
  - **IMPLEMENTED (IZ-4, S96):** the camera QR scan ships as `flutter_zxing`
    (on-device ZXing FFI, Google-free — ADR-0531, NOT `mobile_scanner`). The scan
    affordance is a refund-field suffix button, gated `!kIsWeb && (Android||iOS)`
    (desktop/web paste-only); it opens a short-lived `ReaderWidget` screen
    (QR-only, gallery OFF so CAMERA is the sole permission; the transitive
    `RECORD_AUDIO`/`WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` are stripped `tools:node="remove"`,
    guarded by a test) with an accessible label + an always-present manual-entry
    escape + honest camera-unavailable degradation. The scanned payload is
    URI-unwrapped host-side (`normalizeScannedAddress`: strip a syntactic
    `scheme:` + `?query`/`#fragment`, single-token truncation drops CR/LF/TAB,
    size-capped — the shared address-scanner brick, renamed from the refund-only
    name at S103 since the OutOfZec destination scan reuses it) — then the SAME
    `validate_refund_address` chokepoint + the
    char-by-char review verification still gate it (the scan never bypasses
    them). §5.4-clean (the payload is never logged). Injected via
    `addressScannerProvider` (the shared scanner brick, renamed from
    `refundScannerProvider` at S103) for camera-free widget tests
    (`refund_address_qr_scan_populates_the_field`).

  BY CONSTRUCTION: because the detection set is store-DERIVED (not a rebuilt cache), the

### 3.4 The two consumers, end to end (brief §6 item 3)

| | Third-party app | Relim |
|---|---|---|
| Seed in | Dart `restore(mnemonicWords)` / `create()` → Rust | **Rust-only:** `WalletSeedPort::wallet_sub_seed()` → `SeedSource::RawBytes` at composition (`FreshRawBytes` when the create attests `freshlyGenerated` — FR-24 S213) (identity-core §3; W5) |
| Surface | `sdk/zec_wallet` Dart package | relim-ffi mirrored DTOs (§1.4) |
| Backup | `revealMnemonic` (its own words) | impossible by construction (`NoMnemonic`); the one Relim phrase recovers the wallet via re-derivation |
| Endpoint | its own config | manifest-listed endpoints (W5) |
| Swap gate | constructs provider or not | MiCA matrix decides construction (A5) |

---

### 3.5 The swap off-switch — four independent kill layers (regulatory resilience)

Design requirement (founder, 2026-06-10): swap is designed and implemented
**inside the SDK** (it's part of the community deliverable, ADR-0014), but a
government/regulatory problem must be able to turn it off **without redoing
anything**. **ADR-0525 (founder, 2026-06-13) completes the picture: the NEAR
adapter itself is an SDK deliverable — pluggable, default-ON in the published
package (`swap` + `swap-near` features), full Zodl-parity capability when a
host enables it (§1.7 mined rows are the UX contract), and ALL of the layers
below are the "host doesn't want it ⇒ not shown, zero traffic" mechanism.
Regulatory exposure is HOST policy: Relim keeps its MiCA gate (layers 1+3);
third-party hosts own theirs.** Four independent layers, each sufficient
alone:

| Layer | Mechanism | Who flips it / latency |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Compile-time** | cargo feature `swap` on the core: off ⇒ `SwapService`/`SwapPort` surface not compiled, the `swap()` accessor doesn't exist. The NEAR adapter is additionally a **separate crate** (`zec-wallet-swap-near`, §1.2) linked via the bridge feature **`swap-near`** — feature off ⇒ not linked ⇒ not one byte of it (or its HTTP/TLS deps) in the binary | per build flavor (store / jurisdiction); needs an app release |
| **2. Runtime construction** | the §3.4 gate: the host constructs a provider or doesn't. No provider ⇒ the module doesn't exist, zero traffic, Dart `swap == null`, UI hides | per launch; config only |
| **3. Remote flip (Relim)** | the per-jurisdiction feature matrix rides the **signed network manifest** → the composition root constructs (or drops) the provider from the flag. An operator manifest update kills swap fleet-wide **without an app-store release** | operator; hours, no release cycle |
| **4. Provider replacement** | `SwapPort`: NEAR is one adapter behind a trait — replaceable or removable without touching a line of wallet code (ADR-0014's original rationale) | code-level; next release |

**Layer precedence is MONOTONIC-TOWARD-OFF (review M4):** any layer may
SUBTRACT swap capability at any time; **no remote layer may resurrect it**.
Re-enabling requires an app release (layer 1) or host construction at launch
(layer 2) — the manifest flag (layer 3) is subtract-only by construction.
Dependency stated: layer 3 MUST NOT ship before the network manifest lands
ADR-0012's open threshold/revocation design — without revocation, a forged
"on" flag would be a resurrect vector.

**As built (W-swap-2, LANDED):**

- **Layer 1 at the artifact level** is the bridge `swap-near` cargo feature
  (default-ON): it gates an OPTIONAL `zec-wallet-swap-near` dep — the sole
  entry point of the NEAR swap ADAPTER (its REST-client code + DTOs) into the
  artifact. `--no-default-features` ⇒ the adapter is not linked — verified
  empirically (dep graph + `nm`) and gated deterministically by
  `swap_near_feature_off_ships_no_adapter_symbols`. **CORRECTED 2026-06-23:** the
  base hyper/rustls stack (hyper/hyper-util/rustls/tokio-rustls/ring/webpki-roots)
  is NOT swap-droppable — it is the CORE lightwalletd gRPC transport (tonic),
  present unconditionally with or without `swap-near` (zec-wallet-core declares
  `hyper-util` directly for the `NetDialer`→tonic `TokioIo` bridge). The swap
  adapter REUSES that same raw-`hyper` stack (deliberately not `reqwest`), so
  there is NO swap-exclusive transport crate to drop — only the adapter code
  itself. The off-switch guarantee is the adapter's optional+feature-gated
  absence; the gate bans only the swap-REST-client-class crates (`reqwest`/
  `native-tls`/`openssl`/`ureq`/`curl`) from core, recognising the shared gRPC
  stack as legitimately core (`feature_policy.rs` `CORE_GRPC_TRANSPORT` vs
  `SWAP_ONLY_HTTP_CLIENTS`; the prior "core declares NO HTTP/TLS" premise predated
  the gRPC seam and was structurally unsatisfiable — the gate had been born-red).
  The swap SURFACE (`SwapService`/`SwapPort`/DTOs) stays compiled (core `swap`
  feature, default-on) — `swap-near` gates only the network PROVIDER. The
  provider construction over the injected `NetDialer` lands with the
  dialer/wallet-handle chunk (W-swap-3); the `#[cfg(feature = "swap-near")]
  swap_provider` module is the attach point. **Kill-door contract (pinned at
  W-swap-2, enforced at W-swap-3):** since the kill switch lives on
  `SwapService`, the constructed `Arc<dyn SwapPort>` MUST be consumed by the
  service and never escape — `near_swap_provider` hands its provider straight
  into `SwapService::new` and returns the SERVICE, so no retained provider
  handle can emit traffic past a `Hard` kill (owed test
  `no_swap_traffic_path_bypasses_the_kill_door`).
- **Layers 3/4 as a typed service state:** `SwapKill { Live, WindDown, Hard }`
  (§2.6). The host resolves its flag through `resolve_manifest_kill(enabled,
  declared)` — DEFINED + never unresolved (enabled⇒Live; disabled+Hard⇒Hard;
  disabled+None/partial/contradictory⇒WindDown) — then calls
  `SwapService::set_kill(severity)`, which only ESCALATES (M4: a weaker
  directive is a no-op; a killed instance never resurrects). `quote()` and
  `execute()` check the kill door FIRST and refuse typed (`SwapDisabled`) before
  any provider call. The WindDown↔Hard divergence on in-flight STATUS polling
  lands with the status-poll chunk; the quote/execute refusal is identical for
  both (both refuse NEW work — correct). Gated by
  `manifest_kill_severity_reaches_swap_service`.

Honest notes on the layers:

- **pub.dev reality:** a published Dart package builds with default features
  (Cargokit), so for third-party consumers **layer 2 is the operative
  switch** — unconfigured swap code is inert dead weight emitting zero
  traffic (`swap_disabled_emits_zero_swap_traffic` proves the zero). Layer 1
  serves Relim's own flavor builds and any source-vendoring consumer.
- **In-flight swaps at kill time (the funds-safety analysis):** status
  polling is **observational** — a deposit settles or auto-refunds
  provider-side whether or not we ever poll (refunds go to the quote's
  `refundTo`). So even a hard kill strands *visibility*, never *funds*. Two
  kill severities, host-chosen (Relim: the manifest flag carries it):
  `WindDown` (default — refuse new quotes/executes immediately, poll
  in-flight swaps to terminal) and `Hard` (zero swap traffic from this
  instant; in-flight `SwapRecord`s marked tracking-unavailable, with the
  honest next step surfaced: funds settle or refund provider-side
  regardless).
- **Data isolation:** swap records live in their **own tables** (own
  migration namespace) inside the wallet DB. Swap-off leaves them READABLE —
  local reads are not swap traffic, and the history is the user's data —
  and droppable without touching any money table.
- **UI isolation:** hosts gate screens on `swap == null`; no other coupling
  surface exists, so "remove the feature" is hiding one tab.

---

### 3.6 Checkpoint bundle & birthday estimation (AS BUILT — `estimate_birthday` slice)

Restore needs a starting
height so the scanner doesn't replay the whole chain (§2.3), and
`estimate_birthday` (§3.1) turns "around when did you create this wallet?" into
a height OFFLINE. Both ride a bundle of checkpoints shipped INSIDE the signed
binary (§4.6 M2). This section owns the concrete design; §1.7 (data source),
§3.1 (the API), and §4.6 (the integrity posture) point here.

**Two consumers, two slices of one bundle.** `estimate_birthday` needs only
`(height, block_time)` pairs — a compact embedded table. Sync-start needs the
full `(height, hash, sapling_tree, orchard_tree)` to anchor the commitment trees
without rescanning from activation. The crypto audit (2026-06-14) settled this
slice's role: the backend does NOT self-verify a birthday frontier, so the
tree-state slice is not "hostile input to be checked" — it IS the **trusted
anchor** (signed-binary data) that provisioning uses INSTEAD of a live
`get_tree_state` (the M2 live-frontier threat is eliminated, not mitigated;
§3.2f). **This base chunk delivered the `(height, time)` slice +
`estimate_birthday`; the tree-state slice is AS BUILT in W3-inc-2c-iv-c (§3.2f).**

**Bundle source + format + provenance (M2) — AS BUILT.** The `(height, time)`
slice is the `checkmate`-generated set the ECC mobile SDKs ship (the exact data
Zashi/Zodl use; MIT, consumed AS DATA per §1.7). Codegen'd to
`pub(super) const MAINNET/TESTNET: &[(u32, u64)]` in
`sdk/zec-wallet-core/src/checkpoints/data.rs` (mainnet anchors from the Sapling
activation 419200 to the bundle tail; testnet likewise — the anchor counts and
tail heights live in `CHECKPOINTS.md`, their one home, and move on each bundle
refresh). **Reproducible provenance:** the committed
`sdk/zec-wallet-core/CHECKPOINTS.md` pins the source repo + commit + path +
deterministic extraction (`tools/extract_checkpoints.py`; mirrors the adapter's
`UPSTREAM.md`) so a reviewer regenerates byte-identical data. **The tree-state slice (W3-inc-2c-iv-c, §3.2f)
is ADDITIVE from the SAME pinned source rows:** `pub(super) const
MAINNET_TREESTATES / TESTNET_TREESTATES: &[(u32, &str, &str, &str)]` =
`(height, block_hash_hex, sapling_frontier_hex, orchard_frontier_hex)`, with its
OWN pinned content hash (`treestate_bundle_matches_pinned_provenance_hash`) and a
row-alignment test to the `(height, time)` slice. The `(height, time)` slice +
its hash here are UNTOUCHED by that addition.

**Integrity — TWO layers (M2; security-fold S10d).** (a) A runtime self-check
(`is_monotonic`, fail-closed): heights + block-times STRICTLY increasing; a
violating bundle degrades to the earliest known height (a fuller scan, never a
too-high birthday), never a silent wrong height. This catches REORDER /
DUPLICATION / REGRESSION + accidental corruption — but NOT a still-monotonic
value tamper (a lowered interior `time` stays monotonic yet shifts the floor
later → overshoot). (b) That tamper class is closed by PROVENANCE INTEGRITY: the
canonical content hash is pinned in code (`checkpoint_data_matches_pinned_provenance_hash`)
and recorded in `CHECKPOINTS.md`, so ANY change to `data.rs` fails CI and forces
re-derivation from the pinned source. The bundle ships inside the signed binary,
so production tampering also requires re-signing the app (the threat boundary).

**`estimate_birthday(network, approx_date) -> BlockHeight` — conservative
FLOOR, not interpolation (the silent-fund-loss guard).** A birthday slightly
BEFORE true creation finds ALL notes (a longer scan — cheap); a birthday AFTER
silently loses notes — so the estimate must NEVER overshoot. Algorithm:
1. `approx_date <= bundle.first.time` ⇒ `activation_height`.
2. `approx_date >= bundle.last.time` ⇒ `bundle.last.height` (never extrapolate
   past what we know offline; §2.3 catches an above-tip birthday at sync as
   `BirthdayInFuture`).
3. otherwise return the height of the LATEST checkpoint whose `time <=
   approx_date` (i.e. floor to the lower bracketing checkpoint `h0`).
This REFINES §3.1's earlier "interpolation" wording: flooring to `h0` is
strictly more conservative than interpolating between `h0` and `h1` and bounds
the worst-case over-scan to ≤ the LARGEST inter-anchor gap in the bundle
(mainnet 80,800 blocks across the sparsely-sampled pre-2019 history; 2,500 in
the modern tail) — no float, no division, no overshoot. (Hosts use a month/year
picker, §1.7, so the input is already coarse; flooring adds the safety margin.)

**Named tests (§8) — GREEN:**
- `estimate_birthday_floors_to_bracketing_checkpoint_never_overshoots` —
  against the REAL bundles, both networks: a floor assertion at the midpoint of
  EVERY consecutive checkpoint pair + a proptest that for any `u64` time the
  returned height's block-time ≤ the query (or the activation clamp) — never a
  checkpoint dated after the asked-for time.
- `checkpoint_bundle_monotonic_or_load_fails` — the shipped bundles pass the
  load self-check (strictly increasing heights + times, first == activation);
  reorder/duplication/regression are rejected (it does NOT, by design, catch a
  still-monotonic value tamper — that is the hash gate's job, next).
- `checkpoint_data_matches_pinned_provenance_hash` — pins the canonical content
  hash so any `data.rs` change (incl. a still-monotonic time tamper) fails CI;
  the real M2 defense (security-fold S10d).
- `birthday_out_of_range_arms` — the OFFLINE clamp arms: epoch/pre-activation ⇒
  activation, future ⇒ last checkpoint. (The above-tip restore ⇒ `BirthdayInFuture`
  arm is config validation on the gated wallet handle, §2.3 — not reachable here.)
- `poisoned_checkpoint_or_tree_state_does_not_silently_hide_funds` (§4.6 M2) —
  demonstrates the two-layer defense: a still-monotonic time tamper SLIPS the
  self-check + the floor (and would overshoot) but the pinned content hash
  catches it, so a poisoned bundle can't silently ship. (Live tree-state path
  DROPPED — provisioning anchors on the bundled frontier slice, §3.2f; see
  `provision_never_provisions_from_a_live_frontier`.)
