### 3.7 Watch-only wallets & UFVK export (#397, W-View — ADR-0538)

**The one-sentence contract:** a spending wallet can hand its full viewing
key to a party the user DELIBERATELY chose to trust with total history
visibility, and the SDK can run a complete read-path wallet FROM such a key —
sync, balances, history, receive addresses, honest refusals everywhere spend
authority would be needed.

**Why (demand + lineage).** FR-11/FR-12 established the internal split
("view ops need no seed; spend needs supply"); `None`-persistence is already
"view-only-at-rest" (§4.2). What was missing is the SURFACE for the adoption
scenarios partners actually ask for: a second-device watch wallet, an
accountant/auditor verifying balances against the chain independently,
portfolio tooling reading without spend keys. Every one of those needs BOTH
halves — an export from the spending wallet and an import that creates a
watch-only instance — so #397 ships them as one feature (ADR-0538 D1).

**What a UFVK is (threat framing, LOAD-BEARING for every decision below).**
The unified full viewing key reveals every incoming AND outgoing payment
(the OVK decrypts outgoing), past and future, plus balance — forever, for
anyone who ever holds it. It cannot spend and cannot reach the seed
(derivation is one-way). It is therefore PRIVACY-CRITICAL, SPEND-SAFE
material: the export consequence is surveillance, not theft, and the only
"revocation" is moving funds to a new wallet. The spec treats it exactly one
notch below the seed: same deliberate-action gating bar, weaker
at-rest/zeroization obligations (it is already persisted plaintext-in-
SQLCipher by the engine's own schema).

#### D1 — Export: one method, standard encoding, loud contract

```rust
impl Wallet {
    /// THE ONE SANCTIONED UFVK EGRESS (ADR-0538 / §5.4 HARD-D re-cast).
    /// Returns `UnifiedFullViewingKey::encode(network)` for the wallet's
    /// account — `uview1…` (main) / `uviewtest1…` (test), the standard
    /// Bech32m/F4Jumble unified encoding, network-bound and self-typed.
    /// Works at EVERY custody tier incl. `None`-persistence and watch-only
    /// (read from the engine's stored account — no seed touched, no
    /// `SeedRequired`). `require_open`-gated.
    ///
    /// HOST CONTRACT (LOUD): calling this hands the caller TOTAL HISTORY
    /// VISIBILITY (in + out, past + future). A UI host MUST gate it behind
    /// a deliberate user action at the backup-phrase bar (re-auth +
    /// screenshot protection + the D9 warning copy) — the reference UI's
    /// export screen is the normative example. NEVER call it implicitly,
    /// NEVER persist/log the string host-side beyond the user's explicit
    /// share action.
    pub async fn export_ufvk(&self) -> Result<String, WalletError>;
}
```

- Encoding: audited lib whole — `zcash_keys::keys::UnifiedFullViewingKey::
  encode` (pinned `=0.14.0`). NO custom envelope, NO extra version byte
  (the unified container is already typecoded + jumbled + HRP-network-bound;
  wrapping it would create a second parser — §4.6).
- The string is NOT zeroizing (String across FFI; same class as addresses —
  the engine already persists the UFVK plaintext inside the SQLCipher DB, so
  process-memory residue adds no new tier of exposure; documented residual).
- §5.4 UNCHANGED: `ufvk` stays on the forbidden-token log guard; the method
  emits `wallet.ufvk_export {outcome}` — outcome code ONLY, never the value,
  never a prefix. The extraction-policy deny-list gains the SANCTIONED
  entries for exactly this method + the D2 import param (the S204 designed
  path: sanctioned, never unmatched).

#### D2 — Watch-only create: the fourth constructor arm

```rust
impl Wallet {
    /// Create a WATCH-ONLY wallet from an externally-supplied UFVK string
    /// (the D1 export of some spending wallet). Full read path — sync,
    /// balance, history, receive addresses (UFVK-derived, same G7 default
    /// UA discipline) — and typed `WatchOnly` refusals on every spend-class
    /// surface. `birthday_height` mandatory-with-estimate (same
    /// `estimate_birthday` UX as restore; the checkpoint-bundle frontier ≤
    /// birthday provisions the tree anchor, §3.2f/§3.6 — never live tree
    /// state).
    pub async fn create_watch_only(
        cfg: WalletConfig,
        ufvk: &str,
        birthday_height: BlockHeight,
    ) -> Result<Wallet, WalletError>;
}
```

- Import path: `UnifiedFullViewingKey::decode(network, s)` →
  `import_account_ufvk(ACCOUNT_NAME, &ufvk, &birthday,
  AccountPurpose::ViewOnly, None)` (pinned `zcash_client_sqlite =0.21.0`).
  Still ONE account per instance (§1.6) — a second import is refused.
- Validation is typed and total: garbage/tampered string ⇒
  `InvalidViewingKey` (new §6.1 member, subsystem code `RW-VIEW-002`);
  network mismatch (a WELL-FORMED `uview1…` on a testnet config) ⇒ the SAME
  `NetworkMismatch` arm the seed restore uses (AS SHIPPED: `decode_ufvk`
  distinguishes the two by probe-decoding under the OPPOSITE network params
  on failure — a success there proves a well-formed cross-net artifact — so
  the D5 restore-arm UI renders "wrong network" and "not a viewing key" as
  the distinct inline errors it promises). A wrong-net key CANNOT
  half-import. **SIZE-CAP-BEFORE-ALLOC (§4.6, review security M3):** the
  string is bounded by `UFVK_MAX_BYTES` (4 KiB) INSIDE `decode_ufvk` before
  the upstream length-proportional parse, so a pathological clipboard paste
  rejects `InvalidViewingKey` with zero allocation. Zero panics on any input
  (decode is upstream's parser; our arms only map errors + never echo the
  string — §5.4).
- `SeedPersistence` AND `config.birthday` are MEANINGLESS here — there is no
  seed, and the birthday is the mandatory `birthday_height` param (an
  `Option`-in-config cannot express mandatory-with-estimate). Both config
  fields are ignored-with-documentation (NOT an error: hosts share one config
  type) and the store records the truth (D4).
- **Eager-import + crash-window converge (AS SHIPPED, review CONVERGED
  M2/M6):** the account import is ALWAYS eager (`resolve_watch_only_birthday`
  floors an above-bundle-tail height to the tail — over-scan-safe — since a
  watch-only wallet has no lazy seed-path to defer to). A process kill
  between the completion marker and the import leaves a marker-Complete,
  account-less store; unlike a seeded store it cannot self-heal at first
  sync (no seed to re-derive from), so `provision_account` on a watch-only
  wallet returns typed `ProvisioningIncomplete` (never a `WatchOnly` refusal
  surfaced from SYNC, which D3 declares FULL), and re-running
  `create_watch_only` with the SAME artifact CONVERGES (accepts the Complete
  store, idempotent import). A DIFFERENT artifact over an existing account is
  refused `WalletAlreadyExists` (never silently keeps the old key).
- Open: the existing `Wallet::open(cfg)` transparently opens a watch-only
  store (the manifest says what it is — D4); NO separate `open_watch_only`.
  `openWalletWithHostSeed`/seed-port config on a watch-only store ⇒ typed
  `WatchOnly` (the store can never consume a seed).

#### D3 — The capability matrix (what refuses, and HOW)

| Surface | Watch-only behavior |
|---|---|
| `sync` loop, `sync_status`, `balance`, `snapshot`, history, `watchIncomingFunds`, `estimate_birthday` | FULL — identical semantics (scanning is UFVK-based by construction) |
| rescan family | typed `WatchOnly` (AS SHIPPED — supersedes this section's earlier re-import sketch): the equivalent is wipe + `create_watch_only` with the SAME UFVK at the lower birthday — the UFVK is host-re-suppliable BY DEFINITION (unlike a seed), so the recreate path costs one call, and the delicate atomic-rename rebuild stays seed-shaped (the None-persistence rescan refusal precedent). A bespoke UFVK-capture arm through the temp-DB window is a RECORDED follow-up candidate, its own review |
| `current_address`, diversified mint (FR-8) | FULL — UA derivation reads the stored UFVK (already the §3.3a path) |
| `export_ufvk` | ALLOWED — identity operation (the host supplied the string; ADR-0538 D5) |
| `send` / `propose*` / shield / Move / drain (§3.2h/§3.2i family) | typed **`WalletError::WatchOnly`** at the ENTRY of each pipeline (before any proposal/token mint — a watch-only wallet must never mint a `SpendBinding` or burn a take-once stage) |
| swap — BOTH directions incl. Buy/IntoZec (quote, deposit, drain) | typed `WatchOnly` at the CORE constructor (`enable_swap` now returns `Result` — AS SHIPPED; v1 smallest-honest-surface; Buy-side relaxation = Q12). **Bridge pass-through (review M3/H5 — CLOSED):** the FFI seam `enable_near_swap` passes the core `WatchOnly` through TYPED as `SwapError::WatchOnly` (RW-SWAP-015; `SwapErrorKind.watchOnly` on the Dart surface), and checks it FIRST — ahead of the config-shaped legs (unsupported runtime → `ProviderUnavailable`, bad endpoint → `RequestInvalid`) — so the structural "this wallet can never swap" is never masked as a retryable/fixable config error even when the config is ALSO broken (the sweep-ephemeral WatchOnly-first precedence, this same matrix); any OTHER future `enable_swap` refusal still degrades to `ProviderUnavailable` (fail-safe generic, never a wrong specific). Unreachable from the reference UI (the watch-only chrome hides the whole swap surface; the activation provider degrades every enable failure to swap-off, logging the stable code only) |
| `reveal_mnemonic` | typed `WatchOnly` (NOT `NoMnemonic` — the honest reason is the wallet KIND, and UI copy differs: "this wallet has no keys to back up") |
| `sweep_ephemeral_funds` / `reclaim_ephemeral_slots` (§3.2i-2) | typed `WatchOnly` FIRST (AS SHIPPED, review M1/M5 — ahead of the `can_derive_signing_key` pre-check, so never the `SeedRequired` retry-with-seed lie; no money moves either way — a watch-only wallet has no reserved ephemerals) |
| `wipe` / `wipe_force` / `sever_custody` / `custody_disclosure` / `exists` / `close` | FULL — same crypto-shred discipline (D4); `sever_custody` (FR-53, the duress force-sever) is `wipe`'s custody resolution, run while the wallet may still be held. `custody_disclosure`'s `WalletKind` field is DEFERRED to the bridge slice (D7 step 2 — one FRB regen), read from the manifest; `Wallet::is_watch_only()` ships now as the core chrome key |

`WatchOnly` is a NEW `WalletError` member (code `RW-VIEW-001`;
`InvalidViewingKey` = `RW-VIEW-002`), bridged under the enum-lockstep guard
(`bridge_enums_cover_core_variants`), classified in the reference UI as a
STRUCTURAL refusal (an explanation surface, never a retry affordance — there
is nothing to retry).

#### D4 — The store: manifest v3, no seed artifacts, unchanged shred

- A watch-only provision writes **manifest v3**: same 4-byte layout
  `[ver=0x03][net][persist][seed_source]` with `persist = WatchOnly (0x02)`
  and `seed_source = WatchOnly (0x03)`. Spending wallets KEEP writing v2 —
  the version byte doubles as a capability gate: a pre-#397 binary reading a
  watch-only store fails the version dispatch TYPED (honest "this build
  cannot open this wallet"), never a half-open that later panics hunting a
  seed. `read_manifest` stays exact-version + exact-length; v3 with a
  non-watch-only byte pair is `StoreCorrupt` (no mixed states).
- NO sealed seed, NO seed fingerprint row, NO creation-stamp seed-provenance
  semantics (`store::repair`'s §3.2f stamp arms are seed-provenance logic —
  a v3 manifest never enters them). The UX aux tables (`sync_stamp`,
  `ever_synced`, `rescan_rebuilding`, creation stamp as plain wallet-age)
  work UNCHANGED — they are seed-agnostic.
- DB-at-rest custody UNCHANGED: SQLCipher under the sealed DB key, same
  keychain namespace, same crypto-shred wipe (the UFVK at rest is
  privacy-sensitive; "watch-only" must not silently mean "plaintext").
  `custody_disclosure` gains `kind: WalletKind { Spending, WatchOnly }` —
  read from the manifest (an ACTIVE probe already; one more byte) — so the
  wipe confirmation + custody badge render the truth ("this wallet holds no
  spending keys; deleting it does not endanger funds").
- Rescan: REFUSED typed for watch-only (AS SHIPPED — see the D3 matrix row:
  wipe + recreate from the same UFVK at the lower birthday is the
  equivalent; the temp-DB re-import arm sketched during design was traded
  away deliberately — KISS over a second bespoke path through the
  atomic-rename window).

#### D5 — Reference UI (`zec_wallet_ui`) surfaces

1. **Export screen** (Settings → Security → "Export viewing key"): CLONES
   the backup-phrase gating verbatim — `walletRevealAuthorizerProvider`
   re-auth, `screenSecurityProvider` screenshot/recents protection,
   view-only reveal latch, autoDispose read — plus QR + copy affordances
   (same as receive). Gate bar deliberately EQUAL to the seed's even though
   the key can't spend: the export consequence (total surveillance) is the
   thing being confirmed, and a lower bar would teach users the artifact is
   casual.
2. **D9 warning copy contract** (l10n keys, ×16): the screen MUST state, in
   plain words, ALL of: (a) everything the wallet has ever received AND
   sent, and everything it ever will, becomes visible to whoever holds this
   key; (b) it CANNOT spend or move funds; (c) share it only with someone
   you trust to see your entire history; (d) the only way to un-share is to
   move your funds to a new wallet. No softening.
3. **Watch-only create entry**: the restore flow gains a third tab/arm
   ("Watch-only") — paste/scan a `uview…` string + the SAME birthday
   estimate UX as seed restore. Wrong-network and malformed strings render
   their typed errors inline (§6 tone: next step, never a code).
4. **Watch-only chrome**: a persistent, non-alarming "Watch-only" badge on
   the wallet header (custody-badge sibling); Send/Shield/Swap affordances
   HIDDEN (not disabled-with-tease); Security screen swaps "Backup phrase"
   for "About this watch-only wallet" (no-keys explanation + the export
   entry); delete-wallet copy drops the funds-at-risk framing (nothing at
   risk — D4 disclosure).

#### D6 — Test contract (§8 named-test rows; vectors FIRST)

AS SHIPPED names in parentheses where they diverged from the design sketch
(review M4 — the spec is the truth, so it records what landed):

- `kat_fixed_seed_derives_pinned_ufvk_encoding` (SHIPPED name; the design
  sketched `ufvk_export_matches_upstream_kat_vectors`) — a SELF-GENERATED
  pinned golden for BOTH networks + a decode round-trip that proves the
  exported artifact views the SAME account (default-UA parity ⟺ identical
  receivers) + cross-net reject + hostile-input floor. Rationale for the
  self-golden over official vectors (AS SHIPPED, review H4): the audited
  crate owns ZIP-316 vector conformance UPSTREAM; this pins OUR wiring +
  catches dependency churn (the real in-repo risk), the SAME discipline the
  UA KAT `kat_fixed_seed_derives_pinned_unified_address` already uses.
  Importing the official unified-FVK vectors is a recorded follow-up.
- The export→import→same-account parity is folded INTO the KAT above +
  `create_watch_only_from_an_exported_ufvk_views_the_same_account` (the twin
  test: default-UA parity + re-export string equality + plain-open relaunch).
- `watch_only_balance_parity_with_the_spending_twin` — DEFERRED to the
  device-e2e slice (D7 step 4): the full chain-scan parity needs a live/fake
  chain fixture, exercised there rather than as a core unit test.
- `create_watch_only_rejects_bad_artifacts_typed_and_leaves_no_remnant`
  (SHIPPED; folds `a_wrong_network_ufvk`/`garbage_ufvk`) — garbage ⇒
  `InvalidViewingKey`, a well-formed cross-net key ⇒ `NetworkMismatch`, an
  oversized paste ⇒ `InvalidViewingKey` (size cap), `exists()==false` after
  every reject (no remnant — decode runs before the lock).
- `every_spend_class_surface_refuses_watch_only_typed` (SHIPPED) — the D3
  matrix MECHANICALLY, table-driven: reveal / propose / propose_uri /
  propose_shield / queue_send / queue_send_uri / send_by_id / sweep / reclaim
  / enable_swap each return `WatchOnly`, NO `SpendBinding` minted, NO
  `SeedRequired` lie. (This is the test whose absence hid the review B1.)
- `watch_only_refuses_a_seed_port_attach_typed` (SHIPPED, review H1) — the
  D2 "the store can never consume a seed" contract line.
- `watch_only_create_converges_over_an_account_less_remnant` (SHIPPED,
  review M2/M6) — the crash-window converge + the different-artifact refuse.
- Rescan: `create_watch_only_from_an_exported_ufvk_views_the_same_account`
  asserts the rescan REFUSAL (`WatchOnly`) — the AS-SHIPPED D3 row supersedes
  the design's "rescan re-import" (which was traded away).
- `a_v3_watch_only_manifest_round_trips_and_opens_seedless` +
  `corrupt_manifest_is_typed_reject` (extended: v2-with-watchonly-bytes +
  3× v3-wrong-pair rejects) — the two-live-versions capability gate; the
  "pre-v3 reader rejects" property IS the `_ => StoreCorrupt` version arm.
- Extraction policy: the SANCTIONED entries (exact `export_ufvk` /
  `ufvk: String` / the call declaration + the `InvalidViewingKey` error
  name) land WITH the feature (the scan otherwise fails CI — by design).
- §5.4: the export event is named `wallet.view_export` (AS SHIPPED, review
  M2/H2 — `wallet.ufvk_export` would trip the capture guard's own `ufvk`
  value scan) + `"uview"` added to the guard's FORBIDDEN list (H1: catches a
  leaked VALUE, where `ufvk` catches only the field NAME). A capture test
  driving `export_ufvk` is a recorded follow-up (the guard is `cfg(test)`;
  today no path emits a UFVK value, so nothing regresses).
- Zeroization inventory (§4.7): UNCHANGED list + a documented NON-item (the
  exported String — rationale in D1).

## 4. Security

### 4.1 Keys-in-Rust enforcement points (brief §6 item 6)

1. **Type structure:** `SeedSource`, the internal `UnifiedSpendingKey`
   wrapper, and the DB key are non-`Clone`, non-`Debug`, zeroizing, and not
   reachable from any `pub` DTO. The bridge crate's API module contains no
   function returning them — checkable by the FFI-allowlist named test (§8).
2. **Crate split:** FRB only in the `zec_wallet` bridge crate; the core compiles
   without it. Relim side: only relim-ffi touches FRB (`relim-ext` is the
   slim **FRB-free** C-ABI entry — overview §2/§3); wallet DTOs reach the
   Relim UI only as relim-ffi mirrors, under the §4-rule-6 allowlist.
3. **`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`** in `zec-wallet-core` and the `zec_wallet` bridge crate.
4. **Audited libs whole:** librustzcash performs ALL derivation, note
   en/decryption, proving, signing; our code is glue (crypto-rules Rule
   Zero). Re-implementing any of it is a CRITICAL review finding. The swap
   adapter is the DELIBERATE exception in the other direction (ADR-0525/H1):
   its REST client is OUR hand-audited code — transport + JSON over the
   NetDialer stack, zero crypto in it (§3.2) — because a funds path deserves
   a hand-audited surface and §4.6 demands bounds-before-DTO-entry.

### 4.2 Spending-key lifecycle

Derived from `SeedSource` at create/restore and used to initialize the
zcash_client_sqlite account; zcash_client_sqlite persists only what
librustzcash's design requires (UFVK + note commitments — never spending
keys). Signing re-derives transient spend authority per transaction inside
librustzcash. **Verified (2026-06-10), two upstream sharp edges we own:**
(a) `UnifiedSpendingKey` implements **no Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop** (it is
`Clone + Debug`; zcash_keys' zeroize dep gates on an unrelated feature) —
mitigation, scope-pinned (review HARD-C): the USK lives **only inside the
`spawn_blocking` proving closure** — never held across an `.await`, never
stored, never placed in any container with a transitive `Debug` impl, never
`Clone`-reachable from our API; the un-zeroized residue in freed memory is a
**documented residual for crypto audit** and an upstream-issue candidate. (b)
`UnifiedSpendingKey::from_seed` **panics** on seeds < 32 bytes and does not
enforce the ZIP-32 252-byte upper bound — our `SeedSource` validation (§2.2)
enforces **both bounds before any upstream call**; a panic across FFI is a
crash, not an error (named test §8).

**Seed-at-rest is two-mode (`SeedPersistence`, §2.2) — a deliberate
divergence from upstream.** Their contract (seed per-call, the APP holds it
— §1.7) is right for native apps but wrong for Flutter: it would force the
host to keep the mnemonic in Dart to answer `SeedRequired` (Rust-side DB
migrations occasionally need the seed) and backup-reveal — the exact
keys-in-Dart anti-pattern this SDK exists to kill. So:

- **`SealedKeychain`** (Dart-path default): the SDK seals the seed under a
  keychain-random wrap key (the §4.3 sealing pattern) and handles
  `reveal_mnemonic` + `SeedRequired` internally; the mnemonic touches Dart
  only at the §3.3 carve-outs.
- **`None`** (the Relim path): nothing persisted; `SeedRequired` bubbles to
  the host, which re-derives via `WalletSeedPort` (cheap, Rust-side).

### 4.2a The `SealedKeychain` seal — pinned construction (W2's FIRST crypto-change review chunk)

Manager-confirmed at the W1 review (= old Q9 / review MAJOR-1). The envelope
is frozen HERE so two implementations cannot diverge:

```
[ ver: 1 byte = 0x01 ]
[ nonce: 24 bytes, OsRng ]
[ XChaCha20-Poly1305( length-prefixed plaintext, aad = SEED_SEAL_DOMAIN ) ‖ tag: 16 ]
```

- **Nonce strategy (crypto-rules: documented-or-blocker):** the random
  24-byte OsRng nonce IS the documented misuse-resistance strategy —
  XChaCha's extended nonce makes random collision negligible, and there is
  no counter state to corrupt across the §6.3 kill windows.
- `SEED_SEAL_DOMAIN = "zec-wallet/seal-seed/v1"` — an **AEAD AAD domain
  tag, NOT an HKDF label**: the frozen derivation tree (identity.md §2.1)
  is untouched; this constant is SDK-owned and append-only versioned.
- **Variable, length-prefixed plaintext (review HARD-A):** the sealed blob
  carries the seed bytes AND (when present) the mnemonic words — that is
  what makes `reveal_mnemonic` after restart possible; `RawBytes` wallets
  seal the seed only.
- **Wrap-key ↔ keychain binding:** the AEAD key is keychain-random
  (OsRng), resident under the platform keystore ACL (iOS
  Security.framework; Android Keystore via the Q10 glue) — both platform
  sub-cases bind the seal to the device keystore.
- **Honest at-rest posture, said plainly:** the third-party path is
  keychain-ACL + device-lock protection — **no passphrase KDF**. A seized
  *unlocked* device reads the seed. Argon2id-class at-rest belongs to the
  Relim integration (identity-core owns that posture); the SDK README
  states this, not fine print.
- **Validate-before-use:** version byte + length checks before any decrypt
  attempt on open; tamper/garbage ⇒ typed error, never a panic.
- Named test: `wallet_seed_seal_roundtrip_and_tamper_rejected`.

The upstream `keysMissing` scare cluster (§1.7) shapes the sealed mode:
keychain-says-missing while the wallet DB exists surfaces as typed
`KeystoreInconsistent` (§6.1) — never silently treated as a fresh wallet —
and the keychain accessibility class (`WhenUnlocked…ThisDeviceOnly` et al.)
is a documented, named choice with its restore-to-new-device consequence
stated, not an incidental default.

**Locked ≠ missing ≠ invalidated — the disambiguation rule** (the upstream
scare cluster was exactly this misread): iOS returns *item-not-found* for
items that exist but are lock-protected (prewarming, before-first-unlock),
and Android Keystore keys are **permanently invalidated** by biometric/PIN
reset. So: probe keychain *accessibility/lock state* before ever concluding
*absence*; platform lock errors map to `KeystoreUnavailable` (transient —
"unlock your device"); genuine absence with a DB present maps to
`KeystoreInconsistent { permanently_invalidated: bool }` — the invalidated
arm renders the honest recovery: "restore from your written phrase." Named
test: `locked_keychain_never_misread_as_missing`.

#### FR-13 — per-wallet keychain custody namespacing (✅ AS BUILT S113 — wiring + crypto-change review + code review; ✅ S218/#394 — Android StrongBox device proof + no-migration FINAL)

The wrap-key custody was a process-global keychain item under FIXED names
(Apple `service="zec-wallet.seal"`/`account="wrap-key.v1"`; Android alias
`zec_wallet.wrap.v<gen>`), so a SECOND wallet on a device OVERWROTE the first's
item → the first's on-disk seal orphaned → typed `WrapArtifactInvalid` / forced
rescan. The fix derives a per-wallet **namespace** from `db_dir`
(`keychain_namespace_for` = `hex(SHA256(db_dir.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes())[..16])`
— exact OS path bytes, 128-bit hex, no path chars in a keychain attribute) and
suffixes the Apple account (`wrap-key.v1.<ns>`) / embeds it in the Android alias
prefix (`zec_wallet.wrap.<ns>.v<gen>`), threaded via `platform_vault(namespace)`
into the vault constructors from create/open/open_with_seed_port/rescan (rescan
reuses the wallet's own `db_dir` ⇒ same namespace ⇒ custody survives). The
`KeychainPort` trait is UNCHANGED (the namespace is baked into the vault instance
at construction). **Zero-config** (no `WalletConfig` field): distinct `db_dir`s
get distinct items automatically — the general multi-wallet fix for any consumer,
and a Relim decoy (a SEPARATE `db_dir`) keeps its own custody for free.

**SCOPE — coexistence, NOT deniability (the security review headline).** FR-13
is the PREREQUISITE for a decoy to retain custody; it does NOT make the decoy
deniable. With distinct items, a forensic keychain dump shows N items = N
identities (a new existence oracle), and the namespace is an UNKEYED `SHA256(db_dir)`
an attacker who knows the path convention can recompute and confirm. Hiding the
*count* + making the namespace unguessable (secret-derived + count-padding) is
owed by the duress model (**ADR-0526**), not this FR — the decoy claim stays
gated. The marginal new leak is small today (the decoy's `db_dir`/lock/seal already
sit on disk), but a future hidden-decoy design MUST replace this derivation. The
orphaned old-name item is also forensic residue (**FR-14** crypto-shred territory).

**BACKWARD-COMPAT (pre-prod break):** a wallet provisioned BEFORE FR-13 holds its
item under the bare name; post-FR-13 code only queries the namespaced name, so the
old item is UNREACHABLE — typed `KeystoreInconsistent` (fail-closed, never a wrong
open), recovery = restore-from-mnemonic / re-provision. No auto-migration (no
shipped consumers); the on-device test wallet re-provisions once. **DECISION
(S218, #394 close-out): no bare→namespaced read fallback will EVER ship — FINAL.**
The SDK was never published pre-namespacing (the #388 push gate predates FR-13),
so ZERO EXTERNAL installs hold a bare-name item; GA ships namespaced from day
one. (Internal pre-S113 installs — dev-Mac keychains, the pre-FR-13 example
device wallet — did hold bare items: each fails CLOSED on upgrade and
re-provisions from its recorded phrase, which the device wallet already did;
Apple's `purge_namespace` additionally best-effort-sweeps the bare relic.)
A legacy-name fallback would be dead code guarding an empty set AND a
permanent widening of the custody read path (every open probing a second,
attacker-plantable item name forever). The migration story is therefore
structural: nothing to migrate, fail-closed (`KeystoreInconsistent`) on any
pre-FR-13 relic, never a silent re-key.

**HOST CONTRACT:** the namespace is byte-stable on the `db_dir` STRING — the host
MUST pass a byte-identical `db_dir` across create/open/rescan (the SAME assumption
the on-disk seals + `WalletLock` already carry; the namespace inherits it, adds no
new one).

**SUPERSEDED IN PART — S2 `custody`, [ADR-0559](../adr/0559-wallet-custody-a-wallets-identity-is-a-minted-id-in-the-wrap-artifact-not-its-path.md)
(S296).** The wrap key's namespace is no longer derived from `db_dir`: it is
`hex(SHA256(CUSTODY_DOMAIN ‖ id)[..16])` over a random 128-bit custody
identifier minted at create and carried as a plaintext locator in a
vault-independent outer frame of `wrap.artifact` (integrity is the AEAD's — a
tampered locator can only refuse). A moved or renamed `db_dir` is the SAME
wallet. `keychain_namespace_for(db_dir)` survives with two jobs: the
path-keyed keychain INDEX item (`{id, legacy_ns?, state}`, no key material)
that lets a wipe find the namespace after the host deleted the files, and the
LEGACY namespace a pre-S2 wallet still custodies under until its one-time
migration at first open (one commit point, the `wrap.artifact` rewrite; the
legacy purge deferred to the next open, best-effort). The byte-stable-string
rule above now binds only the index and the migration input: a `db_dir`
variant opens the same wallet, and costs at most one orphan index item.
FR-13's isolation property — distinct wallets, distinct items, equal-length
namespaces — is unchanged, as is the ADR-0526 existence-oracle scope note.

**OPERATIONAL ROUND (post-review, money/unstable-net/mobile/edge lens — no
blockers).** The Android `max_generation` alias-prefix scan stays wallet-local ONLY
because every namespace is equal-length hex; a `debug_assert` would be stripped in
release, so the invariant is now enforced by a `KeychainNamespace` NEWTYPE (the only
constructor validates the 32-char lowercase-hex shape; a malformed namespace is
unconstructable, so a bad value can never reach a vault — panic-free, every build,
the `WrapArtifact::from_bytes` idiom). Added anti-regression tests:
`two_none_mode_wallets_coexist_the_decoy_custody_scenario` (the ACTUAL decoy path —
two `None`-mode DB-key seals coexist), `renamed_keychain_namespace_orphans_custody_fail_closed_not_a_wrong_open`
(the pre-FR-13 upgrade → typed `KeystoreInconsistent`, never a wrong open),
`port_wrong_length_seed_is_typed_invalid_before_consume_not_a_panic` (FR-12 — an
out-of-bounds host seed is `InvalidSeedLength` at `acquire_seed`, caught before the
token consume), `import_via_a_denied_port_is_seed_required_no_oracle` (the
Denied→SeedRequired collapse on the import path), and
`queued_send_with_a_wrong_seed_port_b1_rejects_in_the_drain_stays_queued` (FR-12 B1
in the BACKGROUND drain — a wrong staged seed errors the intent + leaves it Queued,
never built/spent). NO money-loss path: every custody-orphan / wrong-seed / port
failure is fail-closed + recoverable (re-provision from seed; the chain is the
source of truth). Documented residuals: the Android JNI zero-fill is best-effort
(pre-existing), and `rescan_from` on a `None` wallet returns `SeedRequired`
(SealedKeychain-only by design).

Named tests (gate 8): `keychain_namespace_is_stable_and_distinct_per_db_dir`,
`two_wallets_at_distinct_db_dirs_retain_custody_across_switches`,
`same_namespace_collides_proving_the_namespace_is_load_bearing` (host, over a shared-keychain
test double), + `two_namespaces_coexist_in_the_real_apple_keychain` (macOS `#[ignore]`
manual gate — the REAL Apple backend, verified) + the operational-round tests above.
Android production wiring was **DEVICE-PROVEN S218 (#394 close-out)** by the
integration gate `fr13_two_wallets_retain_custody_across_switches`
(`example/integration_test/custody_coexistence_e2e_test.dart` — throwaway
sibling leaves, production custody structurally unreachable): on real StrongBox
hardware, create A → create B → reopen A serves A's ORIGINAL UA (the same seed
unsealed; NOTE this step re-enacts the APPLE pre-FR-13 hazard — fixed-account
delete-first overwrite → `WrapArtifactInvalid` — while pre-FR-13 ANDROID would
have passed it via per-store generations + artifact-pinned loads) → the full
A→B→A switch cycle holds → **the ANDROID teeth: the plain loud-sever `wipe` of
B verify-real-severs exactly B's namespace and A still opens (an un-namespaced
or namespace-collapsed purge scan severs EVERY wallet's wrap key — this leg is
what catches that regression on Android)**; both
wallets measured `tier=strongbox`, `degraded=false`. Scope honesty: the device
run proves PURGE-scan non-crossing; the `max_generation` alias-scan scoping is
structural (equal-length hex namespaces, the newtype invariant) + host-tested —
both wallets sit at generation 1 throughout, so the run cannot distinguish a
generation-scan crossing. (S218 also fixed a same-process pid-collision between
the two macOS `--ignored` raw-keychain gates — the purge gate now claims
`pid+2`, the coexistence gate keeps `pid`/`pid+1`; all three real-keychain
gates re-verified green together at HEAD.) **crypto-change review (S113):
NO BLOCKERS.**

#### FR-14 — public crypto-shred `Wallet::wipe(cfg)` for panic-wipe (✅ AS BUILT S114 chunk 1 — crypto-change review DESIGN + wiring review, NO BLOCKERS)

The only public teardown is `close()`; the wrap-key sever (`SealedSeedVault::wipe`
→ `KeychainPort::delete_wrap_key`) is `pub(crate)`. So a host panic-wipe can only
delete `db_dir` **as files**, leaving the keychain wrap key resident → a forensic
flash-recovery of the deleted `dbkey.seal` + the **surviving keychain wrap key** is
decryptable, and the orphaned keychain item is itself an existence oracle. FR-14
makes the crypto-shred a public verb, finishing the already-declared `Wallet::wipe`
(API surface §3.1, line ~777) + closing audit **A7** / §4.7.

**TWO chunks (founder-steered S114).** Chunk 1 (this block, BUILT) = the `wipe(cfg)`
verb, backend-agnostic. Chunk 2 (NEXT, `#### FR-14 chunk 2` below) = the Apple
Secure-Enclave custody re-architecture that upgrades the Apple shred from best-effort
to a true crypto-erase. The verb does not change between chunks (it calls
`purge_namespace` either way) — chunk 2 transparently upgrades the guarantee.

**CORRECTED 2026-10-06 (ADR-0571; the 2026-10-05 review, F02).** Every "true
cryptographic erase" / "permanently undecryptable" claim in FR-14 below overstates
what deletion establishes. Deleting a hardware-held key (Android StrongBox/TEE, the
Secure Enclave) removes it, but neither platform shows that an EARLIER copy of the
key blob is unusable afterwards on the same device: Android only for a
rollback-resistant key, which we neither request nor check; Apple publishes no
per-key equivalent. The disclosure is now `erase_assurance: HardwareKeyDeleted |
BestEffort` (was `crypto_erases_on_delete: bool`) and the UI says the key is held
by secure hardware and deleted with the wallet. The text below is kept as the
build record; read its "true erase" as `HardwareKeyDeleted`. Its quotation of
Apple ("permanently undecryptable… irreversible by design") has no source we
can cite and is withdrawn (ADR-0571).

**ATTACK-VECTOR ANALYSIS (founder asked "what are we protecting from").** The asset
is the 32-byte `SealKey` → DB key → `wallet.db`. Per Apple's Platform Security docs:
on **Android StrongBox/TEE** the wrap key is hardware-non-exportable, so `deleteEntry`
is a true cryptographic erase (the wrapped SealKey is permanently undecryptable). On
**Apple**, the SealKey is stored AS the keychain item value, and a plain
`SecItemDelete` removes the row but the encrypted blob can linger in `keychain-2.db`
free pages until vacuum. iOS gates the secret behind a Secure-Enclave round-trip +
the `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` class key, so a flash image is NOT decryptable
offline (AV3) or on a locked seizure (AV1), and `ThisDeviceOnly` is never
synced/backed-up (AV4) — but under **AV2 (duress / coerced unlock — Relim's CORE
threat)** the live SEP would decrypt the lingering residual, and combined with a
flash-recovered `dbkey.seal` the funds are recoverable. macOS login-keychain is
weaker still (decryptable under the coercer's login password). **AV2 is the vector
chunk 2 closes**: wrapping the SealKey under a non-extractable Secure-Enclave key
(data-protection keychain) makes its deletion a true erase even under coerced unlock
(Apple docs: data wrapped with a deleted SE key is "permanently undecryptable…
irreversible by design"), bringing Apple to parity with Android. The residual NEITHER
chunk closes (disclose honestly): keychain metadata free-page residue = a weak
EXISTENCE oracle (not a funds path), erased fully only by the OS "Erase All Content
and Settings" (effaceable storage), beyond per-app scope.

**Public API (matches the existing declaration — `cfg`-based, refuses-if-open):**
`Wallet::wipe(cfg: &WalletConfig) -> Result<(), WalletError>` (associated fn, NOT
`self`). It acquires the single-writer `WalletLock` (so a live instance ⇒ typed
refusal, never a wipe under an open DB — the line-777 `WalletOpen` contract), so it
is **also** the `db_dir`-only variant the panic-wipe path needs (panic-wipe runs
AFTER teardown — the lock is free; `cfg` carries `db_dir`). No `self`-consuming
variant + no separate `destroy_custody` (KISS/DRY — one lock-guarded entry covers
both the live-handle case [host `close()`s first, then `wipe(cfg)`] and the
post-teardown case). No key material, no FFI key crossing — a pure lifecycle verb.
*Corrected S306 (INC-027):* `close()` returns `Ok` only after the lock is free —
it takes sole ownership of the handle's state (`Arc::try_unwrap`) and drops it,
so no background holder can keep the lock past it (the Tor-state waker did,
until `f0b84668`). ONE bounded residual remains and the host must plan for it:
a holder that outlives `QUIESCE_MAX` (30 s) — a wedged blocking section, not
the normal path — makes `close()` return `Ok` with the lock still held, logged
as `wallet.close_quiesce_expired`; a `wipe` in that window answers `WalletOpen`
(fail-closed for INTEGRITY — never a shred under a live connection — but not for
secrecy: the keychain wrap is intact until the wipe runs). A duress flow retries
the wipe on `WalletOpen` for a BOUNDED time; past it, the case belongs to the
duress force-sever, **`Wallet::sever_custody(db_dir, deadline)`** (FR-53, stage S16,
ADR-0565; core built S308, the bridge `WalletHandle.severCustody` at ABI 7). It tries the lock
without waiting. Free → the plain wipe, `files: Removed`. Held → it severs the
key-store custody anyway, deletes NO file (`files: LeftForHost`: the host deletes the
directory after it answers), and poisons every instance in this process to `Wiped`.
It answers within the deadline, and every custody outcome is in its `SeverReport`:
- `Severed { count }` is PROVEN (a non-zero count);
- a locked key store gets a blind scoped delete, reported `SeveredUnproven
  { CountUnreadable }`;
- anything else is `NotSevered { cause }`.

The bridge adds a hard bound on the WHOLE call (ADR-0566): `severCustody` clamps
`deadlineMs` to `[0, 4000]` and answers by `deadlineMs + severAnswerGraceMs()` (250 ms)
whatever stalls. An overrun answers `notSevered(stillRunning)` with `files: stillInUse`
and `holder: unknown`: the core call cannot be cancelled and may still be deleting in
`db_dir`. The host purges ONLY on `leftForHost`, never on `stillInUse`; it calls again
with a backoff until the cause is not `stillRunning`. While a sever of a `db_dir` is
still running, a new sever there answers `stillRunning` at once, and every other door
at it (open, the creates, restore, watch-only, the host-seed pair) refuses with
`walletAlreadyOpen`, `wipe` and `wipeForce` with `walletOpen`, before any work. The
key is the directory's real path. While any sever is still resolving that path, the
doors refuse at ANY directory (fail-closed; ADR-0566 §5 "The cost"). Like `wipe`, the
door sets the device log `Off` first.

What it buys is secrecy AT REST ONLY: a live holder keeps the seed and DB key in RAM
until it drops. Its residuals are ADR-0565's, as amended by ADR-0566. Two host fallbacks are WRONG, and the
verb is the remedy for both: deleting `db_dir` (or the lock file) itself
— a fresh inode lets the next open take a "free" lock beside a live connection,
defeating this very check — and treating `wipe_force` as a `WalletOpen` remedy (it
takes the same lock and refuses the same way). And a host that fires `close()`
UNAWAITED and then opens or wipes races by its own ordering: await the close.

**ORDERING — keychain-FIRST (this SUPERSEDES the older §6.3 "sealed seed → DB key →
files" on-disk-first note).** The authoritative shred is severing the keychain wrap
key: the instant it is gone, the §4.2a `SealKey` is unrecoverable ⇒ BOTH on-disk
seals (`seed.seal`, `dbkey.seal`) and the `wallet.db` ciphertext are permanently
dead — file deletion becomes best-effort cleanup of dead bytes, order-irrelevant.
The old files-first ordering is strictly WORSE on a mid-wipe crash: it deletes
`dbkey.seal` (killing the money) but a crash before the keychain step leaves the
SealKey resident — an **existence oracle** AND, with flash-recovery of the just-
deleted `dbkey.seal`, decryptable. Keychain-first leaves only dead ciphertext + NO
keychain item on any crash point — exactly FR-14's "no orphaned keychain item
survives" acceptance. So:
1. **Sever the keychain (THE crypto-shred):** `SealedSeedVault::purge()` →
   `KeychainPort::purge_namespace()` — a NEW port method (below).
2. **Delete files (best-effort cleanup):** `remove_dir_all(db_dir)`, tolerating
   `NotFound` — sweeps `wallet.db` + WAL/SHM sidecars + `block-cache.db` +
   `*.seal` + `wrap.artifact` + manifest + marker + lock + any future file in one
   shot (more complete than enumerating the known constants; `db_dir` is per-wallet
   by the FR-13 host contract, never shared).

**`KeychainPort::purge_namespace(&self) -> Result<usize, WalletError>`** — sever ALL
vault material under THIS vault's baked-in FR-13 namespace, **artifact-independent**,
idempotent. **The `usize` is the COUNT severed — LOAD-BEARING, do not refactor to
`Result<()>`:** it is the verify-real-sever signal (below). Distinct from
`delete_wrap_key(artifact)` (one generation by artifact): purge is the authoritative
shred AND the orphan-sweep the arch seam note (`store.rs` provision Step 1) flagged —
a provision killed after the Custody step leaves a gen-N alias with NO on-disk
artifact (`inspect` reads `Empty`), so an artifact-keyed delete can't reach it; a
namespace scan can.
- **Apple** (`apple.rs`): delete the generic password at `(service,
  account=wrap-key.v1.<ns>)` — one item per namespace; returns 1 if it existed, 0 if
  already gone. PLUS a best-effort sweep of the pre-FR-13 BARE `wrap-key.v1` item
  (the FR-13→FR-14 residue oracle), NOT counted (a non-load-bearing legacy item;
  counting it could mask a mismatch), production-service-scoped (a selftest vault
  never reaches it).
- **Android** (`android.rs`): scan `KeyStore.aliases()`, `deleteEntry` every alias
  whose name starts with `self.alias_prefix` (the namespaced `zec_wallet.wrap.<ns>.v`),
  returns the count — covers the live generation AND orphaned generations from a
  failed provision / incomplete rotation, `with_retry`-wrapped (a non-transient
  partial failure propagates so files are NOT deleted). Idempotent. The FR-13
  equal-length-hex namespace keeps the prefix scan wallet-local (no namespace's prefix
  is another's; `v` is not a hex digit, so a pre-FR-13 bare `…wrap.v<gen>` alias never
  matches — the Android legacy sweep is deferred, documented, pre-prod).
- **Test doubles:** `TestVault` clears its `aliases` map + returns the count (Android
  per-device shape — does NOT model prefix scoping; namespace-isolation tests use
  `SharedKeychainVault`); `SharedKeychainVault` removes `self.namespace`, returns 1/0
  (Apple shape — the namespace-keyed model the B1 fail-closed test needs).
- **Desktop (non-macOS):** `platform_vault` is `VaultAbsent` — see the rule below.

**`store::destroy(lock: &WalletLock, vault: Option<&dyn KeychainPort>)`** (the
witness-signature inverse of `provision` — `db_dir` from `lock.dir()`, never a bare
`&Path`). Order: inspect → keychain `purge()` → verify-real-sever → `remove_dir_all`.
- **Verify-real-sever (the money-safety guard, crypto review B1):** a non-`Empty`
  store whose on-disk `wrap.artifact` is present but whose purge severed **0** is a
  namespace mismatch (a `db_dir` path-variant — trailing slash / case-fold —
  mis-derives `keychain_namespace_for`); `remove_dir_all` would delete the REAL files
  (the OS normalizes the path) while the REAL wrap key SURVIVES + the seals stay
  flash-recoverable. It fails **CLOSED** (`KeystoreInconsistent`), files untouched —
  the same posture `open` takes on a namespace miss. **Two legitimate exits do NOT
  trap (operational-round H1):** (a) an INTERRUPTED wipe — a kill in the
  `purge → remove_file` window leaves the item severed but the artifact present;
  rather than re-trip the guard forever, a `.wipe-committed` breadcrumb (written into
  `db_dir` AFTER a genuine `severed>0` purge, BEFORE the deletes, durably) records the
  real sever so a plain re-run skips the guard + converges; (b) an ALREADY-GONE item
  (a manual keychain deletion, a pre-FR-13 bare-name item, an iOS `ThisDeviceOnly`
  item that didn't migrate while `db_dir` did) — `Wallet::wipe_force(cfg)` is the
  host's explicit "this IS my wallet, delete it" escape hatch (skips the guard; the
  host must be certain `cfg` matches, since force re-opens the B1 hole). (The earlier
  "artifact removed before the bulk delete rules out the re-run" reasoning was WRONG —
  it covered only the `remove_file → remove_dir_all` window, not `purge → remove_file`;
  the breadcrumb is the actual convergence mechanism.)
- **The `.wipe-committed` breadcrumb IS the crash-safety tombstone (#357 —
  scope reconciled).** It is written into `db_dir` AFTER a genuine `severed>0`
  purge and is swept on a SUCCESSFUL wipe — so it survives ONLY an interrupted
  wipe and leaves no durable forensic "a wallet lived here" residue (crash-safety
  ONLY, the founder's chosen semantics). Its convergence role stays where it is
  money-SAFE: the `destroy` RE-RUN path (the `wipe_already_committed` skip of the
  verify-real-sever guard) — a user who re-triggers delete after an interrupted
  wipe converges cleanly. **An OPEN-side auto-converge on the kill-mid-shred state
  was DESIGNED, PROVEN UNSAFE, and DEFERRED (#377 residual s357-1).** The failure
  a kill-mid-shred leaves at `open` is `load_custody → KeystoreInconsistent {
  permanently_invalidated: false }` — but that EXACT variant is ALSO produced by
  (d) a wrong-cfg / namespace-mismatch open where the real wallet's data is STILL
  ALIVE, and by an SE key filtered while the device is merely LOCKED (retryable).
  The `.wipe-committed` breadcrumb is the only discriminator between "interrupted
  wipe (dead)" and "live wallet", yet it can be INHERITED-STALE from a dead prior
  life (the provision-hygiene (b) hazard) and the open-path breadcrumb sweep runs
  only AFTER a successful unseal — so a failed-load converge keyed on `{false}` +
  breadcrumb could `destroy` a LIVE-but-locked or wrong-cfg wallet. On a money
  path that is unacceptable, so `open` does NOT act on the breadcrumb. RESIDUAL
  (s357-1, low-harm): a wipe killed in the narrow post-purge/pre-sweep window
  surfaces `needsRecovery` at the next `open` (a mildly confusing prompt for a
  user who deliberately deleted); recovery is a re-triggered delete (the safe
  destroy re-run converges) or a fresh create (provision hygiene sweeps the dead
  residue). A safe open-side fix needs a device-unlock proof AND an
  own-life-breadcrumb proof — its own careful design, tracked for #377.
- **VaultAbsent rule:** `purge()` errors propagate EXCEPT `VaultAbsent` when the store
  is `Empty` (custody requires the vault, so an `Empty` store has nothing to shred ⇒
  a clean file-only no-op — the headless-desktop path). A `Remnant`/`Complete` store
  whose vault is unreachable is a REAL wallet we cannot crypto-shred ⇒ fail loud, do
  NOT delete files (no silent partial shred, invariant 10). On `Empty` with a
  REACHABLE vault, purge still runs (sweeps a failed-provision orphan alias).
- **A corrupt store IS wipeable:** `inspect` returning `StoreCorrupt` (marker without
  manifest) is treated as non-`Empty` (custody + files still present) — `open`/`create`
  refuse it, so a `?` here would leave it the one thing it can never be: wiped.
- **Best-effort file cleanup:** the crypto-shred is COMPLETE once `purge` returns; a
  `remove_dir_all` failure logs `io_kind` only (§5.4 / no path/namespace) and returns
  Ok (never a hard Err claiming the shred failed when it did not).
- **`temp_store = MEMORY`** on every wallet-DB connection (`db.rs`) — no plaintext
  temp spill OUTSIDE `db_dir` (a sync/migration index build would otherwise land a
  cleartext temp file in the system temp dir that `remove_dir_all(db_dir)` can't reach).

**Named tests (gate 8 — BUILT, 11 host + 1 macOS gate):**
`wipe_severs_keychain_custody_then_open_is_not_found` (the core: the keychain slot is
severed — the crypto-shred itself, not just file deletion — the whole `db_dir` is
gone, and a re-open is `NotFound`), `wipe_with_a_mismatched_namespace_fails_closed_files_preserved`
(**the B1 money-safety guard** — a wrong namespace severs 0 ⇒ `KeystoreInconsistent`,
the real custody + files PRESERVED, never a silent file-only shred),
`wipe_on_a_real_wallet_with_an_unreachable_vault_fails_loud_not_silent` (the
VaultAbsent rule), `wipe_sweeps_a_failed_provision_orphan_alias` (the orphan sweep),
`wipe_refuses_while_an_instance_holds_the_lock` (`WalletOpen`),
`wipe_is_idempotent_and_a_no_wallet_wipe_is_ok`,
`wipe_with_no_vault_on_an_empty_store_is_a_file_only_no_op` (headless desktop),
`wipe_cleans_an_interrupted_provision_remnant` (Remnant), `wipe_can_shred_a_corrupt_store`
(StoreCorrupt), **`an_interrupted_wipe_converges_via_the_breadcrumb`** (H1 — a
mid-wipe kill does not strand a non-convergent wipe), **`wipe_force_completes_when_the_custody_item_is_already_gone`**
(H1 — the escape hatch for an already-severed item), + the macOS `#[ignore]` real-Apple
gate `purge_namespace_removes_the_real_apple_keychain_item` (RAN=PASS). Android production
purge rides the on-device custody gate (`cargo ndk check` GREEN for the blind edit).
**crypto-change review (crypto ∥ security ∥ arch → cr) + an operational round
(money/UX/reliability/unstable-net/mobile/edge/false-alarm + a universal-SDK audit):
NO BLOCKERS.**

**FFI BRIDGE + the H1 custody disclosure — ✅ WIRED (the owed chunk-1 slice).** The
core verbs are now exposed across the `zec_wallet` FRB bridge: `WalletHandle.wipe`,
`WalletHandle.wipeForce`, and the PRODUCTION `WalletHandle.custodyDisclosure` — the
runtime consumer of `VaultTier::erase_assurance()` (closing H1: the predicate
was previously test-only; named `crypto_erase_on_delete()` until ADR-0571).
`custodyDisclosure(cfg)` is an ACTIVE, read-only tier probe
(no seed, no unseal) returning `CustodyDisclosure { tier, eraseAssurance,
degraded }`, so a host renders the wipe confirmation HONESTLY (a hardware-held key
deleted vs best-effort) and an ambient custody badge BEFORE the destructive verb — distinct from
the diagnostic `seed_custody_selftest` (which provisions selftest identities and is NOT
shippable UX). The bridge validates the host config at the SAME `try_from` door
create/open use, and the tier→label map is DRY-shared with selftest (`vault_tier_label`).
Named tests: core `custody_disclosure_reports_each_tier_and_its_erase_assurance`
(the runtime SSOT exercise — every tier's assurance pinned, overclaim blocked),
`custody_disclosure_with_no_vault_is_absent_best_effort` (headless desktop ⇒ `tier:None`,
best-effort), `custody_disclosure_propagates_a_vault_probe_failure_not_a_false_absent`
(fail-honest — a probe error never masquerades as "no keystore"); bridge
`vault_tier_label_maps_every_named_tier` + `custody_disclosure_dto_maps_fields_without_transposition`
(the `eraseAssurance`↔`degraded` honesty, distinct values). Core 718 lib /
bridge 46 lib / clippy `-D warnings` clean / `cargo ndk` GREEN / extraction-policy 5/5.
The funded Some-path wipe + the on-device custodyDisclosure tier are E2E-owed (need a
real platform vault). Then STILL OWED: `panic_wipe_covers_wallet_store` + the duress
hung-wallet force-sever (host kill-switch/duress orchestration). *Updated S308:* the
first EXISTS on Relim `main` (`crates/relim-ffi/src/app.rs:5484`) and covers the
wallet-store directory and the marker only, not the key sever. The second is the
SDK's `Wallet::sever_custody` (FR-53, stage S16, ADR-0565): the core is built, and so
is the bridge (`WalletHandle.severCustody`, ABI 7). Its key-sever coverage is stage
S16's `sever` rows.

**Universal-SDK hygiene (operational round, founder ask).** This is a UNIVERSAL ZEC
wallet SDK (Relim is merely the first host). The operational audit confirmed **zero
functional coupling** to any host — no host crate/type dep (a `core_and_bridge_have_no_relim_deps`
test enforces crates.io-only resolution + rejects a `[patch]` redirect), the public
surface takes only generic primitives (db_dir, raw seed bytes, ZIP-321 URIs), and
`Wallet::wipe`/`purge_namespace` are pure lifecycle verbs. Folded: the persisted
account label (`account.rs`) is now host-neutral (`"zec-wallet"`, an opaque
never-looked-up upstream label), and the host-concept comment leaks
(`A7`/"kill-switch"/"the Relim path") in the wipe + FFI docs are genericized. The
core crate is named `zec-wallet-core` (the Convergence project name) while the Dart
package is the universal `zec_wallet` — a cosmetic naming split, manager/structural
