#### FR-14 chunk 2 — Apple Secure-Enclave custody hardening (✅ WIRED S116 — `apple.rs` SE-wrap + v2 envelope + `VaultTier::AppleSecureEnclave`; host tests green, device gate `#[ignore]`; wiring review crypto∥security∥arch→cr clean, all findings folded)

Closes **AV2** (duress / coerced-unlock; the analysis above): the SealKey is **wrapped
under a non-extractable Secure-Enclave key** rather than stored raw. ECIES-wrap the
32-byte SealKey under the SE key's public key (`SecKey::encrypt_data`, the audited
Security.framework ECIES primitive WHOLE — no custom crypto); `Wallet::wipe` →
`purge_namespace` → `SecItemDelete` the SE key = **true cryptographic erase** (Apple:
data wrapped under a deleted SE key is permanently undecryptable, irreversible by
design), bringing Apple to PARITY with Android's hardware-wrapped custody. The
`Wallet::wipe` verb is UNCHANGED (it calls `purge_namespace` either way); this flips
the §4.7 / `wipe` per-tier disclosure for SE-provisioned wallets from "Apple
best-effort" to "Apple true-shred".

**A 3-angle DESIGN review ran BEFORE wiring (crypto ∥ security ∥ arch, the chunk-1
discipline).** The design is cryptographically sound; the review caught one pivotal
wiring-blocker + the money-critical fallback decision + several must-fix design items,
all folded below. The decisions (frozen):

- **ARCHITECTURE — a leaf crate owns the `unsafe`; `zec-wallet-core` stays
  `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.** PIVOTAL FINDING (verified in `security-framework =3.7.0`
  source, `key.rs::to_dictionary`): the high-level `SecKey::generate` attaches
  `kSecPrivateKeyAttrs` (carrying `kSecAttrIsPermanent` + `kSecAttrAccessControl` + the
  searchable per-key locator) **only under `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`** — on **iOS**
  those private-key attributes are built and silently dropped, so the safe path yields a
  **non-permanent, access-control-less, unsearchable** SE key. A naive impl would pass a
  macOS gate and ship BROKEN to iOS. Fix: a small workspace-local **leaf crate**
  (`apple-secure-enclave`, Apple-only `#[cfg]`) owns ONLY the minimal `unsafe` SE-key
  lifecycle by `kSecAttrApplicationTag`: `generate(tag, access)` building the CORRECT
  CFDictionary (`kSecPrivateKeyAttrs = { kSecAttrIsPermanent, kSecAttrApplicationTag,
  kSecAttrAccessControl }`, `kSecAttrTokenID = SecureEnclave`) and calling the safe
  `SecKey::generate(dict)` (bypassing the buggy `to_dictionary`); `find(tag)`
  (fail-closed on >1 match); `delete_all(tag) -> usize`. `=`-pinned to
  `security-framework-sys` + `core-foundation` (the tiny-unsafe-FFI rule). `zec-wallet-core`
  → leaf is an acyclic forward dep (NOT the bridge crate — that would be circular +
  wrong layering); `zec-wallet-core/apple.rs` keeps the KeychainPort impl, the ECIES
  wrap/unwrap (safe `SecKey::encrypt_data`/`decrypt_data`), the envelope, the tier, the
  fallback, and the purge orchestration. The leaf crate has its own iOS/macOS device gate.

- **v2 ENVELOPE (exact length, validate-before-use).** A new `WRAP_VERSION_APPLE_SE =
  0x02` (FROZEN, append-only, pinned by a 1-char-diff-fails-CI test next to
  `WRAP_KEY_DOMAIN`). The SE-wrapped blob becomes the on-disk `WrapArtifact` (mirroring
  Android — wrapped blob on disk, wrap key in hardware): `[ver:0x02][sha256(sealed_blob):
  32][ecies_wrapped(SealKey)]`. Pin ONE ECIES variant —
  `ECIESEncryptionCofactorVariableIVX963SHA256AESGCM` — whose output for a 32-byte
  secret over P-256 is FIXED at **113 bytes** (65 ephemeral-pubkey + 32 ct + 16 GCM tag;
  the VariableIV is KDF-derived, NOT transmitted — MEASURED on real SE hardware S115: the
  reviews' 129 was wrong, 113 confirmed). So `WRAP_ARTIFACT_APPLE_SE_LEN = 1 + 32 + 113 =
  146`; reject any other length BEFORE any `decrypt_data` (the `envelope.rs`
  validate-before-use discipline). The `sha256(sealed_blob)` is a LOAD-BEARING application-layer blob-bind
  check (ECIES has no AAD param), verified on load — it gives blob-swap rejection within
  a namespace; documented so a future refactor can't remove it as "redundant". The
  per-namespace SE key is the real anti-substitution (a foreign artifact was encrypted to
  a different SE public key → `decrypt_data` fails). Frozen-label discipline: the SE
  application-tag string + the 0x02 byte are append-only — **a rename orphans every SE
  key and SILENTLY defeats the crypto-shred** (the tag is the only `purge` locator).

- **SE-REQUIRED, FAIL-CLOSED BY DEFAULT (the money-critical decision).** There is NO
  automatic raw-item fallback driven by an error-code guess — Apple gives no stable
  "no-SE-here" `OSStatus`, an incomplete allowlist is attacker-inducible (SEP slot
  exhaustion), and the asymmetric failure (misclassify capable→no-SE) **silently
  downgrades a capable device to flash-recoverable raw custody = AV2 reopened, money
  loss**. So: ANY SE-generation failure → fail closed (typed retryable
  `KeystoreUnavailable`). The ONLY sanctioned downgrade to the chunk-1 raw `AppleKeychain`
  tier is an EXPLICIT build-`cfg`/config opt-in the host sets for dev/sim
  (iOS-Simulator emulated-SE, pre-T2 Intel, unsigned macOS), never a runtime decision on
  a production build. One `se_capability` SSOT with a table-driven test whose DEFAULT arm
  is fail-closed. `errSecMissingEntitlement (-34018)` is its own bucket: fail-closed in
  production, the documented unsigned-dev case otherwise.

- **DUAL TIER + a conservative erase predicate.** Add `VaultTier::AppleSecureEnclave`
  (true-erase). `AppleKeychain` stays as the explicit-opt-in fallback tier.
  `software_backed()`/`degraded()` semantics UNCHANGED (neither Apple tier is
  software-rooted). The §4.7/`wipe` true-vs-best-effort disclosure keys off a NEW
  `VaultTier::crypto_erase_on_delete()` predicate returning true ONLY for
  `{StrongBox, Tee, AppleSecureEnclave}` — the `#[non_exhaustive]` default arm and every
  other tier conservatively disclose **best-effort** (never let an unknown tier render
  "true crypto-erase"). `tier()` becomes an ACTIVE probe (search the namespace's SE key:
  found → `AppleSecureEnclave`, else → `AppleKeychain`), mirroring Android's
  `measured_tier` — never a static overclaim.

- **`purge_namespace` is SE-KEY-COUNT-DRIVEN (verify-real-sever).** The load-bearing
  `usize` `store::destroy` fails-closed on (count==0 over a non-empty store) MUST be the
  count of **SE keys actually deleted** (enumerate by tag, count, delete each) — NOT the
  wrapped-blob/raw-item deletion. Else an orphan SE key (failed-provision, or a
  label-miss) survives while `destroy` sees count>0, deletes the files, and reports
  success while the SealKey is still recoverable = AV2. Purge severs: (a) every SE key
  under the namespace tag (the true-erase, counted), (b) the namespaced raw generic-
  password item (the opt-in fallback custody), (c) the legacy bare item (chunk-1 sweep,
  uncounted). Delete-FIRST in `store_wrap_key` (tag is not a uniqueness key — a crashed
  re-provision can leave two keys under one tag → load ambiguity / lockout). Rotation
  stays VACUOUS on Apple (ECIES per-encryption ephemeral key ⇒ no IV budget; SE key
  non-extractable ⇒ no compromise-rotate) — documented + a `finish_rotation` debug-assert
  that old==new so a future generations change can't silently delete the live key.

- **VERIFICATION (real-hardware-gated).** Host-runnable (unsigned `cargo test`): the
  transient SE crypto KAT (gen→ECIES→unwrap, no persist — works unsigned, proven by
  probe), the `se_capability` fail-closed classification table, the v2-artifact format
  round-trip + validate-before-use, and `wipe_wallet_a_leaves_wallet_b_se_key`. The FULL
  persistent KAT (provision→reload→decrypt→purge→**undecryptable** + verify-count) is
  **device-only**: an **iOS device** gate (the founder connects an iPhone — the primary
  platform) + a macOS-SE `#[ignore]` gate runnable on Apple Silicon via an ad-hoc
  `codesign --entitlements` harness (a `just` recipe; macOS SE persistence needs the
  keychain-access-group entitlement — `-34018` on the bare unsigned binary, proven by
  probe). The **iOS Simulator emulates the SE in a host file** — the true-erase KAT MUST
  NOT be allowed to green from the Simulator (it would over-claim); the wrap→delete→
  undecryptable assertion is real-hardware-only. A `SecKeyCopyExternalRepresentation`-
  errors negative test pins the non-extractability the whole claim rests on.

- **HONEST RESIDUALS (disclosed, neither chunk closes).** (1) The SEP-wrapped SE-private-
  key blob may linger in keychain free pages after delete — but the public API offers NO
  path to re-present it (`SecKeyCopyExternalRepresentation` fails for SE keys; importing
  raw SE-private bytes is prohibited), so it folds into the already-disclosed
  metadata/free-page existence-oracle residue (erased only by OS "Erase All Content"
  effaceable storage). Word the claim as "true erase at the Security.framework API
  boundary," not absolute. (2) **Once-raw residual**: any device on which a SealKey was
  EVER stored raw (a chunk-1 / fallback-tier wallet) keeps a best-effort flash residual
  forever; true-erase custody applies to NEWLY-provisioned v2 wallets only — re-provision
  is required to gain it, and an in-place v1→v2 migration would NOT retroactively erase
  that residual. (3) Scope: chunk 2 closes **post-wipe forensic recovery**, NOT a live
  coerced read of an unlocked device (that is the panic-wipe / A7 kill-switch's job).
  (4) **Transit residual (S116 crypto audit):** the SealKey plaintext is copied into a
  Security.framework `CFData` for `encrypt_data`, and `decrypt_data` returns it via a
  `CFData` the framework frees-but-does-not-scrub — inherent to using the audited ECIES
  primitive WHOLE (no buffer-owning safe entry). The Rust side moves the result straight
  into `Zeroizing`/`SealKey` (no Rust-side escape); only the transient CF buffer is
  unscrubbed (the Apple analogue of the Android JNI byte array, except the JNI array IS
  zero-filled — stated, not hidden). (5) **Substitution boundary (S116 security N2):** the
  per-namespace SE key is the anti-substitution measure for a FILESYSTEM adversary (a
  foreign artifact was encrypted to a different SE public key → `decrypt_data` fails). It
  does NOT defend a keychain-level adversary who can read the SE PUBLIC key and forge a
  v2 artifact wrapping a chosen SealKey (seed substitution) — out of the stated threat
  model (app/keychain compromise), unlike Android's non-exportable symmetric Keystore
  wrap which cannot be forged this way. The blob-hash bind stays defense-in-depth.

- **Anti-downgrade (defense-in-depth).** A filesystem adversary swapping a v2 wallet's
  artifact for a forged `[0x01]` cannot open it — a pure-SE wallet has NO raw item, so
  the v1 path hits `errSecItemNotFound` → `KeystoreInconsistent` (fail closed). A
  re-provision under an existing namespace purges BOTH slots first (any old SE key by tag
  AND any old raw item) so a stale artifact can never shadow the live wallet. (Recording
  the provisioned tier in the durable manifest and rejecting a version mismatch on load
  is a tracked HARDENING — the structural "no raw item ⇒ can't open" property already
  blocks the attack for v2 wallets.)

§5.4 in the new paths: loggable = numeric `OSStatus`/`SecError::code()`, the `severed`
count, the `VaultTier`, a coarse `se_available: bool`; NEVER the SE tag/namespace, the
`CFError` `Display`, the wrapped blob, or the SealKey. Cross-link: `local-storage.md §8`
"3-step shred" scopes to the hardware tier until this lands.

#### FR-17 + FR-18 — proposal-bound seed supply + guarded seed-port registration (#396 design, S220)

Two hardenings of the SAME seam — the FR-12 `WalletSeedPort` pull and its FR-15 C-ABI
transport — landed as one batch because both change the seam's signature/contract and
both are wanted **before the wallet holds non-trivial funds** (their premise: an
in-process bug/race today can either sign an unreviewed proposal or substitute the seed
supplier, and neither is detectable after the fact).

**Threat scope (honest):** defense-in-depth against **bugs and races** in the
Dart/host orchestration between the credential-authorize moment and the native sign
moment, and against a co-loaded in-process library racing the registration. A fully
hostile host is OUT of scope — it already holds the credential (FR-17) and lives in
the same address space (FR-18); neither claim changes. **Residual (S220
crypto audit):** FR-17 binds "the DTO whose binding the host recorded" ↔ "the
row/proposal actually signed" — it does NOT bind "the pixels the user reviewed" ↔
"the DTO": a display bug that renders A's facts while recording B's binding AND
sending B passes the compare. That review-surface trust is inherent to
UI-orchestrated custody (the FR-17 register's v1-interim "Dart-trusted +
disclosed" posture) and stays disclosed, not claimed.

**FR-17 mechanism — an SDK-minted, opaque, random `SpendBinding` ([u8; 32], `OsRng`)
carried from the review surface to the seed pull:**

- **Minted at three points, presented at every SIGN pull:**
  1. **Interactive propose** (`Wallet::propose`/`propose_uri`/`propose_shield`): minted
     beside `proposals.reserve_id()`, retained in the in-memory `ProposalRegistry`
     row, and returned on the `SendProposal` DTO (a nonce, NOT key material — safe to
     cross Dart; its only power is to make a mismatch detectable). At
     `sign_proposal_upstream(id)` the registry binding for THE id being signed is
     presented to the port. RAM-only is correct here: interactive proposals are
     TTL-600s/RAM-only by design, so their bindings die with them.
  2. **Queue enqueue** (`queue_send`/`queue_send_uri`/`queue_deposit_send`): minted at
     the durable INSERT, persisted in a new additive `binding BLOB` column on
     `queued_send_intent` (the `deposit_deadline` precedent — pre-existing rows read
     NULL ⇒ the pull presents unbound, honest for rows minted before FR-17). Every
     drain/kick sign (`resubmit_queued_sends`, `try_sign_queued_deposit`) presents the
     ROW's binding, and the queued-row DTO surfaces it so a host re-stage flow can
     record what it re-authorized. This closes the multi-row drain race: a take-once
     stage recorded for row X can no longer be consumed signing row Y.
  3. **Swap quote issue** (OutOfZec): minted when the issued-quote deposit gate row is
     persisted (`issued_swap_quote`, additive `binding BLOB` column), surfaced on the
     `SwapQuote` DTO (reviewed + acked on D5), and COPIED into the deposit's
     `queued_send_intent` row at execute — so the sign-at-execute pull presents the
     binding the host recorded at the execute-authorize bracket. The binding is
     SDK-minted, never derived from the provider quote id (provider-controlled, no
     uniqueness contract — the S219 ack-integrity lesson).
- **Unbound pulls** (present `None`): account import/provision, ephemeral sweep,
  reclaim self-mint, swap refund-address derivation — none moves money to a foreign
  recipient, and for refund-derivation the binding cannot exist yet (the refund
  address is a quote-REQUEST parameter). Host compare contract: **strict `Option`
  equality** — a stage recorded unbound matches ONLY an unbound pull; a stage recorded
  with a binding matches ONLY that binding (constant-time compare host-side). The SDK
  never interprets the token; it round-trips mint→present.
- **Seam signature (BREAKING, pre-publication):** `WalletSeedPort::provide_seed(&self,
  binding: Option<&SpendBinding>)` — one honest method, no silent-ignore default (a
  default-ignoring overload would let a host believe it is protected while the SDK
  never routes the binding). `Inner::acquire_seed(binding)` threads it; C-ABI gains a
  bound supplier type `SeedSupplyBoundFn(ctx, binding: *const u8, binding_len: usize,
  out, out_cap) -> isize` (null/0 = unbound pull). A v1 `SeedSupplyFn` supplier keeps
  working but RECEIVES no binding (cannot enforce FR-17 — documented, host opts in by
  registering the bound form).
- **Dead-id no longer burns the stage:** `sign_proposal_upstream` now PEEKS the
  registry BEFORE the seed pull and returns the typed miss (`ProposalAlreadyUsed`/
  `ProposalStale`) early — today an invalid id pulls the seed first, silently consuming
  the host's take-once stage so the user's NEXT legitimate send needs a re-auth. (The
  one-shot `consume` stays the post-pull authority — B2 order unchanged; the peek is a
  fast-fail, not a second consume, and a peek-live/consume-stale race just degrades to
  today's behavior.)

**FR-18 mechanism — guarded registration (bridge C-ABI registry):**

- The process-global registry becomes **first-wins + token-gated**:
  - `zec_wallet_register_seed_port(ctx, supply)` (v1, ABI unchanged): succeeds only
    into an EMPTY slot and is then **permanent** (no token to mutate with); a second
    register OR a null-supply clear against an occupied slot returns `-2` and the
    first registration stands. (Semantics change from "idempotent/last-wins" —
    deliberate; the null-clear path was itself the substitution primitive: any
    in-process caller could deregister the host then register itself.)
  - `zec_wallet_register_seed_port_bound(ctx, supply, auth_out: *mut u8 /*32*/)`:
    first registration of the BOUND supplier; mints a random 32-byte **registration
    auth token** (core `OsRng`, `Zeroizing` at rest) written to `auth_out`
    (null `auth_out` ⇒ permanent, like v1). The token is a host-held in-process
    capability — the host stores it beside its supplier state.
  - `zec_wallet_update_seed_port(auth: *const u8 /*32*/, ctx, supply /* null=clear */)`:
    token-gated replace/clear (identity switch, shutdown). Compare is
    constant-time (`subtle::ConstantTimeEq`). A successful CLEAR empties the slot AND
    invalidates the token (the next register mints fresh); a replace keeps the existing token.
- Return codes: `0` ok · `-1` registry lock poisoned · `-2` occupied/unauthorized ·
  `-3` bad arguments · `-4` the SDK panicked inside the verb (FR-29 stage 0, S280:
  every verb runs behind `catch_unwind`; a caught panic is reported as this code,
  nothing is registered or changed, and the host's `auth_out` is untouched — a
  non-zero code is fatal to that call and never retried). **No-oracle claim, scoped to the UPDATE verb** (S220 review
  fold): the update verb's every refusal — no registration, permanent registration,
  wrong token — is ONE shared `-2`, so presenting a token never learns registry
  state. The v1 REGISTER verb does leak occupancy (`-2` occupied vs `-3`
  null-into-empty, side-effect-free) — accepted: occupancy is also learnable from
  any real register attempt and grants no capability. Hosts MUST treat any
  non-zero register return as FATAL to the attempt (a `-2` means another
  in-process registrant owns the slot — the host's supplier is NOT installed).

**No new cryptography:** both tokens are pure random nonces compared for equality —
no KDF, no signature, no envelope; official test vectors are N/A (recorded per the
crypto-change review vectors-first step). The seed bytes' path, zeroization, and §4.2
confinement are UNCHANGED; bindings/auth tokens are not key material (the binding
crosses Dart by design; the auth token never crosses any FFI — it exists only in the
two native libraries' memory). §5.4: neither token is logged (a binding would
correlate a proposal↔sign pair in logs; keep `Debug` redacted).

**Named tests (owed with the wiring):** propose mints unique bindings; the spy-port
staging-for-A-then-`send(B)` fail-close (the FR-17 acceptance) + matching-binding
signs; dead-id send pulls NO seed (stage preserved, pull-count 0); queued enqueue
persists the binding across reopen and the drain presents the ROW binding; legacy
NULL rows present unbound; the swap quote→issued-row→deposit-row copy chain presents
the quote binding at deposit sign; unbound ops present `None` (spy assert per op);
C-ABI bound round-trip delivers binding bytes verbatim + null/0 on `None`;
FR-18 acceptance: second register rejected first stands, v1 null-clear rejected once
occupied, token-gated update replaces, token-gated clear empties + old token invalid,
wrong token `-2`; v1 supplier still signs (binding dropped, documented).

### 4.3 Wallet DB at rest

The wallet DB (zcash_client_sqlite) holds UFVK, note commitments, tx
history, memos, swap records — **funds-adjacent + privacy-critical** (threat
model: device seizure T11). Requirement: **encrypted at rest under a
per-wallet random DB key (OsRng), sealed to the platform keychain** —
mirroring the local-storage *pattern* (sealed-key, keychain ACL) with its own
distinct key (never the Relim DB key, never seed-derived ⇒ no frozen label
owed; same completeness note as identity.md §2.2's at-rest paragraph).
**Mechanism AS BUILT (W3-inc-2a, 2026-06-13):** `sdk/zec-wallet-core/src/db.rs`
`open_keyed_connection` opens the connection, applies `PRAGMA key` FIRST (raw-key
`x'<hex>'` form — the 256-bit key used DIRECTLY, no KDF; the statement lives in a
zeroizing buffer), **refuses a connection that is not SQLCipher or whose key did not
attach** (`db::ensure_sqlcipher`, S310, FR-5 D-24 — all three keyed openers:
`PRAGMA cipher_version` AND `PRAGMA cipher_provider` must answer; on plain SQLite
`PRAGMA key` is a silent no-op and the database would be plaintext; the answer is
`VaultAbsent`, a BUILD/linkage defect a host fixes in its link, never `StoreCorrupt`
and never worth a retry), forces header decryption with a probe read so a wrong key /
corrupt header fails HERE as typed `StoreCorrupt` (SQLCipher validates lazily on
first access, not at PRAGMA time), then calls `rusqlite::vtab::array::load_module`
(the rarray vtab `zcash_client_sqlite` requires), wraps the keyed connection in
`WalletDb::from_connection`, and runs `init_wallet_db` to build / migrate the
schema (AS BUILT W3-inc-2b-ii-A — `db.rs::provision_db`). (The upstream
SDKs ship **unencrypted** and let `WalletDb` own the open — §1.7; this is our one
deliberate divergence.) Two constraints, both now RESOLVED: (a) zcash_client_sqlite
pins rusqlite `^0.37` and `libsqlite3-sys` has `links = "sqlite3"` — the former
"whole workspace must converge" W2 gate-0 is **MOOT post-carve**: the wallet SDK is
its own cargo workspace (`sdk/`, own lockfile, gate-0 resolution), so it takes
rusqlite `0.37` (what zcash_client_sqlite wants) WITHOUT touching the main
workspace's rusqlite (relim-store/relim-mls-store); (b) our rusqlite dep enables
`bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl` and `libsqlite3-sys` feature-unifies the whole
sdk graph to SQLCipher (verified: `libsqlite3-sys 0.35.0` + `openssl-src` in the
lock). The wallet build always carries SQLCipher, and the vendored OpenSSL +
SQLCipher C **cross-compiles for Android arm64/x86_64 + iOS** (verified: `libcrypto.a`
/ `libsqlcipher.a` / `sqlite3.o` built as `ELF aarch64` — the
`bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl` mobile gotcha is handled). The encryption is
unconditional — no degraded fallback path ships.
**Linux two-dylib self-bind (FR-19, #395, S221).** Because the wallet cdylib
statically carries its OWN SQLCipher, a host that ALSO links SQLCipher and loads
both `.so`s hits Linux's default flat namespace + `RTLD_GLOBAL`: the first-loaded
`sqlite3_*` wins the global lookup, so the wallet's calls could bind to the host's
copy (plain SQLite or a version/cipher-mismatched SQLCipher) and the encrypted DB
silently fails to open. `sdk/zec_wallet/rust/build.rs` emits
`cargo:rustc-cdylib-link-arg=-Wl,-Bsymbolic` gated to `CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS ==
"linux"`, so every reference to a symbol DEFINED in the `.so` binds to that local
definition — the wallet's SQLCipher/OpenSSL calls resolve to its own copy
regardless of load order. The `.dynsym` export table is untouched (`zec_wallet_*`
FFI + Android `Java_*` stay `dlsym`-able; UNDEFINED symbols like libc `malloc` are
unaffected, so `LD_PRELOAD` shims still interpose). macOS/iOS already use a
two-level namespace (their `sqlite3_*` stay LOCAL) and Apple `ld` rejects the flag;
Windows binds per-DLL — hence the Linux-only gate. CI `linux-symbol-bind` +
`just fr19-symbolic-witness` assert `readelf -d` shows `DT_FLAGS SYMBOLIC`.
Regardless of path, the wallet data dir is **backup-excluded** (Android
`no_backup/`, iOS `isExcludedFromBackup` — §1.7): chain-recoverable state
must never leak into cloud backups.

**Provisioning + open AS BUILT (W3-inc-2b-i — `store.rs`).** The crash-atomic
two-phase provisioning (§6.3) seals the seed + DB key under ONE custodied
`SealKey` (`SealedSeedVault::store_wallet` — never a second key for the DB key)
and persists both blobs + the wrap artifact + a 3-byte manifest durably (tmp →
fsync → atomic rename → fsync dir; ENOSPC ⇒ `DiskFull`), THEN writes the
completion marker LAST. `open()` requires the marker, cross-checks the manifest
network (`NetworkMismatch`), recovers custody (`load_wallet`), and opens the DB
with the create-vs-open guard (`db.rs`: no `SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE` + the
`wallet_provisioning` sentinel). The `WalletDb::from_connection` wrap +
`init_wallet_db` migrations now FILL that `db.rs` seam (AS BUILT W3-inc-2b-ii-A):
`provision_db` runs the migrator with `seed = None` (a fresh wallet has no derived
account for the migrator to require a seed against — the `SeedRequired` retry loop
lands when accounts exist), so crash-recovery (`repair`) re-runs it idempotently.
The seam's `Network` is threaded from the manifest via `Network::consensus()`
(`money.rs`, the single source of truth for the consensus-params mapping).

**The async `Wallet` handle AS BUILT (W3-inc-2b-ii-B — `wallet.rs`).** `create`/
`open`/`close` (§3.1) drive provisioning/open over `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`
(all the file/SQLCipher/migrator work is blocking — off the Dart/UI thread AND off
the async runtime; `close` drops the connection on the blocking pool too, so the
WAL fsync never hits the runtime). Each acquires the exclusive single-writer
`WalletLock` FIRST and holds it for the handle's life (`Drop` releases it AFTER the
DB connection closes — declaration order — so the next opener never sees a
half-closed DB under a freed lock); a second opener is typed `WalletAlreadyOpen`.
The store entry points (`create_or_repair`/`open`) now take a `&WalletLock`
**witness** and derive `db_dir` from `lock.dir()` — operating without holding the
lock, or on a different dir than the one locked, is no longer expressible (the
single-writer guarantee is a type obligation, not a doc comment). `open` re-runs
`init_wallet_db` idempotently (migrate-up at open — `db::open_db_migrated`). The
platform key vault is resolved per-call (`VaultAbsent` fail-closed off-vault); host
unit tests inject a `TestVault` via a crate-internal `*_with_vault` seam so the real
Keychain/Keystore is never touched. The account-import MECHANISM is now built
(W3-inc-2c-iii — `import_account_hd` over a birthday treestate, the seed-retry
loop, and `current_address` reading the stored account UFVK; §3.2b). What remains:
the engine ORCHESTRATION of import (birthday-height resolution + the birthday
FRONTIER source — BUILT in iv-c §3.2f as the TRUSTED bundled slice, NOT a live
`get_tree_state` fetch/continuity check, which the audit dropped) and the `&self`
API surface (`snapshot`/`balance`/`sync`/`send`/`reveal_mnemonic`) —
both ride the sync/send engines (inc-2c-iv/2d) and consume the held `OpenWallet`
carrier + `require_open` + the `import_account` seam this chunk puts in place.

**Keychain access stays in Rust (verified mechanics):** iOS/macOS via the
`security-framework` crate (established, works in any cdylib); Android
Keystore has no NDK API, so the JNI route (`android-keyring`-style) needs a
small Kotlin glue handing the JNI/Activity context to Rust — the glue passes
a *context*, never key material. The well-trodden Flutter alternative
(`flutter_secure_storage`, platform channels) is **rejected**: the wrap key
would transit Dart — the exact violation this SDK exists to prevent. W3
design item (§11 Q10) — designed at §4.3a below.

#### 4.3a Q10 design — the Android Keystore context-handoff shim (IMPLEMENTED + DEVICE-PROVEN 2026-06-12 — all gates closed)

**The mechanical problem.** Android Keystore is a Java-only API (no NDK
surface). Rust needs two things to reach it over JNI: a cached `JavaVM*`
and the **application** `Context`. Neither arrives for free in this
plugin: FRB loads `libzec_wallet.so` via Dart-FFI `dlopen`, which **never
invokes `JNI_OnLoad`** (that fires only under Java's `System.loadLibrary`)
— so without a shim, Rust on Android has a working bridge and no path to
the vault. (`ndk-context` is populated by `ndk-glue` in NativeActivity
apps, not under Flutter — rejected; passing a Context through FRB is
impossible by design — Java objects can't cross Dart FFI, and shouldn't.)

**The shim (the new native surface, in full):** one ~15-line
`ZecWalletPlugin.kt` implementing `FlutterPlugin`, registered alongside
`ffiPlugin: true` in the plugin's pubspec `platforms:` block (Flutter
supports both on one plugin). `onAttachedToEngine` does exactly two
things, once per process: `System.loadLibrary("zec_wallet")` — this fires
`JNI_OnLoad`, where the `jni` crate caches the `JavaVM` — then calls
`private external fun nativeInit(context: Context)` with
`binding.applicationContext`. The Rust export
(`Java_…_ZecWalletPlugin_nativeInit`) stores a JNI `GlobalRef` to that
context in a `OnceLock` (idempotent; second engine attach is a no-op;
tolerates dlopen-before-loadLibrary ordering by contract).
`onDetachedFromEngine` does nothing — the **application** context is
process-global, so holding the GlobalRef leaks nothing. RULE, enforced at
review + by the named policy tests below: the shim passes the APPLICATION
context, never an Activity (leak + lifecycle hazard), and the Kotlin file
contains ZERO key material, ZERO crypto imports, ZERO method channels —
it is a context courier, nothing else.
**Why a planted Context gains nothing (security fold, S6):** the exported
`nativeInit` symbol is process-global and first-caller-wins — and Flutter
plugin registration order is NOT a security guarantee, so the design does
not rest on being first. It rests on the Context being **inert for
custody**: `AndroidKeyStore` is reached by JCA name lookup
(`KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore")`), which never goes through the
Context — a hostile early caller cannot redirect wrap-key custody to a
fake provider. The Context is trusted ONLY as a JavaVM courier and for
app-files-dir resolution, which is pinned to
`context.getNoBackupFilesDir()` (one guarantee with §4.3's
backup-exclusion); `nativeInit` is defensive — it stores
`context.getApplicationContext()`, never the raw caller object.
**Loader-namespace verification gate:** on classloader-isolated linker
namespaces (API 24+), `System.loadLibrary` and FRB's Dart-FFI `dlopen`
are not GUARANTEED one mapping — two mappings would mean two `OnceLock`s
and an invisible JavaVM. The implementation chunk must verify
single-mapping on the min-SDK matrix; the on-device
`wrap_key_roundtrip_via_keystore` E2E is the catch-point (a split mapping
fails it loudly via the typed no-vault error, never silently).

**What Rust does with it (wrap-key custody, two layers).** The §4.2a
envelope stays THE portable sealing construction on every platform; the
vault's only job is wrapping the 32-byte `SealKey`. Android: generate an
AES-256-GCM key **inside** `AndroidKeyStore`
(`KeyGenParameterSpec`, purposes ENCRYPT|DECRYPT, non-exportable, alias
`zec_wallet.wrap.v1`), StrongBox attempted first, TEE fallback,
software-Keystore last — the landed tier recorded in a non-secret status
field AND surfaced per the failure-posture paragraph below. v1 auth
policy matches the stated at-rest posture (vault ACL + device lock, no
passphrase KDF): `setUserAuthenticationRequired(false)` +
`setUnlockedDeviceRequired(true)` where API ≥ 28 (minSdk 23 gates it).
**The wrapped-key artifact is an envelope we define, so it carries the
full discipline (crypto fold, S6):**
`[ver:1=0x01][iv:12][KeystoreGCM(SealKey, aad = "zec-wallet/wrap-key/v1" ‖ H(sealed_blob))‖tag:16]`
— Keystore supplies the GCM IV (randomized encryption REQUIRED — never
`setRandomizedEncryptionRequired(false)`); the SDK persists the returned
IV in the artifact and **never encrypts twice under one alias**. The AAD
binds the wrap artifact to THIS install's sealed blob via
`H(sealed_blob)` (SHA-256): an attacker who swaps both files for an
internally-consistent pair wrapping a known key still fails the AAD check
**loudly and attributably** (`swapped_wrap_artifact_fails_loudly`) — and
the binding lives on the wrap side precisely so the FROZEN
`zec-wallet/seal-seed/v1` AAD is never touched. **Rotation is supported,
not frozen:** the Keystore alias is per-device and NOT recovery-critical
(the phrase + chain are the backup, §10 — the alias is deliberately
outside the freeze class despite the versioned name). Rewrap = generate
`zec_wallet.wrap.vN+1`, wrap under it, atomically replace the artifact
(write + fsync + rename, §6.3 atomicity discipline), THEN delete the old
alias — in-place re-encryption under a live alias is forbidden (the
one-alias-one-encryption rule makes GCM IV reuse structurally
impossible). Rotation triggers: lock-screen reset invalidating the key,
or deliberate rewrap (`wrap_key_rotation_preserves_seal_openability`).
iOS/macOS need no shim at all: `security-framework` directly, the wrap
key as a keychain generic password under
`kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` (foreground-only unseal
need ⇒ the tighter class suffices; ThisDeviceOnly keeps it out of
keychain sync/backups, matching §4.3's backup-exclusion posture).
**No-background-unseal pin:** nothing in v1 unseals seed OR DB key in the
background (§9 iOS row: background sync runs against the already-open
DB/UFVK), so BOTH seals take the tight class
(`WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` / `setUnlockedDeviceRequired`); any future
background-decrypt feature (e.g. background auto-shield) is an explicit,
threat-stated accessibility relaxation — never a silent class change.

**Honest JNI-transit statement (the part naive designs hide):** Keystore
`Cipher.doFinal` returns the unwrapped `SealKey` as a Java `byte[]` — for
that moment the WRAP KEY transits the Java heap, where zeroization is
best-effort (`Arrays.fill` immediately after copy; the GC may have moved
it). The SEED never does — Java only ever sees the 32-byte wrap key,
never the §4.2a plaintext. What the vault buys, stated exactly **per
tier** (security fold, S6 — one blanket claim would overstate the bottom
tier): StrongBox/TEE — key material never leaves secure hardware; an
offline filesystem dump (sealed blob + wrapped-key artifact) decrypts
NOTHING without executing code inside our process on the unlocked
device. Software-Keystore — the same API contract but a software/OS root
of trust: keystore-daemon-mediated, honestly weaker, and surfaced as
degraded (below). What NO tier buys: defense against a same-process
attacker at unlock time — that attacker reads the heap either way. And
the T11 honesty sentence (threat-model: device seizure, locked OR
unlocked): against a seized UNLOCKED device the wrap key unwraps with no
further auth — v1 has no per-use biometric gate
(`setUserAuthenticationRequired(true)` + validity window is a deferred,
named hardening, consistent with §4.2a's stated unlocked-device posture).
No claim beyond that.

**Failure posture (no silent degrade on ANY axis — security fold, S6
closed the in-memory seam):** every Keystore failure is a typed error.
Transient keystore-daemon flakes: retried once (operating principles).
StrongBox unavailable: TEE tier, recorded. Software-Keystore tier: NOT
merely recorded — surfaced as a first-class
`VaultTierDegraded { software_backed: true }` state the host receives on
the open path and must render (the §2.6 disclosure-as-data pattern; the
SDK refuses to label that wallet "vault-protected";
`keystore_software_tier_is_surfaced_not_silent`). **No Keystore tier at
all ⇒ FAIL-CLOSED** — no wallet, typed error naming the missing vault,
exactly the §9 headless-Linux default; holding the wrap key in process
memory "just for this session" is the same forbidden move as persisting a
software wrap labeled vault-backed (both lie about the at-rest posture —
the forbidden move covers BOTH the persisted and the in-memory axis).
Key permanently invalidated / alias missing while a sealed blob exists:
surfaced as the honest unrecoverable-locally state whose recovery path is
named in the error — restore from the phrase (the §10 model: the chain is
the backup).

**Seam shape:** an SDK-internal `KeychainPort`
(store/load/delete wrap key + vault-tier status; pattern parity with
local-storage's `KeychainBackend`, never an import of it — A1), with the
Android impl behind `cfg(target_os = "android")`, Apple impls on
`security-framework`, and a deterministic in-memory test impl — the port
stays host-testable everywhere; only the Android adapter itself is
device-gated.

**Named tests (gate 8; rows added to the §8 register — security fold S6
rescoped the test set so it gates the surface where keys actually live,
not the cosmetic layer above it):**
- `kotlin_shim_is_courier_only` — static-shape policy test over the
  Kotlin glue (exported surface = `nativeInit(Context)` only; no method
  channels, no byte-array params, no crypto imports). Honest SMALL
  guarantee — renamed from the original over-promising
  `keystore_shim_passes_context_never_keys`.
- `jni_custody_zeroizes_and_exports_one_symbol` — the LOAD-BEARING half,
  on the Rust JNI layer: key bytes never passed INTO a Java method (only
  Keystore Cipher APIs touched), the unwrapped `byte[]` from
  `Cipher.doFinal` is zero-filled on EVERY return path including errors,
  and the built `.so`'s `Java_*` symbol table contains exactly one
  export (`nativeInit`) — a second JNI entry point is drift, caught at
  the symbol table.
- `swapped_wrap_artifact_fails_loudly` — valid blob from install A +
  valid wrap artifact from install B ⇒ distinguished error (the AAD
  binding), never a silent open, never bare `SealInvalid`.
- `wrap_key_rotation_preserves_seal_openability` — new-alias rewrap,
  crash-window included.
- `keystore_software_tier_is_surfaced_not_silent` — host-testable via
  the port.
- `keychain_unavailable_yields_typed_error_not_fallback` — asserts the
  in-memory-proceed path is structurally unreachable, not just the
  persisted one.
- `wrap_key_wipe_leaves_seal_unopenable` — delete path actually severs.
- `wrap_key_roundtrip_via_keystore` — Android device, manual E2E gate
  (same lane as device builds); also the catch-point for the
  loader-namespace verification above.

Supply-chain: the `jni` crate (+ `security-framework` for Apple) enters
the workspace WITH the implementation chunk, exact-pinned,
supply-chain-auditor pass in the same change — not before. Reciprocal
edit owed (manager, with the other A9-row items): threat-model T11 gains
the wallet wrap-key vault's unlocked-device limit so the per-tier claims
above are anchored there.

**As-implemented record (S6, all review-folded — 4-angle review
(crypto ∥ security ∥ arch ∥ supply-chain) + code reviewer, ZERO
BLOCKER/MAJOR):**

- **No `JNI_OnLoad` at all** — `nativeInit` receives the env and
  `Env::get_java_vm()` is safe; ONE `Java_*` export (`#[jni_mangle]`),
  ZERO unsafe anywhere in the custody path (the safe jni 0.22 API
  suffices; `forbid(unsafe_code)` holds in the core, the bridge module
  carries `deny(unsafe_code)`; unwind containment via
  `EnvUnowned::with_env`).
- **The courier is Java, not Kotlin** (`ZecWalletPlugin.java` — no Kotlin
  toolchain enters the plugin; same ~30-line courier shape; pubspec
  carries `pluginClass` + `ffiPlugin` together).
- **The ADAPTER lives in `zec-wallet-core`** (`keychain/android.rs`, safe
  jni), not the bridge: Relim's W5 host path needs Keystore custody
  without the Flutter plugin — only the export must live in the loaded
  cdylib. `init_android_vault` is the ONE jni-typed pub symbol,
  CI-enforced (`jni_custody_zeroizes_and_exports_one_symbol` half 5).
- **The wrap artifact gained `[alias_gen: u32 LE]`** between ver and iv
  (65 bytes total): rotation's one-alias-one-encryption needs the
  artifact to name its generation. Header rides OUTSIDE the AAD — a
  tampered gen selects a key that fails the tag or an absent alias; both
  loud (the absent-alias arm surfaces as `KeystoreInconsistent`, the
  second accepted failure class, gated in
  `swapped_wrap_artifact_fails_loudly`). Canonical-suffix check keeps
  alias↔generation invertible.
- **`probe()`/`tier()` split:** the tier is MEASURED on the live key
  (`KeyInfo`; API≥31 `getSecurityLevel`, pre-31 floor = `Tee` — never an
  overclaimed StrongBox; outside secure hardware/unknown = degraded
  floor), read AFTER store/load; `probe()` is only the fail-closed gate.
- **Apple needs no wrap envelope:** the keychain item IS the custody —
  `[ver][SealKey:32][H(sealed_blob):32]` with the hash as binding parity;
  iOS under `SecAccessControl(WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly)`; **macOS uses
  the login keychain** (the data-protection keychain requires a
  signed/provisioned app — migration + the `OSX_10_15` crate feature are
  a NAMED row owed with the first signed macOS build). PROVEN on a real
  macOS keychain (the `#[ignore]` smoke test, run manually at S6).
- Host tests run the REAL framing/binding/rotation logic against a
  real-AEAD test vault (ChaCha20Poly1305 IETF, same 12-byte IV shape,
  already-pinned crate — no new dep); the device E2E covers only what
  host tests cannot (JNI plumbing, Keystore semantics, loader-namespace
  single-mapping).
- Supply-chain ACCEPT on all three deps (sha2 =0.10.9 adds ZERO new lock
  entries; the 0.11 revisit rode the digest-stack situation, now RESOLVED by
  the carve — §1.2a; jni 0.22.4 + security-framework 3.7.0 latest stable, no
  advisories, licenses clean).

**Device-gate record (S6, real hardware — the owed lanes CLOSED):**
`wrap_key_roundtrip_via_keystore` ran via `selftest_seed_custody` (the
runnable harness: full round-trip under SELFTEST-SCOPED vault identities
— disjoint alias namespace/keychain service, production custody
untouched; report = booleans + measured tier, nothing secret crosses) on
TWO physical devices, both Android 16/API 36: Pixel 10 Pro and OnePlus
PLZ110 — **both measured `tier=strongbox`, `degraded=false`; round-trip,
AAD-binding rejection, and wipe-severs all green**. This also confirmed:
the loader-namespace single-mapping (System.loadLibrary + FRB dlopen =
one copy — a split would have failed `VaultAbsent`, loudly), the
StrongBox generation path + API-31 `getSecurityLevel` introspection on

built arm64 `.so`: EXACTLY one `Java_*` export). The 15-check bridge
selftest also ran on-device — the W3 link-level manual gate is closed

**iOS device row (OPEN — S6 mobile-lens catch):** the example Runner has
NO keychain entitlements; on a physical iPhone the selftest fails with

surfaces it diagnosably). Before the first iOS device run: add
`Runner.entitlements` (keychain-access-groups) + pbxproj wiring — owed
