**FR-53 / stage S16 — provision order and the duress sever (ADR-0565).**
- **The index is written BEFORE the key.** `store::provision` writes the
  path-keyed index item (`done(id)`) first, then the wrap key under the new
  id's namespace. The S2 "done from birth" invariant is restated: **the index
  may name an id whose key is not yet written** (a kill between the two
  writes). That resolves as an orphan: the purge severs 0, the store is
  `Empty` so the wipe's guard does not trip, `open` answers `NotFound`, and a
  re-create mints a new id and overwrites the index. Why: a key that lands
  before a duress sever's tombstone is always resolvable by that sever, and
  one that would land after it is refused inside its key-store job (every
  CREATING method of the bounded vault checks the namespace's tombstone in
  its worker job).
- **An index item is rewritten IN PLACE on iOS (S310).** The one write door
  (`keychain/apple.rs::write_keychain_item`) updates an item already pinned
  `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` with one `SecItemUpdate`, so the index holds
  the old entry or the new one, never nothing. It had written delete-then-add
  since `a58e7cb2`, and a kill between the two left no index: a bare-config
  wipe after the host deleted the files answered success with the wrap key
  alive (the S6 review's LOW). **Residual, stated:** an item WITHOUT the pin
  (an index written by a build before 22 Sep 2026) is still replaced
  delete-then-add, once, and is pinned from then on; the window is
  reachable on such a wallet's first rewrite only. macOS writes through the
  login keychain's add-or-update and never had the window.
- **The sever** (`Wallet::sever_custody`, §3.1; bridge
  `WalletHandle.severCustody`, ABI 7) severs this custody even while the
  wallet is held, and reports every outcome as a value. It is complete AT
  REST only: a live holder keeps the seed and the DB key in RAM until it
  drops.
- **Per-tier honesty, the locked device.** Where the key store refuses the
  reads a count needs (a locked iPhone), the sever issues a blind delete
  scoped to this wallet's namespaces and answers
  `SeveredUnproven { CountUnreadable }`, never a bare `Severed`; a `wipe`
  after the next unlock confirms it. **Conditional on the `locked-delete`
  device measurement (stage S16 §2, OWED):** if `SecItemDelete` on class-A
  items fails while locked, the sever answers
  `NotSevered { KeystoreUnavailable }` there, and a phone that locks during
  the panic gesture may keep the wallet key until next unlock.

### 4.4 Swap deposit sends

For `OutOfZec`, the deposit transaction is built/signed **by the wallet in
Rust** (ADR-0014) — the provider supplies only an address. The deposit
address is validated (parseable, right network) before any signing;
`expires_at` is checked before broadcast (expired quote ⇒ typed error, never
a fire-and-hope send) — **and re-checked on every resubmission, on BOTH drain
arms**: deposit sends are tagged; the generic resubmission machinery (§6.1)
excludes a fresh re-propose past the deadline (`deposit_gate` deletes the
lapsed unsigned intent) AND holds the `ReBroadcast` arm for a deposit-tagged
group past it (never a FIRST broadcast into a dead quote — see the
deferred-broadcast rules below). Semi-custodial in-flight window is surfaced via
`SwapStatus` — the SDK never claims custody it doesn't have.

**The deposit signs at EXECUTE, inside the authorize-spend bracket (FR-23-a —
the custody invariant §1.9).** `SwapService::execute` (OutOfZec) is the
chokepoint. It ONE-SHOT-consumes the issued quote (`issued.remove` ⇒ a quote
executes at most once — per-QUOTE no-double, since the §6.3 guard de-dups a single
intent, not two distinct enqueues; the cross-QUOTE double is closed by the
one-deposit-in-flight guard below), re-checks the dual monotonic+wall deadline
(the strict at-execute pre-flight, the canonical `deposit_gate` `>=` edge so it
agrees with the resubmission exclusion on the same instant of death), calls
`provider.execute` to register intent FIRST, re-checks the kill door
(`ensure_live` — a `Hard` kill landing during the provider await still stops a
NEW deposit), then drives the deposit via the **`DepositSender` port** (the
wallet implements it — the `RefundAddressSource` precedent) →
`Wallet::send_deposit_now(blessed_address, zec_side, expires_at)`. **The deposit
address is the EXACT `Address` `validate_quote` blessed** (`validate_quote`
returns it; security L-1 — never a second parse, so a wrong-network/non-transparent
recipient `Payment::new` won't catch can never reach the send).

`send_deposit_now` enqueues the durable deadline-tagged intent, then drives the
SAME propose→claim→create(**sign**) core the §6.3 background drain uses
(`intent_store::enqueue` + `send::prepare_queued`/`create_signed_core`),
**synchronously, at execute** — because the user is present and the seed is
acquirable (`Inner::acquire_seed`: the held seed, or `WalletSeedPort` while the
host's per-spend credential is staged inside the Dart `authorizeSpend`
bracket). It reuses the entire double-send guard (claim-before-create,
txid-before-broadcast); **only the seed-needing SIGN moves from a later
background drain to execute.** The **broadcast STAYS at the drain** — it needs
no seed, so the signed `Sent` deposit rides the §6.1 Phase-1 `ReBroadcast` arm
(seedless) on the next sync pass, the SAME place it broadcast pre-FR-23, until
it mines or the deadline lapses; it never re-signs a deposit signed at execute.
Not broadcast synchronously at execute *by design*: this call runs inside the
host's `swapExecute` future under a fixed Dart timeout, and a broadcast can
stall up to a gRPC unary timeout per tx — an unbounded in-bracket broadcast that
overran the Dart timeout would route the host to a re-quote (a new quote id ⇒ a
fresh single-flight ⇒ a **second** deposit) while the first signed one still
drains: a double-swap (arch review BLOCKER, folded). Keeping the broadcast at
the seedless drain bounds the execute future to `provider.execute` (its
`SWAP_HTTP_TIMEOUT`) + the sign. This is why the deposit works at **every**
custody tier: pre-FR-23 the deposit was an unsigned `Queued` intent signed only
at a background drain the host-custody port can't serve (`SeedRequired`, left
`Queued` forever); signing at the user-present execute moment removes that
seed-gating asymmetry. **Durable-first, best-effort sign:** a sign failure is
swallowed (deposit stays `Queued`, `send_deposit_now` returns `Ok`) — never a
false "failed" that would re-quote into a double deposit; only an enqueue
failure surfaces the honest `DepositSendFailed`. Held custody is improved, not
regressed — an offline held-seed deposit no longer waits for a clean sync pass
to sign. The alpha send ceiling (`walletSendCeilingZat`, founder 2026-07-10)
BOUNDS the deposit: an over-ceiling OutOfZec swap is refused at quote-review,
before the authorize-spend bracket, with the same typed over-ceiling error the
send form uses — every alpha money-out path under one cap.
**TEX/two-step deposit:** production two-step signing is gated OFF (§3.2i-2), so
every production deposit is single-step and fully sign-at-execute-covered; a
future two-step deposit signs the `[tx0, tx1]` chain in ONE in-bracket create
(the engine's ZIP-320 pair — leg-2 needs no second authorization; §1.9.1),
with the `Stranded` sweep as the leg-1-mined/leg-2-dead recovery. IntoZec drives no deposit (ZEC is received to our own fresh address). A
failed deposit leg is typed (`SwapError::DepositSendFailed`) and fail-safe:
nothing left the pool, the provider refunds the registered-but-undeposited
quote after its deadline, the user re-quotes.

**One deposit in flight at a time (the cross-quote double-deposit guard —
S178 re-review, #362).** The per-quote single-flight cannot stop a SECOND
quote: the SIGN is unbounded work (ZK proving, one spend proof per input
note — tens of seconds for a fragmented wallet on a slow phone) inside the
host's fixed `swapExecute` timeout, and Dart's `.timeout` ABANDONS, never
cancels, the Rust future. A sign overrunning the timeout therefore looks like
a failure to the host, invites a re-quote (a NEW quote id ⇒ a fresh
single-flight), and a second deposit would sign while the first drains: 2×
ZEC. The guard is enforced ATOMICALLY at the enqueue: `intent_store::enqueue`
REFUSES a deposit-tagged intent while ANY deposit-tagged row exists
(`deposit_deadline IS NOT NULL`, any state — Queued/Submitting/Sent), checked
inside the same `IMMEDIATE` transaction the insert rides, so two racing
executes serialize and exactly one enqueues. Typed
`WalletError::SwapDepositInFlight` (`RW-BCAST-003`, the `QueuedSendsFull`
sibling), port-mapped to **`SwapError::SwapAlreadyInFlight`**
(`RW-SWAP-013`) — DISTINCT from `DepositSendFailed` because the REMEDY
differs: the host must NOT re-quote (that is the double-deposit door); it
renders "a swap is already in progress" and points at the tracked swap.
**The tag is CLAMPED** (`send::clamped_deposit_deadline`, arch review HIGH;
ceiling re-priced by the W-swap-4-a-3 security review): the durable deadline
is `min(provider expires_at, now + SWAP_DEPOSIT_DEADLINE_OUT_OF_ZEC_SECS)` —
a deadline tag exists ONLY for a wallet-sent OutOfZec deposit, so the window
WE request (15 min) is the honest ceiling; an echo beyond it is hostile or
buggy by definition, and the previous 24 h ceiling left the guard/zombie
lockout 96× looser than the wallet's stated need. The SwapService applies
the SAME direction-aware ceiling to the STORED wall deadline (durable
`expires_at_wall` + the in-memory `valid_for`/`act_deadline`), so a hostile
echo cannot keep the QUOTE executable past the window either — in-process or
across a restart. Too-short is the money-safe direction (past the clamp the
wallet just stops serving the quote; notes recover via expiry).
**Pre-clamp rows are swept, not honored** (W-swap-4-a-4): a durable
issued-quote row with `expires_at_wall > now + SWAP_DEADLINE_DEFAULT_SECS +
FAR_FUTURE_SKEW_ALLOWANCE_SECS` cannot have been written by a post-clamp
build (every persist ceiling-clamps to ≤ 24 h ahead — a bound that only
tightens as `now` advances UNDER A NON-DECREASING CLOCK, which the wall
clock is not: the S183 review's converged finding is that the live provider
ignores our window, so every live IntoZec row sits at EXACTLY the 24 h
ceiling, and a zero-margin cutoff would let a 1-second backward NTP step
refuse and delete a live quote — the one-hour allowance absorbs real clock
corrections while a ~72 h pre-clamp echo still sits ~47 h past the cutoff).
Such a row is pre-upgrade or hostile by construction — the store's inline
prune and the open-time sweep delete it, and `take` refuses it (delete +
miss ⇒ re-quote). Each far-future arm is disabled below the
clock-plausibility floor so a broken-clock device never mass-sweeps live
quotes; a backward step LARGER than the allowance still sweeps (documented
residual — money-safe: re-quote). A pre-upgrade row already within the
bound lives out that remainder one time (its deposit tag was re-clamped to
the 15-min window at enqueue regardless).
**Margins are block-time-sized** (W-swap-4-a-3, the three-review convergence):
`deposit_gate` refuses to sign or FIRST-feed a deposit within
`DEPOSIT_FIRST_FEED_MARGIN_SECS` (240 s ≈ 3.2 block intervals) of its
deadline — a first broadcast inside the final ~75 s block interval is a
refund coin-flip, and a provider refund is INVISIBLE until ADR-0527/#368 —
and the SwapService refuses `execute` on a deposit-carrying quote within
`DEPOSIT_EXECUTE_MARGIN_SECS` (300 s, strictly larger: prove + kick headroom,
so an admitted execute can never enqueue a deposit already dead at its own
gates). The accepted residual: a deposit broadcast legally (≥ 240 s of life)
can still mine past the deadline in the rare slow-mine tail — outside wallet
control, provider-refunded, percent-scale odds; #368 makes that refund
visible, and the review-screen countdown renders the SAME number the execute
gate enforces (#367 made `expiresAt` the actionable deadline; #364/S219 made
the display minute-worded — "15 min", never a "15:00" that misreads as a
clock time in 24h locales — with a minute-granular screen-reader label).
IntoZec keeps the generic `DEADLINE_SAFETY_MARGIN_SECS` (60 s — no
wallet-side send rides it).
The margins assume the DEVICE clock (W-swap-4-a-4): ±4 min of wall-clock
skew consumes the whole 240 s first-feed margin — material at a 15-min
window (a fast clock holds deposits early; a slow one admits a first feed
the provider already counts that much closer to its deadline), invisible at
24 h. Both failure directions are money-safe (an early hold, or a
provider-refunded late mine — never an unrefunded loss), so no NTP
dependency is taken; the skewed-slow tail rides the same #368
refund-visibility remedy as the honest-clock late-mine tail.
**The REQUESTED window is direction-dependent** (the S180 re-pricing ground
fact, W-swap-4-a-3): the adapter itself supplies the provider's
`deadline_window_secs`, so the deposit deadline is OURS to size, not an
ecosystem given. An OutOfZec deposit is sent by the WALLET (signed inside
the execute bracket, kicked to the network within seconds, drain as
fallback), so the adapter requests `SWAP_DEPOSIT_DEADLINE_OUT_OF_ZEC_SECS`
(15 min ≈ 12 blocks — execute + sign + broadcast + mine, with margin);
IntoZec keeps `SWAP_DEADLINE_DEFAULT_SECS` (24 h — an EXTERNAL user deposit
from another wallet/exchange needs the ecosystem-standard window, and no
wallet-side lockout keys on it: IntoZec drives no deposit row). Every
deposit-tag lockout (this guard, a host-custody sign-miss zombie, an
under-funded `Stale`) therefore self-clears on the ~15-min requested window
against an honest provider; the 24 h clamp is only the independent fence
against a hostile one. (Pre-4-a-3 the adapter requested 24 h for BOTH
directions, silently re-pricing every "minutes-scale" residual claim in
this section to a day.)
Ordinary sends are unaffected in both directions (a queued send never blocks
a deposit; an in-flight deposit never blocks a send). The refusal is
deadline-BOUNDED, never a wedge: a signed deposit dies at mined-buried delete
or via expiry→requeue, and a `Queued` one at the drain's **seedless
lapsed-deposit purge** (`send::purge_lapsed_queued_deposits`, run
UNCONDITIONALLY every resubmission pass, before the Phase-2 seed gate). The
purge is load-bearing, not belt (review BLOCKER, folded): the in-gate
`prepare_queued` delete is UNREACHABLE exactly where the guard bites hardest
— a host-custody background pass dies at `acquire_seed` before the gate, and
a portless wallet skips Phase 2 whole — so without it a single swallowed
sign-miss would have bricked swap PERMANENTLY behind "already in progress"
(deposits are excluded from cancel; only a wipe would clear it). With it the
guard self-clears with the quote lifetime at EVERY custody tier — **while
resubmission passes run** (the honest liveness qualifier, W-swap-4-a-3): the
purge rides the drain, so a wallet that never completes a sync pass (killed
app, extended offline) clears at its NEXT clean pass, not by wall-clock
alone.
**Guard before cap** (W-swap-4-a-3): the in-flight refusal is checked BEFORE
the `QueuedSendsFull` table cap inside the same `IMMEDIATE` txn — when both
conditions hold, the deposit enqueue must surface `SwapDepositInFlight`
(remedy: track, never re-quote), not the cap's "let the queue drain" copy,
whose retry guidance is exactly the re-quote the guard exists to refuse.
Ordinary sends still meet the cap first (no deadline tag ⇒ the guard branch
is skipped).
**Known availability residual (deliberate, review-weighed):** a SUCCESSFUL
swap's deposit row lingers `Sent` until burial-delete (`REORG_MAX_BLOCKS` =
100 blocks ≈ 2 h) — back-to-back swaps hit "a swap is already in progress"
for that window even while the tracking screen shows success. Chosen over a
sharper predicate because every refinement weakens the guard: a
deadline-live-only predicate re-opens the confused-retry double for
long-deadline quotes, and a mined-check predicate needs the wallet DB inside
the enqueue's atomic section (a lock-order + TOCTOU surface) and re-opens a
reorg window. The refinement (allow-once-predecessor-mined, done safely)
is earmarked with FR-23-b (#361); the honest fault copy makes the wait
legible meanwhile.
Placement is deliberate: the guard fires at the deposit leg (after the
durable take + `provider.execute`), so the refused execute consumed its quote
and registered intent — fail-safe (a registered-but-undeposited quote refunds
provider-side; the shipped provider's `execute` is a local no-op). Residual
(STILL OPEN after FR-23-b — scope note, S237): a host-custody sign-failure
zombie (deposit durably `Queued`, unsignable until a user-present moment) holds
the guard until its deadline lapses — the purge enforces exactly that bound —
honest ("in progress" is true) but an availability wait. FR-23-b shipped the
MECHANISM that fixes it (`authorize_parked_send` drives any queued row through
a user-present sign) but deliberately NOT the surface: the verb refuses
deposit-tagged rows, mirroring `cancel_parked_send`/`retry_parked_send`, because
`list_parked_sends` excludes them and the `(id, created_at)` pin has no
sanctioned source for one. The remaining work is a SWAP-SCREEN affordance over
the swap↔deposit id linkage, not core.
Second residual (review MED, documented): a SIGNED deposit with an
UNPROVABLE leg (its tx pruned/collected from the store — the pre-existing
conservative eternal-`Awaiting`, which correctly never requeues what might
still mine) now also holds the guard for as long as it waits; reachability
is remote (the engine does not evict own-created txs, which always carry a
real expiry), and the deposit cancel/park affordance that would give it a
user-paced exit is FR-23-b's surface. Third residual (same class): a
CORRUPT in-flight deposit row (mis-sized txid/claim blob) fail-closes the
whole `list_in_flight` read — the pre-existing whole-read conservatism —
and now also holds the guard; a corrupt-URI `Queued` deposit does NOT (the
seedless purge deletes by deadline + id, parse-free, so it stays
deadline-bounded). The widened remedy (purge/cancel for a
lapsed-AND-undecodable deposit row) rides FR-23-b with the cancel surface.
Adjacent spec note (review kill-list): a provider MAY hand a TEX (ZIP-320)
deposit address — `validate_quote`'s transparent check blesses it — which
makes the deposit a gap-limit-consuming two-step; strand-bounded (tx0
burial → reap next pass), but a TEX-deposit provider should be weighed
against FR-23-b's leg-2 parked authorization before onboarding. **Host defense-in-depth (a timeout is NOT
a failure):** on a `swapExecute` timeout the reference UI transitions to
TRACKING (`watchSwapStatus(quote.id)` — the shipped provider's execute
returns the quote id verbatim, and by the timeout the durable enqueue has
long committed), never to the re-quotable form.

**The deferred-broadcast rules (S178 re-review, #363).** Splitting the sign
(execute) from the broadcast (drain) opened a window pre-FR-23 never had: a
signed deposit could wait for the next COMPLETE clean sync pass to
FIRST-broadcast (catch-up, background `stopSync`, stall). Two rules close it:
1. **Prompt kick.** `send_deposit_now` hands the just-signed group's raw
   bytes to a DETACHED broadcast task — the same per-tx open-gated, jittered,
   fresh-circuit `broadcast_group` machinery the drain uses (counts-only
   §5.4; the open-gate is re-checked AFTER the jitter sleep too, so a close
   landing during the window never fires a tx) — so the deposit normally
   broadcasts within seconds of execute WITHOUT extending the timed execute
   future (the spawn returns immediately). A kick failure is swallowed; the
   drain remains the durable fallback (a crash between sign and kick degrades
   to pre-kick latency, never to loss). **The kick carries its OWN
   `deposit_gate` re-check on a fresh clock** (arch review HIGH, folded): the
   sign's gate ran at `prepare_queued` ENTRY, before the unbounded ZK prove —
   the very work the timeout→track arm exists for — so the quote can die
   between gate and kick; a non-`Proceed` gate skips the kick (rule 2's hold
   owns the row). **The kick gates on the DURABLE ROW TAG** (W-swap-4-a-3):
   `try_sign_queued_deposit` returns the intent's stored `deposit_deadline`
   with the signed group, and the kick feeds THAT to `deposit_gate` — the
   clamped column written at the enqueue door is the tag SSOT; re-deriving a
   clamp from the raw provider deadline at kick time (the pre-4-a-3 shape)
   computed a DIFFERENT value (a later `now` moves the ceiling) and quietly
   forked the SSOT. No swap-kill check (drain parity — a signed durable tx is
   generic outbox work). Teardown residual (documented in-code): the task is
   not abortable — one already past its gates can hold the wallet handle up
   to ~one gRPC unary timeout; since S306 (INC-027) `close()` WAITS that out
   (bounded `QUIESCE_MAX`, then the logged residual — the `wipe` API's S306
   correction) instead of returning with the handle held, and the SAME
   straggler holds a
   strong `Inner` ref a concurrent `rescan_from` quiesce must wait out
   (bounded `QUIESCE_MAX`; a typed, retryable `WalletBusy { Rescanning }`
   past it — W-swap-4-a-3 doc extension); the close-integrated abort handle
   is earmarked with FR-23-b.
2. **Deadline hold at `ReBroadcast`.** The drain re-checks `deposit_gate`
   before (re)broadcasting a deposit-tagged group: `Expired`/`Wait` ⇒ HOLD
   (row untouched this pass) — never a FIRST broadcast into a dead quote,
   which the provider would refund as a fee-burning transparent round-trip.
   The terminal arms run FIRST and are unchanged (delete-on-buried for a
   mined deposit; all-legs-dead-buried requeue → next pass's `deposit_gate`
   delete; strand), so the hold can never wedge a row past its tx expiry +
   burial. A deposit already broadcast pre-deadline that mines late is
   outside wallet control either way (the provider refunds a late deposit);
   the hold simply stops the wallet ITSELF from feeding a dead quote.
3. **Deadline re-gate at the drain's broadcast phase** (the S180 twin HIGH,
   W-swap-4-a-3). Rules 1–2 gate the SIGN and the RECONCILE decisions — but
   both run on the PASS-START clock, and the actual network send happens in
   the END-OF-PASS broadcast phase: after every other intent's unbounded ZK
   proving, behind earlier groups inside the 60 s broadcast budget. A
   deposit that read `Proceed` at pass start could therefore FIRST-broadcast
   minutes later into a dead quote, and the collected `outbound` queue had
   dropped the deadline tag (structurally un-recheckable — the exact
   asymmetry the kick's own gate closed, left open on the drain side).
   `outbound` now carries `(group, deposit_deadline)` and the phase re-runs
   the SAME `deposit_gate` on a FRESH per-group wall clock immediately
   before `broadcast_group`: non-`Proceed` skips the group (counted
   `deposit_held`, row untouched — rule 2's hold owns it on the next pass;
   an ordinary send's `None` tag reads `Proceed` bit-identically). Kick
   parity, now total: EVERY path that can FIRST-broadcast a deposit gates on
   a fresh clock at the send moment.

**CORRECTED 2026-10-06 (the 2026-10-05 review, F01; plan
`docs/plan/audit-2026-10-05-fixes.md` §2, four design passes).** Rules 1–3
above gated each GROUP once, before `broadcast_group`'s per-tx jitter, and
used ONE gate. Both were wrong:
- **The check sits after the jitter, per leg.** `broadcast_group` re-runs the
  deposit gate immediately before EACH submit, on the wall clock, after the
  jitter (which sleeps on `tokio::time` and can span a suspension). A held leg
  ends the group, counted `deadline_held` (the drain folds it into
  `deposit_held`), never as an attempt. Residual: the lazy dial and the RPC
  follow the check (≤ `GRPC_UNARY_TIMEOUT_SECS` awake).
- **Two gates, one predicate** (`send::deposit_gate_with_margin`):
  `deposit_gate` (START, `DEPOSIT_FIRST_FEED_MARGIN_SECS` = 240 s) and
  `deposit_gate_continue` (CONTINUE, `DEPOSIT_CONTINUE_MARGIN_SECS` = 90 s).
  A leg CONTINUES when it, or the recorded leg before it, is already on the
  network: mined, or carrying the delivery accepted mark, or answered
  `Accepted` earlier in the same call or kick — never on `Rejected`. The
  240 s margin is for starting a deposit; applied to tx1 of a two-step (TEX)
  deposit whose tx0 is out, it stranded the funds on the one-time address
  where tx1 would most likely have landed. Rule 2's hold and rule 3's re-gate
  use the gate of the group's first unmined leg (`Reconciled::Rebroadcast {
  txs, continues }`, the drain's `OutboundGroup`); the kick carries legs
  accepted in an earlier round; `DeliveryView::state_of` mirrors the same
  rule. The 90 s figure and the evicted-mark residual are priced in the plan
  §2.2 and on the constant.

Named tests: `the_gates_hold_at_their_margins`,
`broadcast_group_rechecks_the_start_gate_after_the_jitter`,
`a_two_step_deposit_sends_its_second_leg_inside_the_start_margin`,
`a_rejected_first_leg_does_not_let_the_second_leg_continue`,
`a_continuation_is_held_inside_the_continue_margin`,
`the_drain_sends_tx1_after_an_accepted_unmined_tx0`,
`the_drain_continues_after_a_mined_tx0`,
`the_drain_holds_a_two_step_deposit_with_nothing_on_the_network`,
`the_drain_carries_continues_into_the_broadcast_phase`,
`the_delivery_view_agrees_with_the_drain`,
`the_kick_continues_only_after_an_accepted_leg`,
`a_jitter_above_the_ceiling_is_refused_at_every_door`,
`a_deposit_group_never_waits_longer_than_the_default_jitter`.

**Rescan × the outbox (the witness-inversion fence, W-swap-4-a-3).**
`rescan_from` rebuilds the data DB from chain while PRESERVING the durable
aux outbox — so a broadcast-but-UNMINED `Sent` intent survives the rebuild
while the notes its tx spends read UNSPENT in the rebuilt view (the tx is
not on chain; the prior spent-marks are gone with the old DB). The next
drain would classify it `ReProposeFresh` over a witness that inverted under
it and re-sign — potentially over DISJOINT notes, and with the original tx
still valid in the mempool BOTH can mine: 2× pay. (Pre-existing class for
any in-flight send; a new money face now that swap deposits put signed sends
in the outbox by default.) The fence: `rescan_inner` REFUSES while
`list_in_flight` is non-empty — typed `WalletError::RescanWithInFlightSend`
(`RW-LIFE-006`, bridge kind mirrored), retryable (an in-flight row resolves
by mine + burial-delete or by expiry → requeue → purge, hours-bounded; the
reference UI's recover-by-reopen already renders a usable wallet at the
prior birthday). The hours bound carries the SAME liveness qualifier as the
purge: it holds while resubmission passes run over an ADVANCING tip — a
frozen/censoring endpoint stalls resolution indefinitely (self-limiting:
sync is visibly stuck; an endpoint change is the remedy). Checked AFTER the
stop-join + quiesce (sole `Inner`
ownership), so no racing drain pass — or orphaned pass straggler — can sign
a row in behind the check; `Queued` rows do NOT block (nothing signed; they
re-propose FRESH against the rebuilt view, which is the correct recovery);
`Stranded` rows do not block (terminal, tx0 mined ⇒ the rescan re-finds it).
A refusal consumes the handle like every rescan fault (seals + DBs intact;
the host re-opens). Availability residual, accepted: a mined-but-unburied
send blocks a rescan for the ≤ ~2 h burial tail — conservative by design
(a mined-check inside the fence would re-open a reorg window). ~~SCOPE
residual (crypto-review MED, documented): the fence covers the OUTBOX
classes only — an INTERACTIVE single-step send keeps no outbox row (its one
tx self-heals via ~50-min expiry), so a rescan during ITS
broadcast-but-unmined window proceeds; the wallet's automation never
re-signs it (no row), but the send vanishes from view until it mines and a
user manually re-sending over the inverted witness could still double-pay —
the engine-side unmined-tx read that would close it rides FR-23-b.~~ Struck
S293, ADR-0556: the fence now reads `delivery::enumerate` on the aux handle
to the same file before the destructive step, so an unmined, unexpired
single-step send the wallet still owes blocks a rescan exactly like an outbox
row (typed `RescanWithInFlightSend`); a host that skips the UI and calls
`rescanFrom` then `propose` sees the same refusal — the rescan never
happened, so there is no inverted witness to re-send over. AVAILABILITY
residual, widened and accepted: a single-step send blocks a rescan until it
mines or expires (`DEFAULT_TX_EXPIRY_DELTA` = 40 blocks ≈ 50 min), where
before only the outbox classes did.

**The dead-order trail (documented residual, W-swap-4-a-3).** When the
wallet itself ends a swap (rule-2/3 hold → tx expiry, the seedless purge, an
under-funded `Stale` riding out its deadline), the provider-side order it
registered at execute simply expires UNFUNDED — nothing further needs
sending, the provider's own deadline machinery retires it. While the durable
row lives, its URI carries the deposit address (the shipped provider's
status handle), so a later surface can reconstruct what the order was (#366
re-attach); after the terminal delete the trail lives only provider-side.
Refund visibility for a PARTIALLY-funded dead order is ADR-0527 (#368).

**The durable swap home (W-swap-5, #366).** An executed swap is money in
motion and MUST remain re-findable across process death, screen re-entry,
session swaps, and the §3.5 kill — the S182 hardware proof photographed the
pre-#366 hole (kill→relaunch mid-armed-window: the in-flight deposit visible
NOWHERE while the in-flight guard refuses new swaps). The mechanism is a
dedicated durable record, deliberately separate from the two existing swap
stores (detection ≠ single-flight ≠ user-visibility — three concerns, three
tables):
1. **The `swap_record` row** — written by the `SwapService` through the
   `SwapRecordSink` port immediately AFTER `provider.execute` succeeds and
   BEFORE the OutOfZec deposit leg. Record-first ordering closes the
   invisible-money window structurally: a deposit can never be durably queued
   without its home row already committed; if the record write fails, the
   typed error propagates and the deposit is NEVER queued — fail-safe (a
   registered-but-unfunded order expires/refunds provider-side, the same
   accepted bound as the §3.5 mid-execute kill abort). Fields are the HONEST
   durable minimum: `id` (the provider status handle — §5.4 never-log; for
   the shipped provider it equals the deposit address), the COARSE direction
   arm (no asset names durably stored — data minimization), `created_at`,
   `deposit_deadline` (OutOfZec: the clamped tag handed to
   `send_deposit_now`; IntoZec: the quote's durable deposit window), and
   `expires_at_wall` (record self-lapse = execute-time + the settlement
   ceiling, the same conservative bound the destination watch uses). NO
   LIVE-status column: provider truth is polled live via `watch_swap_status`;
   the row asserts exactly "an order was registered at execute" — plus, since
   #367, at most one host-pinned OBSERVED TERMINAL `outcome` (a terminal never
   goes stale, so pinning it is not a snapshot-staleness violation; see 3a).
2. **Reads are NOT swap traffic.** `list_in_flight_swaps` /
   `dismiss_swap_record` live UNGATED on the wallet (and the bridge): records
   stay readable when swap is disabled, wound down, or Hard-killed — the §3.5
   kill clears DETECTION state (`swap_destination` `clear_all`, unchanged)
   but never the user's own money-in-motion record (erasing the user's
   knowledge of their order is not "honest-off"; zero provider packets are
   sent by a local read). A wipe destroys records with the wallet — intended
   (§4.5 M3 posture; `WipeWithPendingSwap` warns on the third-party path).
3. **Row lifecycle:** first-wins insert (the execute take's single-flight
   makes a duplicate id structurally dead), capped (`MAX_SWAP_RECORDS`,
   evict-oldest EXEMPTING the just-inserted id — the fresh registration
   survives by construction, not by timestamp ordering, so record-first can
   never lose its own home row to a regressed clock; display-only rows,
   money-safe) with a floor-gated inline prune at insert (lapsed +
   far-future jumped-clock leftovers); DELETE on host dismiss (idempotent).
   **3a. Terminal-outcome pinning (#367).** On an OBSERVED terminal status
   the host PINS the outcome into the record (`record_swap_outcome(id,
   Success|Refunded|Failed)` — UPDATE-only, first-wins, idempotent; a miss on
   an absent or ALREADY-PINNED row is `Ok(false)`; since #382 a LAPSED
   unpinned row is NOT a miss — unresolved rows outlive the window, so the
   pin lands and refreshes the display bound, below) instead of deleting. Pre-#367 the
   reference UI deleted on the notifier's terminal OBSERVATION, which erased
   outcomes the user never SAW (S192-b HIGH-2: with the user at wallet root
   the row vanished with the outcome unrendered; process death in the gap
   erased an OutOfZec `Refunded`/`Failed` entirely — a money outcome the user
   can act on). DELETE is now USER-INTENT only: the terminal card's Done (the
   outcome was rendered full-screen = seen) and the home row's explicit
   Remove affordance (confirmed — removing a non-terminal row drops the
   re-attach handle). Self-lapse is PINNED-ONLY since #382 (the S195
   converged HIGH): an UNPINNED row (`outcome IS NULL` at the SQL level)
   stays listed past `expires_at_wall` and is spared by the inline prune's
   lapse arm (its far-future arm CLAMPS an unpinned row, the watch-store
   precedent, instead of deleting it) — an unresolved swap is money in
   motion and must never leave the user's sight on a wall clock alone; its
   only exits are the user's Remove, a pinned terminal's later lapse, and
   the cap eviction. A PINNED row still self-lapses at `expires_at_wall`,
   and PINNING SETS that bound to EXACTLY one settlement window from the
   observation at a plausible clock (`MAX` — never shrunk — below the
   clock-plausibility floor): with unresolved rows outliving the
   execute-time window, a pin can now land on an already-lapsed row, and
   pinning-then-instantly-delisting would erase the outcome un-rendered —
   the exact #367 regression at the new boundary. EXACT rather than `MAX`
   at a plausible clock (S196 review) because every legitimate prior bound
   is its own write-time + the settlement ceiling ≤ the pin's window, so
   replacement can only collapse a jumped-clock far-future artifact that
   `MAX` would have preserved as an eternal-looking terminal until the next
   insert's reap (documented residual: a backward clock step between write
   and pin shrinks the window by the step — bounded, display-only). So the
   lapse residue bound reads "the outcome had a full window to be seen FROM
   WHEN IT WAS OBSERVED". Storage:
   a nullable `outcome` TEXT column (`'success'`/`'refunded'`/`'failed'`),
   added by the guarded additive `ALTER` (`issued_swap_quote`
   destination-column precedent — no `WALLET_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump, O(1)
   metadata on the boot path); an UNKNOWN stored value (a newer build's
   variant read by this one) reads as `None` = still-in-flight — fail-honest,
   the live poll re-reveals provider truth rather than a wrong terminal
   being asserted. Documented tail of that choice: the unknown text still
   occupies the first-wins slot, so this build's own later observation
   cannot re-pin the row — it renders in-flight/past-window until the user
   removes it or the 48 h self-lapse reaps it (display-only; tracking shows
   live truth throughout). At the `MAX_SWAP_RECORDS` cap, PINNED-terminal
   rows lose the eviction contest to in-flight rows regardless of age
   (money-review: finished business awaiting Remove must never erase a live
   swap's only re-attach handle). Downgrade bound (documented, same class as the
   destination columns): a post-#366/pre-#367 binary's RESCAN of a #367 DB
   fails typed on the column drift (`assert_columns_match`) rather than
   silently mis-mapping — loud, recoverable by re-upgrading, never a silent
   money-column shift. Between execute and terminal the row is the re-attach
   handle: the home surface lists it, "view swap" re-opens tracking via
   `watch_swap_status(id)`, and the `SwapAlreadyInFlight` fault points AT the
   tracked swap (making the §4.4 guard-fault copy's promise true in the
   shipped UI). Post-restart an IntoZec re-attach lands on TRACKING, not the
   deposit-QR screen — the full quote (address/memo/foreign amount) is
   deliberately NOT persisted (the record is the minimum; the D7 screen is
   guaranteed only within the issuing process run) — the `PendingDeposit`
   card carries the deposit window honestly.
4. **Cross-build rescan preservation (the S186 fold, ADR-0534):** the swap
   tables' SCHEMA (`swap_destination`, `swap_record`) is ensured and
   rescan-copied UNCONDITIONALLY — feature gates scope BEHAVIOR (DETECT
   polling, the service), never the durability of money state already
   written: a non-swap build rescanning a swap-build `wallet.db` preserves
   in-flight swap state byte-for-byte instead of silently dropping it. The
   ADR-0534 guard test therefore pins ONE build-independent table set —
   **for builds of this revision** (crypto-review M2 precision): a
   PRE-W-swap-5 binary opening a newer `wallet.db` (no
   `WALLET_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump — deliberately, so a downgrade never bricks
   the wallet) still rescans with its own older preserved set and drops the
   tables it predates. Accepted bound: the exposure needs a binary DOWNGRADE
   plus a rescan, loses detection/visibility rows only (custody state rides
   `queued_send_intent`, which every shipped revision preserves), and the
   alternative — a version bump — would hard-block every downgrade to
   protect display rows.

**The swap trust posture, in one place (review HARD-G):** quotes, statuses,
and deposit addresses are provider **API data** — bounds-validated (the §2.6
M1 ceiling, the §4.6 string/decimal caps) but **not cryptographically
verifiable**. The protections are exactly: the user-anchored sanity ceiling
before signing, the echoed-`refundTo` check, the disclosure DTO the UI must
render, and the deposit size being bounded by the user's own request. We
never imply verification we don't have.

**Swap terminal honesty + display truth (#367).** Four contracts, each
closing an observed lie:
1. **`SwapNotFound` poll policy (the S192-b wedge root).** The status poll
   treats the provider-DEFINITIVE `ProviderProtocol::SwapNotFound` (a 1Click
   404 on the status handle) distinctly from transport faults: after
   `SWAP_NOT_FOUND_TERMINAL_POLLS` CONSECUTIVE such results the loop emits a
   SYNTHETIC terminal `Failed(NotFound)` and ends (`outcome = "not_found"`).
   Never first-404-is-terminal (a transient post-execute 404 while the
   provider indexes the order must not false-fail a live swap — the counter
   resets on ANY other result); never retry-forever (a provider-GC'd order
   re-attached from the durable home would otherwise poll/spin eternally —
   the pre-#367 behavior the S192-b escape button only mitigated).
   `NotFound` is its own `SwapFailureCode` variant: "the provider no longer
   recognizes this swap" is a materially different user fact from `Expired`
   (a deposit that DID land on a GC'd order still refunds provider-side to
   the recorded refund address). The synthesized terminal is NEVER durably
   pinned (money-review HIGH): it is a heuristic derived from bare HTTP
   status codes that infrastructure between wallet and provider can forge,
   and the 3a pin is first-wins — pinning it would let a ≥5-poll 404 blip
   assert an uncorrectable false "didn't complete" over money in motion.
   The reference UI renders it as a session terminal only; the durable row
   stays outcome-NULL, falls to the neutral past-window line, and a later
   re-attach re-polls — the REAL terminal, once observed, pins normally.
2. **The DTO deadline is the ACTIONABLE deadline.** `SwapService::quote`
   returns `SwapQuote.expires_at` ALREADY ceiling-clamped to the wall window
   the wallet itself enforces AND minus the direction-aware execute margin —
   the exact instant `execute` starts refusing (`QuoteExpired`). The raw
   provider echo (observed live: ~72 h/~96 h against a ~10-min actionable
   window — the S182/S184 hardware-photographed countdown lie) never reaches
   a host. Display and enforcement share ONE number by construction; a host
   countdown hitting 0:00 and a rejected execute can no longer disagree in
   either direction (the authorize-then-instant-refuse seam).
3. **Busy is not a dead end.** `WalletError::StoreBusy` surviving the
   in-SDK bounded retry at the QUOTE persist or the EXECUTE take maps to the
   typed retryable `SwapError::SwapStateBusy` (`RW-SWAP-014`), not the
   `SwapStateUnavailable` collapse: at both sites NOTHING was consumed (the
   busy `IMMEDIATE` tx never began), so a plain retry of the SAME action
   genuinely succeeds — the send path's "busy, try again" honesty (S184 F4).
   `record_started` keeps the collapse: it sits POST-claim, where the honest
   remedy is re-quote, not retry.
4. **The swept-row miss reads as what it is.** An execute whose durable
   `take` finds no row is typed `QuoteExpired`, not the generic
   `RequestInvalid` "not issued by this service": every production path to
   that miss — the hygiene sweep of a pre-upgrade far-future row, a lapsed
   row's prune, a >1 h backward clock step, an already-executed replay —
   ends in the same user action, "this quote is no longer valid — get a new
   quote" (the S183 review cross-note; misleading for a quote minted moments
   ago on an old build).
5. **The reference-UI review door (#367, non-normative for hosts but the
   shipped posture).** At quote-review, BEFORE the authorize-spend bracket:
   the FR-23 ceiling check, then the SPENDABLE pre-check — refuse when the
   OutOfZec deposit plus a conservative fee allowance
   (`kSwapDepositFeeAllowanceZat`, UI-side: the exact ZIP-317 fee is
   knowable only at execute-sign) exceeds spendable-now, hedged when the
   catch-up cue is live (the S190-b blast radius: without it a catching-up
   0-balance wallet could quote→ack→execute into an engine-swallowed
   sign-time InsufficientFunds and land "Swap started" over a deposit that
   can never fund). Fails OPEN on a missing snapshot — the engine gate stays
   the money backstop; this check exists for honesty. The review also
   DISCLOSES the network fee's existence (a "You send" that omits the fee
   implies the deposit is the whole debit; no fabricated number is shown),
   renders the countdown from the actionable DTO deadline (item 2), and the
   execute step carries a pop-guard ("still working") for its bounded
   committing window. Terminal honesty in the reference UI: observation PINS
   (3a), Done/Remove DELETE; Refunded/UnderDeposited/NotFound render
   direction-aware copy (since #368 the OutOfZec Refunded body says the ZEC
   returns to this wallet and shows up as unshielded balance after a sync —
   the pre-#368 "may not appear yet" hedge is retired); a
   re-attached IntoZec pending never re-instructs the unpersisted deposit.
   Since #382 the KILL-state tracking body is direction-aware BOTH ways:
   the OutOfZec arm gets the IntoZec L8 mirror (a refunded OutOfZec swap's
   ZEC comes back to THIS wallet and shows in the balance once swap is back
   on and the wallet syncs — the pre-#382 body sent the user to "the
   provider's side", a misdirect once #368 made the refund land here), the
   home row renders an "unresolved past the settlement window" line off the
   record's own `expires_at_wall` (distinct from the deposit-window line),
   and the `RefundAddressUnavailable` fault copy names its dominant real
   cause — a pre-first-sync Sell (the swap slot is activation-gated, not
   provision-gated) — with a "wait for the first sync to finish" hint
   instead of a bare "try again" loop; the IntoZec sibling
   `DestinationAddressUnavailable` gets its own classify arm + the same
   sync hint (pre-#382 it fell through to the generic could-not-quote).

**Swap refund visibility (#368 — discharging the ADR-0527 obligation).**
An OutOfZec refund lands at a wallet transparent address; pre-#368 that
address was derived-and-forgotten (no engine registration, no poll, no
durable handle) — a REFUNDED terminal said "your funds came back" over a
balance that never moved (S180 money F2). Eight contracts close it, all
riding the ADR-0530 scoped-poll machinery ("no new detection code" — the
consequence that ADR reserved). Items 1–7 shipped with #368; item 8 (#382,
the S195 post-ship fold) removes the ONE wall-clock bound items 3/4 and the
home row all shared:

1. **Refunds mint THROUGH the engine at quote.** `WalletRefundSource`
   adopts the destination source's shape: reserve on the shared single-use
   external counter, then `get_address_for_index` at that index (the SAME
   §3.3b D1 receiver request — engine-persists the UA, no gap burn), under
   the SAME db→aux lock order. The refundTo handed to the provider stays
   the bare BIP44 external t-addr — derived RAW from the seed as before and
   CROSS-CHECKED byte-equal against the engine UA's transparent receiver
   (two audited derivations of one address; a mismatch fails closed, the
   address is never handed out). Engine registration is therefore BY
   CONSTRUCTION for every quoted refund: `put_received_transparent_utxo`
   accepts a refund UTXO the moment anything polls the address. KAT-pinned
   (`refund_address_at_index_equals_the_ufvk_external_receiver`). Behavior
   delta (documented): an OutOfZec quote now requires a provisioned account
   (the engine mint needs the UFVK — the destination source's posture since
   IZ-1a); a pre-first-sync quote fails typed `RefundAddressUnavailable` and
   succeeds on retry after the account provisions — honest, since a wallet
   that has never synced has nothing to sell.
2. **The durable refund handle.** `IssuedQuoteRecord` gains
   `refund: Option<IssuedRefund { address, index }>` (`Some` ⟺ OutOfZec,
   alongside `deposit`; additive `refund_address`/`refund_index` columns on
   `issued_swap_quote`, the destination-columns precedent, both-or-neither
   validated at `take`). The refund is no longer forgotten at mint.
3. **The watch arms at `record_started`, atomically with the home row.**
   `execute` threads the taken record's watched inbound leg (IntoZec: the
   destination; OutOfZec: the refund) into `StartedSwap.watch`; the wallet
   sink writes the home row AND the `swap_destination` watch upsert (the
   `mark_executed` MAX-deadline semantics, `now + SWAP_SETTLEMENT_MAX_SECS`)
   in ONE aux `IMMEDIATE` txn. Record-first now also means WATCH-first: a
   deposit can never be durably queued without its refund watch armed. This
   MOVES the destination settlement-extend out of `take` (the S184 NIT
   rider): a refused execute — deadline gate, kill re-check, provider
   failure — no longer parks a 48 h scoped-poll entry (the destination row
   stays at its clamped quote-deadline window and prunes naturally), and a
   refund watch never exists for a deposit that never left. Documented
   asymmetry (unchanged behavior, new site): a far-future-SWEPT quote's
   `take` returns `None` ⇒ no record, no watch extension ⇒ its quote-time
   destination row dies at the clamped quote deadline — bounded, hygiene
   only. The take↔record crash window (quote consumed, no record) keeps its
   #366 posture: no record ⇒ no deposit ⇒ nothing to watch.
4. **A pinned Refunded outcome RE-ARMS the watch.** The `swap_record` row
   gains nullable `watch_address`/`watch_index` columns (additive; written
   at record time; never listed, never crossing FFI). `record_swap_outcome`
   pinning (or re-observing) `Refunded` on an OutOfZec row re-upserts the
   refund watch for a fresh settlement window — so a refund that lands
   AFTER the 48 h execute window (or whose execute-time watch write was
   lost) is re-polled the moment the user actually sees the Refunded
   terminal, which is exactly when they will look for the money. Best
   effort (busy tolerated + logged); idempotent; re-observation retries it.
5. **The ADR-0527 backfill (the named migration obligation) — bounded by a
   CEILING seeded at QUIESCENT points.** A durable bounds row (aux,
   single-row) carries a registration high-water marker AND a
   `backfill_ceiling` snapshotted from the counter (the S194
   review-converged HIGH fix: without the ceiling the sweep would chase the
   live counter and pull every fresh mint into the poll). Since #382 the
   snapshot is taken ONLY where quote issuance cannot race it: `store::open`
   seeds it (first-wins) right after the migrate-up, under the exclusive
   open lock, BEFORE the wallet can serve a quote — so every index this
   build reserves is ≥ the ceiling BY CONSTRUCTION — and the rescan rebuild
   RE-SEEDS it on the temp DB from the copied counter, atomically with the
   marker clear (quote issuance is fenced across a rescan). This CLOSES the
   S194 residual the earlier text overclaimed as already closed: a quote
   whose counter reserve had committed but whose issued row was still
   lock-queued/in provider RTT at snapshot time was INVISIBLE to the
   index-keyed live-quote exclusions (the row did not exist yet) — that gap
   cannot straddle an exclusive open or a fenced rescan. The exclusions
   remain as the guard for PRE-seed live quotes (their rows DO exist); the
   backfill's own lazy seed remains as a defensive fallback only
   (unreachable by construction), and the work path cross-checks
   `marker < ceiling ≤ counter` fail-closed (`StoreCorrupt`) before any
   sweep — a tampered in-range-domain ceiling can never mint+poll
   never-allocated addresses. The transparent-refresh pass registers every
   index in `(marker, ceiling)` via `get_address_for_index` (idempotent,
   bounded per pass) and arms each a one-settlement-window synthetic watch
   row (`backfill:<index>` — a RESERVED id namespace `validate_quote`
   refuses to providers; an index a live watch row covers or a LIVE issued
   quote references is skipped, keyed on the INDEX, never the address
   string) so an ALREADY-LANDED pre-#368 refund is detected once, then the
   rows retire/prune normally. Once the marker reaches the ceiling the
   sweep is done forever; post-snapshot mints self-register at mint and are
   never backfilled. The backfill is SKIPPED while a §3.5 kill stops
   polling (arming rows the same pass's honest-off would clear would burn
   the one-shot window). `rescan_from` RESETS the bounds row: the engine
   rebuild drops `get_address_for_index` registrations, so the next refresh
   re-seeds the ceiling from the copied counter and re-registers the full
   range — healing refund AND destination registrations across a rescan (a
   pre-existing IntoZec hole: a delivery landing post-rescan at a dropped
   registration would be put-rejected).
   **#387 — the RESTORE-PESSIMISTIC first seed.** The quiescent seed above
   snapshots the LOCAL counter — honest for upgrade-in-place and rescan
   (the aux survives / is copied), HOLLOW for a fresh-seed RESTORE: the
   new device's empty aux seeded ceiling = FLOOR ("done forever") while
   the seed's allocation history died with the old device, so a
   pre-restore refund landed at any index ≥ FLOOR was in-app-INVISIBLE
   (the scoped poll set — item 7 — never gap-scans by design; ADR-0527's
   §4.5 recoverability held for THIRD-PARTY BIP44 restores but not for
   the SDK's own). Since #387 the FIRST-EVER seed distinguishes
   provenance at the one point it is knowable: counter row ABSENT ∧
   creation stamp ABSENT (`created_at = None` ⇔ not freshly-generated on
   THIS device — restores, and pre-F4 wallets that never allocated;
   since S213 "freshly generated" = `Generate` OR host-attested
   `FreshRawBytes`, so a LYING fresh attestation also skips this sweep —
   the §3.2f lying-host contract, recovered by the #390 deep scan) ∧
   bounds row ABSENT (first-wins — an already-seeded wallet is never
   retro-widened) ⇒ the seed writes counter = ceiling =
   `RESTORE_BACKFILL_BREADTH` (64) instead of the floor, COUNTER FIRST
   (the load-bearing write order: the reverse order's crash window
   would leave a widened ceiling over an unburned counter — a first
   reserve INSIDE the swept, watched range; counter-first converges to
   the correct end state from either crash side). The STANDARD backfill machinery (this item)
   then registers + one-window-watches external indices
   [FLOOR, breadth) — a pre-restore refund landed within the breadth is
   detected by the first refresh passes — and the BURNED counter means
   post-restore allocations start AT the breadth, so the swept range is
   never reused (HARD-H held within the breadth). A freshly-generated
   wallet (stamp present) keeps the floor seed — no pre-existing
   indices by construction for `Generate`, by ATTESTATION for
   `FreshRawBytes`; a stamp-READ fault degrades to the restore
   arm (a sweep, never a miss — visibility-conservative). Residuals,
   disclosed: (a) pre-restore indices ≥ the breadth are NOT swept by
   the first seed, so absent further action they stay in-app-invisible
   AND their indices may be REUSED by post-restore allocations — the
   information loss inherent to a seed-only restore (the BIP-44
   gap-limit class). RECOVERED two ways for a >63-quote pre-restore
   history: the third-party BIP44 restore (the §4.5 path) AND, since
   #390, the SDK's OWN user-triggered DEEP SCAN (below) — which
   re-widens the counter+ceiling, surfacing the deeper refunds in-app
   AND burning the widened band (closing the reuse half over that
   width); (b) a wallet restored
   on a PRE-#387 build already holds the first-wins floor seed and does
   not self-heal (pre-GA founder devices only; re-restoring on a #387
   build heals); (c) a stamp-absent wallet that never swapped pays one
   breadth-sized registration sweep + one settlement window of widened
   poll set — bounded, self-pruning; (d) TAMPER ASYMMETRY: a FORGED
   creation stamp planted in a restored wallet's sealed DB forces the
   floor arm — the pre-#387 invisibility, for that wallet only (a
   stamp-DELETE tamper merely costs a Generate wallet one bounded
   sweep). Tamper-only (the writer holds the DB key and could hide
   refunds more directly by deleting watch rows); disclosed for the
   asymmetry: stamp ABSENCE fails open toward visibility, forged
   PRESENCE fails toward invisibility.
   **#390 — the user-triggered DEEP SCAN ("Check older swap
   addresses" — in-app recovery of residual (a)).** The #387 first
   seed is BOUNDED (breadth 64) to keep the restore-time poll set
   inside the item-7 envelope; a rare heavy pre-restore history (>63
   lifetime quotes — the counter ticks once per quote, EITHER
   direction, abandoned included) leaves single-use addresses at
   indices ≥ breadth un-swept. The counter is SHARED by OutOfZec
   refund addresses AND IntoZec destination addresses, so the scan
   recovers pre-restore swap DELIVERIES as much as refunds — the
   user-facing name says "swap addresses", never just "refunds", and
   the verb is CHECK, never "recover" (the op cannot know funds
   exist — the "Check one-time addresses" naming precedent). Since
   #390 the user can RE-WIDEN on demand: ONE aux `IMMEDIATE` txn
   raises counter AND ceiling to
   `min(counter + REFUND_DEEP_SCAN_STEP, NON_HARDENED_MAX + 1)`
   (STEP ≈ 1024, a COMPILED constant — never an FFI parameter; at the
   exhaustion sentinel the op refuses typed, mirroring
   `reserve_next_index`'s fail-closed arm). One txn covering both
   singleton tables (the `arm_backfill` cross-table composition — the
   two-bare-statements shape of `seed_from_counter` is FORBIDDEN
   here); the raise fn is MAX-monotonic and fail-closed on a missing
   row (the `set_registered_up_to` shape). The txn SERIALIZES with
   `reserve_next_index` (never a reused index) and holds `ceiling ≤
   counter` by construction (the item-5 cross-check never trips).
   TYPED REFUSALS (the op never silently no-ops or lies): (i) while a
   §3.5 kill stops polling (the backfill would never run — refusing
   beats a success-shaped wedge); (ii) while the PRIOR band is still
   registering (`marker + 1 < ceiling`) or a prior sweep's
   `backfill:` watch row is UNEXPIRED — at most ONE outstanding band
   per settlement window, which makes an ambiguous-outcome retry safe
   (the raise is deliberately NOT idempotent — each accepted run adds
   a STEP), paces reruns, and BOUNDS the hostile-host griefing vector
   (unbounded elective poll-set growth was otherwise the one new
   capability this op added); (iii) at exhaustion. The
   `registered_up_to` marker is PRESERVED, so the standard backfill
   registers + one-window-watches `(marker, counter)` over the next
   chain-advancing transparent-refresh passes
   (`REFUND_BACKFILL_MAX_PER_PASS` = 256 per pass ⇒ ~4 passes for one
   STEP, minutes while foregrounded), and the scoped
   `GetAddressUtxos` poll (item 7) surfaces any UTXOs there — NO full
   chain rescan (the addresses are transparent). SWEPT-POPULATION
   TRUTH: `(marker, counter)` is the never-registered band PLUS any
   RETIRED allocated history above the marker (abandoned quotes'
   refund addresses, served-and-retired legs — the live-row
   exclusions spare only LIVE rows). That re-poll is DELIBERATE for a
   recovery op (a refund landing after its original window expired is
   exactly what the user is looking for) and is the SAME
   user-triggered class as the rescan RECURRENCE arm — item 7's
   "abandoned quote's refund address is never polled" and #385's "the
   envelope only SHRINKS" both read with this disclosed,
   user-triggered exception; one window, self-pruning. DUAL-ROW RULE:
   an execute-time arm DELETES any same-index `backfill:` row in the
   same txn (restoring the S194 one-row-per-receiver rule; without it
   the mid-issuance race below leaves a synthetic twin that
   double-attributes funded/retire signals). OBSERVABILITY: a
   counts-only READ exposes `{coverage = counter, pending = ceiling −
   1 − marker}` — `pending == 0` means the band is registered and
   polled at least once (the only honest "done"; found funds surface
   via the normal balance path). The read is RENDER-ONLY (the
   WalletSpendIntent treatment — the coverage number doubles as the
   lifetime quote count); the op's result DTO carries counts only
   (never an index value), and its tracing logs width/counts only
   (§5.4). GENERATE-WALLET TRUTH: `mint_swap_destination` mints at
   ANY conforming index (that is HOW the restore sweep works), so a
   Generate-created wallet running the scan pays the full residual-
   (c)-shaped cost — one STEP of registrations + one settlement
   window of widened poll — and recovers nothing UNLESS its seed also
   lived elsewhere (the same-seed-second-device history — a real,
   legitimate recovery case, which is why the op is NOT
   provenance-gated; the check-verb naming keeps a fruitless run
   honest). The scan also HEALS residual (b) (a pre-#387 floor-seeded
   restore widens past its hollow seed on the first run). Raising the
   counter BURNS [old, new), closing residual (a)'s reuse half over
   the widened width; HARD-H held (receive index 0 < FLOOR; a swept
   index is never later reserved). Only widens — never lowers counter
   or ceiling; the bounds row's first-wins rule now reads "first-wins
   at seed; raisable ONLY by this op, atomically with an equal-or-
   greater counter raise". Post-widen, every later `rescan_from`
   re-registers the full widened range (the RECURRENCE amplification
   — disclosed). The op routes exactly as sync (same Tor policy +
   isolation key); being ELECTIVE, the UI SHOULD surface degraded-Tor
   state and recommend deferral before running it. RESIDUAL: a quote
   MID-ISSUANCE during the raise (the #382 reserve→persist gap) may
   have its index swept — if later executed, the dual-row rule
   restores one-row; if abandoned, its refund address is polled for
   one window although it otherwise never would be (the same
   disclosed exception class as above). UX shape (D2): the entry
   ("Check older swap addresses…") lives in the wallet overflow menu
   ADJACENT to Rescan and opens a sheet with the coverage line
   ("covers roughly this wallet's first {n} swaps") and a
   Check/Check-deeper action; the RESCAN sheet gains a one-line
   cross-pointer ("looking for funds from an old swap? rescanning
   won't find those") — the rescan's "missing older funds?" hook
   otherwise misdirects the exact affected user to a tool that CANNOT
   find these funds (compact blocks carry no transparent outputs and
   the rescan re-seed keeps the 64 ceiling); the ONE-TIME
   post-first-restore note appears only after the #380 catch-up cue
   clears (never next to a still-empty balance), makes no hard
   swap-count claim (quotes ≠ swaps), and its shown-flag is
   IDENTITY-NAMESPACED (the #348 store) and written only AFTER
   display (a process-death re-show is benign; a never-show is not).
6. **Funded rows never prune.** `swap_destination::prune_expired` gains the
   far-future arm (the issued-quote mirror; tampered/pre-clamp rows only)
   and BOTH arms now spare `funded = 1` rows: a funded-but-unshielded
   delivery or refund (sub-threshold — honestly parked below
   `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT`) must keep its shield-source membership and
   its poll slot until `retire` (funded-then-empty) or a Hard-kill
   `clear_all` removes it — window lapse alone must never orphan visible
   money out of `propose_shield`'s source set (there is no full-set rescan
   to recover it).
7. **The privacy envelope is unchanged going forward, with THREE disclosed
   bounded exceptions.** The poll set stays `{index-0} ∪ {addresses we asked
   a provider to pay}`: a refund address enters the poll only at EXECUTE
   (the deposit actually left the pool) — an abandoned OutOfZec quote's
   refund address is engine-registered but never polled (the
   quiescent-seeded ceiling + the live-quote exclusion enforce this, pinned
   by `backfill_never_sweeps_post_snapshot_mint_indices`; OUTSIDE the two
   user-triggered re-poll events — the rescan RECURRENCE arm and the #390
   deep scan (item 5), both of which deliberately re-poll retired
   allocated history below their ceiling for one window). Exception ONE:
   the one-time pre-#368/post-rescan backfill polls its ceiling-bounded
   range for a single settlement window, and that range is
   provider-disclosed refundTo/recipient values PLUS any index burned by a
   crash between reserve and provider disclosure (indistinguishable
   post-hoc) — a bounded, once-ever widening accepted to discharge the
   ADR-0527 obligation, not a live channel. Exception TWO (#382, item 8):
   an UNRESOLVED executed swap's watched leg stays in the scoped poll until
   its record is pinned or dismissed — no longer exactly one settlement
   window — bounded by `MAX_SWAP_RECORDS` and by the fact that every such
   address is already provider-disclosed; "an idle wallet shrinks back to
   index-0" now reads "an idle wallet with no UNRESOLVED swaps shrinks back
   to index-0". Named consequence (S196 review — the cardinality bound
   alone understated it): a provider that WITHHOLDS terminal statuses keeps
   its swaps unresolved, so their legs stay co-resident in the endpoint's
   query indefinitely — a persistent cross-swap linkage at the endpoint
   that pre-#382 aged out in one window. Convergence/escape: the chain pin
   terminates it for any OutOfZec swap whose refund actually lands, the
   user's Remove (whose dialog now says the watch stops) terminates it per
   row, and since #385 the served latch terminates it for any leg whose
   money arrived and moved (funded-then-empty retire — the envelope only
   SHRINKS between user-triggered widen events, i.e. outside a rescan or a
   #390 deep scan); the endpoint learns no new ADDRESSES either way (it was
   handed each one the moment it was armed; the #390 band's addresses are
   fresh derivations, disclosed under RECURRENCE below). Detection feeds the existing surface
   end-to-end with no new
   plumbing: engine put → `BalanceSnapshot.transparent` → the unshielded
   balance line + shield button + the host auto-shield loop;
   `propose_shield` already sources the store's active set, which now
   includes refunds — the §6.3 auto-shield row's OutOfZec-refund half is
   DISCHARGED. Exception THREE (#387): the restore-pessimistic first
   seed (item 5) makes a RESTORED wallet's one-time backfill range
   [FLOOR, `RESTORE_BACKFILL_BREADTH`) rather than provider-disclosed
   indices — the endpoint sees a once-per-restore, one-settlement-window
   query of ~63 fresh addresses it was never handed (unlike Exception
   ONE's provider-disclosed range), which also means the endpoint can
   INFER a restore occurred (a restored wallet's first-window set size
   is distinguishable from a created wallet's — disclosed, accepted).
   RECURRENCE (review precision): "once per restore" describes the
   FIRST-open sweep; every later user-initiated `rescan_from` re-seeds
   the ceiling from the COPIED counter and re-registers + re-polls the
   full [FLOOR, counter) range for one window (Exception ONE's rescan
   arm), and — since #390 — a user-triggered DEEP SCAN (item 5) widens
   counter+ceiling by a STEP (≈1024 — ~16× Exception THREE's first-seed
   size; the endpoint sees the poll set step up in 256-address pass
   increments and can infer a deep scan ran) and re-polls the
   `(marker, counter)` band — the fresh widened indices PLUS retired
   allocated history — for one window. Reruns ACCUMULATE (another STEP
   each), PACED to one outstanding band per settlement window by the
   item-5 typed refusal (the cap on elective poll-set growth). All
   three widenings are user-observable and bounded per event. For a
   restored wallet that range REMAINS mostly
   never-provider-disclosed, so Exception ONE's "provider-disclosed
   refundTo/recipient values" description reads with this restore
   qualifier. Accepted: the addresses are fresh unlinkable derivations
   unless funded, the widening is per-restore/per-rescan bounded, and
   the alternative — a restored swapper's landed refund silently
   invisible — is a money-visibility failure. After the window the
   unfunded rows prune and the set shrinks to scoped exactly as
   Exception ONE.
8. **An UNRESOLVED swap outlives the settlement window (#382 — the S195
   converged money-visibility HIGH).** Pre-#382 the watch row, the home
   row, AND the Refunded re-arm trigger all died on ONE bound
   (execute + `SWAP_SETTLEMENT_MAX_SECS`) while the poll runs only when the
   app runs — a user who executed an OutOfZec swap and did not reopen the
   app within 48 h had the watch pruned before its first poll, the home row
   dropped from `list_in_flight`, and the re-arm unreachable (no card to
   open), so a refund mining after that landed INVISIBLY (the S180 F2
   symptom re-opened for the common mobile pattern), recoverable only by an
   unprompted rescan. Three sub-contracts remove the shared bound:
   **(a) unpinned rows stay listable** — see the W-swap-5 3a amendment
   (self-lapse is pinned-only; the reference row renders a neutral
   "taking longer than expected" line past the settlement bound, keeping
   the View-swap re-attach + Remove affordances).
   **(b) every transparent-refresh pass RE-ARMS the recorded watch leg of
   every unresolved record** (both directions — the OutOfZec refund AND the
   IntoZec destination share the late-tail exposure) for a fresh settlement
   window, BEFORE the prune runs, in the poll's own set-build txn — a
   lapsed-or-even-pruned row is resurrected and polled by the SAME pass, so
   the first foreground after ANY absence detects a waiting refund; skipped
   under a Hard kill exactly like the poll itself (honest-off), and a
   dismissed record stops re-arming (its engine registration survives, so a
   post-dismiss refund remains rescan-recoverable — the Remove dialog says
   so). "Watchable while unresolved" is thereby a per-pass INVARIANT, not a
   one-shot window; item 4's view-time re-arm remains as the immediate
   in-card path. A RETIRED leg (funded then emptied — its detection purpose
   served) is marked `watch_served` ATOMICALLY with the retire, in ONE aux
   txn (#385: the first cut ran retire and the watch clear as two separate
   transactions — a kill or fault between them durably re-opened the
   retire→re-arm churn, a window every IntoZec delivery crossed since
   deliveries have no chain pin), and a served leg stops per-pass
   re-arming; the watch COLUMNS survive the mark, so item 4's card-visit
   re-arm still heals a lying-endpoint early retire (#385 — the first cut
   CLEARED the columns, silently narrowing that recovery to a full rescan).
   The re-arm extend is also write-throttled (#385): a watch whose deadline
   is still at least half a settlement window out is skipped — no semantic
   change, it just stops rewriting+fsyncing every watch row on every ~75 s
   pass for the entire life of a stuck unresolved record. The funded→empty
   retire that marks a leg served is itself DEBOUNCED (#386): the
   retire+latch fires only once a funded row has polled empty on
   `RETIRE_AFTER_EMPTY_PASSES = 3` CONSECUTIVE passes (`empty_streak`
   column; any pass that sees the row funded resets it, and the bump and
   the threshold-crossing retire commit in one aux txn), so a single
   hostile/reorg "empty" reply cannot latch a still-funded leg served —
   #385's latch had made that early retire durable, leaving a sub-threshold
   parked IntoZec delivery (below the shielding threshold, so never emptied
   by a shield) balance-visible but outside the shield source set until a
   full rescan, the exact stranding the pre-#385 churn had been healing by
   accident.
   **(c) a chain-OBSERVED refund PINS `Refunded`** — a previously-unfunded
   OutOfZec watch row turning funded pins the outcome (first-wins, exactly
   like an API observation): the chain outranks the provider's status API
   (HARD-G — statuses are API data, the UTXO is consensus truth), the home
   row flips to the truth without the card ever being opened, and the
   re-arm loop CONVERGES (a pinned row stops extending; the funded row
   exits through the normal funded→empty retire). Both pin paths (API- and
   chain-observed) refresh the record's self-lapse bound to one settlement
   window from observation — see the W-swap-5 3a amendment — so a pin
   landing on a lapsed unresolved row renders instead of delisting
   un-rendered. Disclosed residual (BOTH parties named — S196 review): a
   party who knows the refund address — by construction the PROVIDER, and
   equally the LIGHTWALLETD ENDPOINT, which receives every watched address
   in the query itself and whose asserted records pass the M2 script check
   for any address it was queried on — can dust/fabricate a funding into a
   false `Refunded` display, first-wins durable, which also stops that
   swap's unresolved re-arm. Display-only either way: the balance facts
   stay chain/engine-derived, and a REAL later refund is still engine-put
   and balance-visible independent of the pinned label — WHILE the watched
   leg still polls (#385 precision): the forged pin stops the per-pass
   re-arm, so once the dusted UTXO is shielded and the leg retires
   (`watch_served`), a later real refund is no longer auto-detected — it
   remains recoverable via item 4's card-visit re-arm (the watch columns
   survive the served mark; NOTE the re-arm fires only on a STREAM-observed
   `Refunded` — a provider that has since GC'd the order answers NotFound
   and the card's pinned-outcome render does NOT re-arm, leaving that
   corner rescan-only) or a full rescan. Sibling residual (#385): a
   chain pin whose write faults on EVERY funded pass until the leg retires
   leaves the record listed as unresolved past its truth — the overdue
   line + the card's live poll still surface the real status; display-only.
   Both parties already sat inside the display-trust boundary (the provider
   via the status API, the endpoint via every balance answer it serves).
   The Refunded-card promise ("shows up in your balance after the wallet
   next syncs") is now MECHANICAL for any post-execute absence, not only
   within 48 h.

### 4.5 Duress / decoy compatibility (Relim consumer — W5 contract)

Identity-core's duress PIN unlocks a **decoy** identity (separate seed,
separate DB — identity.md §7). The wallet must not puncture that story the
moment a coercer taps the wallet tab. Contract (mechanism Relim-side, the
SDK only has to *allow* it):

- The wallet instance is keyed to the **active identity slot**:
  `WalletSeedPort` serves the *active* identity's sub-seed, so a duress
  session derives the **decoy identity's own wallet** (its
  `relim/wallet/zip32-seed/v1` branch off the decoy seed — distinct funds,
  plausibly small/empty), never the real one.
- The real wallet's `db_dir` + sealed DB key are scoped to the real slot
  (per-slot key sealing, same shape as the messaging DBs) — a duress session
  **cannot open the real wallet DB**, cryptographically, not just by UI.
- The SDK side needs nothing special beyond what §2.3 already provides
  (host-supplied `db_dir`, host-sealed key context) — this is why `db_dir`
  is config, not convention. Named test owed at W5:
  `duress_session_cannot_open_real_wallet_db`.
- **W5-binding contracts (manager-confirmed at the W1 review):**
  - **HARD-E:** the wallet DB key seals under the **active-slot keychain
    path** (a `KEYID_WALLET_DB_KEY_PRIMARY/ALT`-class item riding
    local-storage's per-slot sealing) — the duress PIN *structurally* cannot
    reach the real wallet key's seal; the named test proves THAT binding,
    not a path convention.
  - **HARD-F:** the wallet DB enrolls in local-storage's **always-two shape
    parity** — the decoy slot carries a shape-equal wallet DB (else the mere
    existence of a wallet DB on one slot is a duress oracle); the documented
    forensic residuals are inherited honestly. Named test (W5):
    `wallet_decoy_slot_shape_matches_real`.
  - **m3:** decoy-wallet "lived-in" plausibility is the HOST's
    responsibility — the SDK imposes no must-be-empty contract on the decoy.
  - **M3 (Relim half):** Relim's panic-wipe destroying a wallet with a
    pending swap refund is **intended total loss** — the safety kit's
    purpose outranks funds; only the third-party `wipe` path gets the
    `WipeWithPendingSwap` warning (§6.3).

### 4.6 Hostile-input surfaces (every byte hostile)

| Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|
| ZIP-321 URIs (QR codes, links) | parsing REUSED from the maintained `zip321` crate (verified, v0.8.0, librustzcash monorepo — we do NOT write a URI parser); our boundary adds size-cap before parse (`PAYMENT_URI_MAX_BYTES`), network check on every address, **fuzz target** `fuzz_payment_uri` over the whole funnel. **SHIPPED (ZIP-321 chunk, 2026-06-13)**: `crates/zec-wallet-core/fuzz` (own-workspace cargo-fuzz harness, never enters `just ci`); upstream error values echo URI content and are DROPPED at the funnel (payload-free `PaymentUriInvalid`) |
| Addresses (user paste, swap provider) | parse via zcash_keys, network-checked; never truncated |
| lightwalletd gRPC responses | librustzcash's parsing (audited, trial-decrypt is constant-shape); our glue caps message sizes via tonic limits (`GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`) |
| Checkpoints / tree state (review M2) | bundled checkpoints ship **inside the signed binary** with **reproducible provenance** (committed `CHECKPOINTS.md` pins the source REPO + COMMIT + path so a reviewer regenerates byte-identical `data.rs` — §3.6). Integrity is TWO layers (as built): a load-time monotonic self-check (reorder/dup/regression) PLUS a pinned content hash (`checkpoint_data_matches_pinned_provenance_hash`) that catches a still-monotonic value tamper the self-check can't. The **live tree-state path RESOLVED (crypto audit 2026-06-14, §3.2f):** the backend does NOT self-verify a birthday frontier (it trusts lightwalletd for tree state; a recent-birthday `Conflict` cannot fire), so we **DROPPED the live path** — the birthday frontier is provisioned from the BUNDLED tree-state slice in the signed binary ONLY (W3-inc-2c-iv-c), never a live `get_tree_state`. The bundled tree-state slice is the trusted anchor; it carries its own pinned hash (`treestate_bundle_matches_pinned_provenance_hash`). The M2 live-frontier threat is ELIMINATED, not mitigated. Bundle format + the conservative-floor `estimate_birthday` are designed in §3.6. Tests: `poisoned_checkpoint_or_tree_state_does_not_silently_hide_funds` + `provision_never_provisions_from_a_live_frontier` |
| Swap provider REST/SDK responses | **named max-length bounds on every provider string** (`PROVIDER_STR_MAX_*`) + finite/in-range decimal checks BEFORE DTO entry (review m1); the echoed `refundTo` verified equal to ours (§2.6), and every other echoed request term too (`map::check_request_echo`, 2026-10-07; test `quote_refuses_an_echo_that_contradicts_the_request`); status enum closed (unknown → `Failed(ProviderProtocol)`, never a panic); **fuzz target** `fuzz_swap_status_decode` |
| Swap-record / queued-intent DB writes | parameterized statements ONLY — provider strings reach SQL as bind values, never interpolation; injection test `swap_and_intent_tables_reject_injection` (review m6) |
| Memos (inbound, decrypted) | bytes surfaced as content, length already protocol-bounded (512); text validated UTF-8-or-Arbitrary, never panics |
| Mnemonic input | BIP39 checksum validated; word-index-only errors (never the word value — identity-core precedent) |

### 4.7 Zeroization inventory + wipe

Zeroized: `SeedSource` contents · ZIP-32 seed bytes · `UnifiedSpendingKey`
wrapper · mnemonic buffers (incl. the reveal path after FRB copy-out — Dart
residue documented as sanctioned) · wallet DB key · swap JWT
(`Zeroizing<String>`, credential hygiene). `Wallet::wipe(cfg)` = crypto-shred,
**keychain-FIRST** (FR-14 §4.3a, BUILT S114 chunk 1): sever the keychain wrap
key (the §4.2a SealKey dies → seals + DB ciphertext dead), then
`remove_dir_all(db_dir)`. Per-tier honesty: a TRUE erase on Android
StrongBox/TEE; best-effort + disclosed flash-recovery residual on Apple +
software-keystore UNTIL FR-14 chunk 2 (the Secure-Enclave wrap). `wipe` never
opens the DB (crypto-correct — never unseal the key it is about to destroy), so
it does NOT enforce the `WipeWithPendingSwap` guard (a future handle-based wipe
would). **Relim integration requirement (audit A7):** Relim's panic-wipe/
kill-switch MUST cover the wallet store — `relim-wallet-host` registers the
wallet's wipe with the kill-switch sweep; the kill-switch flag is checked before
wallet unseal; the duress hung-wallet force-sever is the SDK's verb
`Wallet::sever_custody` (FR-53, stage S16, ADR-0565; bridged at ABI 7), which the
kill-switch CALLS (close bounded → `severCustody` → its own directory purge only on
`files: LeftForHost`). Named test: `panic_wipe_covers_wallet_store` exists on Relim
`main` (`app.rs:5484`) for the directory and the marker; the key sever is covered by
stage S16's `sever` rows, not by it.
