## 5. Privacy & metadata

### 5.1 What leaves the device, to whom

| Party | Sees | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| lightwalletd/Zaino endpoint | IP (unless Tor), sync cadence, block ranges fetched, broadcast txs + timing | Tor policy (§2.3); broadcast jitter (§5.3); endpoint user-overridable/self-hostable; **cannot decrypt notes** |
| Swap provider (when enabled) | per-swap metadata: assets, amounts, deposit/destination addresses, JWT identity of the *integrator*, IP unless Tor | exists ONLY if host constructs it (honest-off = zero swap traffic); per-direction disclosure DTO rendered to the user BEFORE quote acceptance (§2.6) |
| Zcash chain (public) | shielded: nothing beyond inclusion; transparent legs: amounts/addresses | shielded-first UX; transparent recipient + memo = construction error; de-shielding surfaced via disclosure DTO |
| Relim relays | **nothing** — wallet traffic never touches messaging transports | structural: SDK has no relim dep (A1) |

### 5.2 Traffic patterns

- **Honest-off (vision invariant):** wallet feature off / `sync.stop()` /
  `TorPolicy::Required` without Tor ⇒ **zero packets**. No keepalive, no
  presence-style background beacon. Named test: `wallet_off_emits_zero_traffic`.
- Sync is **foreground/stream-driven** + host-scheduled background windows
  (§9) — never a busy poll.
- Swap status polling exists only while a swap is in flight (§7).
- **`GetSubtreeRootsArg.start_index` (S15-F1, ADR-0569) — why the endpoint may
  see it.** In steady state the start is `floor64(count − 1)`: the last stored
  subtree root, the same for every synced wallet on the same chain. The terms
  that can lower it (the reorg window, a scan-refuted bracket, a newly scanned
  completing block) reveal roughly how far this wallet has scanned — which the
  `GetBlockRange` requests on the same channel already reveal more precisely —
  and rounding DOWN to a multiple of 64 hides the fine signal. Every session's
  first pass is a full fetch (`start_index = 0`), so the value cannot link two
  sessions. `max_entries` stays 0. A non-zero `start_index` does distinguish this
  client from the reference clients (upstream's `sync::run` and the wallets built
  on it always send 0): an endpoint can tell an SDK wallet from them by it — a
  client fingerprint, accepted for the saving (S15-F1 §5).

### 5.3 Broadcast timing

`BROADCAST_JITTER_DEFAULT = 0..=10s` uniform delay before tx broadcast —
decorrelates the user's send action from the endpoint-observable broadcast
(research note "randomized broadcast timing"; same rationale as the
cross-channel randomized delays, sec H1). Host-tunable; `JitterPolicy::None`
allowed (third-party choice), surfaced honestly in docs.

**CORRECTED 2026-10-06 (the 2026-10-05 review, F01; plan
`docs/plan/audit-2026-10-05-fixes.md` §2).** The window is bounded:
`BROADCAST_JITTER_MAX_MS_CEILING` (30 s). `create`, `create_watch_only` and
`open` refuse a larger `Uniform { max_ms }` with `BroadcastJitterTooLong`
(RW-CFG-005); it was unbounded (the bridge takes a `u32`, ~49 days). A
deadline-tagged swap-deposit group draws from at most the 10 s default
whatever the policy (`group_jitter`), and the jitter sleeps on `tokio::time`,
which does not advance while the device is suspended — so every deposit leg is
re-gated on the wall clock AFTER its jitter (the deferred-broadcast rules'
correction below).

### 5.4 Logging (NEVER-log list)

Never: addresses, amounts, memo bytes/text, txids, mnemonic/seed/keys, swap
JWT, deposit addresses, ZIP-321 URI contents, endpoint Basic-auth userinfo.
Allowed: heights, counts, durations, error codes, span outcomes. Tracing
spans: `wallet.sync {from, to, blocks, outcome}` · `wallet.send
{txs: count, accepted: count, rejected: count, outcome}` (AS BUILT inc-2d-3-a, `rejected`
+ the `outcome="rejected"` arm added at #307/S144 — counts only; the
broadcast path knows tx-counts, not the propose-time recipient list) · `wallet.swap
{direction, provider, outcome}` · `wallet.swap_quote {direction, provider, outcome}`
(IZ-1 — the destination-mint at quote time) · `wallet.swap_tokens {count, outcome}`
(IZ-2 — the `/v0/tokens` fetch; coarse count + outcome code, never a token symbol/price)
· `wallet.swap_destination_recovered {count}` (IZ-1 §3.3b L2 — crash-recovery instability
event) · `wallet.utxo_scan` gains a `set_size` count (L5)
· `wallet.incoming_detect {span_from, span_to, count, outcome}` (ADR-0536 #392 —
the scan-edge incoming-funds detect; heights + counts + outcome only, exactly the
`IncomingFundsEvent` payload discipline) — field set is the allowlist; `#[instrument(skip_all)]`
on every secret-touching fn (identity-core precedent). No PII in logs —
this is also the brief §4 standing constraint.

**Heights are loggable — DECIDED (founder, 2026-06-15), closing the S21
docs consistency MAJOR.** The open question was whether an absolute scan/
birthday height is wallet-age metadata that correlates to wallet creation time
and should be reclassified as sensitive (log deltas only). Decision: **keep
heights loggable** as low-sensitivity progress data — a bare height with no
address/amount is weak metadata, and absolute heights ease "stuck at height X"
diagnosis. The capture-layer guard
(`tracing_spans_carry_no_address_amount_or_memo`) therefore enforces the
allowlist over the NEVER-log items, NOT over heights. Span granularity: the
d-3 `SyncController` emits the pass-level `wallet.sync {batches, reorgs,
outcome, backoff_secs}` (counts/durations/codes) + the `wallet.reorg_rewind
{depth}` instability event; the per-range `wallet.sync {from, to, blocks,
outcome}` span (absolute heights) lands inside the engine pass (iv-d-3-b),
where the precise range is known. The guard is **span-aware** (it inspects
span fields, not just events), ready for that height-bearing span. (A future
watch-only/UFVK-export feature could revisit height sensitivity, but that is a
new spec + review cycle, never a flag here.)

**The device log is a SHIPPED, HOST-SWITCHED surface (S288; founder rulings
2026-09-19 — "sdk definitely should include logging layer so you will be able to
debug connectivity first on the android. and then on iphone"; then, on reading
the first cut as an always-on layer: "it shouldnt be always on … configurabale
… depends on the host settings visible to user"; then the levels: "'Off' /
'Errors only' / 'Detailed logging'").** Until S288 the only log sink was a
debug/measurement-build logcat layer, so every build a tester runs was silent
and a connectivity report from a phone was unfalsifiable. `init_app` now
installs a device-log layer in every build, **OFF**
(`sdk/zec_wallet/rust/src/device_log.rs`; Android first, then Apple — both sinks built S288),
and the HOST switches it (FR-35):

- **THE PREMISE OF THIS SECTION CHANGED, and every allowlist entry was written
  under the old one.** The allowlist's per-field reviews asked "is this
  §5.4-loggable" while no shipped build had a sink. A shipped sink changes the
  question to "may a holder of this phone read it" — and the answer this spec
  gives is: **only while the host's user has chosen to keep a log.** The SDK
  never decides on its own to write to a device log; a host that says nothing
  gets nothing (exactly the pre-S288 behaviour). **"The user has chosen"
  (amended S5, founder Q2):** a host may pick a non-Off default as its own
  named choice, shown where the user can change it. The example app's
  Errors-only default outside debug is that named choice. It is not a change
  to the SDK's default, which stays `Off`. That switch is what makes the
  transport-POSTURE lines below acceptable — that a private transport is in
  use, how ready it reports itself, which arm carried a dial. They say nothing
  about WHICH transport (the S287 ruling stands: never the name, never the
  grade), but posture is still posture, and without the switch those fields
  would have to leave the log. Two other entries deserve the same second read
  and are recorded rather than argued away: `wallet.incoming_detect {span_from,
  span_to, count}` (the mined-height span of THIS wallet's incoming notes) and
  `wallet.swap {provider, direction}` (which third-party service was used).
  Both stay — heights are loggable by the 2026-06-15 decision and the provider
  label is a constant — on the same condition: a consented, switchable log.
- **The switch.** `set_device_log(DeviceLogLevel) -> DeviceLogLevel` and
  `device_log_level()`, both sync. `Off` (the default) · `Errors` = WARN and
  above — something went wrong and the wallet carried on · `Detailed` = INFO
  and above. There is no level above `Detailed`: a setting a host could raise
  is a second road to DEBUG on a user's phone, and the measurement build is the
  developer's door for that. Live, no re-init (the gate is read per event —
  NOT by the filter, whose answer `tracing` caches per callsite). Which level
  is the DEFAULT in a debug build, in production, or for a user is the HOST's
  decision. The return is the EFFECTIVE level: `Off` where nothing can write
  (a platform with no sink yet; a process whose `tracing` default another
  library owns), so a settings row renders what is true.
- **Scope.** This SDK's own events only — targets `zec_wallet_core…`,
  `wallet.…` and the bridge's `zec_wallet`, matched on a `::` boundary so a
  sibling crate cannot inherit the log by borrowing the prefix — at INFO and
  above, EVENTS only (no span lines, no span context; the per-batch sync
  timings ride a span and are NOT in this log). A dependency's events are
  refused at the callsite: those crates log addresses and txids.
- **The allowlist is enforced AT RUNTIME, per field.** The layer puts every
  field to the same predicate the capture guard asserts through
  (`zec_wallet_core::log_policy::field_is_loggable`); a name outside the
  allowlist, or a name/value carrying a never-log token, is WITHHELD and the
  line says so (`withheld=<n>`, written BEFORE the fields so the line cap
  cannot erase it). This is what replaces the build-profile gate:
  the capture guard grades the paths a test drives, the runtime layer grades
  every path that runs on a device, and
  `every_info_and_above_field_name_in_the_sdk_is_allowlisted` grades every
  INFO-and-above site in the source — its field names AND its message literal,
  which must be static (no interpolation) and printable as written (the closed
  `SANCTIONED_MESSAGES` vocabulary covers the six event names whose wording
  collides with a never-log token). The value scan keeps the limit stated
  above — a token scan cannot see a neutrally-rendered secret under an
  allowlisted name; the NAME gate is the defence there, and the one structured
  `Debug` value on an INFO line (`verdict`) has its render vocabulary pinned.
  A written line is printable ASCII only and capped at 512 bytes.
- **`wallet.dial {dial_arm, dial_class, outcome}`** — one line per physical
  dial, from the dialer that performed it: `host` (the host's transport) or
  `sdk_direct` (the SDK's direct dialer — `TorPolicy::Off`, or the `Preferred`
  fallback; S302: the values were `private` / `clearnet`, and `private` was
  false for a host whose own transport goes direct — the arm says WHO dialled,
  never how private it was, and the exposure grade stays off the line under
  S287's rule), the circuit family (`sync`/`broadcast`/`other` — S290: and
  `swap`), and `connected` or the typed `DialError` variant name. Never a host, a port, the isolation
  key or the host's transport name. It is the observation that a dial rode the
  host's transport; before it that was an inference about the program. **Its
  LEVEL is part of the contract:** `unreachable` / `timeout` / `unsupported` /
  `io` (S290: and `transport_failed`, a host's own FAILED declaration) are WARN
  — what "errors only" exists to show — while `connected`,
  `not_ready` (a bootstrap in progress) and `retired` (a carrier switch) are
  normal states and INFO. The fall-back event, `wallet.private_path_fell_back`
  (WARN; it was `wallet.tor_fell_back` until S288 — the host names its
  transport and it may not be Tor), is the one line that says traffic left the
  private path, and it survives "errors only".
- **The measurement build is unchanged** and still the only artifact that
  carries the DEBUG + span-close fmt layer and the `+devtiming` mark.
- **Two sinks, in the founder's order.** ANDROID: logcat, tags `zec_wallet_core`
  and `zec_wallet` — `adb logcat -s zec_wallet_core:V zec_wallet:V`. APPLE (iOS
  and macOS): the unified log, subsystem `zec_wallet` with those two as
  categories — `log stream --level info --predicate 'subsystem ==
  "zec_wallet"'`, or Console.app with the device attached — through the pinned
  `oslog` shim (`=0.2.0`, read in full; `"%{public}s"`, which is safe only
  because every field has already been put to the allowlist). **INFO is filed
  as `os_log`'s `default` type and WARN/ERROR as `error`, not as `info`:**
  `info` is kept in memory only and is gone by the time a tester's phone is
  plugged in, which is the only moment this log is read — so the level is
  written INTO the line (`WARN wallet.dial …`), two levels sharing one type.
  The cost, stated because the host's user is owed it: **on Apple a written
  line stays readable on disk for days** (founder 2026-09-19, shown exactly
  this: diagnosability over trace, the host's screen says so where the level
  is chosen). `just wallet-device-log-apple-witness` writes a line through the
  real layer and sink and reads it back from the PERSISTED store. LINUX and
  WINDOWS (S5 `stderr`, FR-42): the process's stderr, one `write_all` per
  line, as `<LEVEL> <tag> <line>`, and the verb answers the level asked. A
  failed write is dropped. A BLOCKED one is not: a host whose piped stderr
  stops draining makes a logging SDK thread wait, as a stalled logd does on
  Android. The Windows arm has not yet been compiled on Windows.
- **The host stream (S5 `sink`, FR-35's deferred half; plan
  `docs/plan/stage-5-the-device-log-a-user-can-send.md` §3.1).**
  `watch_device_log` (Dart `watchDeviceLog()` → `Stream<DeviceLogLine { seq,
  severity, tag, text }>`) hands the host the SAME finished line the platform
  sink gets, from the same `on_event` call and after the same gate check. So
  the switch, the ceiling, the allowlist with `withheld=<n>`, printable ASCII,
  the 512-byte cap and SDK-targets-only hold for the host by construction,
  with no second copy of the rules. Nothing else crosses: no span, no
  dependency's event, nothing below INFO, no timestamp.
  - **What the host may receive:** only that line, plus a severity, one of the
    two tags and a sequence number, none of which describes the wallet. What
    stays loggable and what never crosses are this section's lists above,
    unchanged. A wider audience for the same lines changes which READERS see
    them, not which VALUES reach them.
  - **`text` and `tag` are control-safe, not delimiter-safe.** No control
    character can reach them, so they cannot forge a line. They can hold
    `"`, `\`, `,`, `|` and `=`, and a host that serialises them into JSON or
    CSV escapes them itself.
  - **One subscriber per process**, replaced on re-register. The host arm
    sends at most `HOST_LINES_PER_MINUTE` = 60 lines a minute (a token bucket
    with a burst of 60); a line over budget still reaches the platform sink
    and leaves a gap in `seq`.
  - **The duress seam.** Every `wipe`, `wipe_force` or `sever_custody` call
    through the bridge (`convert::wipe_wallet`, `convert::sever_custody`), a
    refused one included, first stores `Off` into the gate and then, under
    the host arm's lock, drops the host's stream (which closes it) and restarts `seq` at 0.
    Every host send happens under that lock after a check of the gate and of
    the stream. So after the quiesce returns, NO line is enqueued on the host
    stream. Nothing re-opens the log but the host's own `set_device_log` and
    `watch_device_log`, and a host must not re-arm on its duress path.
  - **WHAT THE USER LOSES** (a deviation Relim accepted, relim-18): if device
    logging was on (Detailed, or the example's Errors-only release default
    for error lines), one wallet line
    written just before a panic wipe may remain in the phone's system log.
    It is at most one line per event already past the gate on another thread
    at that instant. This happens ONLY when the host has turned the log on:
    the SDK installs `Off`, and a host that says nothing gets nothing. It is
    the platform arms' residual. The host stream has none. The bound is left
    inexact on purpose: making it exact would make the sever wait on a
    platform write.
- **`wallet.sever`** (FR-53, stage S16 §3.1 "Log") — INFO, FIELD-FREE, emitted
  by `Wallet::sever_custody` BEFORE the sever begins; the outcome is the
  `SeverReport`'s, never a log's. **Nothing is logged once a sever starts:**
  the verb's blocking body runs with no subscriber on its thread
  (`sever_silenced`), and the bridge door runs
  `device_log::quiesce_for_sever()` FIRST, before the `dbDir` gate — so
  through the bridge even `wallet.sever` finds the gate `Off` and never
  reaches the device log; only a direct Rust caller with its own subscriber
  sees it. The exact exceptions (a line raised on the key-store worker
  thread, a poisoned instance's own later lines on other threads) are stated
  once, on `sever_silenced`. There is NO `wallet.broadcast_refused` event
  (withdrawn at the S16 fold).

**Standing privacy invariant (review HARD-D — re-cast at #397/ADR-0538,
which WAS the promised spec + review cycle): the UFVK never leaves the
device SILENTLY.** Viewing-key egress is total-history surveillance, so it
exists at exactly ONE sanctioned, deliberately-gated surface —
`export_ufvk` (§3.7 D1, backup-phrase-bar gating) — and NOWHERE else: no
log/span/error/DTO/stream ever carries a UFVK or any prefix of one (the
forbidden-token guard is unchanged), and any NEW egress surface is again a
new spec + review cycle, never a flag.

**Instability events MUST be observable** (gate 5 — a recovery that happens
silently is a debugging black hole): `wallet.resubmit {tx_count, accepted, rejected,
stranded, blocked, outcome}` (all per-pass COUNTS — `accepted`/`rejected` split `tx_count`
[S125], `stranded` [S124] / `blocked` [S127, a parked queued TEX] ride their own field so a
broadcast-led `outcome` can't shadow a money-serious terminal) ·
`wallet.auto_shield {outcome}` · `wallet.tor_bootstrap {percent}` ·
`wallet.reorg_rewind {depth}` · `wallet.cache_sanitized {dropped}` ·
`wallet.provisioning_repair` · `wallet.keystore_inconsistent` ·
`wallet.private_path_fell_back` · `swap.poll {outcome}` / `swap.kill {severity}`.
Every §6.3 recovery path emits its event — the field sets stay inside the
allowlist above.

---

## 6. Error handling & degradation

### 6.1 Error taxonomy

`WalletError` / `SwapError`: `thiserror` enums, stable **codes** across the
bridge (catch by TYPE, never string-match — known gotcha). Every variant
logged; none silent. The SDK ships **no user-facing strings** — codes +
typed data; the host renders (i18n gate satisfied structurally).

| Case | Recoverable? | Surfaced as |
|---|---|---|
| invalid mnemonic | yes | `InvalidMnemonic { word_index }` (index only, never the word) |
| open() on missing/foreign-network DB | yes | `NotFound` / `NetworkMismatch` |
| create()/restore() on an already-completed wallet | yes | `WalletAlreadyExists` (§6.3 "never clobbers" — the typed non-clobber; the host opens it instead, never a silent open/destroy) |
| open() hits a Rust-side migration needing the seed | yes | `SeedRequired` — caller re-supplies via `SeedSource` (§4.2; the upstream-proven try-without-seed contract) |
| **create()/restore() faults during the migration chain at FIRST OPEN** | yes | **CLASSIFIED, not blanket corruption (T0-7, §4aa, 2026-09-11).** `init_wallet_db` runs the whole chain from an empty file on create AND on restore — 0.22.0 added 19 migrations, one building a UNIQUE index — and every non-seed failure of it used to fold to `StoreCorrupt`, i.e. the RED "restore from your recovery phrase" told to a user whose wallet was never written. The migrator error is now unwrapped to its `WalletMigrationError` (through `source()`, the same door the `SeedRequired` arm already used) and a `DbError` is routed through the #371 SSOT `classify_sqlite_error`: `SQLITE_FULL` → `DiskFull` ("free space and retry"), `SQLITE_BUSY` → the transient `StoreBusy`, `SQLITE_IOERR` → `Io`. Only a fault that IS the wallet being wrong (`CorruptedData`, `CommitmentTree`, `CannotRevert`, …) keeps `StoreCorrupt`, and nothing is ever auto-wiped. The comment that used to call this a structural blocker — "the schemerz migrator wraps the rusqlite error, so the underlying code is not reachable" — was false. **Host:** `classifyOnboardingFailure` already mapped `DiskFull` → `storageFull`; `StoreBusy` now joins `WalletAlreadyOpen` on the retryable `alreadyOpen` kind ("another instance holds this wallet — close it, then retry"), where it used to fall through to `unknown`. No new string. **Measured residual:** a held lock at first open was ALREADY `StoreBusy` before this change, because `ensure_aux_tables` runs on the same connection first and classifies through `map_aux_err` — §4aa's Q2 assumed otherwise and was wrong. What this closes for the lock case is the window between the two calls |
| one tx of a multi-tx send fails midway | yes | per-tx `TxSubmitResult` incl. `NotAttempted` (§2.5); created txs persist, resubmission machinery retries unexpired unmined txs during sync (§1.7) |
| insufficient spendable (incl. unconfirmed-pending case) | yes | `InsufficientFunds { available, required, pending_incoming }` (`RW-SEND-001`) — host can render "wait for confirmations" honestly; `pending_incoming` from the SAME spendable-policy SSOT as the balance |
| `propose()` of a donation-form leg (no amount) | yes | `SendAmountRequired` (`RW-SEND-002`) — valid to DISPLAY (`zcash:ADDR`), not to send; host fills the amount in (§2.4) |
| a prepared `SendProposal` re-`send`/`consume`d (double-tap) | yes | `ProposalAlreadyUsed` (`RW-SEND-003`) — the opaque one-shot token was taken; the notes are never broadcast twice (§6.3 double-spend guard's propose seam) |
| a `SendProposal` past its TTL / un-anchorable wallet | yes | `ProposalStale` (`RW-SEND-004`) — re-`propose()` for a fresh fee; also the fold for upstream `ScanRequired` (not synced far enough) |
| `propose()` fault with no finer mapping that is DETERMINISTIC on the input (change/selection/structural, incl. a >1-step pool-crossing this build can't do) | partial | `ProposeFailed` (`RW-SEND-005`) — payload-free, fail-closed (the selector message can echo amounts — §5.4 — so it is DROPPED); a DB fault is the existing `StoreCorrupt`; the host copy is "check the details" — retrying unchanged re-fails |
| `propose()` refused by a condition the wallet's OWN state clears — a note whose witness the scan has not completed (`CommitmentTree`), an anchor not yet recorded (`Proposal(AnchorNotFound)`), an input a concurrent proposal holds (`Proposal(InputsLocked)`) — INC-018 (b), phase-2 P2-2 | **built, EMPTY at this pin** | `ProposeTransient` (`RW-SEND-008`) — payload-free like its sibling; classified FROM THE ENUM in `send::propose_refusal_is_transient` (the wildcard is NOT transient); the host copy is "Couldn't prepare this payment just now. Try again in a moment." (Send) / "Couldn't prepare the shield just now. Try again in a moment." (Shield) — never "check the details". **Reach (the Batch C security pass, confirmed at `zcash_client_backend` 0.24.0):** none of the three shapes is constructed on the propose path with `lock_inputs: None` — they are create-path and lock-path constructions — so the class is mirrored and guarded end to end but empty in production until INC-018 (a)'s `code` field names the S257 variant; INC-018 stays OWED on (b). The same two upstream shapes on the create+sign path fold to `ProposalStale` (the row below) |
| `send()` create+sign fault — proving/build failure, a structural proposal fault, or the USK's UFVK not the account's (impossible on the seed-derived path; defense-in-depth LOUD catch otherwise) | partial | `SignFailed` (`RW-SEND-006`) — payload-free, fail-closed (the builder message can echo amounts + a txid — §5.4 — DROPPED); ONLY a reorg-pruned anchor (`AnchorNotFound`) or witness (`CommitmentTree`) folds to `ProposalStale` (re-propose), a DB fault to `StoreCorrupt` |
| memo to transparent recipient | yes | `MemoRequiresShieldedRecipient` (construction-time, honest-degradation UI per ADR-0005 r3) |
| a payment leg given BOTH a text memo and machine bytes (FR-28) | yes (fix the caller) | `MemoConflict` (`RW-PAY-011`) — **a CALLER bug, and deliberately NOT `MemoInvalid`.** Neither memo is individually invalid, so folding it into RW-PAY-006 made a host programming error surface to the END USER as *"That memo can't be sent. Remove it and try again."* — wrong for both audiences, and it made one code mean two unrelated things. The reference UI renders *"Couldn't send this payment — the app attached two notes to it. Nothing was sent."*: it names no user action, because there is none |
| `machineMemos(txidHex)` given a txid that is not 64 lowercase-or-uppercase hex characters | yes | `TxidInvalid` (`RW-PAY-009`) — payload-free (txids are §5.4 never-log; the offending string is never echoed). The host passes back the `txidHex` a history row gave it, verbatim |
| `machineMemos` with NO prefix registered, or a `machineMemoPrefixes` entry that is empty / over-long / one too many | yes | `MachineMemoScopeInvalid { reason }` (`RW-PAY-010`) — one class, two moments: the config door refuses a scope that cannot be used, the verb refuses to serve an unconfigured one. **Never an empty list**: a silent `[]` would read as "this transaction carries nothing" over a memo that is there, and an EMPTY prefix would match everything (FR-27's acceptance fails a build that returns everything as surely as one that returns nothing). `reason` is a `&'static str`, no host input echoed |
| endpoint unreachable / TLS / gRPC fault | yes | `SyncStatus::Stalled { EndpointUnreachable }`; sends → queue offered |
| `TorPolicy::Required`, Tor down | yes | `Stalled { TorUnavailable }` — **fail-closed, zero clearnet packets** |
| `TorPolicy::Preferred` fallback | yes | `TorFellBack` event — degradation is VISIBLE, not silent |
| queued tx expired before broadcast (chain moved > expiry) | yes | re-propose from stored intent (§6.2); if funds no longer cover it → `QueuedSendStale` (`RW-BCAST-001`) surfaced, never silently dropped (raised on the inc-2d-3-b-ii-B `prepare_queued` re-propose: InsufficientFunds → `Prepared::Stale`, the intent LEFT Queued — ✅ BUILT S70) |
| `queue_send()` with the durable queue already at `QUEUED_SEND_INTENTS_MAX` | yes | `QueuedSendsFull` (`RW-BCAST-002`) — a defensive bound checked atomically at the enqueue door (inc-2d-3-b-ii-A); let the pending queue drain (sync/resubmit) before queueing more, never a silent drop |
| broadcast accepted then expired unmined | yes | `TxStatus::Expired`; funds **return to spendable** after expiry height — test-covered |
| swap quote expired pre-deposit | yes | `QuoteExpired` — deposit never sent |
| swap refunded | n/a | `SwapStatus::Refunded` — a NAMED state with its own UX row, not an error (ADR-0014) |
| swap provider down / protocol drift | yes | `ProviderUnavailable` / `Failed(ProviderProtocol)`; wallet core unaffected (port isolation) |
| wallet DB key unsealing fails / keychain locked | yes (retry) | `KeystoreUnavailable` — same posture as identity-core "unlock your device" |
| keychain item missing but wallet DB present (sealed mode) | yes | `KeystoreInconsistent` — surfaced, never a silent fresh wallet (§4.2; upstream keysMissing lesson) |
| swap under-deposited | yes | `SwapStatus::UnderDeposited` — top-up by deadline or provider refunds (§2.6) |
| disk full (scan cache or DB write) | yes | `DiskFull` / `Stalled { StorageFull }` — **distinct from `StoreCorrupt`** (SQLITE_FULL is "free space and retry," not corruption). The INTERACTIVE seams (send/shield/move/rescan) surface it and STOP so the user frees space (no auto-retry into a deterministic re-fail); the BACKGROUND sync loop keeps retrying but on the CAPPED backoff ladder (`SYNC_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS`, never a hot spin — one doomed pass per cap-interval), surfacing `Stalled { StorageFull }` honestly meanwhile (a dedicated park-until-freed for the sync loop is a possible future enhancement; the cap bounds the cost today). Honored at EVERY store seam, not just the disposable cache: a mid-scan `SQLITE_FULL` writing OUR wallet DB inside `scan_cached_blocks` is classified `DiskFull` at the engine seam (**#371** — `sync::map_scan_err` PROBES the `SqliteClientError` via `ClassifyStoreFault` instead of folding every wallet-DB fault to `StoreCorrupt`), matching the cache side so one condition never tells two stories (the S186 review's contradictory-story MED). The probe unwraps BOTH the direct `DbError` door AND the commitment-tree **shard-write door** (`CommitmentTree(ShardTreeError::Storage(commitment_tree::Error::Query/Serialization))`) — the shard BLOBs are among the largest per-batch writes, so an out-of-disk scan faults there MOST often; the reliability review caught that leaving the shard door on the blanket `StoreCorrupt` would have defeated the fix on its likeliest real path. A tree-LOGIC `ShardTreeError::Query` fault stays `StoreCorrupt` (local inconsistency, not a disk/IO condition); **`Insert` does NOT, since BIND-1 (S269, §4x)** — a served root the tree refuses is the ENDPOINT's, and the scan door now says so through the same body the ingest door always used (`sync::map_shardtree_err`, one classifier, one grep; this sentence used to name both variants and was the drift). The SAME classification is applied at the sibling write seams via the shared `ClassifyStoreFault` / `classify_sqlite_error`: `sync::map_shardtree_err`'s `Storage` arm (the pre-scan `put_subtree_roots` root write) and `send::map_create_err`'s `DataSource` arm (the create-persist on the send path — a `DiskFull` there routes the send UI to "free up space", not a terminal fault; the create is transactional so retry-after-freeing is safe). **`Insert` is NARROWED and not blanket, since BIND-1-R (S269, §4x-R R9):** `Conflict` and `InputMalformed` — the two variants `shardtree`'s `merge_checked` raises, i.e. the walk that compares the node this wallet holds against the node the serve (or the served frontier) implies — are the endpoint's; `OutOfRange` / `NotContained` / `TreeFull` / `CheckpointOutOfOrder` / `MarkedRetentionInvalid` are address, capacity and retention arithmetic over numbers only this SDK and upstream choose, are unreachable through either door at the `shardtree = "=0.7.1"` pin, and keep the fail-closed local `StoreCorrupt` — the arm in `sync::map_shardtree_err` carries the variant-by-variant reachability argument, which is what §4x-run owed row 4 was re-scoped to. (Residual, WITHDRAWN S269: the reorg-rewind `truncate_to_height` no longer folds to `StoreCorrupt`. Its `TruncateCommitmentTree` variant joined the same three-variant arm at BIND-1 and runs the one `map_shardtree_err` body like the other two, so a full disk during a rewind is `DiskFull` here as well. The sentence that claimed otherwise stood one line from the edit that made it false.) A `SQLITE_BUSY` there is the transient `StoreBusy` (a scan-batch commit lost a WAL writer race — the same class `db::map_aux_err` already types), never corruption. A `SQLITE_IOERR` — iOS Data Protection can surface a device-locked OR an ENOSPC-masked fault as IOERR rather than FULL — is the generic `Io`: honest that an IO fault occurred, WITHOUT `StoreCorrupt`'s false "restore your recovery phrase" scare or `DiskFull`'s possibly-wrong "free space" instruction; surfaced, non-destructive, never auto-wiped. Both the engine seam (`ClassifyStoreFault`) and the aux seam (`map_aux_err`) share this FULL→`DiskFull` / BUSY→`StoreBusy` / IOERR→`Io` classification (DRY). A `SqliteClientError::Io` (and a shard `Serialization`) is NOT file I/O: at the `zcash_client_sqlite` 0.22.0 pin every one is a DECODE of bytes SQLite already returned (`parse_tx`, `read_shard`), so since R12 it is `StorageFull`→`DiskFull` and every other kind `StoreCorrupt` (`sync::engine_io_fault`; it used to go through `WalletError::from_io` to the transient `Io`, which since R10 said "retrying" forever over a damaged row — R12's security review). Everything else stays the fail-closed `StoreCorrupt` default. **R12 (S314):** every engine and `rusqlite` error site in the core now goes through these classifiers (`docs/plan/r12-a-busy-store-is-not-a-corrupt-one.md`; the guard `tests/no_blind_store_corrupt.rs` fails the build on a new blind mapping), and `SQLITE_LOCKED` joins BUSY as `StoreBusy`. |
| DB corruption | no | `StoreCorrupt` — fail-closed, surfaced; never auto-wipe |

### 6.2 Offline-first (queued is a normal state)

`queue_send` persists the **intent** (`PaymentRequest`), not a signed tx —
proposing/signing at broadcast time avoids stale anchors and burned expiry
windows (the worst-case walk: compose on a plane, land 6h later, chain moved
~290 blocks — a compose-time signature would be long-expired; the intent
re-proposes cleanly). `TxStatus::Queued` is a first-class history state.
Zero-connectivity behavior: everything except sync/send/swap works — open,
balances (last-synced, **age surfaced** via `SyncStatus`), history,
addresses, ZIP-321 generation.

**Retry posture (§1.7 lesson, adopted):** while started, the sync loop
**never self-terminates** — transient faults retry with exponential backoff
capped at `SYNC_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS`, surfacing `Stalled` honestly meanwhile; a
stuck run is force-restarted after `SYNC_STUCK_WATCHDOG_SECS` (upstream
shipped retry-capped sync, harvested "manually restart it" bug reports, and
reversed). Only `stop()` stops it.

### 6.3 Crash-safety — the process-kill contract (every flow, every window)

Mobile OSes kill processes routinely (memory pressure, background limits) —
a mid-operation kill is **normal operation, not an edge case**. Ground rule
that bounds the analysis: **the chain is the source of truth; the wallet DB
is a cache of it.** Any signed transaction that escaped the process is
rediscovered by scan (it spends our notes), so no kill window can lose
FUNDS — kill windows lose local *bookkeeping*, and every window below states
its bookkeeping recovery:

| Flow | Kill / cut window | Recovery contract |
|---|---|---|
| create / restore | any point during provisioning | **Two-phase provisioning (AS BUILT W3-inc-2b-i — `store.rs`):** seal seed + DB key + init DB, then write a completion marker LAST (`create_new` CAS — never clobbers; a `create`/`restore` against a completed wallet is typed `WalletAlreadyExists`, never a silent open/clobber). The MANIFEST (written durably AFTER the seal artifacts) is the remnant checkpoint; `open()` on a marker-less remnant ⇒ typed `ProvisioningIncomplete`. **One SealKey, two blobs, no split-brain:** the seed seal AND the DB-key seal are produced together under a single custodied wrap key (`SealedSeedVault::store_wallet`) and persisted together — there is no durable state in which the seed is sealed but the DB key is not, so the seed-vs-DB split-brain is eliminated BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a resume step (the money-lens pin). **Repair resumes FROM the remnant, never re-derives:** the supplied `SeedSource` is verified against the SEALED seed (CONSTANT-TIME via `subtle`; mismatch ⇒ typed `SeedMismatch` — the mistyped-mnemonic re-run); `Generate`-mode repair resumes from the already-sealed seed, NEVER regenerates (a regen against a sealed remnant would split-brain seed-vs-DB); keystore locked during repair ⇒ `KeystoreUnavailable`, not `ProvisioningIncomplete`. **Create-vs-open guard** (the truncation/0-byte hazard, `db.rs`): open-existing uses `OpenFlags` WITHOUT `SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE` (missing ⇒ `NotFound`); a `wallet_provisioning` sentinel row in the encrypted DB catches a marker-present-but-truncated DB (which SQLite would open as a fresh empty DB) ⇒ typed `StoreCorrupt`, never a silent fresh wallet. **The zcash_client_sqlite `WalletDb::from_connection` + `init_wallet_db` migrator now FILLS the `db.rs` provision seam (AS BUILT W3-inc-2b-ii-A):** `provision_db` runs it (`seed = None`, idempotent — `repair` re-runs it on crash recovery; the sentinel is orthogonal to schemerz's own `schemer_migrations`/`user_version`). **The async `Wallet` handle now drives provision/open over `spawn_blocking` (AS BUILT W3-inc-2b-ii-B — `wallet.rs`):** it holds the exclusive `WalletLock` for the handle's life via a `&WalletLock` **witness** the store entry points require (operating without the lock is not expressible), `open` migrates-up idempotently (`db::open_db_migrated`), `close` drops the SQLCipher connection on the blocking pool with the DB closing BEFORE the lock releases (no half-closed-DB-under-freed-lock window) |
| send | between tx creation and broadcast | created txs are persisted before submit (§1.7) → the resubmission machinery re-submits unexpired unmined txs on next sync; broadcast-but-unrecorded → rediscovered by scan |
| queued send | between intent consumption and tx creation | **the double-send guard: an intent can never mint two txs, a tx can never orphan its intent.** ⚠️ REVISED at inc-2d-3-b-ii (S68 — a discovered upstream constraint): the original "ONE DB transaction" mechanism is NOT achievable with the pinned `zcash_client_sqlite =0.21.0` (no connection accessor, private `SqlTransaction`; Rule Zero forbids forking), so the guard uses the engine's OWN atomic note-spend state as the idempotency witness — the intent records its selected-note CLAIM (the chain-stable `(txid, protocol, output_index)` triples) before tx creation, and recovery reconciles by the witness `InputSource::get_spendable_note(…).is_none()` ⟺ those notes are spent by a still-LIVE (unexpired) tx ⟺ the tx was created (don't re-propose); spendable ⟺ never-created or EXPIRED (the ~40-block expiry frees a never-broadcast tx's notes — the upstream-enforced safety net) ⟺ safe to re-propose. The witness `target` is the honest tip+1 (NEVER inflated — a too-high target would read a live tx as expired and double-spend). The re-broadcast txid comes from our own recorded column, not the witness. The guard FOUNDATION (schema + claim codec + witness + reconcile + cap + errors) shipped at inc-2d-3-b-ii-A (S69, upstream-verified, NO BLOCKER); the resubmission HOOK that drives it from the sync loop (the `after_synced` post-clean-pass bridge → `reconcile_inflight` PHASE 1 + `prepare_queued` PHASE 2 → `broadcast_one`, with delete-on-mined gated on `get_tx_height`) shipped at inc-2d-3-b-ii-B (S70, harness-proven, NO BLOCKER) |
| auto-shield (swap-in delivery AND OutOfZec refund delivery) | after delivery detection, before the shield tx; or the shield tx itself fails (keystore locked, endpoint down) | shield intent **keyed by the delivering txid** — at-most-once per delivery AND retried on subsequent syncs until shielded (at-least-once eventually); every attempt emits `wallet.auto_shield {outcome}`; meanwhile the unshielded amount is RENDERABLE (`BalanceSnapshot.transparent`) — never an invisible privacy state. **✅ DISCHARGED for the OutOfZec REFUND half (#368; was ⚠️ DEFERRED per ADR-0527, surfaced W-swap-3-a re-review):** refunds now ride the SAME §3.3b D2 SCOPED active-swap poll as IntoZec deliveries — the refund address is engine-persisted at quote (`get_address_for_index`, cross-checked byte-equal to the raw BIP44 derivation), armed into the `swap_destination` watch at execute (atomically with the W-swap-5 home row; settlement window), re-armed when a `Refunded` terminal is pinned AND on every refresh pass while the swap record is unresolved (#382 — §4.4 item 8, so the watch survives any app-absence length; a chain-observed refund pins `Refunded` first-wins), and every PRE-#368 allocated index is backfill-registered + one-window swept behind a durable high-water marker (the ADR-0527 migration obligation, reset across `rescan_from`; bounds seeded at open/rescan-rebuild since #382). Detection feeds `BalanceSnapshot.transparent` → the Recv-3 shield this row describes; `propose_shield` sources the store's active set, refunds included. (Historical note: the original deferral text predated ADR-0528 — `transparent-inputs` has been ON the engine since Recv-2; what remained missing until #368 was registration + a poll set that includes refunds.) The IntoZec-delivery half was wired first (§3.3b / ADR-0530): 1Click pays the destination's TRANSPARENT receiver via the same scoped poll; a shielded-paying provider would need no scan (the rare case, handled for free) |
| swap execute | response lost / kill after provider registered | idempotent by provider construction: the deposit address is **quote-anchored** — re-execute against the same quote converges on the same `depositAddress`; the `SwapRecord` ↔ deposit-tx linkage is written in one DB transaction. ⚠️ SCOPE (operational round, S72-cont): the quote-anchored idempotency holds WITHIN a process today (inc-2d-swap-b — the deposit address is frozen in the in-memory `IssuedQuote`, so a same-quote re-execute deposits to the same address; the one-shot `issued.remove` makes execute single-flight, incl. a concurrent double-tap). The CROSS-RESTART half — the durable issued-quote registry + the `SwapRecord` ↔ deposit-tx linkage in one DB transaction — is the **W-swap-3 target, NOT yet built**: after a process kill the in-memory registry is empty, so a re-QUOTE (new address) can queue a second deposit. No ZEC is ever LOST (every deposit tx is gated by the durable `deposit_gate` before signing + bounded by the M1 ceiling), but a crash-then-requote can double-CHARGE until W-swap-3 keys single-flight on the quote id. Host contract until then: a dropped `execute` future is UNKNOWN (poll status), not failed-safe-to-retry |
| sync | mid-batch kill | checkpoint/resume, ≤ one batch lost (§7); the disposable block-cache DB **validated-or-deleted on startup** (SQLite atomicity ⇒ no torn rows — a clean height-prefix survives; a corrupt/wrong-key DB is dropped + recreated empty, §3.2e) |
| sync | connection cut / Tor circuit death | retry-forever + backoff (§6.2), `Stalled`/`Offline` surfaced; scan commits per-batch so no corruption is reachable |
| reorg during downtime | killed before the reorg, reopened after | upstream rewind machinery (`REWIND_DISTANCE`) runs on next sync; surfaced as a `wallet.reorg_rewind` event, never silent |
| wipe | mid-wipe kill | strict order (**keychain-FIRST, per FR-14 §4.3a — SUPERSEDES the older "sealed seed → DB key → files" on-disk-first note**): the host **(0) cancels in-flight network + tears down the runtime** (`set_dormant`/dialer close — honest-off holds THROUGH the wipe, review m4) by `close()`ing, then `wipe(cfg)` **(1) severs the keychain wrap key** — the §4.2a SealKey dies, so BOTH on-disk seals AND the DB ciphertext are dead from that instant — then **(2) `remove_dir_all(db_dir)`** as best-effort cleanup. Keychain-first leaves NO orphaned keychain item (existence oracle) on ANY crash point; the old files-first left the SealKey resident on a mid-wipe crash. Idempotent re-run completes any partial wipe. **Partial-wipe honesty (review HARD-B):** the seed dies in step 1, so any interrupted-wipe residual is non-secret chain cache; the third-party path has NO kill-switch — `wipe` is the strongest gesture it owns. **Pending swaps (review M3):** `wipe` with non-terminal `SwapRecord`s surfaces typed `WipeWithPendingSwap { count }` BEFORE proceeding — a refund landing post-wipe is HD-recoverable on the third-party path (restore from phrase re-derives the refund t-addr); on the Relim panic-wipe path it is **intended total loss** (§4.5) |

UX corollary (gate 2): the broadcast-jitter window (§5.3) rides the
`Queued` status — the user who taps send sees an honest "queued → sent"
transition, never an unexplained delay or a fake instant success.

## 7. Performance

- **Sync:** built-in sync machinery (refinement 1); batched compact-block
  scanning with checkpoint/resume so a killed app loses ≤ one batch
  (`SYNC_BATCH_BLOCKS = 1000` — balances scan throughput vs resume
  granularity on mobile; upstream uses 1000/100-adaptive — drop to
  `SYNC_BATCH_BLOCKS_DENSE = 100` in output-dense ranges, the "sandblasting"
  lesson §1.7; pin after W2 measurement). Compact blocks cache in a **separate,
  `CACHE_MAX_BYTES`-bounded, disposable SQLCipher DB, deleted after scan** (their
  failure was an *unbounded* cache, not the engine — §3.2e). Foreground
  tip-following at `POLL_INTERVAL_SECS = 20` (~block_time/4
  at 75 s blocks — upstream-proven; foreground only, this is NOT a background
  timer). Restore cost is bounded by `birthday` (§2.3) + the bundled
  checkpoints (nearest ≤ birthday). gRPC timeouts split unary vs streaming
  (`GRPC_UNARY_TIMEOUT_SECS = 30` / `GRPC_STREAMING_TIMEOUT_SECS = 100`,
  upstream regression §1.7); sync resilience constants
  `SYNC_BACKOFF_MAX_SECS = 600`, `SYNC_STUCK_WATCHDOG_SECS = 600` (§6.2);
  reorg bounds inherited: `REORG_MAX = 100` / `REWIND_DISTANCE = 10`. Intra-batch
  progress fires every `PROGRESS_REPORT_BLOCKS = 5` blocks during a download
  (iv-d-3-b-i) — DERIVED so `PROGRESS_REPORT_BLOCKS × GRPC_STREAMING_TIMEOUT_SECS <
  SYNC_STUCK_WATCHDOG_SECS`, i.e. any link the per-message idle timeout still
  considers alive re-arms the watchdog before it fires (no false force-restart of a
  slow-but-advancing download).
- **No busy polling, no always-on timers.** The only timer-driven activity:
  (a) in-flight swap status poll — exponential `SWAP_POLL_INITIAL_SECS = 5`
  → `SWAP_POLL_MAX_SECS = 60` (provider settle times are tens of seconds to
  minutes; 5s catches fast settles, 60s caps idle cost), foreground-only,
  stops on terminal status, refresh-on-resume; (b) broadcast jitter (§5.3),
  one-shot.
- **Memory:** trial-decryption batches bounded by the sync engine; FRB
  streams carry snapshots/deltas, never unbounded lists (`history` is paged,
  `HISTORY_PAGE_MAX = 100`).
- **DB queries** ride zcash_client_sqlite's indexed schema; our additions
  (queued-send intents, swap records) declare indexes in their migration and
  get `EXPLAIN`-checked in review (rust-patterns DB rules apply).
- Proving (spend proofs) is CPU-heavy → `spawn_blocking` (never blocks the
  runtime); Orchard proving keys bundled, loaded lazily once.
- `SHIELDING_THRESHOLD_ZAT = 100_000` (0.001 ZEC — the upstream-converged
  value on BOTH Zodl platforms, §1.7: don't burn a ZIP-317 fee shielding
  dust; sanity-check against current marginal fees at W2).
- **Change/note fan-out (tips-critical):** sequential small sends must not
  serialize on a single change note's confirmation (upstream issue class,
  §1.7 — and channel tips are EXACTLY sequential small sends). W2 probe:
  librustzcash change-splitting knobs; until resolved the limit is surfaced
  honestly via `InsufficientFunds { pending_change, .. }`, never a hang.
- **Recipient-side tips at scale (review G4, ack):** a thousands-subscriber
  channel owner receiving tip floods (ADR-0024 territory) is acknowledged
  and deferred — v1 note management handles ordinary volumes; the scale
  answer is a **v1.x additive API** (batch note consolidation), not a v1
  reshape.
- `CACHE_MAX_BYTES` — hard bound on how far the compact-block FS cache may
  run ahead of scanning (disk is a shared resource; an unbounded read-ahead
  on a full disk is M4's spin). All internal durations (watchdog, backoff,
  poll, jitter, proposal TTL) use the **monotonic clock** — a wall-clock
  jump (NTP, timezone, manual set) must not fire the watchdog or freeze
  backoff; only swap deadlines touch wall time, display-only (§2.6).
- `PROPOSAL_TTL` — proposals expire (stale anchors after a long background);
  `ProposalStale` ⇒ re-propose, the fee is re-shown (§3.1).
- Checkpoints seed **new scan starts only** — an in-progress scan range is
  never re-anchored by a checkpoint-bundle refresh arriving with an app
  update mid-restore.

## 9. Multi-platform

| Platform | Posture |
|---|---|
| **iOS** | No long-running background sync (OS limit — honest). Sync runs foreground; the HOST may schedule `BGProcessingTask` windows and call `sync.once()` — the SDK ships suspend/resume + checkpointing (≤ one batch lost, §7), **not** scheduling policy. Long restores progress only while foregrounded — the SDK surfaces restore-in-progress state so the host can show "keep the app open" guidance (upstream pattern, §1.7). FRB streams pause on `AppLifecycleState.paused` (flutter-patterns). Keychain: sealed DB key under standard accessibility — the wallet does NOT need NSE/app-group access (no background decrypt requirement), so it stays main-app-scoped — strictly tighter than the messaging keys. |
| **Android** | Same SDK posture; the host may run a foreground service during long restores (user-visible by OS design — honest). Keystore-sealed DB key. `bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl` if SQLCipher path lands (known gotcha). cargo-ndk build gated in CI. |
| **Desktop** (Win/Mac/Linux) | Full function; longer sync windows acceptable; no OS background-kill, but laptop sleep rides the same monotonic-clock posture as mobile (§7). **macOS PROVEN at S6:** first real pod build + on-desktop bridge E2E green (`flutter test integration_test -d macos` — cargokit→staticlib→`-force_load`→`ExternalLibrary.process` loader→API round-trip on aarch64-apple-darwin; this first-ever link of the bridge caught the Cargokit package-name constraint, §1.2). Linux/Windows ride cargokit's CMake glue — same artifact-name constraint, satisfied by construction now; compile proof owed to a CI lane (Q6). Keychain = platform vault behind the SDK's **own** keychain seam — pattern parity with local-storage's `KeychainBackend`, **never an import of it** (A1: no `relim-*` deps; the §8 dep test enforces). Per-OS vault honesty for the desktop adapter (lands with desktop keychain work, v1.x): macOS = Keychain via `security-framework` (same crate family as iOS); Windows = DPAPI/wincred; Linux = secret-service over DBus, with the HONEST caveat that headless / no-keyring Linux sessions (self-hosters) have **no vault at all** — there the adapter **defaults FAIL-CLOSED** (no vault ⇒ no wallet, with a clear error naming the missing keyring); a file-based fallback is admissible ONLY as an explicit host opt-in carrying its own threat statement (a key file in `$HOME` drops the wrap key from vault-ACL protection to filesystem-permissions-only — readable by any same-user process and by backups), never a peer default and never a silent degrade (S6 money fold). Screen-capture protection has no desktop parity (app-frame spec A8 carries the per-OS statement). **Swap transport on desktop (ADR-0525, 3-lens fold):** identical NetDialer contract as sync — no tor-builtin ⇒ ExternalSocks5 or the host's own dialer; the SDK ships no clearnet dialer that masquerades as a privacy transport — only the explicit `TorPolicy::Off` direct dialer (§3.2a); swap traffic gets no special desktop path. |
| **WASM/web** | **OUT of scope, permanently for Relim** (vision: no web client — keys-in-Rust is violable in WASM) and **out for the SDK v1**: no OS keychain, no sqlite file story, no raw-TCP gRPC; a WASM consumer would also break the i64-fits-in-JS-Number guarantee we document (§2.1). Revisit only post-extraction if the community asks, as a separate threat-model exercise. |

Platform gating in the example app: `Platform.isAndroid || Platform.isIOS`
(never single-platform — flutter-patterns).

**`zcash:` URI scheme registration is HOST responsibility (3-lens fold,
2026-06-13):** the SDK's `parsePaymentUri` takes a string — how it arrives is
the host's integration. iOS: register the `zcash` custom URL scheme in
Info.plist + implement the URL-open handler (raw custom scheme, NOT a
universal link — no associated domain exists for a payment scheme). Android:
declare an `<intent-filter>` with `android:scheme="zcash"` on the receiving
activity. Desktop: OS URI-handler registration per platform, same contract.
The example app demonstrates the QR-scan path; deep-link wiring is
documented, not shipped.

## 10. Multi-device & sync

Wallet state is **chain-derived** — the chain itself is the sync substrate,
which makes multi-device structurally simpler than messaging:

- Same seed on N devices ⇒ each independently derives the same account and
  converges by scanning. No CRDT needed for funds correctness; `relim-sync`
  is not involved.
- **Conflict = double-spend race:** two devices spending overlapping notes —
  one tx mines, the other expires; the loser's funds return to spendable
  (`expired_tx_funds_return_to_spendable`). Surfaced as a normal `Expired`
  history row, not data corruption. v1 accepts this (it is how every HD
  wallet behaves); note-locking across devices would require off-chain
  coordination — explicitly out of scope.
- Address reuse across devices (both hand out the current UA) is
  protocol-acceptable (shielded addresses don't leak linkage on-chain);
  diversifier-index coordination is a post-v1 nicety.
- **Honest-restore caveats (documented, not hidden — §1.7):** two things are
  unrecoverable from seed by protocol design: outputs created with a null
  OVK, and the *full UA* a tx was sent to (seed recovery reveals the
  receiver, not the UA). Restore UX copy must not promise byte-perfect
  history reconstruction.
- **NOT synced (and said honestly):** queued-send intents, swap history, and
  local labels are per-device (the swap record exists only where the swap was
  made). If product wants them mirrored later, that's a `relim-sync` (v2)
  item riding the messaging sync — flagged, not designed here.
- Data model: `SwapRecord`/queued intents carry no device-unique assumptions
  that would break under a future sync (stable ids, timestamps) — design
  invariant 6 honored without speculative machinery.

  audited derivation fails CI) and a determinism check.
- **G7 RESOLVED (crypto audit): Orchard AND Sapling REQUIRED, transparent
  OMITTED** — `UnifiedAddressRequest::custom(Require, Require, Omit)`, NOT the
  `SHIELDED` (Allow/Allow/Omit) const. **The review caught a real funds-receive
  MAJOR here:** with `Allow`, a seed whose Sapling diversifier is invalid at the
  smallest index yields an Orchard-ONLY UA SILENTLY (no error, no forward
  search) — a Sapling-only sender then cannot pay it. The BIP39-vector seed is
  exactly such a seed; the original string-only KAT pinned the Orchard-only
  address green. Fixed: `Require` forces `find_address` forward to a diversifier
  valid for BOTH; the receiver set is also enforced as a CHECKED post-condition
  in `default_address_for` (never assumed from the request — defends a future
  UFVK-reconstruction path); and every pinned UA is decoded independently via
  `zcash_address` with its receiver set asserted. Goldens re-pinned under the
  fixed request (only the BIP39 vector changed; the fixed-seed UAs were already
  index-0-valid for both).
- **§4.2(a) USK residual honored as-built:** the `UnifiedSpendingKey`
  (`Clone + Debug`, no Zeroize upstream) is strictly function-local in
  `default_address_for` — fed a borrowed `&[u8]`, consumed into the UFVK,
  dropped at return; never logged/stored/`Clone`-reached from a DTO. Miri is
  not run on this path (our glue is `forbid(unsafe_code)` over audited curve
  crates — no UB surface of ours; the seal's chacha path remains the
  miri-covered crypto).
- **Defense-in-depth (security review):** `derive_default_address` RE-enforces
  the 32..=252 seed bound at its own door (`from_seed` PANICS under 32 bytes) so
  a panic across FFI is structurally impossible for any future caller, not only
  today's validated paths (`short_seed_is_typed_reject_not_panic`).
